ticket.title: Database Schema - Reviews Table
ticket.description:
Create database schema for product reviews using Drizzle ORM patterns.

## Implementation Details

### Schema Location
`packages/api/src/database/schema/reviews.ts`

### Tables to Create

**reviews table:**
- id: uuid (primary key, defaultRandom)
- productId: uuid (FK to products, onDelete cascade)
- userId: uuid (FK to users, onDelete cascade)
- rating: integer (1-5, not null)
- title: varchar(255)
- content: text
- status: review_status enum (pending, approved, rejected)
- moderatorId: uuid (FK to users, nullable)
- moderatorNotes: text (nullable)
- createdAt: timestamp (defaultNow)
- updatedAt: timestamp (onUpdate)

### Enums
- review_status: pgEnum('review_status', ['pending', 'approved', 'rejected'])

### Indexes
- reviews_product_id_idx (productId)
- reviews_user_id_idx (userId)
- reviews_status_idx (status)
- reviews_created_at_idx (createdAt)

### Relations
- Review -> Product (many-to-one)
- Review -> User as author (many-to-one)
- Review -> User as moderator (many-to-one, nullable)

### Type Exports
- export type Review = typeof reviews.$inferSelect
- export type NewReview = typeof reviews.$inferInsert
- export type ReviewStatus = 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (packages/api/tests/schema/reviews.test.ts)
- Schema structure validation
- Rating constraint (1-5 range)
- Status enum values
- Foreign key relationships
- Index definitions exist

### Test Cases
1. test('reviews table has correct columns')
2. test('review_status enum has correct values')
3. test('rating accepts values 1-5')
4. test('productId foreign key references products')
5. test('userId foreign key references users')
6. test('indexes are defined for common queries')

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Schema file created with proper Drizzle patterns
- [ ] Enum for review status defined
- [ ] All indexes created for query optimization
- [ ] Relations properly configured
- [ ] Types exported for use in API
- [ ] Unit tests written and passing
- [ ] Migration generated and tested

ticket.title: API Routes - Public Review Endpoints
ticket.description:
Create public API endpoints for product reviews following Hono patterns.

## Implementation Details

### Route Location
`packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts`

### Endpoints

**GET /api/products/:productId/reviews**
- List approved reviews for a product
- Query params: page, pageSize, sortBy (newest, highest, lowest)
- Returns: reviews array with pagination
- Caching: Redis with 5 min TTL
- Auth: optionalAuth (for showing user's own pending reviews)

**POST /api/products/:productId/reviews**
- Create new review (requires auth)
- Body: { rating: 1-5, title?: string, content: string }
- Validation: User must have purchased product (optional enforcement)
- Returns: created review with pending status
- Auth: requireAuth

**GET /api/reviews/:reviewId**
- Get single review details
- Returns: review with author info
- Auth: optionalAuth

**PATCH /api/reviews/:reviewId**
- Update own review
- Body: { rating?, title?, content? }
- Constraint: Only owner can update
- Returns: updated review (resets to pending status)
- Auth: requireAuth

**DELETE /api/reviews/:reviewId**
- Delete own review
- Constraint: Only owner can delete
- Auth: requireAuth

### Validation Schemas (Zod)
```typescript
const createReviewSchema = z.object({
  rating: z.number().int().min(1).max(5),
  title: z.string().max(255).optional(),
  content: z.string().min(10).max(5000),
});

const listReviewsSchema = z.object({
  page: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(1),
  pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(10),
  sortBy: z.enum(['newest', 'highest', 'lowest']).default('newest'),
});
```

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (packages/api/tests/routes/reviews.test.ts)

**Configuration Tests**
1. test('GET /products/:productId/reviews route exists')
2. test('POST /products/:productId/reviews route exists')

4. test('DELETE /reviews/:reviewId route exists')

**Validation Tests**
5. test('createReviewSchema validates rating 1-5')
6. test('createReviewSchema rejects rating outside 1-5')
7. test('createReviewSchema requires content min 10 chars')
8. test('listReviewsSchema validates sortBy enum')

**Authorization Tests**

10. test('PATCH requires review owner')
11. test('DELETE requires review owner')

**Runtime Tests (skipIf DB unavailable)**
12. test('lists only approved reviews')
13. test('creates review with pending status')
14. test('updates review resets to pending')
15. test('pagination returns correct page')

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Redis caching for list endpoint
- [x] Only approved reviews visible publicly
- [x] Owner-only update/delete enforcement
- [x] Proper error responses (401, 403, 404)

ticket.title: API Routes - Admin Moderation Endpoints
ticket.description:
Create admin API endpoints for review moderation following established patterns.

## Implementation Details

### Route Location
`packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts`

### Endpoints

**GET /api/admin/reviews**
- List all reviews with filters
- Query params: status, productId, userId, page, pageSize, sortBy
- Returns: reviews with author and product info
- Auth: requireAdmin

**GET /api/admin/reviews/stats**
- Get moderation statistics
- Returns: { pending: number, approved: number, rejected: number, today: number }
- Auth: requireAdmin

**PATCH /api/admin/reviews/:reviewId**
- Moderate review (approve/reject)
- Body: { status: 'approved' | 'rejected', moderatorNotes?: string }

- Auth: requireAdmin

**DELETE /api/admin/reviews/:reviewId**

  productId: z.string().uuid().optional(),

  pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(20),

ticket.title: Database Schema - Shipping and Returns Tables
ticket.description:
Create database schema for shipping options, order shipments, and return requests.

## Implementation Details

### Schema Location
`packages/api/src/database/schema/shipping.ts`
`packages/api/src/database/schema/returns.ts`

### Tables to Create

**shipping_options table:**
- id: uuid (primary key)
- name: varchar(100) (e.g., "Standard Shipping", "Express")
- carrier: varchar(100) (e.g., "USPS", "FedEx", "UPS")
- description: text
- baseCost: decimal(10, 2)
- estimatedDaysMin: integer
- estimatedDaysMax: integer
- isActive: boolean (default true)
- sortOrder: integer
- createdAt, updatedAt

**order_shipments table:**
- id: uuid (primary key)
- orderId: uuid (FK to orders)
- shippingOptionId: uuid (FK to shipping_options)
- trackingNumber: varchar(100) (nullable)
- carrier: varchar(100)
- status: shipment_status enum
- shippedAt: timestamp (nullable)
- estimatedDeliveryAt: timestamp (nullable)
- deliveredAt: timestamp (nullable)
- trackingUrl: varchar(500) (nullable)
- notes: text (nullable)
- createdAt, updatedAt

**return_policies table:**
- id: uuid (primary key)
- name: varchar(100)
- description: text
- daysAllowed: integer (e.g., 30)
- conditionRequired: varchar(255) (e.g., "unopened", "unused")
- refundType: refund_type enum (full, partial, store_credit)
- refundPercentage: integer (1-100)
- isActive: boolean
- createdAt, updatedAt

**return_requests table:**
- id: uuid (primary key)
- orderId: uuid (FK to orders)
- userId: uuid (FK to users)
- reason: return_reason enum
- reasonDetails: text
- status: return_status enum
- requestedAt: timestamp (defaultNow)
- approvedAt: timestamp (nullable)
- processedAt: timestamp (nullable)
- refundAmount: decimal(10, 2) (nullable)
- adminNotes: text (nullable)
- createdAt, updatedAt

### Enums
- shipment_status: 'pending', 'label_created', 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered', 'failed'
- return_reason: 'defective', 'wrong_item', 'not_as_described', 'changed_mind', 'other'
- return_status: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'shipped_back', 'received', 'refunded', 'closed'
- refund_type: 'full', 'partial', 'store_credit'

### Indexes
- order_shipments_order_id_idx
- order_shipments_status_idx
- return_requests_order_id_idx
- return_requests_user_id_idx
- return_requests_status_idx

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests
1. test('shipping_options table has correct columns')
2. test('order_shipments table has correct columns')
3. test('return_policies table has correct columns')
4. test('return_requests table has correct columns')

6. test('return_reason enum has all values')
7. test('return_status enum has all values')
8. test('foreign keys reference correct tables')

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All tables created with proper structure
- [x] All enums defined
- [x] Indexes for common queries
- [x] Relations configured
- [x] Types exported
- [x] Unit tests passing (44/44)
- [x] Migration tested

- Alternative: Replicate ESRGAN

- 2x: 1.5x base generation cost

- Deduct from wallet before processing

ticket.title: Test Bug: Google OAuth divider text - incorrect text selector
ticket.description:
## Test Failure
**File**: `tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts`
**Test**: Login Page › Google OAuth › should have divider with "or sign in with email" text
**Line**: 96

## Error (Test Infrastructure Issue)
```
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed

Locator: locator('text=or sign in with email')
Expected: visible
Timeout: 5000ms
Error: element(s) not found
```

## Classification
This is a **test bug** - the selector `text=or sign in with email` doesn't match the actual divider text on the page. The text might be "or continue with email" or similar.

## Fix
Check the actual UI text in the login page and update the test selector to match.

comments.author: mcp-client

**Commit**: `30cd1a59` - fix(tests): Correct auth test selectors for divider and OTP resend

**Files Changed**:
- `tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` - Fixed divider text selector

**Summary**:
Changed test from looking for "or sign in with email" to just "or" with exact match using `getByText('or', { exact: true })` to match the actual UI divider text.

**Root Cause**: The test expected "or sign in with email" but the actual UI only shows "or" in the divider.

**Tests**: Verified passing with `bunx playwright test --grep "should have divider"`

ticket.title: Bug: Boolean filter URL params lost during SSR redirect
ticket.description:
## Issue
When navigating to URLs with boolean filter params (isAiGenerated, isFeatured), the params are stripped during TanStack Router's 307 redirect.

## Test
`tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` - "should show AI Generated in active filter tags"

## Root Cause
The validateSearch function converts string 'true' to boolean true, but TanStack Router doesn't properly serialize booleans back to URL strings during redirect reconstruction.

Evidence:
- `/posters?styles=abstract` → 200 OK (string params work)
- `/posters?isAiGenerated=true` → 307 redirect to `/posters` (boolean param lost)
- `/posters?styles=abstract&isAiGenerated=true` → 307 to `/posters?styles=abstract` (only boolean stripped)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Navigate directly to `/posters?isAiGenerated=true`
2. Server returns 307 redirect to `/posters`
3. Query param is lost, filter not applied

## Fix Options
1. Keep boolean params as strings in validateSearch: `isAiGenerated: search.isAiGenerated as string | undefined`
2. Add search param stringifyFn to route definition
3. Use z.coerce for proper serialization

## Files
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` - Fix validateSearch or add stringifyFn

## Priority
Medium - affects direct URL navigation with boolean filters, but clicking filters in UI works

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
**Investigation Results**

Added 3 AI-generated products to seed data (Neural Dreams, Digital Cosmos, Synthetic Nature).
The API correctly returns only these 3 products when filtered with isAiGenerated=true.

**However**, discovered a deeper bug: TanStack Router/Start 307 redirects strip query parameters.

Evidence:
- `curl -v "http://localhost:3001/posters?isAiGenerated=true"` returns 307 redirect
- Location header: `/posters` (query params stripped!)
- SSR response shows `filters.isAiGenerated: void 0` (undefined)

**Root Cause**: The trailing slash redirect removes query parameters.
This affects ALL filter URLs, not just isAiGenerated.

**Further investigation**: The issue is boolean param serialization!
- `/posters?styles=abstract` → 200 OK
- `/posters?styles=abstract&isAiGenerated=true` → 307 to `/posters?styles=abstract`

The boolean params (isAiGenerated, isFeatured) are being lost during URL reconstruction.
The validateSearch converts string 'true' to boolean true, but TanStack doesn't serialize it back.

**Fix**: Either:
1. Change validateSearch to keep isAiGenerated/isFeatured as string 'true'/'false'
2. Or add proper search param serialization in the route definition

The test should remain skipped until this serialization bug is fixed.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
**Completed**

**Commit**: `532fffe4` - fix(filters): Preserve boolean URL params during SSR redirect

**Root Cause**: TanStack Router's default URL parser (`qss.decode()`) converts `'true'`/`'false'` strings to JavaScript booleans at the URL level, before `validateSearch` runs. During 307 redirects (trailing slash normalization), booleans can't be serialized back to URL strings, so they're silently dropped from the redirect Location header.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/router.tsx` - Added custom `parseSearch`/`stringifySearch` functions that keep all URL values as strings, preventing boolean coercion at the URL parsing layer
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` - Updated `validateSearch` to handle both boolean and string `'true'` values
- `packages/web/app/routes/auth/login.tsx` - Updated Zod schema `registered` field to use `z.preprocess()` for string-to-boolean coercion (needed since URL values are now strings)
- `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` - Unskipped "should show AI Generated in active filter tags" test

**Verification**: All 8 E2E test runs pass (Chromium, Mobile Chrome, Firefox, WebKit, Mobile Safari). All URL scenarios return 200: `?isAiGenerated=true`, `?styles=abstract`, mixed params, and `?registered=true` on login.

ticket.title: Consolidate test runner scripts into single unified script
ticket.description:
## Summary

Consolidated two overlapping test runner scripts (`tests/run-all-tests.sh` and `scripts/run-tests.sh`) into a single unified script at `scripts/run-tests.sh` with a subcommand architecture.

## Problem

Two test runner scripts evolved separately:
- `tests/run-all-tests.sh` — heavily used, referenced in 5+ skill/doc files, had sophisticated features (--setup-only, --file, --grep, --max-failures)
- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — standard location, had unit/integration/CI modes but lacked E2E options

## Solution

Merged both into `scripts/run-tests.sh` with 6 subcommands:
- `all` (default) — setup + unit + integration + E2E
- `unit` — unit tests only, no Docker
- `integration` — setup/integration tests
- `e2e` — setup infra + E2E with Playwright
- `ci` — assume services exist, run everything
- `setup` — setup infra only, leave servers running (replaces --setup-only)

Flags: `--project`, `--file`, `--grep`, `--max-failures`, `--workers`, `--help`

## Files Changed (7 files, +475/-586 lines)

1. `scripts/run-tests.sh` — Rewritten with merged features
2. `tests/run-all-tests.sh` — Deleted
3. `docs/TEST-EXECUTION-REMEDIATION.md` — Updated script reference
4. `docs/manual-tests/smoke-test.md` — `--setup-only` → `setup`
5. `.claude/skills/tt-debug-browser/SKILL.md` — Updated path + command
6. `.claude/skills/tt-fix-tests/SKILL.md` + CLAUDE.md — Updated all references
7. `.claude/skills/tt-run-test-suit/SKILL.md` — Updated all references

## Command Migration

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| `./tests/run-all-tests.sh` | `./scripts/run-tests.sh e2e` |
| `./tests/run-all-tests.sh --setup-only` | `./scripts/run-tests.sh setup` |
| `./tests/run-all-tests.sh --file=X` | `./scripts/run-tests.sh e2e --file=X` |
| `./tests/run-all-tests.sh --max-failures=N` | `./scripts/run-tests.sh e2e --max-failures=N` |

## Verification

- Zero remaining references to `tests/run-all-tests.sh` in codebase

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
## Bugfix: `set -e` incompatibility with `&&` short-circuit

**Amended commit**: `eabe5592`

**Bug**: `[ -z "$COMMAND" ] && COMMAND="all"` on line 111 caused the script to exit immediately when a command was provided (e.g. `setup`). Under `set -e`, when `$COMMAND` is non-empty, `[ -z "$COMMAND" ]` returns 1, and the `&&` short-circuit propagates that as the expression's exit code, triggering `set -e` to abort.

**Fix**: Replaced with `if [ -z "$COMMAND" ]; then COMMAND="all"; fi`.

**Verified**: `./scripts/run-tests.sh setup` now works — Docker, DB, and dev servers come up correctly.

ticket.title: Add stop, clean, and --no-seed commands to unified test runner
ticket.description:
## Summary

Add missing lifecycle commands to `scripts/run-tests.sh` for stopping, cleaning, and controlling database seeding.

## Requirements

### New Subcommands
1. **`stop`** — Kill dev servers and optionally stop Docker services
2. **`clean`** — Stop everything + wipe DB/containers (full teardown)

### New Flag
3. **`--no-seed`** — Bring up infrastructure without seeding test data (for `setup`, `e2e`, `all` commands)

## Context

After #181 consolidated the test runner, the `setup` command starts everything but:
- There's no matching `stop` to tear it down (only manual `kill <PID>`)
- No way to do a full clean teardown (Docker + DB)
- DB always gets reseeded on `setup`, with no option to skip

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `./scripts/run-tests.sh stop` kills dev servers and stops Docker
- [ ] `./scripts/run-tests.sh clean` does full teardown including DB wipe
- [ ] `./scripts/run-tests.sh setup --no-seed` brings up infra without seeding
- [ ] All new commands documented in `--help` output
- [ ] Skill/doc references updated if needed

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
## Implementation Plan

### 1. PID file for cross-session tracking

Write PID to `/tmp/masonart-dev.pid` in `start_dev_servers()`. Read from PID file in `stop`/`clean`. Fallback: kill by port via `lsof`. Clean up PID file after kill.

### 2. New subcommand: `stop`

```
./scripts/run-tests.sh stop
```
- Kill dev servers (PID file → fallback to port-based lsof)
- Stop Docker containers (`docker compose stop` — preserves volumes)

### 3. New subcommand: `clean`

```
./scripts/run-tests.sh clean
```
- Kill dev servers
- Remove Docker containers AND volumes (`docker compose down -v`)
- Remove temp files (PID, dev log, credentials file)

### 4. Seed control — minimal by default, opt-in for more

**Default `setup`**: Migrate schema + seed frames + create one admin user

| Flag | Seeds | Use case |
|------|-------|----------|
| *(none)* | Frames + 1 admin | Clean dev env |
| `--seed-products` | + 36 products | Browse catalog |
| `--seed-users` | + 8 test users | E2E prep |
| Both flags | Everything | Full test data |

**`e2e` and `all` commands**: Auto-enable both flags (tests need full data).

### 5. Credentials output file

Path: `/tmp/masonart-credentials.txt` — written after every seed operation with username/password/role of all seeded users. Also displayed in terminal.

### 6. New file: `packages/api/src/database/seed-admin.ts`

Minimal script: seed frames + 1 admin user (`admin@masonart.com` / `AdminPass123!`). Idempotent. Add `"seed:admin"` to `packages/api/package.json`.

### Files to modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/run-tests.sh` | Add stop, clean, seed flags, PID file, credentials output |
| `packages/api/src/database/seed-admin.ts` | Create: frames + 1 admin user |
| `packages/api/package.json` | Add `seed:admin` script entry |

### Updated help output

```
Commands: all, unit, integration, e2e, ci, setup, stop, clean
Seed flags: --seed-products, --seed-users
```

### Verification

1. `./scripts/run-tests.sh setup` → frames + admin, credentials file written
2. `./scripts/run-tests.sh setup --seed-products --seed-users` → full data
3. `./scripts/run-tests.sh stop` → servers + Docker stopped
4. `./scripts/run-tests.sh clean` → everything wiped
5. `./scripts/run-tests.sh e2e` → auto-seeds everything

|------|--------|-------------|
| `packages/api/src/database/seed-admin.ts` | Created | Minimal seed: 8 frames + 1 admin user (admin@masonart.com / AdminPass123!). Idempotent — skips if data exists. |
| `packages/api/package.json` | Modified | Added `"seed:admin"` script entry |

### New Subcommands

- **`stop`** — Kills dev servers (reads PID from `/tmp/masonart-dev.pid`, fallback to port-based `lsof` on 3000/3001), stops Docker containers with `docker compose stop` (preserves volumes/data)
- **`clean`** — Full destructive teardown: kills dev servers, removes Docker containers AND volumes (`docker compose down -v`), deletes temp files (PID file, dev log, credentials file)

### Seed Control

Default `setup` now seeds minimally (frames + admin only). Opt-in flags for more data:

| Flag | What it seeds | Use case |
|------|--------------|----------|
| *(none)* | Frames + 1 admin user | Clean dev environment |
| `--seed-products` | + 36 sample products with variants | Browse catalog locally |
| `--seed-users` | + 9 test users (customers, admins, trade) | E2E test prep |
| Both flags | Everything | Full test data |

`e2e` and `all` commands automatically enable both `--seed-products` and `--seed-users`.

### Additional Features

- **PID file** at `/tmp/masonart-dev.pid` for cross-session server tracking
- **Credentials file** at `/tmp/masonart-credentials.txt` generated after every seed with all username/password/role combos
- **seed-admin.ts** creates frames idempotently (checks if frames exist before inserting) and creates admin user idempotently (checks if email exists)

### Deviation from Original Ticket

The ticket originally specified `--no-seed`. The plan evolved to use opt-in `--seed-products` and `--seed-users` instead, because the minimal seed (frames + admin) is always needed for a usable app. This is a better UX — default gives you a working app, flags add test data.

ticket.title: Bug: Admin sign out tests fail after domcontentloaded migration
ticket.description:
## Failing Tests
**File**: `tests/e2e/admin-auth.spec.ts`
**Tests**: 
- Admin Sign Out › should redirect to home after sign out
- Admin Sign Out › should not allow access to admin after sign out

## Error
```
Expected pattern: /^\/$|\/auth\/login/
Received string: "http://localhost:3001/admin"
```

## Root Cause
Two issues:
1. After replacing `networkidle` with `domcontentloaded` (ticket #186), the Sign Out button click had no effect because React hadn't hydrated yet - the onClick handler wasn't attached.
2. The URL regex `^\/$` was anchored to match only `/` but Playwright matches against the full URL `http://localhost:3001/`.

## Fix
1. Wait for dashboard API response before clicking Sign Out (proves React hydration):
   ```typescript
   await Promise.all([
     page.waitForResponse(resp => resp.url().includes('/api/admin/') && resp.status() === 200),
     page.goto('/admin')
   ]);
   ```
2. Fixed URL regex to `localhost:\d+\/$|\/auth\/login` to match full URLs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Both sign out tests pass
- [x] All 35 admin-auth tests pass
- [x] No regressions

ticket.title: Bug: Checkout shipping mock data mismatch and wrong assertion text
ticket.description:
## Failing Tests
**File**: `tests/e2e/checkout.spec.ts`

3. **Wrong delivery format**: Tests expected "5-7 business days" text but component shows "Arrives {date range}" via `formatEstimatedDelivery()`

## Fixes

3. Updated delivery days assertions to check for "Arrives" text

- [x] All 111 checkout tests pass
- [x] Mock data matches ShippingEstimateResponse interface

ticket.title: Bug: Customer approval tests failing due to mock pattern and strict mode violations
ticket.description:
## Failing Tests
**File**: `tests/e2e/customer-approval.spec.ts`

### Failures (6 total):
1. **Line 183**: "displays order item information" - strict mode: getByText matched 2 elements
2. **Line 188**: "displays status badge correctly" - strict mode: /Ready for Review/i matched badge + comment text
3. **Line 268**: "gallery has navigation arrows" - locator targeted button but "1/3" is a div
4. **Line 317**: "can submit change request" - mock didn't intercept POST /changes (Unauthorized)
5. **Line 378**: "clicking Approve shows confirmation" - mock didn't intercept POST /approve (Unauthorized)
6. **Line 433**: "shows expired message" - strict mode: regex matched badge "Expired" + heading

## Root Causes
1. **Route glob pattern**: `**/api/approvals/*` only matches single-segment paths. POST endpoints like `/api/approvals/{token}/approve` (2 segments) fell through to real API → 401 Unauthorized
2. **Strict mode violations**: Text selectors matched multiple elements (badge + comment, badge + heading, subtitle + item name)
3. **Gallery locator**: "1 / 3" counter is a div, not inside a button element

## Fixes
1. Changed glob to `**/api/approvals/**` for all 3 mock functions
2. Used `{ exact: true }` for ambiguous text selectors
3. Fixed gallery locator to find text in gallery overlay div
4. Used specific h2 locator for expired heading

All 37 tests pass.

ticket.title: Bug: wallet.spec.ts auth session expires during full suite run
ticket.description:
## Failing Test
**File**: `tests/e2e/wallet.spec.ts`
**Test**: Wallet Page - Authenticated › should load wallet page without redirect
**Line**: 82

## Error
```
page.waitForURL(/\/account\/wallet/) - timeout
Page redirected to /auth/login instead of staying on /account/wallet
```

## Root Cause
Better Auth's cookie cache expires in 5 minutes (`cookieCache: { maxAge: 60 * 5 }`). When running the full E2E suite (7.5+ minutes), the session cookie expires before wallet tests run, causing auth redirects.

## Fix
1. Added re-auth `beforeEach` hooks to all 6 authenticated describe blocks that check auth status and re-login if session expired
2. Replaced `networkidle` with `domcontentloaded` in wait states
3. Removed file-level `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` that caused cascading skips on failure
4. Fixed `.count()` auto-wait issue in quick top-up buttons test by adding `.first().toBeVisible()` before counting

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All 23 wallet tests pass
- [x] Tests resilient to session expiry during long suite runs

ticket.title: Products API (/api/products) hangs indefinitely - empty reply from server
ticket.description:
## Bug
GET `/api/products` never returns a response. After ~9 seconds, curl reports "Empty reply from server" (HTTP 000). This affects the entire product catalog - the /posters page shows "No products found" and product detail pages show "Product Not Found".

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `curl -v http://localhost:3000/api/products` 
2. Wait 10 seconds
3. Observe "Empty reply from server"

## Interesting Detail
- `/api/products/` (WITH trailing slash) returns 401 Unauthorized immediately
- `/api/products` (WITHOUT trailing slash) hangs forever
- This suggests a routing inconsistency

## Impact
- Product listing page shows no products
- Product detail pages show "Product Not Found"
- Cart items link to products that can't be viewed
- Core e-commerce functionality is completely broken

## Expected
200 OK with paginated product list

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text: ✅ Closed as no-longer-reproducible (2026-07-27). GET /api/products returns 200 in 0.73s on local dev (fresh servers, dev DB) and 200 in 0.98s on production https://chobii.art/api/products. The Feb-era hang was fixed by intervening work (server/caching fixes between Feb and the July go-live). The /posters page also verifiedly renders a full catalog in the content-manager E2E suite (passing 2026-07-27).

ticket.title: DELETE /api/cart returns 404 instead of 401 when unauthenticated
ticket.description:
## Bug

When calling `DELETE /api/cart` without authentication, the endpoint returns `{"error":"No cart found"}` with HTTP 404 instead of the expected 401 Unauthorized.

## Expected Behavior
Should return 401 Unauthorized like all other cart endpoints (POST, PUT, DELETE /api/cart/:id).

## Actual Behavior
- `POST /api/cart` → 401 ✅
- `PUT /api/cart/test` → 401 ✅  
- `DELETE /api/cart/test` → 401 ✅
- `DELETE /api/cart` → 404 `{"error":"No cart found"}` ❌

## Impact
1. **Inconsistent API behavior**: One cart endpoint bypasses auth, others don't
2. **Information leakage**: Reveals whether a cart exists without authentication
3. **Security concern**: Auth middleware may not be applied to this route

## Steps to Reproduce
```bash
curl -s -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/api/cart
# Returns: {"error":"No cart found"} HTTP:404
# Expected: {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Authentication required","code":"UNAUTHORIZED"} HTTP:401
```

- Documentation/tests should reference `/api/auth/get-session`

## Actual Behavior
- `GET /api/auth/session` → 404
- `GET /api/auth/get-session` → 200 (returns null for unauthenticated, user data for authenticated)

## Impact
- Developer confusion when integrating
- Test specs reference wrong endpoint
- API inconsistency with Better Auth conventions

## Steps to Reproduce
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/auth/session -w " HTTP:%{http_code}"
# Returns: HTTP:404

curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/auth/get-session -w " HTTP:%{http_code}"

This may be by design with Better Auth - the `/get-session` endpoint is Better Auth's convention. If so, the test documentation should be updated to match.

ticket.title: Web server (SSR) missing ALL security headers
ticket.description:
## Bug

The React Router v7 SSR web server (localhost:3001) serves pages with NO security headers at all, while the API server (localhost:3000) has comprehensive security headers.

## Web Server Headers (Missing ALL)
```
HTTP/1.1 200 
Vary: Origin
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Date: ...
Connection: keep-alive
```

## API Server Headers (Comprehensive)
```
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
X-XSS-Protection: 0
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off
X-Download-Options: noopen
X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none
```

## Missing Security Headers on Web
- `Strict-Transport-Security` (HSTS)
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`
- `Content-Security-Policy`
- `Referrer-Policy`
- `Permissions-Policy`

## Impact
- **Clickjacking vulnerability**: No X-Frame-Options means site can be embedded in iframes
- **MIME type sniffing**: No X-Content-Type-Options
- **No HSTS**: Browser won't enforce HTTPS
- **No CSP**: No Content Security Policy protection
- Affects ALL pages (/, /posters, /create, /gallery, /cart, /checkout, /auth/*)

## Suggestion
Add security headers middleware to the React Router v7 SSR server, similar to what the API uses (likely `helmet` or equivalent for Hono).

ticket.title: No rate limiting on authentication endpoints
ticket.description:
## Bug

Authentication endpoints (sign-in, sign-up) have no rate limiting headers and no apparent rate limiting enforcement.

## Testing
```bash
# No rate limit headers found on any auth endpoint
curl -sI -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/sign-in/email \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"t@t.com","password":"t"}'
# No X-RateLimit-*, Retry-After, or similar headers
```

## Impact
- **Brute force attacks**: Attackers can try unlimited password combinations
- **Credential stuffing**: No protection against automated credential testing
- **Account enumeration**: No throttling on sign-up/sign-in attempts
- **DoS vector**: Auth endpoints likely hit the database per request

## Expected Behavior
Auth endpoints should:
1. Return rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)
2. Return 429 Too Many Requests after threshold (e.g., 5 attempts per minute per IP)
3. Implement progressive delays or CAPTCHA after repeated failures

## Note
The API middleware directory has `rate-limit` referenced. Redis is available for rate limiting. The infrastructure exists but may not be applied to auth routes.

ticket.title: SECURITY: trust cf-connecting-ip for client IPs — first XFF entry is spoofable behind the tunnel
ticket.description:
Phase: Hardening. packages/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:26 takes the FIRST x-forwarded-for entry. Behind the tunnel every socket peer is cloudflared and Cloudflare APPENDS the real client IP — the first entry is attacker-controlled, so per-IP rate limits are trivially bypassed by rotating fake XFF values; conversely a naive peer-address fallback would collapse all users into one shared bucket.

Fix (TDD):
- clientIp(): prefer cf-connecting-ip header; fall back to XFF LAST-hop, then socket peer.
- Better Auth: advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders = ['cf-connecting-ip','x-forwarded-for'].
- Tests: spoofed-first-XFF request does not evade the limit; two distinct cf-connecting-ip values get distinct buckets.

Acceptance: unit tests green; gate walkthrough verifies 429 from one device while a second device is unaffected.
Lesson: cc #95.

ticket.title: BUG: wildcard requireAuth on /api-mounted sub-apps gated health/tracking/webhooks; onError collapsed HTTPExceptions to 500
ticket.description:
Two compounding production bugs found while booting the prod stack: (1) shipmentsApp and returnsApp are mounted at bare /api but registered `use("*", requireAuth)`, which auth-gated every later-registered /api route — /api/health (healthcheck could never pass, so web could never start), public order tracking, approvals, and Razorpay webhooks (payments would break). (2) app.onError converted every HTTPException (401/403/404) into a 500 and paged Sentry/Slack for each, which is also why ~500 unit tests appeared to fail with 500-instead-of-401 and were being misread as environmental.

Fix: scope the middleware to each sub-app's own route patterns; add an HTTPException passthrough at the top of onError (expected HTTP errors keep status, no alerting). Unit suite: 540 failures → 56 (remaining are stale expectations: old /health shape, unmodeled 429s).

ticket.title: Upgrade TanStack Start to 1.168+ and remove custom serve.ts static-serving wrapper
ticket.description:
## Context

The web container originally failed in production because @tanstack/react-start 1.149 (masonart's lockfile pin) does not serve client assets from its SSR bundle. A custom 39-line `packages/web/serve.ts` wrapper was written mid-deploy (commit d79cb4f6) to serve `dist/client` with immutable cache headers and delegate everything else to SSR.

customs-copilot — the proven deployment reference — pins @tanstack/react-start 1.168.27 / react-router 1.170.17, where the server bundle serves client assets natively and the container runs `bun run packages/web/dist/server/server.js` directly. Both repos declare the same `^1.93.0` semver range; the difference is purely lockfile resolution, so the upgrade is a `bun update`, no package.json change.

Latest published: react-start 1.168.32, react-router 1.170.18.

## Goal

Converge masonart with customs-copilot: upgrade the lockfile pins, delete serve.ts, and run the built server bundle directly in the Docker web stage.

## Implementation Steps

- [ ] **Step 1 [verify-pass]**: Baseline — confirm existing build + web tests pass before touching anything
  - Run: `bun run build && bun run test --filter web` (or `cd packages/web && bun run test`)
  - Expected: PASS (existing behavior baseline)

- [ ] **Step 2 [implement]**: Upgrade TanStack packages within the existing semver range
  - Run: `bun update @tanstack/react-start @tanstack/react-router`
  - Verify bun.lock now pins react-start ~1.168.32 and react-router ~1.170.18
  - Regenerate route tree if needed; fix any type/build fallout (expect possible churn from restructured start-plugin-core / new peer deps)

- [ ] **Step 3 [verify-pass]**: Production build passes and server bundle serves client assets natively
  - Run: `cd packages/web && bun run build`, then `bun run dist/server/server.js` and curl `/` (SSR HTML 200) and a `/assets/*.js` file (200 with content)
  - Expected: PASS — assets served without serve.ts

- [ ] **Step 4 [implement]**: Remove the wrapper
  - Delete `packages/web/serve.ts`
  - `packages/web/package.json`: `"start": "bun run dist/server/server.js"` (match customs-copilot)
  - `Dockerfile` web stage: drop the `COPY ... serve.ts` line; `CMD ["bun", "run", "packages/web/dist/server/server.js"]`

- [ ] **Step 5 [verify-pass]**: Docker image works end-to-end
  - Run: `docker build --target web -t masonart-web:tanstack-upgrade .` then run the container and verify: `/` returns SSR HTML 200, `/assets/*.js` returns 200, cache-control headers on /assets/ are long-lived/immutable, healthcheck passes
  - Expected: PASS. If 1.168 does not emit immutable cache headers on /assets/, note it — Cloudflare edge caching may compensate, but record the delta before accepting it

- [ ] **Step 6 [verify-pass]**: Full repo checks — `bun run typecheck && bun run test`
  - Expected: PASS (no regression from router 1.170 type changes)

- [ ] **Step 7 [commit]**: Commit
  - Run: `git add -A && git commit -m "refactor(web): upgrade TanStack Start to 1.168, drop serve.ts wrapper (#<ticket>)"`

## Verification gates

- Production build passes
- Docker web image serves static assets (with acceptable cache headers) and SSR
- routeTree.gen.ts valid, typecheck + tests green
- Deploy to staging afterward via `make -C deploy build-push-deploy` (sha-tag rollback available) — deliberately AFTER this ticket, before/independent of the #294 gate walkthrough

ticket.title: Bug - Phone OTP login never completes: session cookie doesn't match Better Auth format
ticket.description:
## Bug
Phone-OTP login silently fails on any HTTPS deployment: the user enters the correct OTP, the server verifies it (POST /api/phone-auth/verify-otp returns 200 and logs "User logged in via phone"), but the browser stays on the login screen — the session is never recognized.

## Root Cause
packages/api/src/routes/phone-auth.ts creates the Better Auth session row manually and hand-rolls the Set-Cookie header. Two mismatches vs what Better Auth's get-session actually reads:
1. **Cookie name**: on secure (HTTPS) deployments Better Auth uses `__Secure-chobii.session_token`; the code set the unprefixed `chobii.session_token`.
2. **Cookie value**: Better Auth cookies are signed — `<token>.<url-encoded base64 HMAC-SHA256(secret, token)>`; the code set the raw unsigned token, which fails signature validation even under the right name.

Result: get-session finds no valid cookie → returns null → login UI never advances. Latent day-one bug — phone login has never worked over HTTPS; it surfaced during the first real OTP test on staging (2Factor key provisioning, cc #313). Signature format was confirmed by reproducing a captured live Better Auth signature byte-for-byte with HMAC-SHA256.

## Fix
New helper packages/api/src/lib/session-cookie.ts — buildSessionCookie()/signSessionToken() emit Better Auth's exact name + signed value; phone-auth.ts now uses it. TDD: packages/api/tests/lib/session-cookie.test.ts (3 tests, incl. a regression anchor against the captured live signature). Side effect: 2 previously-failing phone-auth.test.ts assertions now pass (18 pre-existing DB-dependent failures remain vs 20 before).

## Commit
d058e0b1 fix(api): phone-auth session cookie now matches Better Auth format (pushed to main)

## Verification
- Unit: session-cookie tests 3/3 green; signature matches live Better Auth cookie
- Staging: api image rebuild + deploy in flight; final gate = user retests phone OTP login on https://chobii.xtoms.xyz and lands in their account

Remaining: step 5 live gate — user retests phone OTP login on https://chobii.xtoms.xyz/auth/login (OTP arrives via voice call until DLT templates are registered, cc #313). On confirmation, move to done.

ticket.title: Bug - Google OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch: chobii.xtoms.xyz callback not registered in Google Cloud Console
ticket.description:
## Bug
Google sign-in on staging fails with **Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch** — Google rejects the flow before any app code runs:
```
redirect_uri=https://chobii.xtoms.xyz/api/auth/callback/google
flowName=GeneralOAuthFlow
```

## Root Cause
No code bug. Better Auth derives the callback URL from BETTER_AUTH_URL (now https://chobii.xtoms.xyz after the rebrand), but the Google Cloud Console OAuth client only has the old hostname(s) in its Authorized redirect URIs. Note: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are reused from the customs-copilot OAuth client (per claude-mem #4904), so the client also serves customs.xtoms.xyz — the fix is to ADD the new URI, not replace existing ones.

## Fix (Google Cloud Console — user/dashboard only, no code change)
1. console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Credentials → the OAuth 2.0 Client ID used by GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
2. Authorized redirect URIs → ADD: `https://chobii.xtoms.xyz/api/auth/callback/google`
3. Authorized JavaScript origins → ADD: `https://chobii.xtoms.xyz` (if origins are enforced)
4. Optionally prune stale masonart.xtoms.xyz / chobi.xtoms.xyz entries
5. Google propagation can take a few minutes

## Cutover Note
The future chobii.art production domain needs the same registration (`https://chobii.art/api/auth/callback/google`) — tracked in cutover checklist #316.

## Context
Config lives in packages/api/src/auth/index.ts:189 (google provider) with BETTER_AUTH_URL from docker/docker-compose.prod.yml. Manual verification — no automated test applicable (external service registration).

JS origins intentionally not required (server-side redirect flow only, no Google JS SDK). Owner account + shared-client gotchas documented in docs/EXTERNAL-SERVICES.md (6f222e29) and project memory.

ticket.title: Bug - AI generation worker never calls real providers: stub pipeline stores JSON placeholders
ticket.description:
## Bug
Every AI generation "succeeds" but stores a 107-byte JSON placeholder ({"type":"placeholder",...}) as the image, served with content-type image/png. Discovered during #315 provider verification on staging: generation completed instantly and the CDN object was not an image.

## Root Cause
Two parallel implementations exist and were never connected:
- packages/api/src/ai/generator.ts exports generateImages() — the REAL implementation (Replicate/DALL-E/FAL/Gemini, built by gemini-direct-provider feature) — but it is never called from anywhere (repo-wide grep: zero call sites).
- packages/api/src/queues/ai-generation.ts (the BullMQ worker that processes every job) has its own older generateImagesWithAI() whose callReplicateAPI/callOpenAIAPI/callFalAI are all TODO stubs returning createPlaceholderImage(), and its dispatch switch has no "gemini" case (falls through to the Replicate stub).

So AI generation has never produced a real image in any environment; keys were never the issue.

## Fix
Wire the worker to the real engine: generateImagesWithAI() delegates to generateImages() from ../ai/generator (which handles provider selection, prompt enhancement, dimensions, and per-provider calls), maps GeneratedImage[] → the worker's GeneratedImageBuffer[] (shapes are near-identical), throws on failure so jobs fail honestly instead of storing placeholders, and the dead stub functions are deleted.

## Verification
Unit: mocked-generator delegation test. Live: real generation on staging via gemini → actual PNG bytes stored in chobii-staging R2 and served from chobii-cdn.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Wiring fix deployed and live-verified in behavior: generation job now honestly FAILS ("AI generation returned no images") instead of storing a placeholder — refund path triggers. Two further blockers found and addressed during the live gate:
1. gemini-2.0-flash-exp was retired by Google (404) — fixed: default now gemini-2.5-flash-image with GEMINI_IMAGE_MODEL env override (commit 3f1f124a; needs next deploy to take effect).
2. HARD BLOCKER for the final PNG-on-CDN gate: the Gemini API free tier has ZERO image-generation quota — all image models (2.5-flash-image, 3.1-flash-image, 3-pro-image) return quota-exceeded on an unbilled key. Real generation requires either billing enabled on the Google key (~$0.04/img flash image) or funded fal.ai credits (~$0.003/img FLUX schnell — key already in deploy/.env, parked). User decision pending.

ticket.description:
## Task
Create a new admin customers route file with two endpoints:
- `GET /api/admin/customers` — paginated user list (id, name, email, role, createdAt)
- `PUT /api/admin/customers/:id/role` — assign role, Zod-restricted to `customer | content-manager`

Both gated `requireAuth` + `requireAdmin` (NOT requireContentManager — content-managers must not manage roles).

## Context
Part of feature: content-manager-role
Phase: Backend API

No admin customers route exists yet (`packages/api/src/routes/admin/` has no customers.ts). Follow the sub-app pattern of sibling files (e.g. products.ts): create Hono sub-app, gate with `.use("*", ...)`, register in `packages/api/src/index.ts` alongside the other /api/admin/* mounts.

Security invariants (design decision 3 — no privilege escalation):
- Zod schema only accepts `customer` or `content-manager` — sending `admin`/`super-admin` is a 400
- Targets that are currently `admin` or `super-admin` cannot be modified — 403
- Verify the exact users table export name in packages/api/src/database/schema/users.ts before writing queries.

ticket.title: BUG: database unit tests DROP and recreate real dev-DB tables with stale schemas
ticket.description:
## Problem
Several unit test files in `packages/api/tests/database/` (at least products.test.ts, users.test.ts, orders.test.ts, cart.test.ts, migrations.test.ts) execute `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` and `CREATE TABLE` with **hand-written, outdated column lists** directly against whatever database DATABASE_URL points to — the shared dev database.

## Impact (observed 2026-07-23 during content-manager-role implementation)
Running the full `vitest` suite:
- Dropped `ai_generations` and other tables entirely
- Recreated `products` without `rooms`, `tags`, `is_ai_generated`, etc. (schema drift → all product queries 500)
- Created junk duplicate tables (`users`, `sessions`, `addresses` alongside the real `user`, `session`, `address`)
- Destroyed all seeded data; 44 unrelated test failures; dev environment broken until manual repair

Recovery required: `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` + `DROP SCHEMA drizzle CASCADE`, re-run `drizzle-kit migrate` (baseline 0000 + 0001), re-run seed.ts and seed-test-users.ts.

## Fix options
1. Point tests at a dedicated throwaway test database (TEST_DATABASE_URL) and refuse to run destructive setup when the URL matches the dev DB
2. Derive test tables from the Drizzle schema (drizzle-kit push onto a temp schema) instead of hand-written CREATE TABLE statements that drift
3. At minimum: guard the DROP/CREATE blocks behind an explicit env flag

## Related
Also worth fixing while in here: sliding-window auth rate limiters share one "unknown" IP bucket in dev, which blocks the Playwright auth setup (worked around by clearing rate-limit:* Redis keys; a DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT env bypass for test runs would be cleaner). Sign-in limiter wiring bug already fixed in commit 27746e37.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commits**: `3bb5f048` (guard + bypass), `7e80dfe6` (customers test alignment)

**Root cause pinpointed deeper than filed**: vitest.config.ts hardcoded the dev DATABASE_URL into every test run, overriding the destructive suites' own *_test fallback intent. Six (not five — ai.test.ts also DROPs ai_generations AND users) suites then ran DROP/CREATE DDL against the dev DB.

**Implemented**:
- `tests/helpers/destructive-db.ts` — destructive suites only receive a connection URL when it points at a `*_test` database (TEST_DATABASE_URL preferred; non-disposable override fails safe → loud skip). TDD: 10 unit tests red→green.
- All 6 destructive suites (products, users, orders, cart, migrations, ai) routed through the guard.
- vitest.config respects external DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL, passes TEST_DATABASE_URL through.
- `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` bypass in rate-limit middleware (TDD, 3 tests incl. production-inert assertion) + wired into Playwright webServer → E2E auth setup passes 4/4 with ZERO redis-flushing workarounds.
- Fixed pre-existing connection.test.ts '0'-vs-0 flake (::int cast).
- .env.example documents TEST_DATABASE_URL + DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT.

**Verification** (incident scenario re-run):
- `bunx vitest run` (full API suite) against dev DB → schema and data INTACT afterward (rooms column ✓, ai_generations ✓, 40 products ✓); destructive suites skip loudly. Remaining 29 failures are pre-existing environmental (phone-auth mocking etc., match incident-era baseline).
- With TEST_DATABASE_URL → DDL runs against poster_app_test (DROP notices observed), dev DB untouched.
- Touched suites: 98/98 passing.

**Discovery / follow-up candidate**: the destructive suites use `it.skipIf(shouldSkip())` evaluated at collection time — their assertions have NEVER run anywhere (only the DDL side effects did). They also build tables from the dead legacy `src/db/schema`. A rewrite against the real schema would make them meaningful; today they are safely caged.

ticket.title: Ops: Cloudflare redirect rule www.chobii.art -> chobii.art (301)
ticket.description:
## Task
Deploy the www-to-apex redirect in the chobii.art Cloudflare zone. Easiest path: Rules -> Create rule -> template "Redirect from WWW to Root". Manual equivalent: If Hostname equals `www.chobii.art` -> Dynamic redirect `concat("https://chobii.art", http.request.uri.path)`, status 301, preserve query string.

## Context
`www.chobii.art` currently returns a bare traefik "404 page not found" to real visitors (verified live 2026-07-25): the proxied `www` CNAME makes the name resolve, but no traefik router matches the www host — intentionally, since Better Auth cookies are host-only and canonicals are apex. The redirect must happen at the Cloudflare edge, NOT by adding www to traefik Host rules (that would fork sessions).

## Acceptance
`curl -sI https://www.chobii.art/x` returns 301 with `location: https://chobii.art/x`; a browser visit to www lands on the apex store.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Redirect rule deployed manually in the chobii.art Cloudflare zone (dashboard, by Dhruv) on 2026-07-29. Verified live from outside the LAN at 08:01 UTC:

- `curl -sI https://www.chobii.art/x` -> 301, `location: https://chobii.art/x` (acceptance criterion, met)
- `curl -sI https://www.chobii.art/` -> 301, `location: https://chobii.art/`
- `curl -sI "https://www.chobii.art/products?a=1&b=2"` -> 301, `location: https://chobii.art/products?a=1&b=2` (query string preserved)
- `curl -sL https://www.chobii.art/` -> final url `https://chobii.art/`, 200, num_redirects=1 (single hop, no loop) — browser criterion met
- Apex regression check: `https://chobii.art/` still 200 with 0 redirects

Pre-fix baseline for the record: www returned a bare traefik `404 page not found` with no app headers. Fix is edge-only; no traefik Host rule was touched, so Better Auth host-only cookies remain apex-scoped and sessions cannot fork.

Also satisfies the www half of the Phase 4 verification gate in docs/CUTOVER-CHOBII-ART.md:79-80.

verification.test_command: curl -sI https://www.chobii.art/x ; curl -sI "https://www.chobii.art/products?a=1&b=2" ; curl -sL -o /dev/null -w "%{url_effective} %{http_code} %{num_redirects}" https://www.chobii.art/
verification.test_output: All acceptance checks pass (live, 2026-07-29 08:01 UTC). /x -> 301 location: https://chobii.art/x. Query string preserved: /products?a=1&b=2 -> 301 https://chobii.art/products?a=1&b=2. Follow-redirect: final url https://chobii.art/, 200, num_redirects=1. Apex regression: https://chobii.art/ 200, 0 redirects. Ops-only change (Cloudflare edge redirect rule); no code, so no build run.

ticket.title: Bug - authApi.getSession hits wrong endpoint (/api/auth/session), bouncing Orders and AI Creations to login
ticket.description:
## Bug
With a valid session, /account/orders and /account/ai-creations redirect to /auth/login. Reproduced locally with an injected API session: those two pages bounce while sibling pages (wallet, addresses, notifications) work.

## Root Cause
packages/web/app/lib/api.ts:866 authApi.getSession() fetches /api/auth/session — Better Auth's endpoint is /api/auth/get-session. Proven with the same cookie: /api/auth/session → 404, /api/auth/get-session → 200. The 404 makes getSession() return null; orders.tsx:112 and ai-creations.tsx:137 run a redundant client-side useEffect auth check against it and navigate to login. Working siblings rely only on the _authed layout guard.

## Fix
Correct the URL in api.ts, flip the mocked-endpoint assertions in packages/web/tests/lib/api.test.ts, and remove the redundant client-side checks from the two routes (the _authed layout already guards them).

ticket.title: BUG: Admin sidebar sign-out redirects home without ending the session
ticket.description:
## Bug
Clicking **Sign Out** at the bottom-left of the admin sidebar redirects to the home page but does NOT log the user out — revisiting /admin shows the panel with the session intact. Observed on production (chobii.art) 2026-07-26.

## Root cause (confirmed by probing production)
`AdminSidebar.handleSignOut` (packages/web/app/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx:169-175) calls the hand-rolled `authApi.signOut()` (packages/web/app/lib/api.ts:929), which POSTs `/api/auth/sign-out` with `Content-Type: application/json` and **no request body**. Better Auth fails to parse the empty JSON body and returns **500**:

```
POST /api/auth/sign-out  (Content-Type: application/json, no body)  -> HTTP 500
POST /api/auth/sign-out  (same, body '{}')                          -> HTTP 200 {"success":true}
```

The sidebar's `catch` block then swallows the error and unconditionally redirects to `/`, so the failure is invisible and the session cookie is never cleared.

The account page's sign-out (packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/index.tsx:154) works because it uses the official Better Auth React client `signOut()` from `~/lib/auth-client`.

## Fix
Use the proven Better Auth client path in the sidebar and delete the broken duplicate:
1. In AdminSidebar.tsx: import `signOut` from `~/lib/auth-client`, call it in `handleSignOut`, keep the hard redirect (`window.location.href = '/'`) so client state resets; log the error in the catch instead of swallowing silently.
2. Remove `authApi.signOut` from packages/web/app/lib/api.ts (AdminSidebar is its only consumer — grep confirmed).

## Notes
- Existing E2E coverage: tests/e2e/admin-auth.spec.ts "Admin Sign Out" describe (lines ~353-388) asserts exactly this behavior (sign out then /admin redirects to login) — investigate why it did not catch the bug (it appeared among skipped tests in the last full run; check for .skip / project filters / button-selector mismatch) and make sure it runs in the chromium project going forward.
- After the fix lands, production deploy is required (web image rebuild: `make -C deploy build-push-deploy`).

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `03de3f42` - fix(web): admin sidebar sign-out now actually ends the session

**Root Cause** (deeper than first diagnosed): the sidebar's hand-rolled `authApi.signOut()` sent a body-less POST with a JSON content-type. That works locally (Content-Length: 0), but through the production edge the empty body is re-framed as `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and Better Auth 500s parsing it — **reproduced against the exact prod image**: chunked-empty → 500, Content-Length:0 → 200. This is why the existing E2E sign-out tests passed locally while production was broken. The silent catch then redirected home with the session alive.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx` — sign out via Better Auth client (same path as account page); failures logged, not swallowed
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — removed footgun `authApi.signOut` (comment points to auth-client)
- `tests/e2e/admin-auth.spec.ts` — new test "sign-out request carries a JSON body (prod edge compat)" — red against old code (postData empty), green after fix

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/admin-auth.spec.ts --project=chromium`
- Result: PASS (37/37; new body-assertion test red-then-green)
- Typecheck: no new errors in touched files

**⚠️ Not yet on production** — needs `make -C deploy build-push-deploy` (web image rebuild). Until then, admin sign-out on chobii.art remains broken; account-page sign-out works.

ticket.title: BUG: Mobile nav drawer is transparent — page content bleeds through, menu illegible
ticket.description:
## Problem

On mobile (<768px) the hamburger menu opens a nav panel that has **no background of its own**. It is rendered as a plain `<nav>` inside the sticky `<header>`, so it inherits the header's translucent `bg-background/95 backdrop-blur supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-background/60`.

A 60%-opaque white + 8px blur reads fine over a 64px header strip, but the expanded menu panel is ~359px tall and sits over vivid page content. On the homepage the saturated 'Shop by Style' cards (purple/pink, green/teal) show straight through the open menu, and the nav labels — Posters, Create with AI, Gallery, About, Account — become very hard to read.

**Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28.**

Measured computed styles with the menu open:
- `header` → `background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6)`, `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)`, height grows 64px → 359px
- the mobile `<nav>` itself → `background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`
- no scrim/overlay element exists behind the panel (queried for fixed elements with z-index > 10 and height > 500 → none)

This affects **every page on mobile**, since the header is global.

## Root cause

`packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx:131` renders the mobile menu as:
```tsx
<nav className="border-t border-border py-4 md:hidden">
```
with no background, inside the translucent header declared at `Header.tsx:36`.

## Note — the fix pattern already exists in this codebase

The mobile **Filters** drawer on `/posters` is built correctly: solid background, backdrop scrim, sticky 'Apply Filters' CTA. The header should use that same Sheet component rather than expanding the header element. Preferred fix is to render the mobile nav as a Sheet; the minimal fix is to give the `<nav>` an opaque `bg-background` and add a scrim.

## Acceptance criteria

- Open mobile menu on the homepage → no page content visible through the panel
- A scrim covers the rest of the viewport; tapping it closes the menu
- Body scroll is locked while the menu is open
- Escape closes the menu and focus is trapped within it while open

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `5c0e0730` — fix(web): opaque mobile nav drawer with scrim, scroll lock and Escape

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — rebuilt the mobile menu as a real drawer
- `tests/e2e/mobile-nav.spec.ts` — new spec (8 tests)

**Implementation**: took the ticket's preferred route — matched the pattern `MobileFiltersSheet` on `/posters` already uses (scrim, opaque panel, scroll lock, Escape, `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`). Did not extract a shared Sheet component: that would have meant touching the working filter drawer, which is a refactor rather than this fix.

**A second bug surfaced during implementation.** My first attempt nested the drawer inside `<header>` and the spec failed — the scrim measured `height: 0`. Cause: the header sets `backdrop-blur`, and a `backdrop-filter` establishes a containing block for fixed-position descendants, so `fixed inset-0` resolved against the 64px header box instead of the viewport. The drawer is now a **sibling** of `<header>`, with a comment recording why. Without the scrim assertion this would have shipped looking fine in a screenshot.

**Verification**:
- RED against production (unfixed): 7 of 8 failed. The single pass was "scroll restored after closing" — trivially true when scroll was never locked.
- GREEN against local dev: `8 passed`
- Live check at 390×844: drawer background `rgb(255, 255, 255)` (alpha 1), scrim present, `body overflow: hidden`, Escape and scrim-tap both close. Screenshot confirms nav labels legible with the page dimmed behind.
- Full web suite after the change: 1362 passed / 1362

**Test-robustness note**: the spec retries the open click until the toggle reports `aria-expanded="true"`. The button is server-rendered and clickable before hydration, so a single early click lands on inert markup and the menu never opens — the same hydration race that breaks cart seeding in #359.

ticket.title: BUG: All form inputs render at 14px — iOS Safari auto-zooms the viewport on every focus
ticket.description:
## Problem

Every text input, select and textarea in the app computes to `font-size: 14px`. iOS Safari automatically zooms the viewport whenever a focused input has a font-size below **16px**, and it does not zoom back out on blur. On a real iPhone the user is left pinch-zoomed after tapping any field, and must manually zoom out before continuing.

**Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28.** Confirmed 14px on:
- **Checkout** — all 10 fields: fullName, email, phone, addressLine1, addressLine2, landmark, city, state, postalCode, order notes
- **Login** — email, password
- **Create** — the prompt textarea
- **Footer newsletter** — email (present on every page)

This is worst on checkout, where the user tabs through ten fields in sequence and gets zoomed on each one.

## Fix

Raise the base input font-size to 16px at mobile widths. Since this is the shared shadcn/ui input styling, fix it at the component level rather than per-page — e.g. `text-base md:text-sm` on the Input/Textarea/Select primitives, which keeps the 14px look on desktop while satisfying iOS below the md breakpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every input, textarea and select computes to >= 16px font-size below 768px
- Desktop appearance is unchanged
- Verified on checkout, login, register, create, and the footer newsletter

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `9bd4dade` — fix(web): 16px form controls on mobile to stop iOS Safari auto-zoom

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/styles/globals.css` — one media-query rule below the `md` breakpoint
- `tests/e2e/mobile-input-zoom.spec.ts` — new spec

**Approach note**: the ticket assumed a shared Input primitive to patch. There isn't one — `packages/web/app/components/ui/` holds only `OptimizedImage.tsx`, and field styling is inlined as `text-sm` across 34 files (96 matches, including non-inputs). Per-field edits would have been noisy and easy to miss, so this is a single rule instead. It also covers controls added later.

The rule sits outside `@layer` and uses `:not()` to clear the specificity of the `.text-sm` utility (0,1,0), which would otherwise win regardless of source order. Checkboxes and radios are excluded — they render no text and never trigger the zoom.

**Verification**:
- RED against production (unfixed): 7 failed, all reporting 14px — `/checkout`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/forgot-password`, `/create`, `/track`, footer newsletter
- GREEN against local dev with the fix: `7 passed`
- Live spot-check at 390px: login email/password/footer-email all `16px`; at 1280px all three still `14px`

**Test-quality note**: an earlier run of this spec passed 7/8 against `localhost:5173` — which turned out to be a *different app* squatting that port. The checks were passing vacuously against pages with no matching inputs. The spec now asserts `visibleCount > 0` per page so it cannot pass without finding controls, and `/checkout` was removed from its page list (it short-circuits to an empty-cart state; its fields are covered by the AddressForm component test).

ticket.title: BUG: Checkout address form has zero autocomplete attributes — mobile autofill cannot work
ticket.description:
## Problem

Not one field on the checkout shipping form carries an `autocomplete` attribute. Browser and OS address autofill therefore cannot populate any of them, so mobile users must hand-type their full name, email, phone, street address, city, state and PIN code on a phone keyboard.

**Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28.** All 10 checkout fields returned `autocomplete: null`:
fullName, email, phone, addressLine1, addressLine2, landmark, city, state, postalCode, order notes.

## This is an oversight, not a project convention

The **auth** forms do this correctly — the login page ships `autocomplete="email"` and `autocomplete="current-password"`. Only checkout was missed, which is the one form where autofill matters most for conversion.

## Fix

Add the standard autofill tokens:

| Field | autocomplete |
|---|---|

ticket.title: BUG: Homepage Featured Collection is always empty — loader reads .products, API returns .items
ticket.description:
## Problem

The homepage's primary merchandising block renders the 'Coming Soon — Our featured collection is being curated' empty state on every load, even though featured products exist and the API serves them correctly.

**Verified on production chobii.art, 2026-07-28.**
- `GET https://chobii.art/api/products/featured?limit=8` → **200**, returns `{"items":[{..."title":"Cosmic Harmony"...}]}`
- Homepage still shows the empty state

## Root cause — response shape mismatch

The API returns `{ items: [...] }`:
```ts
// packages/api/src/routes/products.ts:378
return c.json({ items: featuredProducts });
```

The web loader reads `.products`:
```ts
// packages/web/app/routes/index.tsx:49
const featuredResponse = await productsApi.featured({ limit: 8 })
return { featuredProducts: featuredResponse.products || [] }
```

`productsApi.featured()` (`packages/web/app/lib/api.ts:246`) returns the raw parsed JSON, so `.products` is `undefined`, `|| []` yields an empty array, and the component falls through to its empty state. The surrounding `try/catch` returns `[]` on error too, so the failure is completely silent.

Not mobile-specific — this affects every viewport. Surfaced during the mobile sweep.

## Fix

Read `.items` in the loader (or normalise the shape inside `productsApi.featured()` so callers get a consistent `{ products }`). Prefer typing the client method's return so this mismatch is a compile error rather than a silent empty array.

## Acceptance criteria

- Homepage renders the featured product grid, not the 'Coming Soon' state
- The loader's return type is tied to the API response shape so drift fails typecheck

ticket.title: BUG: PDP 'You May Also Like' is a hardcoded permanent skeleton — never implemented
ticket.description:
## Problem The 'You May Also Like' section on every product detail page renders five `animate-pulse` grey placeholder blocks that never resolve into products. It is not a loading state — the section was shipped as a hardcoded placeholder and the real implementation never landed. **Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28** on `/posters/cosmic-harmony`. At 2 columns on mobile this consumes roughly 800px of continuously-pulsing dead space near the bottom of the page, reading as a permanently broken section. ## Root cause `packages/web/app/routes/posters/$slug.tsx:443-461`: ```tsx function RelatedProductsSection() { return (

You May Also Like

{/* Placeholder for related products - will be implemented with actual products */} {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((i) => (
...
))} ``` There is no data fetch behind it. Confirmed `GET /api/products/:id/related` → **404** (no such endpoint exists, by id or by slug). ## Fix — decide scope Two options; either is acceptable, pick one: 1. **Implement it** — add a related-products API endpoint (match on shared styles/subjects, exclude the current product, limit 5) and wire the section to it with a real loading state and an empty fallback. 2. **Remove it** — delete the section until it can be built properly. A missing section is strictly better than a permanently pulsing one. Option 2 is the fast unblock; option 1 is the real fix. ## Acceptance criteria - No permanently-animating skeleton on the PDP - If implemented: real related products render, with a genuine loading state and an empty-state fallback - If removed: the section is gone and page flow is intact on mobile

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
✅ **Completed** — implemented rather than removed

**Commit**: `b8cfaa66` — feat: related products on the product page

**Scope call**: the ticket allowed either building it or deleting the section. Built it — the row is already part of the design and the matching data (styles/subjects) is already on every product, so the endpoint was the only missing piece.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts` — new `GET /api/products/:slug/related`
- `packages/api/tests/routes/products.test.ts` — 5 tests
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `productsApi.related()`
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/$slug.tsx` — loader fetch + real section

**Matching**: products sharing a style or subject, active only, self excluded, ranked by how many tag families overlap (both style and subject beats style alone), cached like featured. Data loads in the route loader alongside the product, so there is no loading state left to get stuck in, and the section renders nothing when there is nothing to recommend.

**Two Postgres gotchas worth remembering**:
1. `text[]` has no core `&` intersection operator — that is the `intarray` extension and integers only. First attempt failed with `cannot cast type record to text[]`; the score now uses two `&&` overlap checks, giving 0-2 by family rather than counting individual shared tags.
2. Interpolating a JS array into a drizzle `sql``` template binds it as a **record tuple**, not an array. Arrays are now built as real `ARRAY[...]` literals with each element bound separately.

**Verification** (live against dev DB):
- `synthetic-nature` → 16 matches, exactly the count a direct SQL query returns
- Ranking correct: `floating-islands` first (shares `modern-contemporary` **and** `nature-landscape` → score 2), style-only matches after
- Self excluded; `limit=2` → 2 items; unknown slug → 404; `limit=100` → 400
- PDP renders 5 real cards; `.animate-pulse` count on the page is **0** after hydration
- Web suite 1362/1362; API failures 83 vs 86 on `main` (no new ones)

**Note**: the 5 API runtime tests skip locally — the vitest process cannot reach the database (see #359 for the same root cause). They are written to run in CI where it can; the behaviour above was verified against the live API instead.

ticket.title: BUG: GET /api/products/:id/reviews/stats returns 404 — 3 console errors per PDP load
ticket.description:
## Problem

Every product detail page load fires `GET /api/products/:productId/reviews/stats`, which returns **404**. The request is issued three times per page load, producing three console errors, and the review summary block stays in a skeleton state.

**Verified on production chobii.art, 2026-07-28** on `/posters/cosmic-harmony`:
```
[ERROR] Failed to load resource: 404 @ /api/products/84341a4e-.../reviews/stats  (x3)
```

Endpoint probe:
- `GET /api/products/:id/reviews` → **200** (works)
- `GET /api/products/:id/reviews/stats` → **404**

## Root cause

The client calls it at `packages/web/app/hooks/useReviews.ts:107`:
```ts
const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/products/${productId}/reviews/stats`, ...)
```

But `productReviewsApp` — mounted at `/api/products/:productId/reviews` (`packages/api/src/index.ts:136`) — defines exactly one route, the list handler at `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts:90`. There is no `/stats` sub-route, so the path 404s.

Note an admin equivalent does exist (`/api/admin/reviews/stats`), but no public per-product one.

## Fix

Add `GET /stats` to `productReviewsApp` returning the per-product aggregate the hook expects (average rating, total count, and the 1-5 star distribution). Also worth investigating why the request fires three times per load — likely a missing query key or an unmemoised effect dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- `GET /api/products/:id/reviews/stats` returns 200 with average, total and distribution
- No console errors on PDP load
- The review summary renders real values instead of a skeleton
- The endpoint is requested once per page load, not three times

comments.text:

**Commit**: `361bffa9` — feat(api): per-product review stats endpoint

**Files Changed**:

- `packages/api/tests/routes/reviews.test.ts` — route, validation and aggregation tests

**Returns** the shape `useReviews.ts` already expects: `averageRating` (1 dp), `totalReviews`, and a `distribution` of all five star buckets highest-first — empty ones included, so the UI renders a stable five-row breakdown without filling gaps itself. Single grouped query, cached for the same 5 minutes as the review lists.

**Testability**: the aggregation is a separate exported function so its arithmetic can be tested without a database. Seeding real reviews is not viable locally — `reviews.order_item_id` is NOT NULL with an FK and the dev DB has zero `order_items`. One of the tests covers pg returning aggregate counts as **strings**, where a missing `Number()` would concatenate instead of add.

**Bonus fix — cache invalidation was broken.** Both existing call sites passed a `"...:*"` wildcard to `deleteCached`, which deletes one exact key; the wildcard was never expanded. Edited and deleted reviews therefore kept serving stale lists for the full TTL. Now routed through `invalidateProductReviewCaches()` using `deleteCachedPattern`, covering the new stats key too.

**Verification**:

- GREEN: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/reviews.test.ts` → **51 passed / 51**

ticket.title: BUG: /posters grid renders ragged — uniformAspectRatio is never passed to ProductGrid
ticket.description:
## Problem

The product listing grid on `/posters` is visually ragged: cards in the same row have images of different heights, so titles and prices sit at different baselines, and row heights jump between rows. It is most obvious on mobile, where the 2-column layout puts two mismatched cards side by side at all times.

**Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28.** Measured card heights in one grid: **368px, 263px, 207px**. Within the first row alone the two images measured **254px vs 169px** tall.

Each card wraps its image in a per-orientation aspect class — `aspect-[2/3]`, `aspect-square`, `aspect-[3/2]`, `aspect-video` — driven by `product.orientation`.

## Root cause — the fix already exists but is not wired up

Tickets **#287** (ProductCard — add `uniformAspectRatio` prop) and **#288** (ProductGrid — pass `uniformAspectRatio` to ProductCard) are both **done**, and the plumbing is present:
- `ProductCard.tsx:52` accepts `uniformAspectRatio`
- `ProductCard.tsx:92` — `uniformAspectRatio || ASPECT_RATIO_MAP[product.orientation]`
- `ProductGrid.tsx:133` forwards it

But the main catalog page never passes it:
```tsx
// packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx:519
<ProductGrid
  products={products}
  columns={{ default: 2, sm: 2, md: 3, lg: 4 }}
  gap="md"
/>
```

The hero-grid-alignment work only covered the homepage grid; the listing page was left on per-orientation ratios.

## Fix

Pass `uniformAspectRatio="aspect-[2/3]"` (portrait — matches the majority of the catalogue and the existing skeleton at `ProductCard.tsx:222`) to the ProductGrid on the listing page. Audit any other ProductGrid call sites for the same omission.

## Acceptance criteria

- All cards in the `/posters` grid have identical height
- Image heights match within and across rows; titles and prices align on a common baseline
- Verified at 390px and at desktop widths

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `c386e8a5` — fix(web): uniform aspect ratio on the posters listing grid

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` — pass `uniformAspectRatio="aspect-[2/3]"` to ProductGrid

**Root Cause**: the listing page never passed the prop, so each card fell back to `ASPECT_RATIO_MAP[product.orientation]`. The plumbing from #287/#288 only reached the home page.

**Ratio choice**: `aspect-[2/3]` matches `ProductCardSkeleton`, so cards do not shift when skeletons resolve. Note the home page uses `aspect-[3/4]` (set deliberately in #289) — left as-is, but the skeleton/card mismatch there is a latent layout-shift source worth a separate look.

**Audit**: `/posters` is the only ProductGrid consumer in the app; no other call sites to fix.

**Verification** (local dev, 390x844, measured via getBoundingClientRect):
- Before: card heights `[368, 263, 207]`, image heights `[254, 169, 113, 95]`, 4 distinct aspect classes
- After: image heights `[254]` — all identical; aspect classes `[aspect-[2/3]]` — all identical
- Titles and prices now share a baseline within each row (screenshot confirmed)
- Residual: card heights `[368, 348]` — a 20px cross-row variance from cards having 1 vs 2 metadata lines. Not visually ragged, since grid rows stretch and images align. Flagging rather than clamping the text, as that is a design call.

ticket.title: BUG: Home 'Minimalist' style card caption is illegible — grey overlay too weak over a light image
ticket.description:
## Problem

In the homepage 'Shop by Style' grid, the **Minimalist** card's caption ('Clean lines, simple beauty') is hard to read. The white text lands directly on a dark ring and a brown dot from the underlying `minimalist.jpg`, with too little separation.

**Verified on production chobii.art at 390x844, 2026-07-28.**

## Root cause

All four cards use the same structure — background image, colour gradient overlay at 70% alpha and 75% opacity, then white text. The other three overlays are strongly saturated and mask their images well:
- Abstract → `from-purple-600/70 to-pink-600/70`
- Nature → `from-green-600/70 to-teal-600/70`
- Typography → `from-amber-600/70 to-orange-600/70`
- **Minimalist → `from-gray-600/70 to-slate-600/70`**

A desaturated grey/slate wash over an intentionally light, high-key minimalist photograph does not build enough contrast for white text. This is the only card where the overlay colour and the image tone work against each other.

## Fix

Options:
- Darken the Minimalist overlay (e.g. `from-slate-800/80 to-slate-900/70`), or
- Add a text-protection scrim behind the caption on all four cards, or
- Swap `minimalist.jpg` for a darker-toned image

A scrim behind the caption is the most robust — it makes the component safe against any future category image.

## Acceptance criteria

- Caption text on all four style cards meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) against the composited background
- The minimalist aesthetic of the card is preserved
