ticket.title: Wishlist store fetches before it knows the session — six 401s per collection load
ticket.description:
## Task

A signed-out visitor loading a collection page fires ~6 `GET /api/wishlist` requests, all 401. Nothing breaks visibly, but the store is fetching an auth-gated resource before it knows whether anyone is signed in, and it is doing so once per mounting component instead of once per page.

Two separate defects, both in `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts`:

**1. No in-flight dedupe.** `load()` guards on `if (get().isLoaded) return` (wishlist.ts:48), but `isLoaded` only flips *after* the await resolves. Every caller that mounts in the same tick passes the guard and issues its own request. Callers are `Header.tsx:64` (one) and `WishlistButton.tsx:41` (one per heart), so a grid produces one request per visible card. The comment at `WishlistButton.tsx:39` — "24 cards mounting produce one request, not 24" — is only true for sequential calls.

**2. The store never sees auth.** It fetches unconditionally and swallows the 401 in the catch (wishlist.ts:53-60). The session is already resolved server-side in the root route (`routes/__root.tsx:60`, `session: Session | null` in the router context), so the client can know it is a guest before spending any request.

The existing test `tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts:61` ("fetches once, not once per card") awaits the two `load()` calls sequentially, which is why this never showed up.

**Fix scope agreed:** dedupe *and* auth gate. After the fix a signed-out visitor makes zero `/api/wishlist` requests; a signed-in one makes exactly one per page load regardless of card count.

## Context

**Design — keep the router out of the leaf components.** `WishlistButton` is rendered bare in `tests/components/product/WishlistButton.test.tsx` with no router; calling `useRouteContext` inside it (or inside a hook it uses) breaks those tests. Instead the store carries a tri-state `isAuthenticated: boolean | null`:

- `null` = the root route has not reported yet. `load()` does nothing — this is what stops the guest 401s, since leaf effects run before the root effect.
- `false` = guest. `setAuthenticated(false)` marks `{ ids: [], isLoaded: true }` so every heart renders in its empty state and nothing waits.
- `true` = signed in. `setAuthenticated(true)` kicks the single load.

`Header.tsx` and `WishlistButton.tsx` keep their existing `load()` effects — they become harmless no-ops until auth is known, and still cover components that mount after that point.

**Existing tests need adjusting, not deleting:** the `reset()` helper at `tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts:19` must also clear `isAuthenticated` and `inFlight`, and the existing `describe('load')` cases must set `isAuthenticated: true` first or they will now correctly make no request.

Related files: `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts`, `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx`, `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx`, `packages/web/app/components/product/WishlistButton.tsx`.

**Commit**: `bdcc03ea` - fix(web): gate the wishlist load on the session and dedupe it in flight

2. The store fetched the auth-gated `/api/wishlist` without knowing the session and swallowed the 401.

- `setAuthenticated(true)` kicks the single load; concurrent callers await the same promise, which is cleared in a `finally` so a failed load does not wedge the store.
- `__root.tsx` reports the session it already has in `beforeLoad`. `Header` and `WishlistButton` keep their `load()` effects (harmless no-ops until auth is known), so `WishlistButton` still renders routerless in its own tests.

**Files Changed**:

- `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx` — reports the session to the store

ticket.title: Card media shows two mats — match ours to the source background
ticket.description:
## Task

Our cards currently show two nested mats. `--mat: 0 0% 98%` pads every image to square in `matToSquare`, but the seed artwork was captured from a storefront that already sits its pieces on its own light background. The result is a mat inside a mat, with a visible seam between the two tones.

This is only visible now because the seed carries real captured artwork rather than stock photography that filled the frame.

## Context

- Token: `--mat` in `packages/web/app/styles/globals.css`
- Padding happens in `matToSquare`, `packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts` — the colour is baked into the pixels, so changing the token alone will NOT fix existing images; they need a reseed.
- Sample the actual background colour from a seed file in `.cache/seed-media/` (e.g. `tx462-main.webp`, a corner pixel) rather than eyeballing it from a screenshot.
- The analysis §2 lists mat colour as an open decision: theirs is `rgb(250 250 250)` per their served tokens, ours is `0 0% 98%` — nominally the same, so confirm by measurement whether the seam is a token mismatch or the captured images carrying a different background from their own token.
- Do not break the square contract (#360–#375). Only the fill colour is in scope.

## Acceptance

One mat visible per card, no seam, at both grid and PDP sizes. Verified against a reseeded catalogue, not just a token change.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `f495f9b8` — fix(api): strip the border a source arrives with, so cards show one mat

**Root cause — the ticket's premise was wrong.**

Not a token mismatch. `--mat` is `0 0% 98%` and `MAT_COLOR` is `{250,250,250}` — already identical, already guarded by `mat-token.test.ts`. Two separate defects, both measured:

1. **The captured artwork carries its own field** at rgb(240,240,240) — ten levels off our mat, over a band 90–347px wide. That step is the seam.
2. **`matToSquare` ran twice.** `.cache/seed-media/tools/fetch-media.ts:109` mats on capture, `product-media.ts:61` mats again on seed. Art landed at 0.88² = **77.5%** of canvas instead of 88%.

The existing idempotency test (`image-processing-mat.test.ts:104`) only asserted the canvas stayed 1500×1500, which is true of both correct and broken output. Size stability is not idempotency — the art box is what moved, and nothing was watching it.

**Files Changed**
- `packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts` — `stripUniformBorder()` trims a uniform border before insetting. Guarded two ways: a trim leaving under half the longest side is refused, so a piece composed *as* a light field is matted as it came; and art may grow back toward the inset but never past the longest side the source delivered.
- `packages/api/tests/lib/image-processing-mat.test.ts` — 4 tests for bordered sources; 3 failed first for the right reason (90px of tone 240 in the mat, art box 198px short, 158px lost on re-run).
- `packages/api/tests/lib/image-processing-seed-media.test.ts` — new; runs the real captured artwork through the pipeline. Skips when the machine-local seed directory is absent.

**Why not change MAT_COLOR to 240**: that matches our design token to throwaway third-party placeholder imagery and diverges from mesonart's actual served token, which analysis §2 measures at `rgb(250 250 250)`. The source is what was wrong, not the mat.

**Verification** (against a reseeded catalogue, per acceptance)
- Reseed run, catalogue rebuilt: 41 products, 629 variants, 122 room-mockups
- All 41 **stored** `main` images pulled back from MinIO and measured: canvas 1500×1500, content longest side **1320–1325px** vs the 1320 target, **0** second-mat pixels
- Visual at 1440×900: grid and PDP both show one uniform mat, no seam
- `image-processing-mat` + `image-processing-seed-media` + `product-media` + `seed-images`: 47 passed
- `image-processing-crop`: 13 passed · web `mat-token`: 9 passed
- `product-grid-alignment.spec.ts`: **68 passed** — square contract (#360–#375) intact
- `tsc --noEmit` (packages/api): 0 errors

**Found while working, not fixed — worth its own ticket.** `SEED_MEDIA_DIR` (`seed-images.ts:40`) resolves off `process.cwd()`, but `bun run seed` runs from `packages/api`. Seeding from there silently swaps the whole catalogue to stock URLs — room-mockups drop 122 → 3 with no warning and no error. It caught me mid-ticket. Correct invocation needs `SEED_MEDIA_DIR` set explicitly.

**Decision recorded**: mat stays baked into pixels rather than moving to display-time CSS. Display-time was the stronger option on one axis only — dark mode, which a baked near-white block cannot adapt to — and dark mode is not shipping. Baking also can't be eliminated anyway, since OG images and email have no CSS; moving would have duplicated the mat definition across two rendering paths instead of removing one.

work_sessions.summary: Diagnosed and fixed the double mat. Root cause was NOT the token: --mat and MAT_COLOR are both rgb(250,250,250) and already guarded. Measured two real defects — the captured artwork carries its own rgb(240,240,240) field (a 10-level step over a 90-347px band), and matToSquare ran twice (fetch-media.ts on capture, product-media.ts on seed), leaving art at 0.88^2 = 77.5% of canvas. Fixed by trimming a uniform border before insetting, with a 50% floor so light-field compositions are not eaten, and an enlargement cap at the source's own longest side so mat width stays consistent across a grid row. Added 4 TDD tests plus a real-media regression suite over all 41 captured artworks. Committed f495f9b8. Remaining: reseed the dev catalogue and verify visually at grid and PDP sizes.

Dropped the proposed ProductCardMedia guard hardening — that component only sees ProductImage metadata, no pixels, so a uniform-border check is not implementable there, and the trim already makes matToSquare idempotent so it is not needed server-side. Confirmed mat architecture decision: keep baking (dark mode is not shipping, which was the only cost that could not be engineered away). Ran the reseed and it reverted the reference imagery — room-mockups 122 to 3 — because SEED_MEDIA_DIR resolves off process.cwd() and bun run seed runs from packages/api. Corrective re-run with SEED_MEDIA_DIR set was declined, so the dev catalogue is currently on stock URLs. Code fix remains verified and committed at f495f9b8. Outstanding: restore the catalogue, then verify one mat at grid and PDP sizes in a browser.

Restored the reference imagery (room-mockups 3 back to 122) by reseeding with SEED_MEDIA_DIR set explicitly. Verified the acceptance against the reseeded catalogue: pulled all 41 stored main images from MinIO and measured 1500x1500 canvas, content longest side 1320-1325px against the 1320 target, zero second-mat pixels. Visual check at 1440x900 on grid and PDP shows one uniform mat, no seam. product-grid-alignment.spec.ts 68 passed, so the square contract survives. Ticket complete.

ticket.title: Move the Hide filters control above the facet rail
ticket.description:
## Task

Their "Hide filters" pill sits at the top of the LEFT column, directly above the facet groups it collapses. Ours sits in the toolbar row above the GRID, to the right of the sidebar — so the control is not adjacent to the thing it controls.

## Context

- `packages/web/app/components/product/CollectionToolbar.tsx` currently owns the pill alongside the count and the sort control.
- `FILTER_SIDEBAR_ID` already exists so the toggle can point `aria-controls` at the rail — moving the button should keep that wiring intact.

- Watch the sticky offset: the toolbar is `top-16` and agrees with `HEADER_HEIGHT_CLASS` by hand. #401's commit records how a 37px overlap happened last time these two numbers drifted.

## Acceptance

Toggle renders at the head of the facet rail on desktop, keeps its `aria-controls` and expanded state, and the toolbar row still carries count + sort. Mobile layout unchanged.

ticket.title: Choose options — add to cart without leaving the collection page
ticket.description:
## Task

The last card affordance we do not have. Theirs is a labelled button on hover that opens a Quickview panel where size and finish are picked and the item added to cart, so the shopper keeps their scroll position and their place in the grid.

## Context

- Measured on their site: `<button is="hover-button" aria-controls="Quickview-...">Choose options</button>`, one per card, opening a panel. Whether their eye icon triggers the same panel was NOT confirmed — two probes failed — so do not assume it.
- Ours today: `ProductCardMedia.tsx:144` renders an eye that is `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events-none`. It is decorative; it opens nothing.
- **Decision needed before building:** one modal with two triggers, or drop the eye and keep a single labelled control. Recommendation is the latter — an unlabelled icon duplicating a labelled button is a worse a11y story than theirs.
- Variant data is already available: the size ladder comes from `getSizesForOrientation()` (#386) and frames are a separate add-on list, not a matrix axis (analysis §5.6 item 4).
- Cart store already exists; this is a new surface over it, not new cart logic.

## Acceptance

Opens from the card without navigation, picks size and frame, adds to cart, closes and restores focus to the trigger. Scroll position preserved. Keyboard reachable and Escape closes — the hover-only affordance must not be the only route in.

comments.author: user
comments.text: my decision is keep the  eye , that takes you to the product page as does clicking anywhere else on the product picture, add the labelled control for options.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `5165f631` — feat(web): buy from the grid — Choose options opens size, frame and add to cart

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/product/ChooseOptions.tsx` — new; the trigger and the panel
- `packages/web/app/components/product/ProductCard.tsx` — renders the trigger as a sibling of the media link
- `packages/web/tests/components/product/ChooseOptions.test.tsx` — new, 15 tests
- `packages/web/tests/components/product/ProductCard.test.tsx` — 3 tests for the card wiring

**Summary**:
Built to the decision recorded on this ticket: the eye stays decoration on a media box that already navigates to the product page, and a labelled control is added beside it. The eye keeps `aria-hidden` + `pointer-events-none`; the new button is real, named and focusable.

**The panel fetches, and that was not optional.** The grid carries `basePrice` and images and nothing else, while the cart carries `variantId` through to checkout. A ladder synthesised on the client from `getSizesForOrientation()` would render correctly and fail to resolve at order time. So `ChooseOptions` calls `productsApi.getBySlug()` on first open and caches for reopens — one request per card, only for cards a shopper actually opens. Verified against the running app: the cart receives `822c5871-8265-4346-aa30-e3f1b167769a`, a real variant row, with `sizeLabel: 16" × 20" / 41 × 51 cm`.

Reuses `SizeSelectorCompact` and `FrameSelectorCompact` rather than growing a second selector vocabulary; the frame list arrives with its own "No Frame" entry.

**Keyboard**: the trigger is `opacity-0` on hover-capable widths and visible at rest below `md`, but never `pointer-events-none` — it stays in the tab order at every width, because a hover-only affordance is not a route in. Opens on Enter, closes on Escape / the close button / the backdrop, and restores focus to the trigger on every path.

**Two things worth recording:**

1. Two of my own assumptions about the scroll behaviour were wrong and both were caught by measuring rather than reasoning. First I attributed a 900 → 707 drop to the body-scroll lock; it was Playwright's `hover()` scrolling an off-screen card into view. Then I switched the lock to the root element on the theory that `body { overflow: hidden }` clamps the offset — measured at a scroll depth that does not trigger pagination, neither element clamps. The lock is back on `<body>`, matching ReviewModal, and the comment says only what was measured.

2. **Pre-existing, unrelated, worth its own ticket**: scrolling /posters past the pagination threshold loads `?page=2` and then the page scrolls itself to 0. Reproduced with no modal involved — wheel to 2400, and ~900ms later `scrollY` is 107, then 0, with `document.scrollHeight` growing 3797 → 5207 the whole time. That is scroll restoration firing on the append navigation, not a height collapse.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/components tests/routes --maxWorkers=2`
- Result: PASS — 50 files, 947/947 (15 new for ChooseOptions, 3 for the card)
- Command: `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/product-grid-alignment.spec.ts tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps --workers=2`
- Result: PASS — 131 passed, 1 skipped. Card-click navigation still works, so the overlay does not swallow it.
- Command: `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (packages/web)
- Result: 23 errors, unchanged baseline, none in the touched files.
- Browser, against the running app at 1440x900: scrollY 900 before open and 900 after; opened by keyboard; Escape closed it; focus back on the trigger; `body.style.overflow` released; console clean.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
🔁 **Reworked — the first pass did not look like theirs**

**Commit**: `d0287ca1` — feat(web): rebuild the Quickview against the measured mesonart panel

The first attempt was functionally complete and visually wrong: a 448px centred card with a 64px thumbnail, seventeen size chips wrapped over five rows, and a full-bleed black bar for a trigger. I had measured their *trigger* and not their *panel*.

**Re-measured at 1440x1000** (headless Chromium, computed boxes):

```
backdrop            rgba(23,23,23,0.7), flat — no blur
modal               x 48..1392, y 116..884 — 1344 x 768, TWO COLUMNS
  left              product image 671 x 768, carousel dots along the foot
  right             content column x 780..1332 (552 wide)
    title + price   price right-aligned on the title line, 24px/300
    rating          14px/300
    "Size <value>"  label at 300, the chosen value at 500
    SELECT          552 x 52, bg rgba(23,23,23,0.024), radius 6, no border
    "Frame: <value>" the same label/value pair
    swatches        60px circles on a 100px pitch, 5 per row
    stock line      only when the count is genuinely low
    CTA row         h 60 — quantity stepper + black pill at radius 60,
                    the pill quoting the total: "Add to cart - $260.00"
    full details    footer link out to the product page

card trigger        172 x 40, radius 60, WHITE pill, black label 16px/400,
                    centred over the foot of the artwork
```

Ours now lands the swatches at exactly their pitch — 780, 880, 980, 1080, 1180, second row 100 below — and the trigger reuses the `outline` variant's circle-wipe over a white fill, which is what their `button--primary` does.

**Decisions worth recording:**

- The size ladder is a native `<select>`. It is theirs, and it is the right call for our 17 steps — as chips it pushed the frame row below the fold.
- The chosen size sits **outside** the `<label>`. Folded in, it joins the select's accessible name and the control announces as "Size 24 x 36" instead of "Size".
- Frame swatches are painted from the frame's own `color`, not its `imageUrl` — those point at placehold.co and would have put a grey "Black+Frame" placard on the panel.
- The stock line only appears when a real variant has ≤5 left. Theirs reads "Hurry, only 1 item left in stock!"; ours repeats a number we actually have, with no urgency copy.

- Result: 132 passed, 2 failed. Both unrelated: "offers no category tile the catalogue cannot fill" belongs to a parallel session's commit `089ffa41` and asserts the absence of `a[href="/posters?subjects=typography"]`, which nothing in this ticket renders; "should handle rapid filter changes" passed on re-run.

|---|---|
| `5165f631` | first pass: trigger, panel, real variants, add to cart |
| `d0287ca1` | rebuilt against the measured Quickview — two columns, select, swatches |
| `f7411e0e` | swatches read as mouldings and take real photography |
| `1c60bba2` | sell their format ladder — Rolled Canvas / Frameless / Stretch + Frame |
| `1c7ff2c9` | priced by size, their swatch photography, X wipe, backdrop close |

**What the reviews caught, in order**

1. *"a very poor implementation"* — I had measured their trigger and never opened their panel. Theirs is 1344x768 in two columns with the artwork in its own half; mine was a 448px centred card with a 64px thumbnail and seventeen wrapped size chips. Rebuilt to the measurement, and the size ladder became a native `<select>` — theirs, and the only thing that fits 17 steps without pushing the frame row below the fold.

2. *"the frame options need to match, use the photos from mesonart"* — ours was a moulding catalogue (No Frame, Classic Black, Natural Oak…). Theirs is a FORMAT axis under the heading "Rolled Canvas/Frameless/Framed": the print in a tube, stretched, or stretched and framed. Reseeded to their seven. `rolled` and `frameless` joined `frame_type` (migration `0004_perfect_stardust`); `none`, `oak` and `walnut` stay in the enum unseeded because Postgres cannot drop an enum value without recreating the type. Safe to reshape because the store is pre-launch with no live orders carrying the old `frameName`.

3. *"won't the frame price depend on size as well"* — it does on theirs, and ours was flat. Measured across three sizes of one piece:

   ```
   24x24   $260 rolled   $460 frameless (+77%)   $480 framed (+85%)
   40x40   $585          $990           (+69%)   $1,030      (+76%)
   72x72   $1,625        $3,020         (+86%)   $3,100      (+91%)
   ```

   So the frame is a multiplier on the piece. `priceModifier` carries it, `priceAddition` is zero everywhere, magnitude stays ours (+33% stretched, +40% framed — within a few rupees of the old flat ₹499/₹599 on a small print). **That made `priceAddition` a silent-zero trap**, so `routes/posters/$slug.tsx` moved with it: it read the flat field and would have quoted every frame at ₹0 while the quickview charged correctly. `tests/routes/posters-frame-pricing.test.ts` now pins both surfaces to `priceModifier`.

4. *"the X should have the same black effect, and hovering outside should show a cross"* — the close button took the toolbar pills' circle-wipe on a 48px circle, and the backdrop hides the native cursor and follows the pointer with a round X, as theirs does. Escape and the button still cover everyone the pointer does not.

**Things fixed on the way that were not asked for**

- **Reseeding left stale prices and assets in Redis.** `GET /api/products/:slug` caches its whole payload, frames included, so after a reseed that endpoint served the previous run's data while `/api/products/frames` served the new — and the storefront looked like it had ignored the seed. `clearData()` now drops `product:*` and `product-list:*`. This cost real time to diagnose; it will not again.
- **The frames list was duplicated** between `seed.ts` and `seed-admin.ts`, the second under a comment promising it was "same data as seed.ts to keep them in sync". Moved to `seed-frames.ts`; the integration test asserts neither file declares its own.

**Corrections to my own earlier claims on this ticket** — both caught by measuring rather than reasoning:
- I blamed a 900 → 707 scroll drop on the body-scroll lock. It was Playwright's `hover()` scrolling an off-screen card into view.
- I then moved the lock to the root element on the theory that `body { overflow: hidden }` clamps the offset. Measured at a depth that does not trigger pagination, neither element clamps. The lock is back on `<body>`, matching ReviewModal.

**Not done, deliberately**: the swatch images are mesonart's product photography, served from our own `/frames` at the owner's explicit direction after I raised it twice. The drawn fallback stays for any row without an asset, so replacing them with our own photography is a drop-in — the panel renders whatever `thumbnailUrl` points at.

**Verification**
- `bunx vitest run tests/components/product tests/routes/posters-frame-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/posters-toolbar-placement.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → PASS, 14 files, 254/254. ChooseOptions went 15 → 40 tests across the rework.
- `bunx vitest run tests/integration/seed.test.ts` → all Frame Options assertions pass. Four Product Variants failures remain and fail at HEAD too — they assert `sizeLabel` / `square:` in `seed.ts`, where the variant ladder no longer lives.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → web 22 (baseline), api 0.
- Browser, 1440x1000: 12x16 + black = ₹1,699 → ₹2,379; 60x80 + black = ₹41,031; seven swatch photographs load; backdrop cursor and click-to-close work; focus returns to the trigger; console clean.

**Unrelated, still open** (both from parallel session commit `089ffa41`): `home-tokens.test.ts` expects `from-slate-700/80` on a home page that now uses a flat scrim, and the `?subjects=typography` E2E assertion fails against the seeded catalogue.

Found a pre-existing scroll-reset on the ?page=2 append, unrelated and unticketed.

ticket.title: Reveal the nav rows on scroll up, collapse on scroll down
ticket.description:
## Task

On their site the header collapses to a compact bar — wordmark plus the four action icons — once you scroll down, and the two nav rows come back the moment you scroll up, without needing to return to the top. Ours keeps a single fixed bar and the nav rows scroll away for good.

## Context

- Confirmed from captures of their collection page: scrolled down shows the compact bar only; scrolling up re-reveals both the pages row and the styles row.
- I could not reverse-engineer their exact mechanism — their header carries no `sticky-header` element and my nav-row measurements came back degenerate. Build ours on scroll direction; do not try to match their implementation.
- Ours: `Header.tsx` exports `HEADER_HEIGHT_CLASS`, and `CollectionToolbar` sticks at `top-16` in agreement with it. **A reveal changes the header's effective height at runtime**, which is exactly the drift that put the toolbar 37px behind the header in #401. Whatever lands here has to keep those two in agreement while the header is animating, or pin the toolbar to the collapsed height.
- The styles row deliberately lives OUTSIDE `<header>` (#401) so the sticky box stays one row tall. Reintroducing it into the sticky box is the regression to avoid.

## Acceptance

Scroll down collapses to the compact bar; scroll up reveals the nav rows at any scroll position. Toolbar never sits behind the header — assert both bounding boxes after a scroll, as #401 did. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `56f23914` - feat(web): reveal the nav rows on scroll up, collapse on scroll down

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useNavReveal.ts` — new; scroll-direction state with a 96px top threshold and a 6px jitter floor
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — pages row and styles row both bound to the flag; styles row now `sticky top-16 z-40`, collapsed state translates up and goes `invisible`
- `packages/web/app/components/product/CollectionToolbar.tsx` — `data-testid="collection-toolbar"` for the bounding-box assertion; comment says why top-16 is a constant (also removed a duplicated comment pair)
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useNavReveal.test.ts` — new; 7 cases
- `packages/web/tests/components/layout/Header.structure.test.tsx` — 7 new source-level guards
- `tests/e2e/header-reveal.spec.ts` — new; 5 cases

**Summary**:
Direction, not position. Scrolling down collapses to the compact bar (wordmark + four action icons); scrolling up reveals both nav rows at any scroll position. Guards: always revealed within 96px of the top, and deltas under 6px are treated as trackpad/rubber-band wobble.

On the sticky-offset question the ticket posed, this takes the second option — **pin the toolbar to the collapsed height**. `HEADER_HEIGHT_CLASS` stays `h-16` and the styles row sticks *below* the header on its own account (z-40 under the header's z-50) rather than rejoining the sticky box, so the toolbar's `top-16` never has to track a runtime-varying header height. Consequence, deliberate and documented in the source: a revealed styles row passes over the toolbar for as long as the user is scrolling up. The alternative — a CSS-variable offset both sides transition in lockstep — is exactly the kind of drift that put the toolbar 37px behind the header in #401.

Collapsed rows use `invisible`, not just `opacity-0`, so twelve style links and four page links leave the tab order instead of remaining focusable but unseen. `motion-reduce:transition-none` on both rows.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run` (packages/web)
- Result: PASS — 1793 tests, 69 files, 0 failing
- Command: `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/header-reveal.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps`
- Result: PASS — 5/5. Includes the acceptance assertion: after each of +1200 / -300 / +800 scroll steps, `toolbar.y >= header.y + header.height - 1` and `header.height <= 65`.
- Regression check: `layout.spec.ts` + `mobile-nav.spec.ts` → 53 passed / 9 failed. Re-ran the identical pair with this ticket's changes stashed: **same 9 failures, same 53 passes** — all pre-existing (strict-mode violations from two `nav a[href="/posters"]` matches, and the orange `theme-color` meta from the rebrand).
- Typecheck: `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports 23 errors, all pre-existing and none in the files this ticket touched (verified by grepping the output for Header.tsx / useNavReveal / CollectionToolbar — no hits). Recorded as build FAILED because the repo's typecheck does not currently pass on this branch.

**Note on the reduced-motion test**: `test.use({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` did not reach the page in this Playwright setup (`matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` came back `false`); `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` does, and the spec uses that.

comments.text:
🔄 **Reopened — feedback from dhruv**

> when the nav row shows up, it should push the rest of the page down, currently it hides the filter button

The overlay trade-off taken in `56f23914` is wrong in practice: the revealed styles row passes over `CollectionToolbar`, and the "Hide filters" button is the first thing it covers. The toolbar's `sticky top-16` has to follow the revealed chrome instead of being pinned to the collapsed height.

**Files Changed**:

The overlay trade-off from `56f23914` is gone. The revealed styles row now pushes the toolbar down by exactly its measured height, over the same 200ms, instead of passing over it and burying the Hide-filters button.

ticket.description:
## Overview

Build the wishlist destination page. Analysis §3.5 lists Wishlist among the pages we don't have; mesonart routes theirs at `/apps/wishlist`.

This un-defers what the feature scope deliberately pushed to Phase F ("the parity work needs the affordance and the count, not the destination"). The affordance and count shipped with #387–#389; the destination is what's left.

## Why it's cheap now

Backend and client are already complete — this is a UI-only ticket:

- `packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts` — `GET /` (:68), `GET /count` (:113), `POST /:productId` (:145), `DELETE /:productId` (:181)
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts:2199` — `wishlistApi`, all four methods
- `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` — hydration-safe store, 131 lines
- `WishlistButton`, header count badge — live

Nothing new needed in `packages/api`.

## Rough scope

- New route (auth-gated; `routes/_authed/` is the existing pattern for account pages)
- Reuse `ProductGrid` / `ProductCard` rather than inventing a card
- Empty state
- Header/account nav entry point

## Open questions — decide when planning

- `/wishlist` top-level vs `_authed/account/wishlist` (all other authed pages live under `account/`)
- Signed-out behaviour: sign-in prompt vs redirect
- Whether the list endpoint's dangling-id drop needs surfacing ("2 items no longer available") or stays silent

## Notes

- Both this and the reviews page add routes, so both write `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts` — tracked, not gitignored. If worked in parallel, stay in one checkout and stage by explicit path.
- Details to be planned at work time; this is a placeholder with the groundwork recorded.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commits**: `1bb591c2` - feat(web): wishlist page at /wishlist · `e7da9edb` - test(e2e): wishlist, signed out end to end

**The three open questions, answered**:
1. **`/wishlist` top-level, not `_authed/account/wishlist`** — the feature changed under this ticket: saving no longer requires an account (#477), so an auth guard would bounce a guest to login and hide the list they had just built.
2. **Signed-out behaviour: it is their page too.** No sign-in prompt, no redirect. The store holds ids either way — localStorage for a guest, the account for a signed-in user — and the page hydrates them through the **public** `POST /api/products/by-ids`, so one code path serves both. Going through `/api/wishlist` would 401 every guest.
3. **Dangling ids stay silent.** The API already drops them and `/count` counts live products, so the badge and the list agree; a deleted product is one fewer card, not a broken one or a "2 items no longer available" notice.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/wishlist.tsx` — public route, beige header band, `noindex` (per-visitor content)

- Products are cached by id, so unsaving one card does not re-fetch the rest, and the effect keys on the *missing* ids — a dangling id never resolves, and that is what stops it looping.
- Requests are batched at 50; the by-ids endpoint 400s past that, which would blank the page for a long list.

**Verification**:
- Unit: `bunx vitest run tests/components tests/routes tests/stores` — 1108 passed. One pre-existing unrelated failure: `tests/routes/home-tokens.test.ts` expects `from-slate-700/80` in `app/routes/index.tsx`, removed by commit `089ffa41`; that file is untouched here.

ticket.title: Schema - promotion, promotion_product and promotion_exclusion tables
ticket.description:
## Task
Add the promotion entity. Three tables in a new `packages/api/src/database/schema/promotions.ts`, exported from `schema/index.ts`, plus the generated migration.

State is DERIVED, never stored: a promotion is active when `isEnabled && now >= startsAt && (endsAt is null || now < endsAt)`. No `status` column — it would fall out of sync and a sale would need someone to remember to switch it off.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 1 — Schema + contracts
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §4

Follow the idiom in `packages/api/src/database/schema/products.ts` (pgTable + pgEnum + index callbacks). Test as shape assertions on the drizzle object, like `tests/database/product-popularity-columns.test.ts` — the route suites mock `db`, so nothing else catches a column that does not exist (see #387).

`endsAt` is nullable and PRIVATE — it must never be serialized to the storefront (enforced in T6/T10, documented here).

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `4b8edcd5` - feat(api): promotion entity — scope, exclusions and derived active state

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/promotions.ts` - new: `promotions`, `promotionProducts`, `promotionExclusions`, three pgEnums (`discount_type`, `promotion_scope`, `countdown_mode`), relations and inferred types
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/index.ts` - re-exports the new module
- `packages/api/tests/database/promotions-schema.test.ts` - 9 shape assertions
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/0007_marvelous_king_cobra.sql` + `meta/0007_snapshot.json` + `meta/_journal.json` - generated migration, applied

**Summary**:
Three tables as designed. No `status` column — active state is derived from `isEnabled && now in [startsAt, endsAt)`. `endsAt` is nullable (open-ended sale) and documented private. Countdown behaviour is configuration (`countdownMode` default `rolling`, `rollingWindowMinutes` 720, `rollingJitterMinutes` 90); `priority` (default 0) breaks overlap so promotions never stack. `membersOnly` defaults true, `isEnabled` defaults false. `promotion_exclusion` is a separate table from `promotion_product` so an exclusion can beat every scope. Composite PKs on both membership tables plus a product-side index each; `promotion_active_idx` on (is_enabled, starts_at, ends_at) and `promotion_priority_idx`.

Code follows repo style rather than the verbatim step snippet: `packages/api/src` is double-quote + semicolon (matching `collections.ts`), `tests/database` is single-quote + semicolon (matching `product-popularity-columns.test.ts`). Also added the two `one()` relations and `$inferSelect/$inferInsert` types the collections module carries, so the module matches its neighbour.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/api && bunx vitest run tests/database/promotions-schema.test.ts`
- Result (RED, before implementation): FAIL — `Cannot find module '../../src/database/schema/promotions'`
- Result (GREEN): PASS (9 tests, 9 passing, 0 failing)
- Regression: `bunx vitest run tests/database/promotions-schema.test.ts tests/database/migrations.test.ts` → PASS (36 passing, 63 skipped, 0 failing)
- Type-check: `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no errors referencing `promotions` or `schema/index`
- Migration reviewed before applying: purely additive (3 CREATE TYPE, 3 CREATE TABLE, 5 FKs, 4 indexes). No drops, no alters to existing tables.
- Applied to dev DB (localhost:5440) and confirmed live: all three tables present, `ends_at` `is_nullable=YES`, `is_enabled` default `false`, `members_only` default `true`, `countdown_mode` default `'rolling'`, `rolling_window_minutes` 720, `rolling_jitter_minutes` 90, `priority` 0, and no `status` column.

ticket.title: Schema - record the promotion and its discount on orders
ticket.description:
## Task
Add `orders.promotionId` (nullable FK) so a settled order records which promotion priced it, add `orders.promotionDiscount` as the promotion's own money bucket, and confirm `order_items.itemDiscount` (already declared at `orders.ts:258`) is the per-line store. Migration included.

This is the design's §4 point about the compare-at trap: a discount recorded as a discount keeps revenue reporting honest, where inflating a compare-at price would hide it.

## One bucket per discount source (design D8)
The promotion must NOT write into `orders.discount` or `orders.couponDiscount`:

- `orders.promotionDiscount` — this feature, automatic, sum of the line discounts
- `orders.couponDiscount` — reserved for codes, stays `'0.00'`, nothing in this feature writes it
- `orders.discount` — derived total, `promotionDiscount + couponDiscount`

Without the split, a settled order cannot be attributed once codes exist — reporting cannot separate "the sale worked" from "a code leaked". One migration line now; after orders exist there is no source data to backfill from.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 1 — Schema + contracts
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §4, D8

Columns only — the write path lands in T8 (order creation). `orders.discount` and `orders.couponDiscount` already exist (`schema/orders.ts:171,179`) and today are always `"0.00"` (`routes/orders.ts:268,299`).

ticket.title: API - order creation writes the real discount and enforces the per-customer limit
ticket.description:
## Task
Replace `const discount = "0.00"; // TODO: Apply coupon if provided` (`routes/orders.ts:268`). Order creation re-resolves sale pricing from the database, writes `promotionId`, `orders.promotionDiscount`, a derived `orders.discount`, and per-line `order_items.itemDiscount`, and enforces `perCustomerOrderLimit`.

**The server is the only pricing authority.** Any price sent by the client is ignored. A non-member at order time pays base, so the gate cannot be bypassed by holding a cart open through a logout.

## Money buckets (design D8)
```
orders.promotionDiscount = sum of line discounts   <- this feature writes it
orders.couponDiscount    = '0.00'                  <- reserved for codes, untouched
orders.discount          = promotionDiscount + couponDiscount   <- derived total
```
Compose `discount` from the two source columns rather than assigning the promotion total to it directly, so the expression is already correct on the day codes land.

`routes/orders.ts:298` persists `input.couponCode` — unvalidated client text stored beside a hardcoded `couponDiscount: "0.00"`, making the order record claim a code was applied when none was. The dormant checkout UI at `OrderSummary.tsx:201` stays as-is: it never renders, because no caller passes `onApplyCoupon`.

Gift cards are tender, not a discount — they apply after tax against the total and are out of scope here entirely (`gift-cards` feature owns them). Nothing in this ticket touches `giftCardAmount`.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 3 — API surfaces
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5 (layering order), D8

Order creation already requires an account (`routes/orders.ts` builds from `user.id`). `perCustomerOrderLimit` counts that customer's settled orders carrying the same `promotionId` — reuse the settled-order status logic from `lib/product-sales.ts` (`VOIDED_ORDER_STATUSES`).

Interim assumption for the totals block, pending #568 (DECISION NEEDED — subtotal semantics and free-shipping threshold):

`orders.subtotal` stays GROSS (sum of base line totals, unchanged from today) and `total = subtotal + shipping − discount + tax` keeps subtracting the discount exactly once. The free-shipping threshold therefore keeps reading the gross figure, as it does today.

ticket.title: API - countdown deadline resolution, cookie mint and clamp
ticket.description:
## Task
`packages/api/src/lib/promotion-countdown.ts`: resolve the deadline a visitor sees.

1. Cookie `promo_deadline_<promotionId>` holds this visitor's deadline. Absent or already past → mint `now + rollingWindowMinutes − rand(rollingJitterMinutes)` and set it. Jitter stops every visitor seeing an identical `12:00:00`.
2. Displayed deadline = `min(cookieDeadline, endsAt)` when `endsAt` is set — so the number drops below the usual window when the sale genuinely is ending, and never exceeds the time actually remaining.
3. Zero reached mid-session while the sale is live → next load mints a fresh window.
4. `countdownMode = 'real'` → deadline is `endsAt`, cookie unused.

Only the resolved deadline is serialized. `endsAt` never crosses the wire.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 3 — API surfaces
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §6 — read the CCPA dark-patterns note there before implementing. The behaviour is configurable precisely so it can be switched to a truthful countdown in one admin edit.

Resolution runs server-side (SSR) so there is no hydration flicker and no client clock to tamper with. Cookie handling follows `routes/cart.ts:272-283` (`getCookie`/`setCookie` from `hono/cookie`). Inject `now` and the random source for testability.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `a5ccfc92` - feat(api): per-visitor countdown deadline, clamped by the real end

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/lib/promotion-countdown.ts` (new) — `resolveCountdownDeadline(promotion, cookieDeadline, now, random)`, plus `countdownCookieName` / `parseCountdownCookie` / `serializeCountdownCookie`. `now` and `random` are injected, so the tests need no fake timers.
- `packages/api/src/routes/promotions.ts` (new) — public `GET /api/promotions/active`.
- `packages/api/src/index.ts` — mounted at `/api/promotions`, beside the other storefront routers.
- `packages/api/tests/lib/promotion-countdown.test.ts` (new) — 9 tests.
- `packages/api/tests/routes/promotions.test.ts` (new) — 14 tests.

**Summary**:
Mint on a fresh or spent cookie (`now + rollingWindowMinutes − rand(rollingJitterMinutes)`), reuse a live one, re-mint once a window runs out. Displayed deadline is always `min(minted, endsAt)` — verified both for a fresh mint and for a still-live cookie, so the timer can never show more time than remains. `countdownMode='real'` returns `endsAt` directly and leaves the cookie untouched.

Two hardening decisions beyond the ticket text:
- The response payload is an explicit five-field allowlist (`promotionId`, `headline`, `percentOff`, `membersOnly`, `deadline`), never a spread row — that is what makes the `endsAt` guarantee structural rather than incidental. A test asserts the exact key set.
- `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. The deadline is per-visitor; a shared cache serving one browser's countdown to everyone would defeat the jitter entirely.
- The jitter is capped below the window, so a misconfigured row (jitter wider than window) cannot mint a deadline already in the past and spin the visitor through a re-mint on every load.

A failed promotion lookup logs and reads as "no sale running" — a decorative strip must not take the storefront down.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/api && bunx vitest run tests/lib/promotion-countdown.test.ts tests/routes/promotions.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (23 tests, 23 passing, 0 failing)
- Command: `cd packages/api && bunx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors
- Leak assertions (raw body, not a parsed shape): `not.toContain("endsAt")`, `not.toContain("ends_at")`, `not.toContain(REAL_END.toISOString())`, `not.toContain(String(REAL_END.getTime()))`, `not.toContain("2026-12-31")`.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/product/SalePrice.tsx` (new) — the one component that prints a possibly-discounted price: sale price, base struck through, percent-off marker, "Members" tag when locked. Pure/hook-free so it can mount once per grid cell.

- `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts` — new `onSale` query parameter on `GET /api/products`; the sale context now loads before the query so the predicate lands in the same `where` the count and the page window run against
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `onSale?: boolean` on `ProductFilters`
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useActivePromotion.ts` — new: shared `useActivePromotion()` lookup (in-flight deduped) and `useCountdown()`, which formats through SaleStrip's exported `formatRemaining`
- `packages/web/app/routes/sale.tsx` — new: the /sale route, hero, empty state, grid
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — `SaleNavLink` appended after the `STYLE_OPTIONS` map in nav row 2, `SaleMobileNavLink` in the drawer
- `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts` — /sale registered
- `packages/web/tests/routes/sale.test.tsx` — new: 29 tests

The grid is `ProductGrid`, fed by `GET /api/products?onSale=true`. Scope minus exclusions is resolved entirely server-side: `promotionScopeCondition` mirrors `matchesScope` branch for branch (including the two odd ones — a `filter` scope with no keys matches nothing, one whose keys are all empty arrays matches everything — and the flat `includedIds`) and is pushed into `conditions`, so the count, the page window and the resolved prices all come out of one `where`. Filtering after `limit/offset` would have returned short pages and a total counting products the sale never touched. Nothing describing a scope crosses the wire.

`onSale` is a literal `'true'`/`'false'` pair rather than `z.coerce.boolean()` like its neighbours: coercion reads the string `'false'` as `true`, which on this parameter silently swaps the whole catalogue for the sale.

The countdown reuses SaleStrip's exported `formatRemaining` via `useCountdown`, so the strip and the page cannot print different digits for the same second. `SaleStrip.tsx` itself is untouched — folding its own lookup into the new hook is a change to a component with its own suite and belongs in its own ticket.

The nav link is absent (not greyed) when nothing is running, and absent while the lookup is still out, so it cannot flash and withdraw.

`validateSearch` coerces `page` from the string `router.tsx` hands it and floors junk to 1. `SaleSearchParams.page` is optional in the TYPE and always present in the VALUE, so `<Link to="/sale">` does not have to carry `?page=1`.

ticket.title: E2E - sale lifecycle from no promotion to expiry
ticket.description:
## Task
Playwright spec covering the whole lifecycle, because the honest-by-construction claim is only true if the absence and expiry paths are tested as hard as the active one:

1. No promotion → no strip, no timer, no badges, no Sale nav link, `/sale` shows the empty state, announcement bar carries its usual messages.
2. Active promotion → strip with headline + timer, struck prices on grid and PDP, cart saving row, `/sale` lists exactly the eligible products.
3. Excluded product → no sale price anywhere.
4. Expired promotion → prices revert, all chrome disappears, no manual step required.
5. Countdown → a second page load inside the window continues the same deadline rather than restarting it.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 5 — E2E
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §10

Per the repo gotchas: use `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` in `beforeEach`, and scope selectors for mobile vs desktop (`div.hidden.lg\\:block`) because the same test ids exist in both trees. Seed promotions through the admin API rather than direct SQL so the test exercises the real write path.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `33f66ce5` — test(e2e): sale lifecycle from no promotion through expiry

**Files Changed**:
- `tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts` — 16 tests across four legs (no promotion → active → expiry → countdown continuity)
- `tests/e2e/helpers/promotions.ts` — seeding surface: `createPromotion` / `expirePromotion` / `deletePromotion` / `deleteAllPromotions` / `listPromotions` / `getPromotion` / `setPromotionEnabled` / `getActivePromotion` / `waitForNoActivePromotion` / `purgeProductCache`, all through the admin API using `tests/.auth/admin.json`

**Verification**:
- Command: `SKIP_E2E_SERVER=true bunx playwright test tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps --workers=1 --reporter=line`
- Result: PASS (16 tests, 16 passing, 0 failing) in 1.9m
- `tsc --noEmit` strict over both files: clean

**Lifecycle coverage**
1. *No promotion* — no strip, no countdown, no `sale-nav-link` (desktop) and no `sale-mobile-nav-link` (drawer opened explicitly, since the mobile tree is a separate render), plain PDP and grid prices, `/sale` empty state with the `Sale` fallback heading, announcement bar still rotating its three usual messages.
2. *Active* — strip headline + a countdown asserted to actually tick, Sale link in both nav trees, struck price + `price-was` + `25% off` in the buy panel, `buybox-sale-countdown`, `/sale` listing exactly `catalogueTotal − 1` products with the excluded poster absent by href.
3. *Excluded product* — base price in the buy panel while the sale runs on around it.
4. *Expiry* — a 10s window left to lapse with no admin write; chrome gone, then prices reverted.
5. *Countdown* — the rolling deadline is identical across a reload, checked against a cookie-less context that mints a different one, so the assertion has teeth.

**Asserted at API level, not through the UI** (spelled out in the spec header)
- **Cart saving row.** `/cart` renders lines from the local zustand store and takes savings from `GET /api/cart`, joined per line. Every `cartApi` mutation hook has zero call sites, so a UI add-to-cart makes a local line with no server line to join — the row cannot render for a real user. Covered by seeding the server cart via `POST /api/cart/items` and asserting `pricing.sale`, `pricing.locked`, `pricing.percentOff`, `pricing.headline` and `savingTotal`.
- **Order creation.** Out of scope and unreachable for the same reason.
- **Exact discounted amounts.** DOM assertions are structural; the arithmetic is cross-checked against `GET /api/products/:slug`.

**Two defects found and filed**
- **#524** — `/sale` and `/posters` card mappers drop the `sale` field, so every card on those grids prints its base price mid-sale. `ProductCard` is fine; the PDP "You May Also Like" row proves it (raw API items via the `toFeaturedProducts` pass-through). Grid coverage was pointed at that row instead, with a comment naming #524 and the tightened `/sale` assertion to adopt once it is fixed.
- **#525** — promotion writes call only `invalidateActivePromotions()` and never purge the Redis product-response cache (`product-list:` 300s, `product:` 600s), so the storefront serves pre-change prices for minutes after a sale starts or ends. `purgeProductCache()` in the helper works around it between legs. The expiry leg keeps the two apart deliberately: it proves the chrome vanishes with nothing purged and nothing touched, and only purges before asserting on prices.

**Environment note**: the shared dev API on :3000 was wedged (hung, and before that serving 500s on `?onSale=true` from a stale `bun --hot` module graph while the code on disk was fine). Restarted it in place — the storefront on :3001 and the API on :3000 are both this repo, `:5173` is not.

ticket.title: API - POST /api/gallery/join
ticket.description:
## Task
Authenticated, idempotent endpoint that joins the caller to the gallery: sets `galleryMember`, `galleryJoinedAt`, `marketingConsentAt` and `joinSource`.

Idempotent means a second call does not move `galleryJoinedAt` or re-stamp consent — the original consent date is the one that matters. Returns the membership state either way so the client can unlock without a refetch.

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 2 — API
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §8

New router `packages/api/src/routes/gallery.ts`, mounted like the other storefront routers. `joinSource` is validated against the fixed set (`banner` | `rail` | `cart` | `registration` | `sale-page`) rather than stored as free text from the client. Guests get 401 — the join modal routes them through registration first (T-G3).

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `5eae8765` - feat(api): idempotent gallery join endpoint

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/gallery.ts` (new) — POST /api/gallery/join, guarded by `requireAuth` like the other authenticated storefront routers
- `packages/api/tests/routes/gallery.test.ts` (new) — 19 tests
- `packages/api/src/index.ts` — two lines: import + `app.route("/api/gallery", galleryApp)`

**Summary**:
Authenticated, idempotent opt-in. Sets `galleryMember`, `galleryJoinedAt`, `marketingConsentAt`, `joinSource` and returns the membership state on every call so the client unlocks without a refetch.

Idempotence is implemented as a read-then-short-circuit: an existing member's re-join returns the stored state and issues no write at all, so `galleryJoinedAt` cannot move and consent cannot be re-stamped. The first-join write also preserves any pre-existing `marketingConsentAt` rather than overwriting it just because `galleryMember` was false — consent can predate the flag (older opt-in, or a half-landed write), and re-stamping there loses the real date just as surely.

`joinSource` is validated against the fixed enum (banner | rail | cart | registration | sale-page); the column is plain `text` with nothing behind it, so the zod enum is the only gate. Body accepts the field as either `source` or `joinSource`, both through the same enum. Guests get 401 from `requireAuth`. A session over a deleted user row gets 404 rather than a silent success claiming a membership no row holds.

**Verification**:

- Result: PASS (19 tests, 19 passing, 0 failing)
- Output: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 19 passed (19)`

- Type check: `tsc --noEmit` scoped to `src/routes/gallery.ts` reports no errors in the new file.

ticket.title: Web - SSR-safe member state hook
ticket.description:
## Task
One hook, `useGalleryMembership()`, reading `galleryMember` from the better-auth session and exposing `{ isMember, isLoading, join }`. Every surface that shows a locked price reads it from here rather than deriving membership itself.

SSR-safe: the server already knows the answer from the session, so the first paint must not flash an unlocked price and then lock it (or the reverse).

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 3 — Frontend
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §8

`galleryMember` reaches the client through better-auth `additionalFields` (T-G1), so `authClient.$Infer.Session['user']` carries it — see `packages/web/app/lib/auth-client.ts`. `join()` posts to the T-G2 endpoint and optimistically flips local state on success.

Note the price shown is still the server's: the hook decides whether the saving reads as locked, never what the saving is.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `09142083` - feat(web): SSR-safe gallery membership hook

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useGalleryMembership.ts` (new) - the hook
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useGalleryMembership.test.ts` (new) - 21 tests

**Summary**:
`useGalleryMembership()` returns `{ isMember, isLoading, join }`.

Membership is read from the root route's session via `useRouteContext({ from: '__root__' })`, **not** from better-auth's `useSession()`. This is a deliberate departure from the ticket's suggested implementation, and it is what makes the SSR requirement achievable — see the spec note below.

`join(source)` posts to `${getApiUrl()}/api/gallery/join` with `credentials: 'include'`, trusts the idempotent endpoint's returned `galleryMember` rather than assuming success flipped anything, and optimistically flips local state so the price unlocks on the page it was unlocked from (router context keeps its loaded value until the next navigation revalidates). Any non-ok response or thrown request leaves state untouched and resolves `false`.

`isLoading` describes the join write only — membership itself is never pending, because the server resolved it in `beforeLoad`.

The hook computes no price. Its surface is asserted key-by-key (`isLoading`, `isMember`, `join`) so a `memberPrice` cannot quietly grow onto it later; the numbers stay resolved by the API.

**⚠️ Spec defect in this ticket's step 3 code**

The proposed implementation cannot satisfy the ticket's own third test:

1. `useSession()` from `better-auth/react` starts at `{ data: null, isPending: true }` and only settles after a client round trip. During SSR no fetch happens, so the server paints `isMember: false` for a member and the client corrects it after hydration — exactly the flash of an unlocked-then-locked price the ticket forbids. The repo already solved this: `__root.tsx` fetches `/api/auth/get-session` in `beforeLoad` and puts the session in router context, which `Header.tsx` (#362) and `wishlist.tsx` read. `galleryMember` still arrives as a better-auth additional field (#439); the root route just resolves it early enough for SSR.
2. `fetch('/api/gallery/join')` is relative. There is no Vite `/api` proxy in this repo and the API is a separate origin in dev, so that request hits the web server. Every other call in `app/lib/api.ts` prefixes `getApiUrl()`.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/web && bunx vitest run tests/hooks/useGalleryMembership.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (21 tests, 21 passing, 0 failing)
- Typecheck: `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in either new file
- **Mutation-tested the no-flash claim** rather than asserting it on faith: temporarily replacing the hook with a fetch-in-`useEffect` implementation (what `useSession()` amounts to) killed 18 of the 21 tests, including all four SSR ones — `renders a member as a member on the server, before any effect runs`, `does not flash the wrong state on first paint`, `does not flash the wrong state for a guest either`, and `never fetches to discover membership`. The SSR assertions go through `renderToStaticMarkup`, where effects never run, so a fetch-based implementation cannot pass them.

**Note on history**: a concurrent agent's `git add -A` briefly swept these two files into `3f65d864` (#431). That agent re-cut its commit as `a9cdf9df` with only its own API files, and these two were committed cleanly afterwards as `09142083`. No history was rewritten by this ticket.

ticket.description:
## Task
The modal the offer opens: promotion headline, what joining unlocks, one email field, one button. Signed-in visitors join in place; guests are routed to registration carrying `?join=gallery` and the prefilled email.

One field is the research finding, not a stylistic preference — minimal-field capture converts best, and every extra field on this modal is a member we do not get.

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 3 — Frontend
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §2, §7, §8

New `packages/web/app/components/promo/JoinGalleryModal.tsx`, shadcn/ui dialog. Headline and depth come from the active promotion — the modal renders nothing when no promotion is active, and contains no hardcoded discount. Uses `useGalleryMembership().join('banner' | 'rail' | 'cart' | 'sale-page')` from T-G5, passing the surface that opened it.

Do not trigger a browser dialog/alert anywhere in this flow.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `e55ec152` - feat(web): join-the-gallery modal, one email field

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/promo/JoinGalleryModal.tsx` - new dialog
- `packages/web/tests/components/promo/JoinGalleryModal.test.tsx` - 20 tests

**Summary**:
- Headline and depth come from `GET /api/promotions/active` (#432). No discount is written down in the component; no active promotion (or a failed lookup) renders `null`. `percentOff: null` (fixed-amount sale) drops the percentage line rather than printing `null%`.

- Signed in → `useGalleryMembership().join(source)` in place, with the address prefilled from the session. Guest → `navigate({ href: '/auth/register?join=gallery&email=<encoded>' })`, which #441 picks up.

ticket.title: Web - dismissible sale banner with session and 7-day cooldown
ticket.description:
## Task
The banner that opens the offer: shown once per session for a non-member while a promotion is active, dismissible, and suppressed for 7 days after a dismissal.

Never shown to a member — they already have the price — and never shown when no promotion is active.

Dismissal is what hands over to the rail tab (T-G8): the offer moves out of the way rather than disappearing.

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 3 — Frontend
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §2, §7

`packages/web/app/components/promo/SaleBanner.tsx`. Frequency state lives in `localStorage` keyed by promotion id, so a new sale gets a fresh chance rather than inheriting the last one's dismissal. Cadence (once per session, then ~weekly) is the researched default, not a guess.

SSR: render nothing on the server pass and mount after hydration, or the banner flashes for members whose session resolves a beat later.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `86087164` - feat(web): sale banner, once a session and cooled for a week after a no

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/promo/SaleBanner.tsx` (new) — the banner, plus the module store that owns the frequency decision and the `useSaleOffer()` handover
- `packages/web/tests/components/promo/SaleBanner.test.tsx` (new) — 27 tests
- `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx` — mounted once after `<ReviewToast />`, behind the existing `!isAdminRoute` gate

**Summary**:
`SaleBanner` renders `JoinGalleryModal` (#444) and owns only the decision to open it. No numbers of its own — the headline and depth come from `GET /api/promotions/active` (#432), fetched once per page load and handed to the modal so it does not look it up again.

Frequency, per design §2:
- **Seen** → `sessionStorage`, key `chobii:sale-banner-seen:<promotionId>`. Written the moment the banner shows, so "once per session" holds even if the visitor navigates away with it open.
- **Dismissed** → `localStorage`, key `chobii:sale-banner-dismissed:<promotionId>`, storing the timestamp of the refusal. `SALE_BANNER_COOLDOWN_MS` (7 days) is applied at read time, so changing it reaches dismissals already on disk.
- Both keys carry the promotion id, so a new sale is a new question rather than an inherited "no".
- A missing, unparseable or future-dated timestamp reads as "not cooling" — a corrupt byte must not silently retire a campaign.

**Handover to the rail (#446)**: `useSaleOffer()` returns `{ promotion, stage, dismiss, reopen }` where `stage` is `'hidden' | 'banner' | 'rail'`. The rail renders on `stage === 'rail'`, labels itself from `promotion`, and calls `reopen()`. It must not read a storage key or fetch the promotion itself. The state is a module store rather than component state precisely because the two are root-mounted siblings: derived independently, the banner would mark the session seen and the rail would read that same key a beat later and conclude the banner had already been shown. The stage is decided once when the promotion resolves and then moves only on `dismiss()` / `reopen()`; recomputing from storage each render would close the banner the instant it marked itself seen.

**SSR**: `getServerSnapshot` reports the idle state and a `mounted` flag holds the first client paint, so the server pass renders nothing and a member never sees a flash. All storage access lives inside the post-mount resolver — never at module scope, never in a render body — and is guarded, so a browser that refuses storage loses the memory rather than the page.

**Known seam for #446**: #444's `onClose` fires on a successful join and on a dismissal alike, and `useGalleryMembership`'s optimistic flip is per-hook-instance, so the banner's own instance still reads `isMember === false` right after a join. Recording a cooldown there is inert, but the rail can briefly offer a price a fresh member already has, until the router context revalidates on the next navigation. #446 should decide whether that needs a shared membership signal.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/web && bunx vitest run tests/components/promo/SaleBanner.test.tsx`
- Result: PASS (27 tests, 27 passing, 0 failing)
- Output: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 27 passed (27)`

ticket.title: Web - black vertical rail tab on the right edge
ticket.description:
## Task
Black vertical tab pinned to the right edge, mid-viewport, reading the promotion's offer (their `Get 40% OFF`). Appears when the banner is dismissed or in cooldown; clicking reopens the modal.

This is the recovery path for a dismissed offer — the documented sticky-teaser pattern — so it must persist across navigation within the session rather than resetting per page.

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 3 — Frontend
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §2, §7
Closes: mesonart parity analysis §3.1 "Floating offer tab" row

`packages/web/app/components/promo/OfferRail.tsx`. Label text is derived from the promotion (`Get {percentOff}% OFF`), never hardcoded. Hidden for members and when no promotion is active.

Mobile: their layout runs a bottom dock, and a right-edge rail collides with it — constrain the rail to `lg:` and up, or place it clear of the dock. Accessibility: it is a `<button>` with a discernible name, not a decorated `div`.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `9f5b4836` — feat(web): black offer rail on the right edge, and one membership signal

**Files Changed**
- `packages/web/app/components/promo/OfferRail.tsx` (new) — the tab itself. Renders on `stage === 'rail'` from `useSaleOffer()` and calls `reopen()`; it resolves nothing of its own.
- `packages/web/tests/components/promo/OfferRail.test.tsx` (new) — 26 tests.
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useGalleryMembership.ts` — optimistic join flip lifted from per-instance `useState` to one module signal (`useSyncExternalStore`), pinned to the identity that joined. Exports `resetGalleryMembershipSignal()` for tests.
- `packages/web/app/components/promo/SaleBanner.tsx` — the store now carries `source`, so the modal is tagged with the surface that opened it.
- `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx` — mounts `<OfferRail />` beside `<SaleBanner />`.
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useGalleryMembership.test.ts` — resets the shared signal in `beforeEach`.

**Summary**
Black vertical tab (`[writing-mode:vertical-rl]`, `bg-black`, `fixed right-0 top-1/2 z-40`), labelled `Get {percentOff}% OFF` read from the promotion payload on every render, with wording rather than `Get null% OFF` for a fixed-amount sale. Nothing renders with no promotion, for a member, during the server pass, or while the banner is still open. It appears on dismissal and on a load inside the 7-day cooldown or the session mark, and clicking it reopens the modal. Mounted once at the root so it survives navigation. `hidden lg:flex` keeps it off the phone, where their layout runs a bottom dock, and `z-40` keeps it under the `z-50` dialog it opens.

**Design decision — one shared membership signal, not a close-reason handshake**

Options considered:
- **A. Lift the optimistic flip to a shared signal.** Fixes the defect at its source, so the cart (#436) and the sale page get it too. Costs module state that must be reset between tests.
- **B. Have the banner tell the rail why it closed.** Cheaper, no module state, but it patches the symptom for one pair of surfaces and leaves the same staleness for every other consumer of `useGalleryMembership`.

Chosen A. The bug is not "the rail and the banner disagree", it is "`useGalleryMembership` gives a different answer per call site", and B would leave that true. The signal is pinned to `session.user.id` so it can only ever unlock the account that earned it — a sign-out or a different user drops straight back to what the session says — and it only turns membership on, so it cannot mask an authoritative `galleryMember`.

**Second defect found while testing**: `SaleBanner` hardcoded `source="banner"` on the one modal both surfaces share, so a join recovered by the rail was recorded as `joinSource: 'banner'` — hiding exactly the conversions the rail exists to produce. `source` now lives in the store and moves to `'rail'` on `reopen()`.

**Tests**
- `tests/components/promo/OfferRail.test.tsx` (26) — an integration suite: real `SaleBanner`, real `JoinGalleryModal`, real `useGalleryMembership`, with only the router context and `fetch` stubbed, so membership is set the way production sets it. Covers the empty cases, appearance on dismissal / cooldown / session mark, the label tracking the promotion (and never containing `40`), reopen + `{ source: 'rail' }` on the POST, one promotion lookup across remounts, `<button type="button">` with a discernible name and keyboard reachability, the `hidden lg:flex` breakpoint, and four cases pinning the post-join behaviour including "stays hidden after navigating, before the session has caught up".

**Verification**: `OfferRail` 26 ✓, `SaleBanner` 27 ✓ (handover not regressed), `useGalleryMembership` 21 ✓ — 74 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean on all six files.

ticket.title: E2E - locked to unlocked, and the banner-rail handover
ticket.description:
## Task
Playwright spec for the gate:

1. Guest with an active membersOnly promotion sees the teased price and a locked saving in the cart.
2. Joining through the modal unlocks the price on grid, PDP and cart without a manual reload.
3. Checkout charges the sale price for a member and the base price for a non-member.
4. Banner shows once, dismissal reveals the rail, the rail reopens the banner, and the banner stays away on the next visit within the cooldown.
5. A member never sees banner or rail.

## Context
Part of feature: gallery-membership
Phase: 4 — E2E
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §10

Use `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` in `beforeEach` and scope selectors for the mobile/desktop trees. Reuse the promotion seeding helper from the sale-promotions E2E ticket rather than writing a second one. Clear `localStorage` between frequency assertions, or the cooldown from one test suppresses the banner in the next.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `f5432bc3` — test(e2e): gallery membership gate, from locked price to banner-rail handover

**Files Changed**:
- `tests/e2e/gallery-membership.spec.ts` (new, 719 lines) — 8 tests, serial, reusing `tests/e2e/helpers/promotions.ts` from #438 for seeding.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/gallery-membership.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps --reporter=line --workers=1`
- Result: PASS (8 tests, 8 passing, 0 failing)
- Run three times — 20.9s / 49.9s / 22.5s. The middle run was a deliberate back-to-back re-run to prove no leftover-state dependence; the extra 29s is the auth rate-limit backoff engaging, as designed.

**Coverage**

| Leg | Claim |
|---|---|
| 1 | Non-member sees the teased sale price on the PDP behind the `Members` tag, cross-checked against the API's own `sale.locked` |
| 2 | Server cart quotes the sale price and credits **none** of it — a locked line contributes 0 to `savingTotal` — then the same cart, same line unlocks on join *(API level)* |
| 3 | Joining through the modal drops the Members tag in place: no reload, no navigation, no refetch |
| 4 | A member sees neither banner nor rail, **and** no frequency key is written on their behalf |
| 5 | Banner and rail are never on screen together; dismissal hands over to the rail, the rail hands back |
| 6 | The banner shows once per session even when never dismissed (no cooldown key exists in that leg, so only the session flag can be suppressing) |
| 7+8 | Cooldown control pair: a dismissal from yesterday suppresses the banner in a fresh session, one from eight days ago does not |

Legs 7 and 8 are a pair on purpose. Leg 7 alone would also pass against a component that suppressed on the mere *presence* of the key, so the cooldown is only asserted as a duration once its complement is asserted too. The frequency legs keep `sessionStorage` and `localStorage` apart deliberately rather than clearing between tests — Playwright already gives each test a fresh context, but the two rules would mask each other *within* a test.

**Asserted at API level, and why**
- **The cart leg.** The web app never writes to the server cart (every `cartApi` mutation hook has zero call sites), so a UI add-to-cart has no server line to join against and the saving row cannot render for a real user — the same filed bug #438 worked around. Seeded via `POST /api/cart/items`, read via `GET /api/cart`. The arithmetic is the sharper claim anyway: `pricing.sale` is populated and below `pricing.base` while `savingTotal` is exactly 0. `GET /api/cart` caches per `cartCacheKey(cartId, isMember)`, so the post-join read is a genuine recompute.
- **Order creation** left out — out of scope here and unreachable for the same reason (`POST /api/orders` builds from the same empty basket).
- **Grid cards** deliberately not asserted (#524 mapper drops `sale`). Every price assertion reads the PDP `buy-panel`, scoped so the "You May Also Like" row's identical testids can't answer for it.

**Two findings worth carrying forward**

1. **`session.cookieCache` masks a join server-side for 5 minutes.** better-auth is configured with `cookieCache: { enabled: true, maxAge: 300 }`, which serves the whole user object — `galleryMember` included — out of the signed `chobii.session_data` cookie instead of the DB. `joinGallery` writes the column and never refreshes or clears that cookie. Verified directly: `POST /api/gallery/join` returns `{"galleryMember":true}` while `GET /api/auth/get-session` on the same cookie jar still answers `false`, and answers `true` the instant that one cookie is dropped. So cart, product and order pricing all keep treating a fresh member as a non-member for up to five minutes. The UI is insulated because `useGalleryMembership` flips optimistically on the client — which is exactly why leg 3 passes — but the server-side lag is real. **Probably worth its own ticket.** This spec does not assert the stale behaviour (that would pin the bug in place); it drops the cookie in fixtures and documents why, the session-cache counterpart of #438's `purgeProductCache()`.

2. **No "leave the gallery" endpoint, so the shared customer fixture is one-way.** Using `tests/.auth/customer.json` would have made it a member on the first run and asserted "locked" vacuously against a member forever after. Each leg needing a non-member now registers its own account via `POST /api/auth/sign-up/email`, with backoff on the 5/60s auth rate limiter so a quick re-run doesn't read as a product failure.

**Note on step 2 (`verify-fail`)**: the implementation for this feature had already landed, so a red-before-green gate doesn't apply literally. The spec did fail on its first execution — the locked→unlocked cart assertion — and that failure was diagnostic rather than cosmetic: it is what surfaced finding (1) above, and the fix was to the fixtures, not to the assertion.

ticket.title: Remove dark mode — palette, config and .dark branches
ticket.description:
## Task

Dark mode is out. Decided 2026-08-05. Remove the palette, the config and every
`.dark` branch rather than leaving a half-supported theme in the tree.

## Why

Analysis §6 left this open — "Decide explicitly whether dark mode survives;
mesonart has none, and light-only is simpler to match." §2 records it as
`ours extra`. It is now decided: light only.

This also settles #418's architecture question. A baked mat cannot respond to a
theme, which was the one argument for moving matting from the image pipeline to
CSS. With dark mode gone, matting stays baked in `matToSquare` and that decision
needs no revisiting.

## Scope (verified 2026-08-05)

- `.dark` palette block — `packages/web/app/styles/globals.css:212`
- `darkMode: ['class']` — `packages/web/tailwind.config.ts:5`
- `dark:` utility variants — 69 occurrences across exactly 5 files:
  - `app/components/ai-generator/PromptSuggestions.tsx`
  - `app/components/product/FrameSelector.tsx`
  - `app/components/reviews/ReviewCard.tsx`
  - `app/routes/admin/approvals/$id.tsx`
  - `app/routes/admin/approvals/index.tsx`

## Not in scope — no such thing exists

There is **no theme toggle**, no theme provider, no persisted theme preference
and no SSR theme bootstrapping. Grep for `ThemeToggle`, `useTheme`,
`theme-provider`, `next-themes`, `class="dark"` and `classList` returns nothing
in `packages/web/app`. The only `documentElement` writes are in
`app/hooks/useChromeOffset.ts` and are unrelated (they set `--chrome-offset`).

Consequence: the `.dark` block is already unreachable dead code — nothing ever
adds the `dark` class to the root. This is a pure deletion, not a behaviour
change. Light rendering cannot regress because dark rendering never happened.

## Watch for

- `--mat` (globals.css:143) has no dark override and does not need one; leave the
  token itself alone, it is load-bearing as the image-loading placeholder and is
  kept in sync with `MAT_COLOR` by `mat-token.test.ts`.
- Do not delete tokens that light mode also consumes; only the dark overrides
  inside the `.dark` block.
- Three of the five files are admin surfaces — the diff is wider than the
  storefront but not visually risky.

## Acceptance

No `dark:` variants, no `.dark` block, no `darkMode` config. Token compliance
and web test suites pass. Light rendering unchanged (trivially — see above).
