ticket.title: SEED_MEDIA_DIR resolves off cwd — seeding from packages/api silently drops the reference imagery
ticket.description:
## Bug

`SEED_MEDIA_DIR` is anchored to `process.cwd()`, so which directory you invoke
the seed from decides whether the catalogue gets the reference imagery or
quietly falls back to stock URLs. No warning, no error, exit code 0.

`packages/api/src/database/seed-images.ts:39`

```ts
export const SEED_MEDIA_DIR =
  process.env.SEED_MEDIA_DIR ?? join(process.cwd(), ".cache", "seed-media");
```

The media lives at repo root: `.cache/seed-media/`. But the seed's own script
runs from the package directory — `packages/api/package.json:31`:

```
"seed": "bun run --env-file=../../.env src/database/seed.ts"
```

A package script executes with cwd at the package root, so the canonical
invocation resolves to `packages/api/.cache/seed-media`, which does not exist.

## Why it is silent

`localSeedMediaSet` (`seed-images.ts:114`) returns `[]` when the directory or the
`-main.webp` file is missing, and `seed.ts:1629` reads an empty set as "no local
media, use the declared URLs". That degradation is deliberate and correct — a
fresh clone has no `.cache/seed-media/` and must still seed. The defect is that
a *wrong cwd* is indistinguishable from *a clone that never had the files*. Both
produce the same successful-looking run.

## Observed

Today's reseed produced 41 products with room-mockup images on only **3** of
them. `docs/design/mesonart/PLAN-OF-ACTION.md:148` names that exact number as
the degraded signature — the healthy count is **122**:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM products p, jsonb_array_elements(p.images) i
WHERE i->>'type' = 'room-mockup';
```

So this is not hypothetical; it has already silently produced a degraded dev
catalogue during design-parity work.

## Prior art in the tree

`packages/api/tests/lib/image-processing-seed-media.test.ts:25-32` already hit
this and worked around it locally, with a comment naming the cause:

> Anchored to this file rather than reused from seed-images.ts, whose
> SEED_MEDIA_DIR resolves off process.cwd() — correct when the seed runs from
> the repo root, wrong under vitest, which runs from packages/api.

That workaround should collapse into the shared fix rather than stay duplicated.

## Separate from #418

#418 was the double-mat defect in `matToSquare` — wrong pixels in images that
were present. This is wrong images being absent. Same reseed surfaced both;
different causes.

## Fix direction

Anchor the default to the repo root rather than the caller's cwd — resolve
relative to the module (`import.meta.url`) or walk up to the workspace root.
The `SEED_MEDIA_DIR` env override stays as-is. Once the default is
cwd-independent, the test file can import `SEED_MEDIA_DIR` instead of
re-deriving it.

Then close the silence: when `REFERENCE_MEDIA` maps a slug but the directory is
absent, log once at the top of the run — how many of the 41 slugs resolved to
local media and how many fell back. A clone with no media prints "0 of 41, using
declared URLs" and proceeds; a bad cwd prints the same line, which is now
visible rather than inferred from a SQL count afterwards.

## Note on CACHE_DIR

`seed-images.ts:25` has the same cwd-relative shape for `.cache/seed-images/`.
Harmless by comparison — a wrong path is a cache miss that re-downloads — but
worth fixing in the same pass for consistency.

## Acceptance

`bun run seed` from `packages/api`, from the repo root, and via
`pnpm --filter api seed` all pick up the same reference imagery. Room-mockup
count is 122 after a reseed on a machine that has `.cache/seed-media/`. A run
without the directory still succeeds, and says so. The test file's local
re-derivation is gone.

ticket.title: Test Bug: auth.setup fails for trade/admin/content-manager, blocking 90 E2E tests
ticket.description:
## Symptom

A normal `npx playwright test` run dies in setup. Three of the four auth setups fail and **90 tests never run**:

```
3 failed
  [setup] › tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts › authenticate as trade
  [setup] › tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts › authenticate as admin
  [setup] › tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts › authenticate as content manager
90 did not run
1 passed (1.0m)
```

Failure surfaces as `Login failed with unexpected error` thrown from `loginUser` (`tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts:94`).

The suite currently gives no coverage on an ordinary invocation. `--no-deps` is the workaround — `product-grid-alignment.spec.ts` passed 68/68 that way during #418.

## Ruled out

- **Missing accounts.** All four exist with correct roles: `test-customer@example.com` (customer), `test-trade@interior.com` (trade), `test-admin@chobii.art` (admin), `test-content-manager@chobii.art` (content-manager).
- **Reseed side effect.** `seed.ts:1534-1536` deletes only `productVariants`, `products`, `frames`. Users are untouched.
- **Broken credentials or selectors.** The customer setup passes using the same `loginUser` helper, so the flow works at least once per run.

## Leading hypothesis: auth rate limit

`authRateLimit` is **5 requests per 60 seconds** (`middleware/rate-limit.ts:102`) and is applied to sign-in at `index.ts:96`:

```ts
app.post("/api/auth/sign-in/*", authRateLimit); // 5/min
```

Four setups log in from the same host inside one minute, plus any Playwright retries. The first succeeds and the rest exceed the window.

What makes this fit rather than merely plausible: a 429 response renders **neither** of the two strings `loginUser` checks for at `auth.setup.ts:89-90` (`Sign in failed`, `Invalid email or password`), so the helper falls through to the generic `throw` at :94 — which is exactly the error observed. A genuine credential failure would have returned `false` instead.

Not yet confirmed by observing a 429 directly. Do that first.

## Suggested approach

1. Capture the sign-in response status in the setup run to confirm the 429.
2. Then pick a fix: exempt the rate limiter in test env, raise the limit when `NODE_ENV=test`, key it per-account rather than per-IP, or serialise the setups with a delay.
3. Either way, teach `loginUser` to recognise a 429 and report it as such — the generic "unexpected error" cost real diagnosis time here and would again.

## Related

Same class as #142 (customer login timeout) and #143 (admin login timeout), both closed. Recurrence suggests the earlier fixes treated the timeout symptom rather than the throttle.

Found while working #418; not caused by it.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `86471907` - fix(tests): auth setup survives the sign-in rate limiter

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/package.json` — dev script now sets `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` inline
- `tests/e2e/helpers/auth-diagnostics.ts` — new: `findRateLimitHit` / `loginFailureMessage`
- `tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts` — `loginUser` records auth responses, reports a 429 as a 429
- `tests/setup/auth-setup-rate-limit.test.ts` — new: 6 regression guards

**Root Cause**: The hypothesis in the description was right, and there was a second layer to it. The 5/60s auth limiter fires because all local traffic shares the "unknown" IP bucket. The #332 bypass already existed — but only in `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer.env`. Locally `reuseExistingServer` is true and a dev server is almost always already running, so Playwright never spawns the server and that env never reaches the API. Ditto `SKIP_E2E_SERVER=true`. The bypass was declared in the one place it could not take effect, which is why #142/#143 "recurred".

**Location**: `playwright.config.ts:130` (`reuseExistingServer`), `packages/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:54-59` (the bypass), `tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts:94` (old generic throw).

**Fix**: Move the guarantee onto the API dev entrypoint — `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` is set inline in `packages/api`'s `dev` script, so it holds regardless of who started the server and does not depend on turbo env passthrough. The middleware still refuses the bypass under `NODE_ENV=production`, and the production `start` script is untouched (guarded by a test). `loginUser` now attaches a response listener and, on a failed navigation, throws a message naming the status, the URL, the Retry-After window and the remedy.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/setup/auth-setup-rate-limit.test.ts tests/setup/workspaces.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (39 tests, 39 passing) — 6 new guards, 33 pre-existing workspace tests unaffected by the script edit
- Command: `cd packages/api && bunx vitest run tests/middleware/rate-limit.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (9 tests) — #332 bypass semantics unchanged

- Live probe, old API on :3000 (no bypass): `signin1=200 signin2=200 signin3=429 … signin7=429`, body `{"error":"Too Many Requests",…,"retryAfter":60}` — hypothesis confirmed by observation, as asked.
- Live probe, API started via the edited dev script on :3018: `signin1..8 = 200` — no throttle. Sign-up bucket likewise clean (422 "already exists", not 429).
- Real setup run against the *un-restarted* :3000 server, `SKIP_E2E_SERVER=true bunx playwright test --project=setup`: 2 passed / 2 failed, and the failures now read

  > Error: Login for test-admin@chobii.art was rate limited: 429 Too Many Requests from http://localhost:3000/api/auth/sign-in/email (retry after 24s). The auth limiter allows 5 requests/60s per IP … Start the API with DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true (the packages/api dev script does this) and retry.

  instead of "Login failed with unexpected error". That run is the pre-fix server by design — it proves the diagnostic on real traffic.

**Not verified**: a full 4/4 green setup run against a live server, because the API on :3000 is a 23h-old process owned by another concurrent session and restarting it would disrupt that work. The mechanism is proven on :3018 via the actual `bun run dev` script; the next API restart picks it up.

**Note**: `playwright.config.ts` carries a comment explaining why its env block alone is insufficient, but it was left OUT of this commit — the file has unrelated uncommitted changes from a parallel session (browser-matrix limits) and staging it would have swept that work.

ticket.title: Home category tiles link to style ids that no longer exist
ticket.description:
## Task

Every category tile on the home page links to a collection filtered by a style id that is not in the vocabulary any more, so the four busiest entry points into `/posters` land on a page that cannot filter by what the tile promised.

## Context

`packages/web/app/routes/index.tsx:294` still carries the pre-#395 slugs:

```ts
const categories = [
  { name: 'Abstract',   slug: 'abstract',   ... },
  { name: 'Nature',     slug: 'nature',     ... },
  { name: 'Minimalist', slug: 'minimalist', ... },
  { name: 'Typography', slug: 'typography', ... },
]
```

and renders them at `:348` as `` href={`/posters?styles=${category.slug}`} ``.

`STYLE_OPTIONS` (`packages/shared/src/constants/facets.ts:44`) has none of those four. The ids are `wabi-sabi-art`, `plaster-and-texture-art`, `colorful-art`, `minimalist-art`, `pop-art`, `surrealist-art`, `pollock-art`, `bohemian-art`, `expressionist-art`, `hyperrealism-art`, `graffiti-art`, `ukiyo-e-art`. `abstract` exists, but as a SUBJECT, not a style. There is no `nature` or `typography` in either vocabulary.

Found while repairing `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` for #448 — the test that clicks a home tile is `test.fixme` and points here, because repointing it at a valid id would have made the suite green while leaving the tiles broken.

## Decisions this needs

- `Abstract` should probably become `?subjects=abstract`, not a style at all.
- `Minimalist` maps cleanly to `minimalist-art`.
- `Nature` has no style equivalent; the nearest honest mapping is `?subjects=landscape`.
- `Typography` has no equivalent in either vocabulary. Either drop the tile or add the value — do not point it at something close enough.

The images (`/images/categories/*.jpg`) are keyed off the same slug, so any renaming has to keep the tile's art matched to its destination.

## Acceptance

Every home category tile lands on a collection actually filtered by the tile's subject, with the corresponding chip visible. `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` — "should navigate from home page category link" — comes off `fixme` and passes. Ideally the tile list derives from the shared vocabulary rather than restating it, so this cannot drift again.

ticket.title: activeFilterCount misses six facets, so their chips and badge never show
ticket.description:
## Task

Filter the collection by Featured, Vibe, Aesthetic, Medium, Uniqueness or Availability and the page shows no active-filter chips at all and no count on the mobile Filters button — the grid narrows with no visible sign of why.

## Context

`packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx:592`:

```ts
const activeFilterCount =
  filters.styles.length +
  filters.subjects.length +
  filters.colors.length +
  filters.rooms.length +
  (filters.orientation ? 1 : 0) +
  (filters.priceMin !== undefined ? 1 : 0) +
  (filters.priceMax !== undefined ? 1 : 0) +
  (filters.isAiGenerated !== undefined ? 1 : 0)
```

Missing: `vibe`, `aesthetic`, `medium`, `uniqueness`, `availability`, `isFeatured`. The first five are facet groups the #415 rework added to the rail from `FACET_GROUPS`; the sum was never updated to match.

That number gates the whole chip row — `{activeFilterCount > 0 && (...)}` at `:735` (desktop) and `:687` (mobile) — and feeds `MobileFilterButton`'s badge. `ActiveFilterTags` itself already builds a Featured chip (`:997`), so the chip exists and is never rendered.

Verified in the browser: `/posters?isAiGenerated=true` renders "Active filters: AI Generated / Clear all"; `/posters?isFeatured=true` renders no chip row whatsoever, though the API filters correctly (`GET /api/products?isFeatured=true` → 200 with items).

Found while repairing `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` for #448; the chip test is `test.fixme` and points here.

## Note on scope

`ActiveFilterTags` also has no branch for vibe / aesthetic / medium / uniqueness / availability, so fixing only the count would give those five a row with no chip in it. Both halves need doing together.

## Acceptance

Every facet the rail can set produces a chip and counts toward the mobile badge, including `isFeatured`. Derive the count from the filter state rather than restating the field list, so the next facet added cannot silently fall out of it. `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` — "should chip isFeatured like every other filter" — comes off `fixme` and passes.

ticket.title: Active filter chips move into the toolbar row so they always show
ticket.description:
## Task

Put the desktop active-filter chips in the toolbar row, alongside "Hide filters", the product count and the sort control. They render in the products column today (`posters/index.tsx:737`, a `lg:block` div sitting *after* the `</aside>`), which is why they read as belonging to the grid rather than to the filters.

## Why the toolbar rather than the filter lane

The lane was the first instinct, because it puts the chips next to the checkboxes that produced them and it is where mesonart puts theirs. It is the wrong place for us:

**The `<aside>` is `lg:hidden` when filters are hidden** (`filtersHidden ? 'lg:hidden' : 'lg:block'`, :659) — the same trap #419's commit called out for the Hide-filters pill. Chips nested in the rail vanish with the rail, leaving a shopper with an active filter, a reduced product count, and no way to see or clear what is filtering. That is worse than today.

The toolbar dissolves the problem instead of working around it: it already spans both columns as of #419, it is sticky, and it survives the rail being hidden. One render site, no state to keep in sync, chips visible in every combination of (filters active, rail hidden). This is a deliberate departure from mesonart's placement — record it as such so it is not "corrected" back later.

## The constraint this must not break

The rail's sticky offset is `calc(var(--chrome-offset) + 5rem)` — 5rem being the toolbar's own height, a 56px pill inside `py-3`, hardcoded by #419. **A chips row that wraps makes the toolbar taller and silently breaks that**, putting the rail behind the bar. Same class of bug as the 37px header/toolbar overlap in #401 and the push-down fix in #421.

So either:

1. **Keep the toolbar one row tall** — chips on a single line that scrolls horizontally when they overflow. Preferred: the offset constant stays true, and a long filter set cannot push the grid down the page.
2. **Let it wrap and publish the height** — toolbar measures itself into a CSS custom property that the rail's `top` consumes, so the two cannot drift. More correct, more moving parts.

Do not add a third hardcoded height. Two constants in two files with nothing connecting them is exactly how #401 happened.

## Context

- Mobile copy at :695 is already inside the mobile filter sheet and stays as is.
- Chip source stays `ActiveFilterTags` in the same file; this is a placement change, not a rewrite.
- Layout order at `lg`: Hide filters · count · chips · sort. Chips take the flexible space so the sort pill stays right-aligned.

## Acceptance

- Chips render in the toolbar row at `lg`, visible with the rail both shown and hidden.
- Removing a chip and "Clear all" behave exactly as now (#147 fixed a chip-click regression once already — keep its test green).
- **Toolbar height is unchanged with 0, 1 and 10 active filters**, or the rail offset is derived rather than hardcoded. Assert the toolbar and rail bounding boxes after scrolling, as #401 and #419 did — a unit test cannot catch this.
- Mobile unchanged.

ticket.title: Chrome - move the pages nav below the wordmark line and add Best Sellers / New In
ticket.description:
## Problem

Nav row 1 shared the 64px bar with the wordmark and the cart. Mesonart stacks it BELOW that line (analysis §1.1: "Header row — centered wordmark + right cluster" then "Nav row 1 — pages"). Sharing the bar capped row 1 at four links, which is what blocks adding the rest of the §3.5 page inventory later.

## Change

`packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx`:

- Pulled `pages-nav` out of the compact bar. The bar is now wordmark + actions only, `md:justify-end` — the wordmark is absolutely centred at that width, so the actions cluster is the only child left in flow and `justify-between` alone stranded it at the left edge.
- New sticky wrapper below `<header>` holds row 1 (pages, centred) then row 2 (styles). Both stay OUTSIDE `<header>`: inside the sticky box they stand it ~140px tall and swallow the collection toolbar, which is the #401 regression.
- `useChromeOffset` now measures the wrapper rather than the styles row, so both rows count and a third row would need no new number. `stylesRowRef` -> `navRowsRef`.
- Row 1 scrolls (`overflow-x-auto`) and `NavLink` is `whitespace-nowrap`, so added links will not wrap to two lines.
- Added **Best Sellers** and **New In** to row 1 and to the mobile drawer. Neither needs a route: both are `/posters` under a sort the toolbar already offers.

```ts
const BEST_SELLERS_SEARCH = { sortBy: 'salesCount', sortOrder: 'desc' }
const NEW_IN_SEARCH = { sortBy: 'createdAt', sortOrder: 'desc' }
```

Both ids exist verbatim in `SORT_OPTIONS` (`components/product/CollectionToolbar.tsx`), and a test asserts the pairing — renaming a sort id now breaks the nav loudly instead of silently. `NavLink` gained a `search` prop; `MobileNavLink` already had one. Passing `search` wholesale also clears active facets, which is what a top-level nav entry should do.

Row 1 reads: Posters · Best Sellers · New In · Create · Gallery · About

## Verification

Measured headless at 1440x900 on `/posters`:

| state | header | pages | styles | toolbar | --chrome-offset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| top | y36 h65 | y101 | y138 | y632 | 138px |
| scrolled down | y0 h65 | hidden | hidden | y64 | 64px |
| scrolled up mid-page | y0 h65 | y64 | y101 | y138 | 138px |

Header never exceeds 65px; the toolbar always lands at or below the revealed chrome.

Link behaviour, clicked in-browser:

- Best Sellers -> `/posters?sortBy=salesCount&sortOrder=desc`, toolbar reads "Sort by: Best selling", API call `?page=1&pageSize=24&sortBy=salesCount&sortOrder=desc`
- New In -> `/posters?sortBy=createdAt&sortOrder=desc`, toolbar reads "Sort by: Newest First"

## Known and deliberate

**New In never renders as the active link.** `createdAt-desc` is the collection default and the route strips default sort params from the URL, so the link's search is never a subset of the current search. Kept anyway: arriving from a filtered or differently-sorted view, it resets to newest rather than quietly keeping whatever sort was in play.

**The §3.5 pages are still not linked.** Artists index, artist detail, Reviews, Sale/promo, Trade, Commission art, Gift card, Blog and Wishlist have no routes in `packages/web/app/routes/`. Linking them now is nine 404s and a typed-route failure. This ticket makes the room; the pages have to land first.

ticket.title: Bug: infinite scroll on /posters jumps back to the top when page 2 appends
ticket.description:
## Symptom

Scrolling /posters past the pagination threshold loads `?page=2` and the page then scrolls itself back to the top.

Reproduced in the browser with no modal involved:

- wheel down to `scrollY` 2400
- ~900ms later `scrollY` reads 107, then 0
- `scrollHeight` grows 3797 -> 5207 over the same window (page 2 really did append)

So the products load correctly and the reader is thrown back to the first row. Pre-existing; found while working the collection-page parity tickets, not caused by them.

## Leading hypothesis: router scroll restoration on the append navigation

`loadMore` widens the URL rather than stitching pages client-side (`packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx:563-576`):

```ts
navigate({
  to: '/posters',
  search: { ...search, page: pagination.page + 1 },
  replace: true,
})
```

and the router runs with `scrollRestoration: true` (`packages/web/app/router.tsx:75`). Appending a batch is therefore a location change as far as the router is concerned, so it restores the scroll position it has stored for that location — 0 — instead of leaving the reader where they were. The `scrollY` 2400 -> 107 -> 0 sequence matches a restore landing while the new rows are still laying out.

The IntersectionObserver at `:586` presses `loadMore` with `rootMargin: '400px'`, so this fires while scrolling rather than only on the Load more button — which is why it reads as the page fighting the reader.

Not yet confirmed by instrumenting the restore itself. Worth one check before fixing, because a layout-shift-driven jump would look similar in the numbers.

## Suggested approach

`navigate` accepts `resetScroll` (present in `@tanstack/react-router` 1.93's `link.d.ts`). Passing `resetScroll: false` on the `loadMore` navigation keeps the position across the append while leaving scroll restoration on for real navigations. Verify the Load more button path too — it calls the same `loadMore` (`:820`).

## Context

- `?page=N` means "everything up to page N" here — the loader returns the accumulated set (`:119-128`), so nothing on the client re-renders from scratch. The scroll reset is the router's, not a remount.
- `/gallery` does not share this pattern — no `loadMore` there — so the fix is local to the posters route.
- Existing pagination coverage lives in `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts:807-845`.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `3ea53e79` - fix(web): keep the scroll position when posters appends the next page

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` — `resetScroll: false` on the `loadMore` navigation
- `tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts` — new test: scroll into the append, assert the position survives

**Root Cause**: Confirmed by instrumentation, not inferred from the numbers. Patching `window.scrollTo`/`scrollIntoView`/`scrollTop` before app code ran caught the caller with a stack:

```
2267ms  window.scrollTo([{"top":0,"left":0}])  from scrollY=2400
  at Object.fn (@tanstack/router-core/dist/esm/scroll-restoration.js:174:32)
  at RouterCore.emit (router.js:138:24)
  at Match.js:116:138
```

`loadMore` widens the URL (`replace: true`) rather than stitching pages client-side, so the router treats the append as a fresh location and restores that location's stored position — 0.

Two things the original report could not have known:

1. The reset is a **~750ms smooth glide**, not a jump: `html` computes `scroll-behavior: smooth`. The sampled descent — 2400, 2375, 2270, 2154, 1368, 870, 621, 465, 326, 229, 176, 98, 63, 32, 18, 5, 0 — is an easing curve, which is why it reads as the page fighting the reader.
2. The descent begins **after** `scrollHeight` has already grown (append at 480ms, descent starts 558ms, `replaceState` at 86ms). Timing alone was therefore ambiguous between "router restore" and "layout shift" — hence the stack trace. Layout shift is ruled out.

**Location**: `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx:571-583` (the navigate), `packages/web/app/router.tsx:75` (`scrollRestoration: true`).

**Fix**: `resetScroll: false` on that one navigation. Scroll restoration stays on for real navigations; the Load more button shares the same `loadMore` callback, so it is covered by the same line.

**Verification**:
- Command: `SKIP_E2E_SERVER=true bunx playwright test tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps --grep="keep the scroll position"`
- Result before the fix: FAIL — `Expected: > 1000 / Received: 0`, having already passed the `page=2` and `scrollHeight` growth assertions (so the append really happened and the test is not vacuous)
- Result after the fix: PASS (1 test)

- Command: `SKIP_E2E_SERVER=true bunx playwright test tests/e2e/product-listing.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps`
- Result: 115 passed, 1 failed (`offers no category tile the catalogue cannot fill`). That failure is **not** from this change — reverting `posters/index.tsx` to HEAD and re-running it reproduces the same failure, `a[href="/posters?subjects=typography"]` expected count 0. It belongs to the category-tile/facet work in #448/#455.

- Command: `cd packages/web && bunx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors in `posters/index.tsx`
- Instrumented probe after the fix: the `scrollTo` call from `scrollY=2400` is gone entirely, `final scrollY = 2400`. The two remaining calls are the ordinary page-load restore at `scrollY=0`.

**Note**: `--no-deps` was needed because auth setup still fails against the API on :3000, which predates #451's fix and belongs to another session's process. Unrelated to this ticket.

ticket.title: Verify enforced CSP on production after deploy (post-#344 gate)
ticket.description:
## Task

#344 flipped the SSR `Content-Security-Policy` from Report-Only to **enforced** (commit `c124c13d`, `docker/docker-compose.prod.yml`, `chobii-web-headers` traefik middleware). That change is config-only and has NOT reached production — it lands on the next `make -C deploy deploy`.

The policy was derived by auditing the app source at HEAD, not by observing violation reports: production is still serving a pre-parity image, so the origins that would break under the old policy never appeared in a production console. That audit is thorough but it is static analysis. This ticket is the runtime confirmation, and it is a launch gate — an enforced CSP that is missing one source fails **silently to the user** (blank image, dead pay button) while the server still returns 200.

## Prerequisite

The deploy carrying `c124c13d` must be live. Confirm first:

```bash
curl -sSI https://chobii.art/ | grep -i '^content-security-policy'
```

Expect `content-security-policy:` with NO `-report-only` suffix, and the value must contain `blob:`, `https://fonts.googleapis.com`, `https://fonts.gstatic.com` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. If it still says `content-security-policy-report-only`, the deploy has not happened — stop here.

## Scope — walk these three flows with the browser console open

Every step means: perform the action, then read the console for `Refused to ...` / `violates the following Content Security Policy directive`. Zero violations is the pass condition.

1. **Razorpay checkout** — add to cart, reach checkout, open the payment modal, confirm the iframe renders and the card form is interactive. Do NOT complete a real payment; Razorpay is on test keys, so a test-card run is fine if you want full coverage. Watches `script-src https://checkout.razorpay.com`, `frame-src`, `connect-src https://api.razorpay.com https://lumberjack.razorpay.com`.
2. **AI generator with a reference image** — upload a reference image and confirm the local preview thumbnail renders before generation, then generate. The preview is `URL.createObjectURL(file)`, which is exactly what `img-src blob:` was added for.
3. **Google sign-in** — sign in with Google end to end and confirm the account avatar renders. Watches `lh3.googleusercontent.com` in `img-src` and confirms `form-action 'self'` does not interfere with the redirect.

Also check on any page: **Poppins and Urbanist actually load** (not fallback). DevTools > Network, filter `fonts.gstatic.com`, expect 200s; or computed `font-family` on a heading.

## If a violation appears

The fix is one line — add the source to the single CSP label in `docker/docker-compose.prod.yml` and redeploy. Do NOT relax a whole directive (no `'unsafe-eval'`, no wildcard host, no dropping back to Report-Only) to make a symptom go away. Add the specific origin, add a comment saying which code path needs it, and extend `packages/web/tests/security-headers.test.ts` so the gap cannot reappear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `curl -sSI https://chobii.art/` shows enforcing `content-security-policy` (no `-report-only`) with the #344 sources present
- [ ] Razorpay checkout modal opens and is interactive, zero CSP violations in console
- [ ] AI generator reference-image upload shows its preview and generates, zero CSP violations
- [ ] Google sign-in completes and the avatar renders, zero CSP violations
- [ ] Poppins + Urbanist load from `fonts.gstatic.com` (200s in Network), not fallback fonts
- [ ] Any source added as a result of this pass is committed to `docker/docker-compose.prod.yml` AND guarded in `packages/web/tests/security-headers.test.ts`

## Context

- #344 — the change being verified (done). Full audit notes, including what was deliberately left OUT of the policy (`placehold.co`, Sentry ingest, CDN `connect-src`, `accounts.google.com`), are in its completion comment.
- #264 — the original security-header work this extends.
- The policy lives in exactly one place now; `packages/web/app/ssr.tsx` held a second, contradictory enforcing CSP and was deleted in #344.

blocked_by.description: Content-Security-Policy for SSR pages (deferred from #264)

ticket.title: Unscoped test runs from parallel agents saturate the 8-core box — cap workers and enforce scope
ticket.description:
## Problem

Many Claude sessions work this single checkout at once (measured 2026-08-05:
5 CLI + 8 VS Code extension, no worktrees). Every agent verified its ticket by
running far more than the ticket touched, and nothing bounded the result.

Measured at 15:08 on 2026-08-05 — **load average 58 on 8 logical cores**:

- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/web`, no path — 888 tests, ~7 forks
- `playwright test tests/e2e/product-grid-alignment.spec.ts --no-deps`, no
  `--project` — one spec against all 5 browser projects, 11 headless Chromes
- a second concurrent `playwright test` from another session
- a 22-hour-old `pnpm -r test` + `node (vitest)` leaked from an Aug 4 session
  (cwd inside a `/private/tmp/claude-501/...` scratchpad of another project)

## Causes

1. `.claude/skills/tt-work-ticket/SKILL.md:56` said `VERIFY -> Run full relevant
   test suite`, contradicting the path-scoped step template 160 lines below it.
2. No worker caps. Vitest defaults to cores-1; `playwright.config.ts` had
   `workers: CI ? 1 : undefined` = half the cores. Each run claimed the machine.
3. No default project filter — a bare `playwright test <spec>` is 5x the work.
4. `turbo.json` `test` has `dependsOn: ["build"]`, `cache: false`, so a
   repo-root run rebuilds all three packages first. Turbo concurrency was 10.
5. Nothing serialised across agents and nothing reaped strays.

## Fix

Caps, so one run cannot claim the box:

- `maxWorkers: Number(process.env.VITEST_MAX_WORKERS ?? 2)` in all four
  vitest configs (root, api, web, shared)
- `workers: CI ? 1 : Number(process.env.PW_WORKERS ?? 2)` in playwright.config
- firefox / webkit / Mobile Chrome / Mobile Safari projects exist only under
  `CI` or `PW_ALL_BROWSERS=true` — verified 11 tests locally vs 39 with the
  matrix on
- `--concurrency=2` on the three root turbo test scripts
- `scripts/run-tests.sh` default workers 4 -> 2 (`PW_WORKERS` honoured)

Enforcement, because caps do not undo a run that never needed to happen —
`.claude/hooks/guard-test-scope.py`, PreToolUse on Bash via `.claude/settings.json`:

- **deny**: pathless `vitest run`, watch-mode `vitest`, bare `playwright test`,
  `--ui`/`--debug`, root-wide `bun test` / `npm test` / `pnpm -r test` /
  `turbo run test` / `bun run test`. Each deny names the scoped command.
- **repair**: `playwright test <spec>` with no `--project` is rewritten with
  `--project=chromium` inserted after `playwright test` (not appended, which
  would land past a `| head` pipe) — the run proceeds, on one browser.
- **allow**: everything scoped, `./scripts/run-tests.sh` in any form,
  `--list`/`--version`/`show-report`, and all non-test commands.
- escape hatch `ALLOW_FULL_SUITE=1` for a deliberate whole-suite run.
- fails open — a missing python3 or script allows everything rather than
  blocking every Bash call.

Plus `tt-work-ticket` VERIFY rewritten to demand a path, with a "One Machine,
Many Agents" section documenting the guard, the escape hatch and a pre-run
`uptime` check.

## Verification

- 37/37 cases in an offline battery, including false-positive guards:
  `grep -rn "vitest run" docs/`, `git commit -m 'test: bunx vitest run ...'`,
  unbalanced quotes, and `bun test` inside `packages/shared` (bun's own runner,
  one process, 4.5s) all pass clean while root `bun test` is denied.
- Live in-session: deny fired on `node ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run`;
  `ALLOW_FULL_SUITE=1` passed through; the repair path rewrote a real
  `playwright test ... --grep "reduced motion"` and it ran chromium-only.
- Configs re-validated: web `styles.test.ts` 205 passed, api
  `image-processing-seed-media.test.ts` 1 passed, shared 880 passed.
- Load average 58 -> 24 after the stale processes were killed.

## Follow-ups not done here

- Nothing serialises heavy runs across agents; a lock wrapper would.
- Nothing reaps strays. Two `auth.setup.ts` failures (trade + admin) are
  pre-existing and unrelated.

## Task
mesonart.com's cart is a slide-out drawer anchored to the **left** edge; ours navigates to a full `/cart` page. Make the header cart control open a left drawer, and auto-open it when an item is added.

Decisions taken at ticket creation:
- The drawer becomes the primary path. `/cart` **stays routable** (deep links, `tests/e2e/cart.spec.ts`) but the header no longer links to it.
- `addItem` auto-opens the drawer, so PDP and Quickview get the behaviour for free.

## Context

**Dead code to reuse, not rewrite:** `packages/web/app/components/cart/CartSheet.tsx` already implements a slide-out cart (items list, subtotal, empty state, Escape, scroll lock) — but it is anchored `fixed right-0` + `slide-in-from-right`, and it is **imported nowhere**. Rename/retarget it rather than writing a third panel.

**Drawer pattern to mirror:** `packages/web/app/components/layout/SearchDrawer.tsx` — backdrop `z-40`, panel `z-50`, `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`, Escape handler, `document.body.style.overflow` lock with restore on unmount.

**Today's header wiring:** `Header.tsx:230` (desktop) and `Header.tsx:253` (mobile) render `<Link to="/cart">` with the hydration-gated `displayCartCount` badge.

**Store:** `packages/web/app/stores/cart.ts` has no UI state. Its `persist` config already uses `partialize: (state) => ({ items: state.items })` (line ~360), so a new `isDrawerOpen` field will not leak into `localStorage` — do not widen that partialize.

**Tests that pin current behaviour and must move with the change:**
- `packages/web/tests/components/layout/Header.structure.test.tsx:58` and `chrome-tokens.test.ts:66` assert the source still contains `` 'Shopping cart${' `` (#248). The aria-label item count must survive the Link→button swap.
- `tests/e2e/layout.spec.ts:54` and `:178` assert `a[href="/cart"]` is visible in the header and navigates. Both must be rewritten against the drawer.

**Out of scope:** restyling the `/cart` page itself, checkout, and the sale/promotion row work tracked under `sale-promotions`.

ticket.title: Shared - collection contracts, superseding the dead collectionSchema
ticket.description:
## Task

Add the collection vocabulary and validation to `@chobii/shared`, and deprecate the orphan `collectionSchema` already sitting in `packages/shared/src/schemas/product.ts`.

That schema is referenced only by its own test — the same dead-but-tested state `styles.ts` and the size ladders were in before #386. Its `CollectionType` is a closed six-value marketing enum (`new-arrivals` | `best-sellers` | `staff-picks` | `seasonal` | `sale` | `ai-generated-gallery`) which cannot express an admin-authored collection. Supersede it; do not extend it, and do not leave two collection vocabularies alive.

New module `packages/shared/src/schemas/collection.ts`:

- `collectionKindSchema` = `z.enum(['rule','manual'])`
- `collectionRuleSchema` — the facet + sort payload. Every field must be a value `/api/products` already validates: styles, subjects, colors, rooms, vibe, aesthetic, medium, uniqueness, availability, orientation, priceMin, priceMax, isAiGenerated, isFeatured, sortBy, sortOrder. Facet arrays validate against the vocabularies in `constants/facets.ts` — a rule that names a style that does not exist is a rule that renders an empty page.
- `curatedCollectionSchema` — id, slug (kebab regex), title, subtitle, description, kind, rule (null when manual), imageUrl, isActive, showInDiscover, discoverOrder, sortOrder, seoTitle, seoDescription, timestamps.
- `createCollectionSchema` / `updateCollectionSchema` for the admin API, with the cross-field rule: `kind==='rule'` requires a rule, `kind==='manual'` forbids one.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 1 (foundations).

Export from `packages/shared/src/schemas/index.ts`. Follow the doc-comment style of `constants/facets.ts` — it explains WHY the module is the single source of truth, which is the convention here.

Mark the old `collectionSchema` deprecated in place with a pointer to this module, in the style of the `@deprecated` block at the top of `constants/styles.ts`. Leave its existing test passing.

ticket.title: Schema - collections and collection_products tables
ticket.description:
## Task

Add the Drizzle tables backing the feature.

```
collections
  id uuid pk
  slug text unique not null
  title text not null
  subtitle text
  description text
  kind collection_kind not null           -- pgEnum('rule','manual')
  rule jsonb                              -- null when manual
  image_url text                          -- null falls back to a representative product
  is_active boolean not null default true
  show_in_discover boolean not null default false
  discover_order integer
  sort_order integer not null default 0
  seo_title text, seo_description text
  created_at, updated_at

collection_products                        -- manual kind only
  collection_id uuid -> collections.id on delete cascade
  product_id uuid -> products.id on delete cascade
  position integer not null
  primary key (collection_id, product_id)
```

Indexes: unique on `slug`; index on `(show_in_discover, discover_order)` for the rail; index on `(collection_id, position)` for member ordering.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 1 (foundations). Depends on the shared contracts ticket for the rule's shape.

Follow `packages/api/src/database/schema/reviews.ts` — pgEnum block, table block, relations block, doc comments explaining each non-obvious column. Export from `packages/api/src/database/schema/index.ts`.

Migration via `pnpm --filter @chobii/api db:generate`; the repo keeps generated SQL under `packages/api/src/database/migrations/`. Do NOT hand-write the SQL.

ticket.title: API - collection resolver: one collection to one product query
ticket.description:
## Task

A single place that turns a collection row into the product query behind it, so nothing downstream has to know which `kind` it is.

`packages/api/src/lib/collection-resolver.ts`:

- `resolveCollectionFilters(collection, shopperFilters)` — for `kind='rule'`, merges the stored rule as the BASE and the shopper's facets on top. Intersection semantics: a shopper narrowing inside a collection must never widen out of it. A shopper style that is not in the rule's style set yields the empty intersection, not the union.
- `resolveManualMembers(collectionId)` — ordered product ids from `collection_products` by `position`.
- `countCollection(collection)` — the product count for the chip, honouring `isActive`/published status the same way the list endpoint does.

The rule's `sortBy`/`sortOrder` is the collection's default sort; an explicit shopper sort wins.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 1 (foundations).

This is what makes decision 2 of the design real — the rule IS the existing filter payload, so reuse the filter path `productsApp` already runs rather than writing a second query planner. Read `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts` list handler first and lift, don't fork.

The intersection rule is the part most likely to be got wrong; test it directly.

ticket.description:
## Task

Seed fourteen collections so the Discover rail cannot empty out the moment it stops reading `STYLE_OPTIONS`:

- Twelve rule collections, one per `STYLE_OPTIONS` entry — slug from the style id, rule `{ styles: [id] }`, `showInDiscover: true`, `discoverOrder` following the vocabulary order.

- **Best Sellers** — slug `best-selling`, rule `{ sortBy: 'salesCount', sortOrder: 'desc' }`, no facets.

Those last two are the whole point of the feature: they are the two mesonart chips that no facet vocabulary can express.

Idempotent on slug — re-running the seed must not duplicate or clobber an admin's later edits to title/image.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 2. Depends on the schema and the shared contracts.

Find the existing seed entry point under `packages/api/src` and follow its structure. #414 seeded settled orders and approved reviews; match that shape.

The twelve style collections preserve today's twelve chips in link form, so the storefront change is not also a content change.

ticket.title: API - GET /api/collections for the Discover rail
ticket.description:
## Task

Public list endpoint feeding the rail and anything else that needs the collection inventory.

`GET /api/collections?discover=true` returns active collections ordered by `discoverOrder`, each with:

- id, slug, title, subtitle
- `count` — resolved product count (rule or manual)
- `image` — `imageUrl` when the admin set one, else the main image of a representative product, else null
- `imageIsMatted` — true only for the product fallback

That last flag matters: `chipArtScale()` in `DiscoverChips.tsx` exists because product `main` images are matted at a fixed fraction of the longest side. An admin-uploaded image is not matted, and scaling it by the same factor crops into it wrongly. The API is where the two cases are distinguishable, so say so here rather than guessing in the component.

Drop collections that resolve to zero products — a chip leading to an empty grid is worse than no chip (the rule #406 already established).

Cache it the way `collections:v2` is cached today, under a new key.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 3.

This supersedes `GET /api/products/collections` (#406) at `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts:601`. Leave the old route in place for now; the web ticket removes its last caller and a later step deletes it.

Keep #406's representative-product assignment logic — it hands each product to at most one chip so the rail does not show the same picture three times.

ticket.title: API - GET /api/collections/:slug resolving a collection to products
ticket.description:
## Task

The collection page's data endpoint.

`GET /api/collections/:slug` accepts the same query parameters `/api/products` does (facets, price, page, pageSize, sortBy, sortOrder) and returns:

- the collection itself — title, subtitle, description, seoTitle, seoDescription, imageUrl
- the resolved, paginated products
- facet counts scoped to the collection, not to the whole catalogue

The collection's rule is the base query; shopper facets narrow within it, per the resolver's intersection rule. The rule's sort is the default; an explicit `sortBy` wins.

404 on an unknown or inactive slug — an inactive collection must not be reachable by guessing the URL.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 3. Depends on the resolver.

Facet counts: reuse the path from #392 rather than issuing a per-facet count query. Scoping them to the collection is the part that differs — counts from the whole catalogue would offer a shopper filters that return nothing inside this collection.

Manual collections keep `position` as their default order, so paging must be stable across requests.

ticket.description:
## Task

`/api/admin/collections`, behind the same staff-role middleware as `/api/admin/products`:

- `GET /` — list with counts, including inactive ones

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `7a4187d9` — feat(api): admin CRUD for collections

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/collections.ts` — new. GET `/`, GET `/:id`, POST `/`, PATCH `/:id`, DELETE `/:id`.
- `packages/api/src/index.ts` — mounted at `/api/admin/collections`.
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/collections.test.ts` — 23 tests.

**A bug a live probe caught that the tests could not**

The 409 mapping was wrong on the first pass. **Drizzle wraps the driver error**: the object it throws carries `{ query, params, cause, stack }` with `code: undefined` at the top level and the postgres code on `error.cause.code`. Checking `error.code === '23505'` matched nothing, so every slug collision would have surfaced as a 500.

Verified directly against the database:
```
name: Error
own keys: query, params, cause, stack
cause.code: 23505
cause.constraint: collections_slug_unique
```

The original test passed because its fixture rejected with `Object.assign(new Error(), { code: '23505' })` — the shape I had assumed, not the shape Drizzle produces. **A hand-written error fixture only tests the fixture.** The regression test now uses the wrapped shape, and `isUniqueViolation` checks both levels.

**Role gate**: `requireContentManager`, matching `/api/admin/products` rather than `requireAdmin`. A collection is catalogue content — a content-manager who can create products should be able to group them.

**Other decisions**
- The list applies **no `isActive` filter**, deliberately unlike the public endpoint. An admin who deactivated a collection still has to find it again.
- Counts come from `countCollection`, so the admin list and the storefront cannot disagree about what a rule resolves to. This is where a rule matching nothing should be noticed.
- PATCH writes only supplied keys, keeping `undefined` ("not changing") distinct from explicit `null` ("clear it"). Collapsing them means renaming a collection also wipes its image.
- DELETE relies on the FK cascade rather than a second statement that could fail after the parent is gone.

**Verification**

- Result: PASS — 23 tests, 0 failing
- Live auth gate: `GET /api/admin/collections` → **401**, `POST` → **401**
- Live database probe:
  - duplicate slug → `cause.code 23505`, constraint `collections_slug_unique` → route returns 409
  - manual collection delete → `collection_products` rows went **1 → 0**, cascade confirmed
- Build: `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors in this module

ticket.description:
## Task

The two admin operations CRUD alone cannot express.

- `PUT /api/admin/collections/:id/products` — replace the manual member list with an ordered array of product ids. Whole-list replace, not per-row add/remove: the order IS the data, and incremental edits make position arithmetic the client's problem.
- `PUT /api/admin/collections/discover-order` — accepts an ordered array of collection ids and rewrites `discoverOrder` in one transaction, so the rail cannot be observed half-reordered.

Rejects: member ids that are not real products; manual operations against a `kind='rule'` collection; duplicate ids in either array.

Both bust the public cache.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 4. Depends on the admin CRUD route.

The transaction on reorder is the point — a per-row update loop leaves the rail in an order that never existed if it fails halfway.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `6df8873e` — feat(api): manual membership and Discover ordering

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/collections.ts` — added `PUT /discover-order` and `PUT /:id/products`.
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/collection-membership.test.ts` — 13 tests.

**Route registration order is load-bearing.** `PUT /discover-order` is registered **above** `/:id/products` and `/:id`. **Both operations are transactional, for different reasons**
- **Reorder**: a per-row update loop that fails halfway leaves the rail in an order that never existed and nobody chose — worse than either the old order or the new one.
- **Membership**: clear-and-reinsert inside one transaction, so a collection is never observable as empty midway through a reorder.

ticket.title: Web - Discover chips become links to collections
ticket.description:
## Task

Re-point `DiscoverChips.tsx` from the style vocabulary to the collections endpoint, and turn each chip from a filter toggle into a link to `/collections/$slug`.

This is the behaviour change the whole feature exists for. A chip that toggles `styles` structurally cannot express Bestseller or Set of 2/3 — the payload is typed to a style id. Mesonart's own chips are `<a href="/collections/...">`, measured 2026-08-05.

Keep:

- the count under the label
- the empty-collection cull (the API already drops them)
- the round 80px chip, the hover lift, the scroll rail and its arrows

Change:

- `onSelect(styleId)` → a `<Link to="/collections/$slug">`. `aria-pressed` goes; the chip for the collection you are on gets `aria-current="page"`, which is now the truthful attribute.
- `chipArtScale()` applies ONLY when the image is the matted product fallback. Read `imageIsMatted` from the API rather than inferring it — an admin-uploaded image scaled by the matting factor is cropped into wrongly.

Drop the `activeStyle`/`onSelect` props and the route wiring that fed them in `routes/posters/index.tsx`.

## Context

Feature: curated-collections, Phase 5. Depends on GET /api/collections.

`DiscoverChips.tsx` carries a long doc comment explaining why selection went through the route's filter handler — router.tsx overrides TanStack's search serialisation, so a hand-built search object blank-pages the route. That reasoning dies with the toggle, since a link to a path carries no search at all. Update the comment; do not leave it describing behaviour the file no longer has.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `1f1e46da` — feat(web): Discover chips link to collections instead of toggling a style

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/product/DiscoverChips.tsx` — `<Link to="/collections/$slug">` replaces the toggle button; props are now `collections` + `activeSlug`.
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `productsApi.collections()` now hits `/api/collections?discover=true` and returns `slug`, `title`, `imageIsMatted`.
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` — chip wiring removed; the rail takes no handler.
- `packages/web/tests/components/product/DiscoverChips.test.tsx` — rewritten, 17 tests.

**The dependency was inverted, and it mattered.** #469 was ordered before #470, but a typed `<Link to="/collections/$slug">` **cannot compile** until that route exists — TanStack derives the union of valid paths from `routeTree.gen.ts`. Two errors, ~40 lines of union in each. So #470's route was built first and committed first (`b79bfe3d`), and this commit landed on top. Worth remembering for any future ticket that adds a link before its destination.

**`routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by the dev server, not by a script.** There is no `routes:generate` in `package.json`; starting `npm run dev` in `packages/web` regenerates it. Typecheck fails confusingly until that happens.

**Semantics changed deliberately**
- `aria-pressed` → `aria-current="page"`. The first described a button that could be un-pressed; these navigate.
- `chipArtScale` now applies **only** when `imageIsMatted`. Product `main` images sit on a mat at a fixed fraction of the longest side and the circle must cut inside the artwork; an admin upload has no mat and the same factor crops into it.
- The long module comment about routing selection through the route's filter handler is deleted, not edited. It documented why a hand-built search object blank-pages the route — true, and irrelevant to a link that carries no search at all. Leaving it would have described behaviour the file no longer has.

ticket.description:
## Task

Make collection pages findable.

- Per-collection `head()`: title from `seoTitle` falling back to `title`, description from `seoDescription` falling back to `description`, canonical at `/collections/<slug>`, OpenGraph image from `imageUrl` or the representative product.
- Add active collections to `packages/api/src/routes/sitemap.ts`.

Inactive collections must appear in neither. They 404, and a sitemap entry pointing at a 404 is worse than no entry.

## Context

Follow the `head()` block in `routes/posters/index.tsx` — it already builds a canonical URL and the twitter/og tag set.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `3c268bfc` — feat(web): collection SEO and sitemap entries

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/sitemap.ts` — active collections queried and emitted.
- `packages/web/app/routes/collections/$slug.tsx` — `og:image` added to the head (title/description/canonical landed with #470).
- `packages/api/tests/routes/sitemap-collections.test.ts` — 5 tests.

**Decisions**
- **Separate query, not a join.** Joining collections to products would tie a collection's presence in the sitemap to its products', so deactivating one collection would drag its products out with it. A test asserts two selects rather than one.
- **`isActive` is the whole filter.** An inactive collection 404s (#466), and an entry pointing at a 404 is worse than no entry — search engines read it as a signal about the site, not about the one URL.
- **Priority 0.85**: above products (0.8), below `/posters` (0.9). A collection is a curated entry point into the catalogue, not the catalogue.

https://chobii.art/collections/plaster-and-texture-art

| title | Pop Art \| chobii.art | Best Sellers \| chobii.art |
| description | the collection's own copy | the collection's own copy |
| canonical | `https://chobii.art/collections/pop-art` | `…/best-selling` |

The descriptions come from the seeded rows, so Best Sellers reads "Ranked by units actually sold on settled orders, not by editorial pick" rather than boilerplate — which is both true and the thing worth ranking on.

## Task

`/admin/collections/new` and `/admin/collections/$id` — one form, both modes.

Fields: title, slug (suggested from the title, editable, checked for collision before submit), subtitle, description, image URL, active, show-in-discover, SEO title and description.

ticket.title: Chrome - All Art opens the filter mega menu (mesonart parity)
ticket.description:
## Task

Our styles row's **All Art** is a bare `<Link to="/posters">` (`Header.tsx:402-409`). Mesonart's is the entry point to a full-width mega panel that opens the site's whole filter vocabulary in one view.

Measured on mesonart.com/collections/artworks (2026-08-05, desktop 1566px):

**Mechanism**
- `<details>` whose `<summary>` carries `data-link="/collections/artworks"` — pointer **hover** sets `open`, a **click** still navigates to the collection.
- Panel is `.mega-menu` `position:absolute`, full viewport width, white; the inner `.mega-menu__container` starts `invisible` and animates open on `padding 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.6, 0, 0.4, 1)` — the sheet grows downward rather than sliding.
- Content is lazy: for the first ~400ms the panel shows five grey skeleton blocks where the columns land, then the real links swap in.
- The rest of the page dims behind the open panel; it closes on mouse-leave.

**Layout** — `.mega-menu__list` is `display:grid`, `grid-template-columns: 4fr 1fr`, `gap: 24px`, `padding: 12px <page-gutter> 56px`. The 4fr track holds five link columns; the 1fr track holds two promo image cards.

**Columns (theirs → ours)**
| # | mesonart heading | mesonart contents | our source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | All Artworks › | 8 monthly drops (New Art-202607 …) + All Art | no drop entity here — use All Art / New In / Best Sellers, the row-1 destinations `Header.tsx` already defines |
| 2 | Style › | 11 styles | `STYLE_OPTIONS` → `?styles=<id>` |
| 3 | Subject | 13 subjects | `SUBJECT_OPTIONS` → `?subjects=<id>` |
| 4 | Orientation | 6 orientations | `ORIENTATION_OPTIONS` → `?orientation=<id>` (single, not a list) |
| 5 | Color | 14 colors | `COLOR_OPTIONS` → `?colors=<id>` |

Every axis is already accepted by `/posters` (`routes/posters/index.tsx:236-245`), so this is links over existing filters — no new API, no new route.

**Type** — headings 16px / weight 500 / black / `letter-spacing: -0.4px` / capitalize; headings 1 and 2 carry a chevron-right and are themselves links. Options 14px, `rgb(159,159,159)`, line-height 21px, 8px bottom padding, hover runs an underline wipe on `background-size 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.3, 1, 0.3, 1)`.

**Promo cards** — right-hand column, two image cards: a 4:3 card with a caption and a trailing arrow, then a square card. Feed both from `CATEGORY_TILES` (`app/lib/homeCategories.ts`), which already pairs a curated image with a real facet value and a group — no invented promotion, same rule that kept the sale strip out of this feature.

## Context

**Decisions taken with the user (2026-08-05)**
1. **Hover opens it**, matching mesonart, and the trigger still navigates on click. This is a deliberate departure from #416, where hover-open was rejected for the sort pill. Accepted cost: no keyboard path to open the panel — the user asked for the mesonart behaviour without keyboard shortcuts. Every link inside stays a real `<a>`, so the panel is still reachable with a mouse and readable to a screen reader once open; keep Escape and outside-click closing it.
2. **Five columns, copied from mesonart**, promo cards included, same open animation and hover effects.
3. **Desktop only.** The mobile drawer's own All Art accordion is a follow-up ticket.

**Constraints**
- Options come from `@chobii/shared` — never a hardcoded list. Hardcoding is what #395 ended and what `Header.structure.test.tsx` pins.
- The panel must not be a child of `<header>`: the header sets `backdrop-blur`, which establishes a containing block and collapsed a fixed overlay to zero height in #348. It belongs in the nav-rows block, which is already a sibling.
- The nav rows are `sticky top-16` and publish `--chrome-offset` through `useChromeOffset` (#401 / #421). The panel is an overlay and must NOT enter that measurement, or the collection toolbar jumps down by the panel's height every time it opens.
- Column 1's `All Art` entry passes `search` wholesale so it clears any active facets, the same way row 1's entries do.

**Files**
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx:402-409` — the trigger
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/AllArtMegaMenu.tsx` — new
- `packages/shared/src/constants/facets.ts` — the four vocabularies
- `packages/web/app/lib/homeCategories.ts` — promo card source

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `2e29b27c` — feat(web): All Art opens the whole filter vocabulary, not a collection

**Files Changed**
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/AllArtMegaMenu.tsx` — new. Five columns generated from the shared vocabulary, promo column from `CATEGORY_TILES`, hover-open sheet on the measured curve.
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — trigger swapped in, styles row made a positioning context, scrim raised to header level, header opaque while the panel is open.
- `packages/web/tests/components/layout/AllArtMegaMenu.test.tsx` — new, 21 tests.
- `tests/e2e/all-art-mega.spec.ts` — new, 6 tests.

**Verification**
- Command: `cd packages/web && npx vitest run tests/components/layout`
  Result: PASS — 94 tests across 6 files (21 new; `Header.structure.test.tsx` still 25/25).
- Command: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/all-art-mega.spec.ts tests/e2e/header-reveal.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps`
  Result: PASS — 13 passed (23.4s), including the #401/#421 guards and a new assertion that opening the panel does not move the collection toolbar.
- Command: `cd packages/web && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`
  Result: 22 errors, all pre-existing and in unrelated files (`app/routes/track/index.tsx`, …). None in either file this ticket touched.
- Visual: screenshotted at 1440×1100 against the dev server with the panel open — five columns, promo cards, page dimmed behind.

**Deviations from the plan, and why**

1. **The unit test renders the component rather than asserting on its source.** The drafted step was a `readFileSync` string test. `SearchDrawer.test.tsx` already shows the better pattern — stub `@tanstack/react-router`'s `Link` — and the stub here folds `search` into the `href`, so every column's destination is asserted for real (`?styles=`, `?subjects=`, `?orientation=`, `?colors=`). Source assertions are kept only for the measured values a DOM test cannot see: the two cubic-beziers, the 4fr/1fr split, reduced motion.

2. **The E2E spec lives at `tests/e2e/`, not `packages/web/tests/e2e/`.** The ticket named a directory that does not exist; the root Playwright config's `testDir` is `./tests/e2e`.

3. **The scrim is rendered by `Header`, not by the panel.** It cannot live in the component: the nav-rows block carries a transform for its reveal, and a transform establishes a containing block for fixed descendants — exactly the collapse-to-zero-height of #348. The component reports its state up through `onOpenChange`; the header renders the scrim as a sibling of `<header>`, where the mobile drawer's scrim already lives.

4. **The header goes opaque while the panel is open.** Unplanned, found by looking at it: the bar is `bg-background/60` with `backdrop-blur`, so the scrim showed through and the chrome read as dimmed. mesonart's header stays white over its own panel.

5. **No skeleton state.** Theirs shows five grey blocks for ~400ms because Shopify renders the section on demand. Our vocabulary is already in the bundle, so a skeleton would be a delay we manufacture. Skipped deliberately.

**Known, and left for the owner**

The Subject column renders all of `SUBJECT_OPTIONS`, including `typography`, which nothing in the catalogue carries — that one option lands on an empty grid. It matches the existing header precedent (the styles row already renders all of `STYLE_OPTIONS` ungated) but not #452's home-tile rule, which hides a category nothing is filed under. Gating the panel on facet counts would mean the header fetching counts on every page: a design call, not a fix to slip in here.

`tests/e2e/home.spec.ts › hides a category nothing is filed under` fails — **pre-existing**. Verified by stashing this ticket's `Header.tsx` and re-running that single test on the clean tree, where it fails identically (`h3:has-text("Typography")` resolved to 1). Not caused by this work.

ticket.title: Guest wishlist persists locally and merges into the account on sign-in
ticket.description:
## Task

Saving a poster must not require an account. A signed-out visitor's hearts live in localStorage; when they sign in, that list merges into their account and the server becomes the source of truth.

This reverses one of the two deliberate decisions recorded at the top of `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` ("no `persist` middleware"). The reason it was written — a shared machine showing the *previous* user's hearts — still stands, so only the GUEST list is ever persisted; once `isAuthenticated === true` the persisted slice writes empty.

**Merge semantics**: union, never delete. Signing in adds the guest's ids to whatever the account already holds; it never removes an account id because the guest list lacked it. The local list is dropped after a successful merge — the server owns it from then on.

## Context

#417 just landed the tri-state `isAuthenticated` (`null` = the root route has not reported yet) and the shared in-flight promise. This ticket builds on that hook rather than replacing it:

- `setAuthenticated(false)` → guest. Today it clears `ids`; it must instead keep the rehydrated local ids and mark loaded, still making zero requests.
- `setAuthenticated(true)` → merge the local ids, then take the server response as the id set.
- `toggle()` while a guest → local only, no request, no rollback path.

**API**: `POST /api/wishlist/merge` with `{ productIds: string[] }`, returning the same `{ items }` shape as `GET /` so the client merges and loads in one round trip. Do the union in SQL like the existing POST does (`packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts:145`) — read-modify-write races two tabs against each other. Existing shape:

```sql
COALESCE(wishlist_product_ids,'{}') || ARRAY(
  SELECT DISTINCT x FROM unnest($ids::text[]) AS x
  WHERE NOT COALESCE(wishlist_product_ids,'{}') @> ARRAY[x]
)
```

**Persist gotcha**: Node 25 exposes an inert `localStorage` global that shadows jsdom's, and zustand's persist captures the storage object at module init — the stub has to go in `vi.hoisted` above the store import. `packages/web/tests/stores/cart-drawer.test.ts:18` has the working pattern.

**Existing test to reverse**: `tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts` asserts the store does NOT write to localStorage. That assertion becomes "persists the guest list, and writes nothing once signed in".

Related files: `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts`, `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts:2199`, `packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts`, `packages/api/tests/routes/wishlist.test.ts`, `packages/web/tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts`.

comments.text:

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts` — `POST /merge`, registered before `/:productId`; hydration extracted so merge and `GET /` return the identical shape
- `packages/api/tests/routes/wishlist.test.ts` — 8 merge cases
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `wishlistApi.merge(productIds)`
- `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` — persist (guest-only), guest-local toggle, merge-on-sign-in
- `packages/web/tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts` — guest saving, merge, and the two ordering regressions
- `packages/web/tests/components/product/WishlistButton.test.tsx` — pins that SSR renders the heart unsaved
- `packages/web/tests/setup.ts` — working `localStorage` for every suite

**Two bugs the unit tests could not have found — both caught in a real browser, both now pinned by tests**:
1. `setAuthenticated(true)` flipped the flag before rehydration finished. `partialize` writes an empty list the moment the store counts as signed in, so the stored guest list was wiped while zustand was still reading it and the merge sent nothing. The flip now waits on `persist.onFinishHydration`.
2. A guest is marked `isLoaded` (nothing to wait for), which sent the merge straight into `load()`'s already-loaded guard. Signing in now clears `isLoaded`.

**Decisions**:
- Merge is a **union, never a delete** — one device's list cannot remove what the account holds.
- `returning()` on the update, so the response reflects the column rather than the payload a concurrent tab never saw.
- Payload capped at 500 ids; the union is built from bound parameters, not string concatenation.
- A guest toggle is local and final — no request, so no rollback path.

**Verification**:
- API: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/wishlist.test.ts` — PASS (28 tests)
- Web: `bunx vitest run tests/stores tests/components` — PASS (50 files, 1057 tests)
- Typecheck: 0 errors in touched files (web has 22 pre-existing admin-route errors, unchanged)
- Browser, live dev server + Postgres: guest saves 2 posters → **0** `/api/wishlist` requests, survives a reload, no hydration errors; registers → `POST /api/wishlist/merge` fires → both hearts come back filled from the account and localStorage is emptied.

**Note**: the API unit tests mock `db`, so the union SQL itself is only exercised by that browser run.

ticket.title: Database Schema - reviewMedia table, enums, relations and migration
ticket.description:
## Task

Add a media-agnostic `reviewMedia` table so reviews can carry customer photos AND videos. `mediaType` enum from day one means video is additive later rather than a migration rewrite.

Media has no moderation status of its own — it inherits the parent review's `status`. `processingStatus` tracks the transcode pipeline only (`processing` | `ready` | `failed`), not moderation.

## Context

ticket.title: Media Infrastructure - video validation, ffmpeg processing and Docker image
ticket.description:
## Task

Teach the storage layer about video and add an ffmpeg wrapper that can probe a customer upload, normalise it to a web-playable H.264/AAC MP4, and extract a poster frame.

Customer phone uploads are HEVC `.mov`, which Chrome and Firefox will not play — normalising is not optional.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Media Infrastructure

- `packages/api/src/lib/storage.ts:513` `isValidImageType` is the pattern; video needs a **sibling**, not a widened allowlist — different size caps and a different downstream path
- `StoragePaths` at `storage.ts:49`; presign helper already exists at `storage.ts:410` (currently unused)
- `packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts` is `sharp` and cannot touch video
- Dockerfile api stage is `oven/bun:1-slim` (line 47) — Debian, so `apt-get install -y ffmpeg` works
- **Local dev on macOS needs `brew install ffmpeg`.** Provide a clear startup error, not a stack trace, when the binary is absent
- Shell out to `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` via `node:child_process`; do not add a wrapper dependency

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `67b440d4` - feat(api): ffmpeg video processing and review media storage limits

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/lib/storage.ts` - `isValidVideoType` (sibling of `isValidImageType`, not a widened allowlist), `REVIEW_MEDIA_LIMITS` (image 10MB; video 200MB / 60s), `StoragePaths.REVIEW_MEDIA` prefix + `StoragePaths.reviewMedia(reviewId, filename)` key builder
- `packages/api/src/lib/video-processing.ts` - NEW. `isFfmpegAvailable`, `assertFfmpegAvailable`, `probeVideo`, `transcodeToMp4`, `extractPosterFrame`, `VideoProcessingError`
- `packages/api/tests/lib/storage-video.test.ts` - NEW, 15 tests
- `packages/api/tests/lib/video-processing.test.ts` - NEW, 9 tests against the real binaries
- `packages/api/tests/lib/storage.test.ts` - existing StoragePaths invariant updated for the key builder
- `Dockerfile` - `apt-get install ffmpeg` in the `api` stage only

**Summary**:
Shells out to ffmpeg/ffprobe with `execFile` from `node:child_process` — no wrapper dependency added. Every function rejects with `VideoProcessingError` carrying the tail of ffmpeg's stderr (2000 chars), which the worker persists on `reviewMedia.processingError`. A missing binary produces an actionable message ("macOS: `brew install ffmpeg`") rather than a raw ENOENT stack trace.

Transcode is `libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 26 -vf scale='min(1280,iw)':-2 -c:a aac -b:a 128k -movflags +faststart`, plus `-pix_fmt yuv420p` since phone footage is sometimes 4:2:2 or 10-bit that Chrome will not decode.

**Decisions worth noting**:
1. The test fixture is generated at runtime by ffmpeg's own synthetic sources, so no binary blob is committed. It is deliberately **mpeg4 video + mp3 audio** rather than the plain `testsrc` in the ticket sketch: the sketch's video-only H.264 fixture would have made the "emits h264 + aac" assertion pass trivially (no audio stream to convert, and the source already h264). Encoding the fixture in codecs the normaliser must convert *away from* makes the assertion prove real work.
2. `StoragePaths.reviewMedia` is a function on an object whose other members are string prefixes, which broke the existing `storage.test.ts` invariant "all values are strings ending with /". That test now skips function members and the prefix invariant is preserved for the string constants; a `REVIEW_MEDIA: 'reviews/'` prefix was also added. No production code iterates `StoragePaths` (verified by grep).
3. Keys are sanitised so customer filenames cannot escape their prefix: unsafe chars collapse to `_`, dot runs collapse to a single dot (killing `..` traversal), leading dots/dashes stripped.
4. `extractPosterFrame` checks the output is non-empty — ffmpeg exits 0 while writing nothing when the `-ss 00:00:01` seek lands past the end of a very short clip.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/lib/storage-video.test.ts tests/lib/video-processing.test.ts tests/lib/storage.test.ts` (from `packages/api`)
- Result: PASS — Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests **136 passed (136)**, 0 skipped
- The video suite ran the real binaries (ffmpeg 8.1.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin) — it did **not** skip; 9 tests, ~495ms of actual transcode/probe work. Named passes include `isFfmpegAvailable > returns false when PATH is emptied`, `probeVideo > reports duration, dimensions and codecs`, `transcodeToMp4 > normalises to h264 + aac while preserving duration and dimensions`, `extractPosterFrame > writes a jpeg poster frame at the source dimensions`.
- Typecheck: `bunx tsc --noEmit` → 4 errors, all in `src/routes/reviews.ts` (another agent's concurrent in-flight work, untouched here). Zero errors in `storage.ts` or `video-processing.ts`.

**Scope note**: `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts` was deliberately not touched — concurrent agent owns it. Nothing wires these helpers into a route yet; that is downstream work.

ticket.title: Media Infrastructure - BullMQ review-media transcode queue and worker
ticket.description:
## Task

Async transcode so submitting a review is never blocked on ffmpeg. The review saves immediately at `pending` with its media at `processing`; the worker normalises the video, uploads the MP4 and poster frame, and flips the row to `ready`.

A failed transcode marks that media row `failed` and drops it from every read surface. It must never fail the review.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Media Infrastructure
Depends on: reviewMedia schema, ffmpeg wrapper

- Model on `packages/api/src/queues/ai-generation.ts` — Queue + Worker + QueueEvents, `createRedisConnection()` for the worker per BullMQ guidance (`lib/redis.ts:39`)
- **Worker concurrency must be 1.** This box runs 13+ concurrent agent sessions on 8 cores; an unbounded transcode pool starves every other session. Make the concurrency an env var defaulting to 1
- Images skip the queue entirely — `uploadOptimizedImage` (`storage.ts:170`) already handles them synchronously
- Clean up temp files in a `finally`, including on the failure path

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:

**Commit**: `de562ff0` - feat(api): async review media transcode queue

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/queues/review-media.ts` (new) - Queue, exported `processReviewMediaJob`, `startReviewMediaWorker`, `enqueueReviewMediaJob`, `closeReviewMediaQueue`
- `packages/api/src/index.ts` - starts the worker outside tests, closes the queue on SIGTERM/SIGINT
- `packages/api/tests/queues/review-media.test.ts` (new) - 10 tests

**Summary**:
getFile(sourceKey) -> temp dir -> probeVideo -> duration + dimension guard -> transcodeToMp4 + extractPosterFrame (poster taken off the normalised copy) -> two uploadFile calls (`<base>-web.mp4`, `<base>-poster.jpg`, never clobbering the original) -> row set to `ready` with url, posterUrl, thumbnailUrl, durationSeconds, width, height, sizeBytes.

Failure path marks only that media row `failed` with a collapsed/truncated processingError (ffmpeg stderr tail preferred) and never rethrows, so the review is untouched — asserted in the test by checking `db.update` is only ever called with the `reviewMedia` table. Scratch dir removed in `finally` on both paths, verified against the real filesystem (probe's input path -> `existsSync(dir) === false`).

Concurrency: `REVIEW_MEDIA_CONCURRENCY`, default 1, garbage/0/negative falls back to 1. `attempts: 1` — retrying ffmpeg on the same bad bytes only burns CPU.

**Verification**:
