ticket.title: Backend API - review media presign and complete upload endpoints
ticket.description:
## Task

Two endpoints that let a review author attach media. Uploads go **direct to R2** via a presigned PUT — 200MB video cannot route through Hono.

`POST /api/reviews/:reviewId/media/presign` validates ownership, mime and declared size, then returns a presigned URL plus the object key. `POST /api/reviews/:reviewId/media/complete` records the `reviewMedia` row; images land `ready`, videos land `processing` and enqueue a transcode job.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Backend API
Depends on: reviewMedia schema, storage limits, transcode queue

- `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts` is already 612 lines. Put media endpoints in a new `packages/api/src/routes/review-media.ts` and mount it alongside `reviewsApp` in `packages/api/src/index.ts` (reviewsApp is mounted at index.ts:138)
- `getPresignedUploadUrl` already exists at `packages/api/src/lib/storage.ts:410`
- Auth: `requireAuth`; only the review's own author may attach media, and only while the review is still `pending`
- Cap media per review at 5. Hard-fail the 6th rather than silently dropping it
- Follow the Hono + zValidator + `c.json` error shape used throughout `routes/reviews.ts`

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `62cfe2b3` — feat(api): presigned review media upload endpoints

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/review-media.ts` (new) — presign + complete endpoints
- `packages/api/src/index.ts` — mounted `reviewMediaApp` at `/api/reviews`
- `packages/api/tests/routes/review-media.test.ts` (new) — 32 tests

**Summary**:
- `POST /api/reviews/:reviewId/media/presign` — requireAuth, exact author match (not `canAccess`: staff have no business attaching photos to a customer's review), review must still be `pending`. Resolves mime against `REVIEW_MEDIA_LIMITS` and applies the matching byte cap (10MB image / 200MB video), counts existing media and 409s at 5, then returns `{ uploadUrl, key, contentType, mediaType, maxBytes, expiresInSeconds }`. No row is created — an abandoned upload leaves only an unreferenced object.
- `POST /api/reviews/:reviewId/media/complete` — re-validates all of the above (the two calls are minutes apart), inserts the `reviewMedia` row, invalidates the `reviews:` cache keys, returns 201.
  - image → `processingStatus: 'ready'`, `thumbnailUrl = url`, nothing enqueued
  - video → `processingStatus: 'processing'`, `thumbnailUrl: null`, exactly one `reviewMediaQueue.add('transcode', { mediaId, sourceKey })`

**Decisions worth recording**:
- **Presign returns no `mediaId`.** The ticket's test sketch asked for one, but its own implementation sketch creates the row at `complete`. The row lifecycle won; presign returns `{ uploadUrl, key }` and the id comes back from `complete`.
- **Key ownership is enforced at `complete`.** `key` is client-supplied; without a prefix check against `StoragePaths.reviewMedia(reviewId, …)` a caller could point a media row at any object in the bucket, including another customer's upload. Two tests cover this (400).
- **Mime gate uses `REVIEW_MEDIA_LIMITS.*.types`, not `isValidImageType`.** The latter also admits `image/gif`, which the limits table deliberately excludes — an animated gif has no transcode path and would render as a still first frame on some clients.
- **Local extension map instead of `getExtensionFromContentType`.** That helper only knows images and falls back to `'jpg'`, which would key an `.mp4` as `.jpg`; the transcode worker recomputes derivative keys from the source key, so the mistake would follow the file to playback. `video/quicktime` keeps `.mov` (test asserts this).
- **Hono middleware scoping verified empirically** before mounting: a third `app.route('/api/reviews', …)` whose sub-app does `use('*', requireAuth)` does NOT leak onto the public `GET /api/reviews/:reviewId`. Confirmed with a standalone probe (anon GET → 200, anon POST presign → 401), then by the reviews suite still passing.
- **Test harness mocks db/auth/storage/redis/queue and imports the route directly**, following `tests/routes/wishlist.test.ts` rather than the try/catch-into-null pattern in `tests/routes/reviews.test.ts` — that pattern makes every assertion pass vacuously when the DB is unreachable, which is exactly the state a new route's first run is in. Mounting is asserted against `src/index.ts` source text so the suite never has to boot a pool.

**Verification**:

ticket.title: Backend API - site-wide review list, media feed, and media on existing reads
ticket.description:
## Task

The read side every new surface depends on:

- `GET /api/reviews` — all approved reviews, paginated, newest first, each with its product (title, slug, image) and its ready media. This is the gap the `/reviews` page and the home strip both need.
- `GET /api/reviews/media` — flat feed of ready media for the PDP wall, optionally filtered by `productId`.
- Media embedded on the existing product-scoped list and single-review reads.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Backend API
Depends on: reviewMedia schema

- `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts`: `reviewsApp.get("/stats")` at :380 must stay registered **before** any `/:reviewId` route or "stats" parses as a review id. The same trap applies to a new literal `/media` segment — register it before `/:reviewId`
- Reuse `REVIEW_CACHE_PREFIX` + `getCached`/`setCached` + `CACHE_TTL_REVIEWS`
- **Bump the cache key version** on the product-scoped list, or deployed nodes serve media-less payloads from warm cache
- Only `processingStatus = 'ready'` media is ever returned. `processing` and `failed` are invisible to the public
- Reuse the existing `listReviewsQuerySchema` page/pageSize shape

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `73dd3d59` — feat(api): site-wide review list and media feed endpoints

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts` — two new read endpoints, shared media helper, media embedded on the two pre-existing reads, cache key bump
- `packages/api/tests/routes/review-feed.test.ts` — new, 22 tests

**Summary**:
- `GET /api/reviews` — all approved reviews, paginated, newest first, each with `product { id, title, slug, imageUrl }` (imageUrl via `mainImage()`, not `images[0]`) and `media[]`. Inner-joins products, so a review whose product is gone is not showable.
- `GET /api/reviews/media` — flat feed of ready media, each row carrying `reviewId`, `rating`, `productId`. `?productId=` filters; a malformed uuid is a 400 rather than a silently unfiltered feed. Capped at `MEDIA_FEED_LIMIT = 60` since neither consuming surface paginates.
- `media[]` embedded on `GET /api/products/:productId/reviews` and `GET /api/reviews/:reviewId`. On the single read it is fetched *after* the visibility gate.
- One shared `fetchMediaByReview()` backs all four paths: a single `inArray` query per page filtered to `processingStatus = 'ready'`, ordered by `sortOrder`. `processing`/`failed` are never public. A test asserts exactly 3 selects for a 3-review page, so an N+1 regression fails the suite.

**Decisions worth recording**:
- Cache key is `all:v1:${page}:${pageSize}:${sortBy}`, not the sketched `all:v1:${page}:${pageSize}`. `listReviewsQuerySchema` carries `sortBy`, so a key without it serves "highest" out of the "newest" entry.
- Bumping the product list key to `product:v2:` required moving `invalidateProductReviewCaches` with it — the old pattern `product:${id}:*` would have matched nothing and stale entries would have lived out the full TTL. That function now also clears the site-wide list, media feed and catalogue stats, which a review edit/deletion equally moves.
- Route order: `/stats` → `/media` → `/` → `/:reviewId`. Both literals have a test asserting they still resolve.
- Tests mock the db (reviews.order_item_id is NOT NULL behind an FK, so a real review needs a whole order chain) but assert the *rendered* WHERE clauses via `PgDialect().sqlToQuery()` — a handler that dropped the `approved` or `ready` filter would still return a plausible payload from a mock, so those two invisibility rules are read off the SQL rather than assumed.

ticket.title: Backend API - review media in the admin moderation queue
ticket.description:
## Task

Admins moderate media by moderating the review that carries it — there is deliberately no second queue. For that to be safe, the moderation payload has to actually show them what they are approving.

Add media to the admin review list and detail payloads, plus a delete-media endpoint so an admin can strip one bad photo without rejecting an otherwise good review.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Backend API
Depends on: reviewMedia schema, read helpers

- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts` and its tests at `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/reviews.test.ts`
- Admins see media at **every** `processingStatus`, including `processing` and `failed` — unlike the public reads. A stuck transcode should be visible in the queue, not invisible
- Deleting media removes the R2 objects too (`deleteFile` at `storage.ts:351`) — both the rendition and the poster frame
- Note the known gap: `services/ai-moderation.ts` is text-only, so this media is unscreened until a human looks at it

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `4ebfb8e6` - feat(api): review media in the admin moderation queue

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts` — media embedded on the list and detail payloads; new `DELETE /:reviewId/media/:mediaId`
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/review-media.test.ts` — 20 new tests (new file)

**Summary**:
- `withAdminMedia()` attaches `media[]` to a page of reviews in one grouped `inArray` query — never one per review — with **no** `processingStatus` filter. Admins see `processing` and `failed` rows with their `processingError`; the public reads keep their `ready`-only filter. A test reads the rendered WHERE clause so a handler that quietly re-added the public filter fails rather than returning a plausible payload.
- Admin media payload adds `processingStatus`, `processingError`, `sizeBytes` and `createdAt` over the public shape.
- `DELETE /api/admin/reviews/:reviewId/media/:mediaId` — lookup scoped to the review in the path (a mediaId on another review is a 404, not a cross-review delete), joins `reviews` for the productId. R2 objects for url, thumbnailUrl and posterUrl go via `Promise.allSettled` so an already-missing object cannot leave a row pointing at a dead URL. Keys are only derived inside the `reviews/` prefix, so a malformed row cannot escalate into deleting product imagery. The parent review's status/moderator/notes are untouched, and the product/all/media review caches are invalidated (mirrors `invalidateProductReviewCaches` in routes/reviews.ts, v2 key included).

ticket.title: Frontend - API client functions and hooks for review feed and media
ticket.description:
## Task

Client layer every new surface sits on: fetch functions for the site-wide review list and the media feed, the two-step media upload (presign then PUT to R2), and TanStack Query hooks with keys that invalidate correctly.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: backend read and upload endpoints

- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `catalogueReviewStats` at :291 is the existing precedent for a review call that lives here rather than in the hook file, because it is not product-scoped. The new site-wide calls belong here for the same reason
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useReviews.ts` — `reviewKeys` at :27, existing hooks `useReviews` (:149), `useReviewStats` (:165), `useCreateReview` (:184)
- The presigned PUT goes **straight to R2**, not through `getApiUrl()`. Do not attach auth headers to it — the signature is the auth, and an extra header breaks it
- There is no Vite `/api` proxy in this repo; calls need the absolute `getApiUrl()` base

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `1c2ac016` - feat(web): review feed client functions and media upload helper

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — new `reviewsApi` with `listAll(params?)` → `ReviewFeedResponse` and `mediaFeed({ productId })` → `ReviewMediaFeedItem[]`; exported types `ReviewMediaType`, `ReviewMediaProcessingStatus`, `ReviewMediaItem`, `ReviewMediaFeedItem`, `ReviewFeedItem`, `ReviewFeedResponse` (= `PaginatedResponse<ReviewFeedItem>`), `ReviewFeedParams`
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useReviews.ts` — `reviewKeys.feeds()/feed(page,pageSize)` and `reviewKeys.mediaFeeds()/mediaFeed(productId?)`; `useReviewFeed(page, pageSize = 20)`; `useReviewMediaFeed(productId?)`; `uploadReviewMedia(reviewId, file)`; `useCreateReview` now invalidates the two new prefix keys as well as the old ones
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useReviewFeed.test.tsx` — 19 tests, `fetch` stubbed (not `~/lib/api`), so the URLs and the R2 PUT shape are actually asserted

**Naming note**: the step-1 test sketch named `reviewsApi.listAll` / `reviewsApi.mediaFeed` while the step-3 sketch named `listAllReviews` / `reviewMediaFeed`. Went with the test-sketch names — step 2's expected failure is literally "listAll is not a function", so that is the contract. Downstream #485-#489 import `reviewsApi.listAll` / `reviewsApi.mediaFeed`.

**Design decisions**:
- `mediaFeed` unwraps the `{ items, total }` envelope to a plain array: the API caps the feed at 60 and never paginates it, so `total` is only ever `items.length`
- `ReviewMediaItem` is the shape embedded in every review read; `ReviewMediaFeedItem extends` it with the `productId` / `rating` / `reviewCreatedAt` that only the flat feed's join carries. Review cards get the former, the media wall the latter
- `mediaFeed()` keys on `'all'` rather than `undefined` — an undefined tail serialises to the same key as a missing one, so the site-wide strip and a product wall would collide
- The R2 PUT sends `Content-Type` and nothing else, with no `credentials`. Two tests pin this (`expect(putInit.headers).toEqual({...})` exactly, `credentials` undefined) because an extra header or a cookie ride-along changes what R2 hashes and returns 403

ticket.title: Frontend - photo and video upload in ReviewForm
ticket.description:
## Task

Let a customer attach up to 5 photos or videos when writing a review. Client-side validation rejects the obvious failures before burning a presign round trip; video uploads show that processing continues after submit rather than pretending the media is live.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the upload helper

- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewForm.tsx`, tests at `packages/web/tests/components/reviews/ReviewForm.test.tsx`
- Limits must match `REVIEW_MEDIA_LIMITS` on the server: images 10MB, video 200MB and 60s, 5 items total
- Duration cannot be checked client-side without decoding — read `videoElement.duration` from an object URL and reject over 60s before upload, but treat the server as the real gate
- Order matters: the review is created first (`useCreateReview`), then media uploads against the returned review id. A failed upload must leave the already-created review intact and surface a retry, not a lost review
- Revoke every object URL on unmount

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `7971b361` - feat(web): photo and video upload in the review form

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewMediaUpload.tsx` (new) - controlled picker, previews, client-side gate, object-URL lifecycle
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewForm.tsx` - two-phase submit, media-error state, retry
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewModal.tsx` - returns the created review id so uploads have a target
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/index.ts` - barrel exports
- `packages/web/tests/components/reviews/ReviewMediaUpload.test.tsx` (new) - 14 tests
- `packages/web/tests/components/reviews/ReviewForm.test.tsx` - +12 media tests, 34 total

**Summary**:
Client-side limits mirror `REVIEW_MEDIA_LIMITS` / `MAX_MEDIA_PER_REVIEW` exactly: images 10MB, video 200MB and 60s, 5 items per review. Duration is read from a detached `<video>` pointed at an object URL before any presign; an unreadable duration is allowed through and left to the server, which remains the real gate. Object URLs are revoked on item removal and on unmount (both tested).

Order of operations, the load-bearing behaviour: the review is created first via the existing `onSubmit`, which now resolves `{ id }`; only then does `uploadReviewMedia(reviewId, file)` run, serially. An upload failure can never lose a review — the form enters a distinct `media-error` state ("Your review was saved"), keeps every failed file listed with its error, and offers a per-item retry plus a "Try again" that re-uploads only failed items and never re-sends the review. Verified by test: after a failed upload `onSubmit` has been called exactly once, and after retry it is still once while `uploadReviewMedia` has run twice.

**Note for review**: `ReviewModal.tsx` was edited beyond the ticket's file list. It is the only mount point for ReviewForm and its submit handler discarded the response body, so without returning `{ id: body.review.id }` the picker would have had no upload target and the feature would be unreachable for #492's E2E. Change is 4 lines, no test file exists for that component, and no concurrent ticket owns it.

ticket.title: Frontend - /reviews page with aggregate header, plus nav, footer and sitemap links
ticket.description:
## Task

The destination page. Aggregate score band over a reverse-chronological list of every approved review, each linking back to the product it reviews. Linked from the header nav, the footer, and the sitemap — mesonart surfaces it in all three.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the client layer

- **`validateSearch` must coerce `page` to a number.** `packages/web/app/routes/router.tsx` overrides TanStack's search serialisation so every param arrives as a string; a bare `z.number()` throws and the route error-boundaries to a blank page
- Adding a route rewrites `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts`, which is **tracked, not gitignored**. Stay in one checkout and `git add` by explicit path
- Aggregate header reuses the suppression rule: render nothing below 10 approved reviews rather than rounding a thin sample into a marketing number. `GET /api/reviews/stats` already returns `averageRating: null` for that case — honour the null, do not coalesce it to 0
- Follow `packages/web/app/routes/wishlist.tsx` for route-file shape and `SectionBand` / `DisplayHeading` for the beige header band
- Header nav links live in `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` (desktop ~line 376 and mobile ~line 504 — both trees need the link); footer in `Footer.tsx`; sitemap in `packages/api/src/routes/sitemap.ts`

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `49663f67` — feat(web): reviews page with aggregate header and nav links

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/reviews.tsx` (new) — the /reviews route. Exports `Route`, `reviewsSearchSchema`, `MIN_REVIEWS_FOR_AGGREGATE`, `ReviewsAggregate`, `ReviewFeedRow`, `ReviewFeedList` so the pieces are testable without a live router
- `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts` — regenerated (21 lines added) by running `vite dev` briefly rather than hand-editing, so the file stays byte-identical to what the plugin produces
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — Reviews link in BOTH nav trees: desktop `<NavLink to="/reviews">` and mobile `<MobileNavLink to="/reviews">`
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Footer.tsx` — "Reviews & Ratings" in the Company column (this footer's customer-services column, alongside FAQs / Shipping / Returns)
- `packages/api/src/routes/sitemap.ts` — `/reviews` static entry, `changefreq: daily`, priority 0.6
- `packages/web/tests/routes/reviews.test.tsx` (new) — 15 tests

**Summary**:
Aggregate score band over a reverse-chronological feed of every approved review, each row linking back to `/posters/$slug`. Prev/next paging writes `?page=` through the router as real `<Link>`s. Reads go through `productsApi.catalogueReviewStats()` and `useReviewFeed(page, 20)` from the #484 client layer.

Two rules from the ticket are guarded by tests rather than by comments:

1. **`validateSearch` coerces.** `reviewsSearchSchema = z.object({ page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).catch(1) })`, applied through an explicit function so the test can call `Route.options.validateSearch({ page: '2' })` and get `{ page: 2 }`. `.catch(1)` also lands `'nonsense'`, `'0'`, `'-4'` and `'2.5'` on page 1 instead of error-boundarying the route.

2. **Aggregate suppression.** `ReviewsAggregate` returns `null` when `averageRating === null` OR `reviewCount < 10` — asserted by `container.innerHTML === ''`, plus an explicit assertion that no `"0.0"` is printed for the null case.

Unlike the other suites in `tests/routes/` these are real rendering tests, not source greps — route modules import cleanly into jsdom here. Only the three entry-point assertions are source-level, since "a link exists in three separate files" is a wiring fact.

ticket.title: Frontend - PDP review media wall with lightbox and video playback
ticket.description:
## Task

Mesonart's PDP runs a Loox photo-review wall below the tabbed content. Ours renders customer photos **and videos** from the same wall, opening into a lightbox that plays video inline and shows the review the media came from.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the media feed endpoint and client layer

- PDP is `packages/web/app/routes/posters/$slug.tsx`; the existing reviews block is `packages/web/app/components/product/ProductReviews.tsx` (section at :75, heading "Customer Reviews" at :85)
- Place the wall **above** `ProductReviews`, matching mesonart's order: media wall, then the written reviews
- Videos render `poster={posterUrl}` and only load on play — never `autoPlay`, never `preload="auto"`. A dozen autoplaying clips on a product page is a bandwidth and layout disaster on mobile
- The wall renders nothing when the feed is empty; it must not leave an empty heading behind
- Lightbox needs keyboard escape, arrow navigation, and focus trapping. Do not trigger a native dialog

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `3419af3f` - feat(web): PDP review media wall with video lightbox

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/product/ReviewMediaWall.tsx` (new) - media grid + portal lightbox
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/$slug.tsx` - mounts `<ReviewMediaWall>` directly above `<ProductReviews>`
- `packages/web/tests/components/product/ReviewMediaWall.test.tsx` (new) - 11 tests

**Summary**:
- Reads `useReviewMediaFeed(productId)` from the #484 client layer. Square-tile grid, 2 cols mobile / 3 sm / 6 desktop, images `loading="lazy"`.
- Video tiles: `poster` (posterUrl, falling back to thumbnailUrl), `preload="none"`, `muted`, `playsInline`, `controls={false}`, no `autoPlay`, with a play badge and a `0:12`-style duration chip. The lightbox video also keeps `preload="none"` so arrowing past a clip never fetches it — only pressing play does.
- Returns `null` when the feed is empty **or still loading**: no orphan heading, no skeleton that resolves to nothing (which would be a layout shift on most products).
- Lightbox is a `createPortal` overlay, not a native `<dialog>` — `showModal` puts the page in the top layer and blocks the e2e harness. Focus moves to the close button on open, Tab is trapped both directions, Escape closes and restores focus to the tile that opened it, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walk the wall (wrapping), click-outside closes via an `aria-hidden` backdrop that is deliberately not a tab stop.
- Review title/body/author beside the media come from `useReviews(productId, { sortBy: 'newest', page: 1, limit: 10 })` — filters chosen to be byte-identical to `ProductReviews`' so both share one cache entry — and gated with `enabled: openIndex !== null`. ticket.title: Frontend - site-wide floating review toast
ticket.description:
## Task

Mesonart runs a bottom-left toast that cycles recent reviews on every page. Ours does the same, mounted once in the root route, dismissible, and remembered for the session.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the client layer

- Mount in `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx` so it survives navigation and fetches once rather than per route
- **Suppressed on `/checkout`** and on any admin route — a social-proof popup over a payment form is a conversion and trust problem, not a feature
- Mobile: must sit **under** the cart drawer's z-index and clear of the sticky add-to-cart bar on the PDP. Check the drawer's z-index before picking one rather than guessing
- `sessionStorage`, not `localStorage` — dismissal lasts the session, not forever
- **`sessionStorage` needs a `vi.hoisted` stub in tests.** Node 25's inert `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` shadows jsdom's and throws `setItem is not a function`
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: no slide-in animation when it is set

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `947115d6` — feat(web): site-wide floating review toast

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewToast.tsx` (new) — the toast
- `packages/web/app/routes/__root.tsx` — mounted once, after the outlet, before the drawer
- `packages/web/tests/components/reviews/ReviewToast.test.tsx` (new) — 16 tests

**Summary**:

Bottom-left card, 4s opening delay, cycles every 8s over one page of `useReviewFeed(1, 10)`. Card is thumbnail (review media first, product image as fallback) + star row + one-line excerpt + author · product title + close button, linking to `/posters/$slug`.

The three constraints that were correctness rather than styling:

1. **Suppression before fetch.** `ReviewToast` reads the pathname, and `/checkout*` or `/admin*` returns null *before* `ReviewToastCard` — the component holding `useReviewFeed` — is rendered. That two-component split is the whole point: an early return inside one component cannot legally skip a hook, so a single-component version would still have fired the request. Tests assert `useReviewFeed` was **not called** on those routes, not merely that the DOM is empty. The same holds for an already-dismissed session.

2. **Z-index read, not guessed.** `CartDrawer.tsx` uses `z-40` (backdrop) / `z-50` (panel), so the toast is `z-30` and the drawer's scrim covers it. `bottom-24` on mobile to clear a PDP sticky add-to-cart bar (none exists in `routes/posters/$slug.tsx` today — the offset is there so adding one does not collide), `sm:bottom-6` above.

3. **`sessionStorage`, not `localStorage`** — key `chobii:review-toast-dismissed`, wrapped in try/catch for Safari private mode.

Reduced motion is read via `matchMedia` in JS rather than left to a `motion-reduce:` variant: the slide-in is a whole animation class, so the variant would have to override a keyframe mid-flight, and it would not be assertable. `animate-slide-in-from-left` is dropped entirely when the preference is set.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/web && bunx vitest run tests/components/reviews/ReviewToast.test.tsx`
- Result: PASS (16 tests, 16 passing, 0 failing)
```
 ✓ tests/components/reviews/ReviewToast.test.tsx (16 tests) 142ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```
- **Mutation-checked**: replacing `isReviewToastSuppressed` with `return false` fails exactly the 3 suppression tests (13 passed / 3 failed), so those assertions bite rather than passing vacuously. Restored after.
- Regression: `bunx vitest run tests/components/reviews tests/routes/reviews.test.tsx` → 184 passed; the 7 suites that reference `__root.tsx` or grep style tokens (security-headers, build, storefront-token-compliance, cart-drawer, typography, chrome-tokens, Header.structure) → 197 passed.
- Types: `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports **zero** errors in the three files touched. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` initially flagged `reviews[index % count]`; guarded with a real `if (!review) return null`, which also covers a refetch returning fewer rows than the current index. Remaining `app/routes/admin/**` errors are the pre-existing baseline, untouched.

**Note for the feature owner**: `components/reviews/index.ts` was deliberately not touched — another agent is working in that directory and `__root.tsx` imports the component by full path. Worth adding the barrel export in a later sweep.

ticket.title: Frontend - review media in the admin moderation UI
ticket.description:
## Task

Admins cannot moderate media they cannot see. Render each pending review's photos and videos in the moderation queue, with playback, per-item delete, and a visible transcode state.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the admin API changes

- `packages/web/app/routes/admin/reviews.tsx`
- Admins see **every** `processingStatus`, unlike the public surfaces. `processing` shows a spinner, `failed` shows the `processingError`. A transcode stuck for hours should be obvious in this queue, not silent
- Per-item delete calls `DELETE /api/admin/reviews/:reviewId/media/:mediaId` and must not change the parent review's status
- Deletion is destructive and removes the R2 objects. Use an inline confirm affordance — **not** `window.confirm`, which blocks the automation harness

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `d734a89d` — feat(web): review media in the admin moderation queue

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/admin/reviews.tsx` — new exported `ReviewMediaStrip` + `AdminReviewMedia` type, `deleteReviewMedia()` API fn, `media?: AdminReviewMedia[]` on `AdminReview`, strip wired into every `ReviewRow` preview cell, `handleMediaDeleted` on the page
- `packages/web/tests/routes/admin/review-media.test.tsx` — new, 21 tests

**Summary**:
The moderation queue now renders each review's attachments at **every** `processingStatus`, unlike the public surfaces which filter to `ready`:
- `ready` photo → thumbnail (falls back to full-size url when `thumbnailUrl` is null); `ready` video → `<video controls>` with its poster
- `processing` → spinner, and deliberately **no** play control — there is no playable rendition yet and a dead `<video>` reads as a bug
- `failed` → the `processingError` text verbatim, plus delete (a failed upload is exactly what gets cleaned up)

Per-item delete calls `DELETE /api/admin/reviews/:reviewId/media/:mediaId` with `credentials: 'include'` and **never** touches the parent review — no PATCH, no refetch. The page drops the item from local state; refetching would reorder or re-page the row out from under the moderator mid-decision, and the review's own status is not what changed.

Deletion is gated behind a **two-step inline confirm** (Delete → Confirm/Cancel), not `window.confirm` — the native dialog blocks the browser automation harness outright. A failed delete keeps the tile and shows an inline error rather than removing optimistically, which would lie about an object still sitting in R2.

**Verification**:

- Result: PASS (31 tests, 31 passing, 0 failing — 21 new in `review-media.test.tsx`, 10 pre-existing in `collections-list.test.tsx`)
- Output:
```

 ✓ tests/routes/admin/review-media.test.tsx (21 tests) 158ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```
- RED first: the same file ran 21 failed / 0 passed before the component existed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors in either touched file (40 lines of pre-existing baseline errors elsewhere, untouched).

**Notes**:
- Scope respected — nothing under `packages/api/` was modified (another agent is concurrently editing `review-media.ts` / `index.ts`).

ticket.title: Seed - attach photo and video media to approved reviews
ticket.description:
## Task

Give the new surfaces something true to render. Seed media onto the existing approved reviews so the PDP wall, the home strip and the toast are exercised against real rows rather than empty states.

## Context

Phase: Seed and E2E
Depends on: reviewMedia schema

- `packages/api/src/database/seed-orders-reviews.ts` created the 12 approved reviews across 9 products (#414), with the settled orders that authorise them. Extend that script; do not write a new one
- Reuse the room-mockup images the seed pipeline already generates (`seed-images.ts`, `lib/product-media.ts`) as review photos. Do not commit new binaries
- At least one **video** row so the wall, the lightbox and the admin queue all get exercised. Generate it with ffmpeg's own `testsrc` at seed time rather than committing an MP4
- Idempotent, like the rest of the seeds: re-running must not duplicate media
- Tests follow `packages/api/tests/database/seed-orders-reviews.test.ts`

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `8bb06017` - feat(db): seed photo and video media onto approved reviews

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/database/seed-orders-reviews.ts` — added `REVIEW_MEDIA_PLAN` fixture, pure `pickReviewPhotos()` selector, `buildSeedVideo()` and `seedReviewMedia()`; called at the end of `seedOrdersAndReviews()`
- `packages/api/tests/database/seed-review-media.test.ts` — new, 18 tests

**Summary**:
Five of the twelve approved reviews now carry media (8 photos + 1 video across 5 reviews), leaving seven without so the wall's empty-state branch stays reachable in dev.

- **ffmpeg absent**: logs a warning and skips the video half; photos still seed. Verified by running with `FFMPEG_PATH=/nonexistent/ffmpeg` → `image=8, video=0`.

ticket.title: E2E - review surfaces and media upload flows
ticket.description:
## Task

Feature-level Playwright coverage for everything this feature added: the `/reviews` page, the home strip, the PDP media wall and lightbox, the toast, and a signed-in review submission carrying a photo.

## Context

Part of feature: review-surfaces-parity
Phase: Seed and E2E
Depends on: every prior ticket

- `tests/e2e/`, following `wishlist.spec.ts` and `all-art-mega.spec.ts`
- `test.beforeEach` must `page.goto(path, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })` — the established pattern in this suite
- **Scope every selector to the desktop or mobile tree.** The same test ids exist in both; `page.locator('div.hidden.lg\\:block')` is the idiom used here. Unscoped selectors are the standard false result in this repo
- **Confirm the app under test is the real one.** Port `:5173` serves a different app and makes these specs pass vacuously. Verify against a known chobii marker before trusting a green run
- Video upload is not worth an E2E — the transcode is async and the assertion would be a sleep. Cover photo upload end to end and leave video to the queue unit tests
- The toast has a deliberate initial delay; wait on its selector rather than adding a fixed timeout

comments.author: mcp-client

**Commit**: `7f08bbd6` — test(e2e): review surfaces and media upload

- `tests/e2e/review-surfaces.spec.ts` — 14 tests, all passing
- `tests/e2e/review-media-upload.spec.ts` — written and type-clean, `test.fixme()`'d against #493

**Verification**

ticket.title: Bug - /account/orders/$id never renders; the order-list route swallows it
ticket.description:
## What happens

Every URL under `/account/orders/<anything>` renders the **order history list**, never the order detail page. Verified in a real browser against the running app with the signed-in customer storage state:

```
{"target":"/account/orders",                                       "url":".../account/orders?page=1",              "h1":"Order History","writeReview":0}
{"target":"/account/orders/CH-SEED-0006",                          "url":".../account/orders/CH-SEED-0006?page=1", "h1":"Order History","writeReview":0}
{"target":"/account/orders/b4a39113-cf0d-436f-b8d3-d7c115d09b8d",  "url":".../account/orders/b4a39...?page=1",     "h1":"Order History","writeReview":0}
```

The `?page=1` appended to every one of them is the list route's own `validateSearch` running — the parent route is what rendered.

## Root cause

`app/routes/_authed/account/orders.tsx` is a *leaf* page (`component: OrderHistoryPage`) but file-based routing makes it the **parent** of `orders.$id.tsx`. `routeTree.gen.ts` confirms it:

```ts
const AuthedAccountOrdersIdRoute = AuthedAccountOrdersIdRouteImport.update({
  getParentRoute: () => AuthedAccountOrdersRoute,
```

`OrderHistoryPage` renders no `<Outlet />`, so the child's component is never mounted. The list is what you get at every child URL.

The likely fix is to move the list to `orders.index.tsx` and leave `orders.tsx` as a pass-through layout (`<Outlet />`), or add an `<Outlet />` to the current component. Route-shape change — wants its own verification pass, not a drive-by.

## Blast radius

`orders.$id.tsx` is the **only** mount point of `ReviewModal` → `ReviewForm` → `ReviewMediaUpload`. So the entire customer-facing review-writing flow, including the photo/video attachment shipped in #485, has no reachable entry point in the app today. The API side is fine (`POST /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/review`, presign, complete all work when called directly).

Also worth noting: the order list's own "View Details" links point at `/account/orders/CH-SEED-0006` — the **order number** — while `GET /api/orders/:id` 400s on anything that is not a UUID. So even once the `<Outlet />` lands, the link target needs checking.

## Pre-existing, not introduced here

`main` has the same shape: `git show main:app/routes/_authed/account/orders.tsx | grep -c Outlet` → `0`, and `main`'s `routeTree.gen.ts` carries the same `getParentRoute: () => AuthedAccountOrdersRoute`.

It stayed invisible because every existing e2e test that touches the flow guards itself out — `tests/e2e/reviews.spec.ts` calls `test.skip()` when the "Write Review" button is not found, which is exactly the symptom.

## How it was found

Writing the E2E for #492. `tests/e2e/review-media-upload.spec.ts` is written against the real flow and is currently `test.fixme()`'d against this ticket; dropping the annotation is the acceptance test for the fix.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `bc63c02d` — fix(web): render the order detail route, and the review flow behind it
(the two file renames themselves landed a moment earlier inside `c2ef1792`, a concurrent agent's commit that swept up the staged `git mv`; the route ids, generated tree and everything else are in `bc63c02d`.)

**Root Cause**: `packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/orders.tsx` was a leaf page (`component: OrderHistoryPage`, no `<Outlet />`) that TanStack's flat file routing made the PARENT of `orders.$id.tsx`. The child's component never mounted, so every `/account/orders/<id>` URL rendered the LIST. `orders.$id.return.tsx` was caught the same way one level down, under `orders.$id.tsx`.

**Fix**: moved both leaves to index routes — `orders.index.tsx` and `orders.$id.index.tsx` — so the list, the detail and the return flow all parent directly to `_authed`. This matches the shape `admin/orders/{index,$id}.tsx` already uses in this repo; nothing had to become a layout. Verified live with the signed-in customer:

```
/account/orders                       -> "Order History | chobii.art"  h1: Order History      final: /account/orders?page=1
/account/orders/<uuid>                -> "Order Details | chobii.art"  h1: Order CH-SEED-0011 final: /account/orders/<uuid>
/account/orders/<uuid>/return         -> "Request Return | chobii.art" h1: Request Return     final: /account/orders/<uuid>/return
```

**Two further defects were behind it**, both hit by the acceptance spec once the route rendered, both fixed here:

1. `ReviewModal.handleSubmit` posted the review at a **relative** `/api/...` URL. The API is a separate origin in dev with no `/api` proxy, so the submit 404'd against the web app and the form showed "Failed to submit review". Now absolute via `getApiUrl()` (which is `''` in the production image, so same-origin still holds). Same fix applied to the review fetch in `handleEditReview`.
2. On success the page called `fetchOrder()`, which flips `isLoading` — and the loading skeleton `return`s **above** the `ReviewModal`, so the confirmation panel was unmounted the same tick it rendered and the dialog just vanished. `fetchOrder` now takes a `background` mode.

The note in the description about "View Details" linking by order number is **not** a defect: `GET /api/orders/:id` accepts an order number as well as a UUID.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/orders.index.tsx` — route id `/_authed/account/orders/`, `useSearch` from updated
- `packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/orders.$id.index.tsx` — route id `/_authed/account/orders/$id/`, absolute review fetch, background refetch
- `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts` — regenerated; all three order routes now `getParentRoute: () => AuthedRoute`
- `packages/web/app/components/reviews/ReviewModal.tsx` — absolute submit URL
- `packages/web/tests/routes/account-orders-routing.test.ts` — new regression test
- `tests/e2e/review-media-upload.spec.ts` — `fixme` removed, routing guard added, setup made worker-safe and duplicate-safe

**Regression test**: the sharpest assertion is deliberately general — it reads the generated tree and fails ANY route the generator gives children to while its module renders no `<Outlet />`. That guards the class of bug, not just this instance. Plus specific guards that `/account/orders/$id` is not nested under the list, that the detail module carries `ReviewModal` and none of the list's markers, and that `to="/account/orders"` still resolves.

**Verification**:
- Command: `cd packages/web && bunx vitest run tests/routes/account-orders-routing.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (8 tests, 8 passing)
```
 ✓ tests/routes/account-orders-routing.test.ts (8 tests) 6ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```
- Command: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review-media-upload.spec.ts --workers=1`
- Result: PASS (6 tests incl. 4 auth setup, 6 passing) — run twice consecutively from a canonical seed
```
  ✓  5 [chromium] › review-media-upload.spec.ts:297:3 › renders the order detail page, not the order history list (1.8s)
  ✓  6 [chromium] › review-media-upload.spec.ts:323:3 › carries the photo through and says it publishes after approval (2.1s)
  6 passed (1.4m)
```
- Database unchanged after each run: 12 approved reviews, 2 pending, 8 photos + 1 video = 9 `review_media`.
- Also ran `packages/web/tests/routes/` + `tests/build.test.ts`: 233 passing, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`home-tokens.test.ts`, `from-slate-700/80` on the untouched home route).

**Two environment hazards found, worth their own tickets:**
1. `./scripts/run-tests.sh e2e` **reseeds the real database**. It reports "PostgreSQL (port 5433)" — which is a *different app's* container — but `bun run seed` resolves `DATABASE_URL` from the root `.env` and hits `poster-app-postgres` on 5440, wiping and recreating orders + reviews mid-flight. Order ids changed under every run. Run this spec with `npx playwright test` directly to avoid it.
2. The seed writes a review per delivered **order item** while `GET /api/orders/:id` resolves an item's review by **(productId, userId)**, so `test-customer-001` holds *two* reviews for the one poster they bought twice — a violation of the API's own one-review-per-(product, customer) rule, and invisible because the map keeps only the last. The spec now works around it by borrowing only a review reported against exactly one item, but the seed should stop emitting the duplicate.

ticket.title: Wishlist page looks empty when every saved id has gone stale
ticket.description:
## Task

Reported from a real browser, signed out on :3001: the header badge shows the right number of saved items, but `/wishlist` renders nothing at all — no cards, and not the "Nothing saved yet" state either, so the page reads as broken.

The two numbers come from different places, and only one of them is filtered:

- the badge is `ids.length` straight off the store — for a guest, whatever is in localStorage;
- the page renders only the ids `POST /api/products/by-ids` returns, which filters `status = 'active'` and, more importantly, cannot return a product that no longer exists.

A guest's ids outlive the catalogue. The dev database gets reseeded and every product id changes; a product can also be deactivated or deleted after being saved. Every saved id then dangles, `products` is empty, `ids.length` is not zero, so `isEmpty` is false and `WishlistContents` renders an empty `ProductGrid` with no empty state and no explanation.

The `catch` in the fetch effect is silent for the same reason — a failed request also renders as a blank grid.

## Context

`packages/web/app/components/wishlist/WishlistContents.tsx` — the resolved list is `ids.map((id) => known[id]).filter(Boolean)`, and `isEmpty` is `isHydrated && ids.length === 0`. Neither notices that every id resolved to nothing.

**Fix scope**:
1. Prune ids the catalogue did not return from the GUEST list, once they have actually been asked for and not found — a dangling id is dead weight in localStorage and it is what makes the badge disagree with the page. Do NOT prune for a signed-in user: the server already filters, and a transient failure must not delete an account's saves.
2. When the list resolves to nothing but ids were saved, say so, rather than rendering a bare grid.
3. Surface a fetch failure instead of swallowing it, with a retry.

The existing test `quietly drops an id whose product has left the catalogue` covers the partial case and must keep passing; the missing case is all of them dangling.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `c2ef1792` - fix(web): explain an empty wishlist instead of showing the filter copy

**Root Cause**: the badge and the page count different things, and only one is filtered. The badge is `ids.length` off the store — for a guest, whatever localStorage holds. The page renders only what `POST /api/products/by-ids` returns. A guest's ids outlive the catalogue (a reseeded dev database changes every product id), so all of them can dangle at once: `products` is empty but `ids.length` is 3, `isEmpty` stays false, and `emptyState` was passed as `undefined` — so `ProductGrid` fell through to its own collection copy, "No products found. Try adjusting your filters", on a page with no filters. The screenshot showed exactly that.

**Location**: `packages/web/app/components/wishlist/WishlistContents.tsx`

**Fix**:
- Ids asked for and not returned are remembered (`gone`), so the effect stops re-asking, and dropped from a **guest** list via a new `dropMissing` store action — that is what stops the badge counting saves the page cannot show.
- **Never dropped for a signed-in user.** That list came from the server already filtered to live products, so an empty answer means the request failed; deleting an account's wishlist over a bad round-trip is unrecoverable. `dropMissing` enforces this itself rather than trusting callers.
- A failed lookup was silently swallowed and rendered as a blank grid; it now says "Could not load your saved items — they are still saved" with a **Try again** button.
- `emptyState` is now always supplied, so the collection copy cannot reappear here for any reason.

**Tests**: 3 component cases (all-stale explained + cleared, signed-in list untouched, retry after failure), 2 store cases for `dropMissing`, 1 E2E seeding a dead id into localStorage and asserting the filter copy is absent.

**Verification**:
- `bunx vitest run tests/stores/wishlist.test.ts tests/components/wishlist tests/routes/wishlist-page.test.ts` — PASS (43 tests)
- `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/wishlist.spec.ts --project=chromium --no-deps` — PASS (7)
- Browser, reproducing the reported state with three stale ids: page reads "Those posters are no longer available", the header badge drops back to no count, and the stored list is emptied.

**Note for the reporter**: your three saved ids no longer match anything in the dev catalogue, which is why they vanished — the database was reseeded after you saved them. Saving again now works; this fix makes the failure legible rather than silent.

work_sessions.summary: Stale guest ids now explained and pruned; failed lookup gets a retry; emptyState always supplied so the collection filter copy cannot appear. Commit c2ef1792.

ticket.title: Backend API - widen the review read shape with itemType, verified and product chip
ticket.description:
## Task

The Loox card carries three things our payload does not: the exact variant purchased ("Item type: 40''Hx 30''W / Stretch+Gold Frame"), a Verified badge, and a product chip with thumbnail, title and SKU.

Add all three to the shared review read shape so every surface gets them from one definition.

## Context

Part of feature: review-grid-loox-parity
Phase: Backend API

- `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts` already has a single shared media-select definition and an `attachMedia` helper explicitly written so no read can regress into an N+1. Follow that pattern exactly — one join, applied to all callers.
- `itemType` comes from the `orderItems` row the review already points at via `orderItemId`. Columns exist: `sizeLabel`, `frameName`, `frameType` (`packages/api/src/database/schema/orders.ts:77-81`). No schema change.
- `verified` is DERIVED, not stored. Every review is `orderItemId`-gated and that column is `notNull`, so it is true for all of them. Do not add a column.
- Product chip: title, slug, sku and a thumbnail from `products`. The list-all read already joins products for the link — widen that select rather than adding a second join.
- **Bump the cache key version.** The payload shape changes; warm nodes would otherwise serve cards with no chip and no item type. The prior feature bumped `product:` to `product:v2:` for exactly this reason.
- Affects three reads: `GET /api/reviews`, `GET /api/products/:productId/reviews`, `GET /api/reviews/:reviewId`. The flat media feed does not need it — the grid renders whole reviews now.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `d7ee35e1` - feat(api): carry item type, verified and product chip on review reads

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/reviews.ts` — shared card definitions (`reviewProductColumns`, `reviewOrderItemColumns`, `toItemType`, `toProductChip`, `toReviewCard`) beside the existing media select; applied to all three whole-review reads; cache keys bumped
- `packages/api/tests/routes/review-card-shape.test.ts` — new, 17 tests

- `packages/api/src/routes/review-media.ts`, `packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts` — duplicate invalidation patterns moved to the new versions

**Summary**:
- `verified: true` is derived in the mapper, not stored and not selected — `reviews.order_item_id` is NOT NULL behind an FK, so every row is a purchase. No schema change.
- `itemType` is returned as **parts** (`{ sizeLabel, frameName, frameType }`), per the ticket's preference — the separator/ordering is presentation, and a frameless purchase keeps its size with the frame fields null. Null overall when the order item is gone or carries none of the three.
- `product` chip is `{ id, title, slug, sku, imageUrl }`; `imageUrl` picked with `mainImage()` the way the product cards pick it. The raw `images` array never leaves the API.
- **No N+1.** The two list reads take one `leftJoin` on `order_items` for the whole page. The product-scoped list reuses the product lookup it already ran to decide its 404 rather than joining `products` down a page where every row is the same product — query counts per request are unchanged (4 / 3 / 2), and the tests assert the counts and read the JOIN condition itself.
- Media stays exactly as it was: still embedded, still `ready`-only on public reads. The flat media feed is untouched (tiles, not cards) and `media:v1:` is deliberately not bumped.
- **Cache**: `product:v2:` → `product:v3:`, `all:v1:` → `all:v2:`. `review-media.ts` and `admin/reviews.ts` hold copies of the same invalidation patterns; left on the old versions they would have matched nothing and moderation/media uploads would have silently stopped busting the lists.

ticket.title: Frontend - ReviewGrid masonry and the fused ReviewGridCard
ticket.description:
## Task

The structural correction. One card holds media AND text; one grid holds every review. This replaces the invented media-wall / written-list split.

Card anatomy, top to bottom, per `docs/design/mesonart/mesonart-reviews-page-loox.png`:
media slot (photo, or video with poster + play overlay, `+N` corner badge when the review has more than one) → author name + Verified check badge → date → star row → body text → "Item type:" line → product chip (thumbnail, title, SKU).

A review with no media renders the same card with the media slot omitted. That is the whole point — they are not different things.

## Context

Part of feature: review-grid-loox-parity
Phase: Frontend
Depends on: the widened read shape

- Reference screenshots: `docs/design/mesonart/mesonart-reviews-page-loox.png` (unfiltered, 6 columns) and `mesonart-pdp-reviews-loox.png` (product-filtered, 5 columns).
- `ReviewGrid` takes an optional `productId` — the PDP passes it, `/reviews` does not. One component, two filters, mirroring how Loox itself is deployed.
- **CSS `columns` masonry, not a JS layout pass.** No measuring, no layout dependency. Reading order goes down each column; that is what Loox does and it is acceptable for a review wall.
- The media slot MUST hold its aspect ratio before the image decodes, or the whole column reflows as images land. The `+N` badge and play overlay are absolutely positioned inside it.
- Video: `preload="none"`, `poster` set, never `autoPlay`. This was a hard requirement in #488 with a test asserting it — carry the assertion over, do not drop it.
- Reuse the lightbox already built for `ReviewMediaWall` rather than writing a second one.
- Do NOT delete `ReviewMediaWall` in this ticket — the PDP still imports it until the next one. Deleting here breaks the build midway.
- vitest gotcha: Node 25's inert localStorage/sessionStorage shadows jsdom's. Stub in `vi.hoisted` above the imports if you hit `setItem is not a function`.

ticket.title: API - PUT /api/wishlist to rewrite the order, permutation-guarded
ticket.description:
## Task

One endpoint that rewrites the wishlist's order.

`PUT /api/wishlist` takes `{ productIds: string[] }` and writes it to `user.wishlist_product_ids` — which is a `text[]` column on the user row, so the array order IS the order. No migration, no position column.

**The guard is the whole ticket.** A plain replace endpoint is a data-loss bug: a tab open since before an item was added on another device posts a stale list and silently drops it. So the write is accepted only when the incoming ids are a **permutation of the stored set** — same members, different order. A different set returns **409** carrying the current list, and the client refreshes rather than overwriting.

Same-set-different-order is exactly what a reorder is, so the guard rejects nothing legitimate.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-curation, Phase 1.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `228ecd33` — feat(api): reorder the wishlist, and actually return the stored order

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts` — `PUT /`, `reorderBodySchema`, and a fix to `hydrate()`
- `packages/api/tests/routes/wishlist-reorder.test.ts` — 14 tests

**A pre-existing bug this feature would have been blamed for**

The endpoint worked first try. Then the live probe showed the reorder returning **200 while `GET /api/wishlist` came back in the same order as before**.

Cause: `hydrate()` selected with `inArray(products.id, ids)` and **no ordering**. `inArray` places none, so the response was in whatever order the planner produced. The web store sets its `ids` from that response — which means a signed-in shopper's "saved order" was never their order at all. `WishlistContents.tsx` carries a comment saying items are "rendered in the order they were saved"; that was only ever true for guests, whose list lives in a localStorage array.

Dragging a card would have persisted correctly and then appeared to do nothing after a reload — and the reorder feature, not the six-month-old hydrate, would have taken the blame.

Fixed by sorting rows into array order in JS rather than with `array_position` in SQL: the miss case has to be handled anyway, since a product deleted from the catalogue leaves a dangling id with no row to sort, and dropping it is already this function's contract.

**The guard**

Accepts only a **permutation** of the stored ids. Permutation, not merely the same set — `[A, A, B]` shares a set with `[A, B]`, and de-duplicating silently would make the response disagree with what was written. A mismatch returns 409 carrying the current list so the client resyncs rather than overwriting.

Adding and removing stay on `POST`/`DELETE /:productId`, which mutate the array in place in SQL and cannot clobber a concurrent write. This endpoint is only for order.

**Live verification** against the running API, signed in as `test-admin`:

```
before: Synthetic Nature | Neural Dreams | Digital Cosmos
PUT  -> 200
after : Digital Cosmos | Synthetic Nature | Neural Dreams
order matches what was written: true

drop one   -> 409 (body carries all 3 current ids)
foreign id -> 409
duplicates -> 409
same order -> 200
```

**Verification**
- Command: `cd packages/api && npx vitest run tests/routes/wishlist-reorder.test.ts tests/routes/wishlist.test.ts`
- Result: PASS — 42 tests, 0 failing
- Build: `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean

ticket.title: Store - reorder action, optimistic, guest and signed-in
ticket.description:
## Task

A `reorder(from, to)` action on the wishlist store.

- Moves the id within `ids` and applies it immediately — the interaction has to feel like dragging, not like waiting.
- Signed in: `PUT /api/wishlist` with the new order. On failure, reload from the server rather than leaving the list disagreeing with storage.
- Signed out: nothing to call. The persisted slice writes localStorage and that is the whole of it.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-curation, Phase 1. Depends on the endpoint.

`packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` already distinguishes the two cases — `isAuthenticated` gates the API calls in `toggle`, and the `persist` middleware handles guests. Follow `toggle`'s shape exactly: it applies optimistically and rolls back on failure, and it is the precedent for this.

Watch the rollback: `toggle` restores the previous array. A reorder failure should re-fetch instead, because the server may have changed underneath — which is the 409 case the endpoint returns.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `77ca6b34` — feat(web): reorder action on the wishlist store

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` — `reorder(from, to)`
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` — `wishlistApi.reorder(productIds)`, carrying the response status on the thrown error so a 409 is distinguishable
- `packages/web/tests/stores/wishlist-reorder.test.ts` — 10 tests

**Indices, not ids.** Both callers — the drag handler and the move buttons — already know positions. An id-based signature would make them look one up only for the store to look it up again.

**The failure path differs from `toggle`'s, deliberately.** `toggle` rolls back to the previous array, which is correct when the server refused *one item*. A reorder is refused when **the list changed underneath** — that is exactly the 409 #500 returns — so the previous array is stale too, and rolling back would leave the client wrong in a second way. It reloads instead, and falls back to the previous array only if the reload also fails, because a stale usable list beats an empty one.

**Out-of-range indices are ignored, not thrown on.** A drop outside the list is an ordinary mouse event. A store that throws there would surface as an error boundary over a dropped card.

**Optimism is asserted directly** rather than assumed — one test holds the request open and checks the ids have already moved. "Applies eventually" and "applies immediately" are indistinguishable once the promise resolves, and only the second feels like dragging.

**Verification**
- Command: `cd packages/web && npx vitest run tests/stores/`
- Result: PASS — 95 tests across 4 suites, 0 failing
- Build: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean

The existing wishlist store tests (85) still pass unchanged, so the new action did not disturb `toggle`, `load`, `merge` or the guest persistence path.

The list must stay in the store's order throughout: `WishlistContents.tsx` already renders `ids.map(...)`, which is the contract to preserve.

Feature: wishlist-curation, Phase 2. Depends on the store action.

ticket.description:

A bar above the wishlist grid, **staff only**, turning the list into a curated collection.

- Reads the count: *"12 items — staging for a collection"*, with a line saying this is the admin's own wishlist and curating a second collection means clearing it. Better stated than discovered.

Feature: wishlist-curation, Phase 2. Depends on reordering, because the order is the entire value.

Clipboard: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is unavailable on insecure origins and in some browsers. Fall back to showing the ids in a selectable field rather than failing silently — a copy button that does nothing is worse than no button.

ticket.title: Bug - a late wishlist load() reverts a reorder made during it
ticket.description:
## The bug

`load()` in `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` sets `ids` unconditionally when it resolves. A reorder made while that request is still in flight is applied optimistically, then **overwritten** when the load lands — the shopper's move visibly undoes itself.

## How it was found

Not by a unit test. The E2E round trip in #504 failed repeatedly on `expect(staged[0]).toBe(initial[1])` even running **serially with one worker**, which ruled out contention. The move was being applied and then reverted by the page-mount `load()` completing afterwards.

The assertion now polls, which is correct for the test — the order does settle. But the polling is hiding a real, if narrow, product behaviour and that should not be mistaken for the bug being fixed.

## Why it was not fixed with #504

Guarding `load()` against in-flight writes means touching a store with 85 existing tests covering `toggle`, `merge`, guest persistence and the tri-state auth flag, at the end of a long session. A rushed concurrency change there is a worse trade than a recorded bug.

## The window

Small. `load()` normally settles before anyone can click a move button, and the reorder controls only appear once cards have rendered — which is after hydration. It needs a slow API or a fast user.

## Suggested fix

Have `load()` decline to overwrite `ids` while a write is outstanding, or version the state so a stale response is discarded. `isPending` already exists and is set by both `toggle` and `reorder`; the cheap version is to skip the `set` when it is true, and the correct version is a request sequence number, since `isPending` is shared by all writers.

Either way it needs a test that fails first: resolve `load()` after a `reorder()` and assert the reordered ids survive.

- `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts` - Added loadVersion versioning, updated load/toggle/reorder to check/increment version
- `packages/web/tests/stores/wishlist-load-race.test.ts` - New test suite for race condition

**Summary**:
Fixed bug #505 where load() would unconditionally overwrite ids with server response, losing any optimistic reorder made while the request was in flight. Solution uses version number: when a write (reorder or toggle) happens, it increments loadVersion, and load() checks the version before applying its response. If the version changed, the response is considered stale and discarded.

- Result: PASS (41 tests passing)
- Included: 2 new tests specifically for the race condition scenario

- All reorder tests still pass (10 tests)

ticket.title: API - POST /api/wishlist/replace, the explicit set change
ticket.description:
## Task

`POST /api/wishlist/replace` takes `{ productIds }` and writes it to `users.wishlist_product_ids` wholesale — a different set, in a given order.

## Why this cannot just be PUT

`PUT /api/wishlist` **refuses any change to the set**. Its permutation guard exists so a stale tab cannot silently drop an item saved on another device (#500), and loading a collection into the wishlist is exactly a set change.

Loosening the guard to accommodate this would reopen the hole it closed. Two operations, two endpoints: reordering stays absolutely guarded, replacement is opt-in and named for what it does.

Validate every id is a real product before writing, the way `PUT /:id/products` does — a wishlist full of ids matching nothing renders as an empty page with a non-zero badge.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-collection-editing, Phase 1.

`packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts`. Register BEFORE `/:productId` — both are POST, Hono matches in registration order, and `replace` is not a uuid, so the param route would answer 400. `/merge` carries the same warning for the same reason; read it first.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `3a624412` — feat(api): POST /api/wishlist/replace

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/wishlist.ts` — the handler, registered above `/:productId`
- `packages/api/tests/routes/wishlist-replace.test.ts` — 10 tests

**The point of a second endpoint, verified rather than argued**

`PUT /api/wishlist` refuses any change to the set, and that refusal is load-bearing — it is what stops a stale tab dropping an item saved on another device (#500). Loading a collection into the wishlist is exactly a set change, so it needs its own door.

Live proof the split holds, same payload both ways:

```
PUT   different set -> 409
POST  /replace      -> 200
before: Emerald Dreams | Urban Soul | Paper Layers | Synthetic Nature
after : Blush Hour | Emerald Dreams | Urban Soul
unknown id -> 400 (names 1)
duplicates -> 400
```

Worth stating plainly because the obvious "simplification" here is to loosen the `PUT` guard and delete this endpoint. That would reopen the data-loss hole. The doc comment says so at the handler.

**Two behaviours that differ from `PUT` on purpose**
- **An empty list is legitimate** — it clears the wishlist. On `PUT`, an empty list against a non-empty wishlist is a stale write and gets 409.
- **Ids are checked against the catalogue**, not just against what is already saved. `PUT` only permutes what is there, so its members are known-good by construction; `replace` accepts arbitrary ids and a wishlist full of ones matching nothing renders as an empty page with a non-zero badge.

ticket.description:
## Task

On the admin collection edit form, for **manual collections only**: a **Load into wishlist** action.

- Warns first, naming how many items are currently in the wishlist and that they will be replaced. The admin's wishlist is a work list, not precious — but destroying it silently is still wrong.
- Offers **Copy IDs** of the current wishlist in the same warning, so what is about to be lost can be recovered by hand.
- On confirm: `POST /api/wishlist/replace` with the collection's members in position order, then navigate to `/wishlist`.

Rule collections do not get the action at all. Their rule IS their membership; there is no explicit list to load.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-collection-editing, Phase 2. Depends on the replace endpoint.

`packages/web/app/routes/admin/collections/$id.tsx` already loads `productIds` (added in #503 to stop the form wiping membership), so the members are in hand — no extra fetch.

The store needs a matching action so the client state does not go stale against the server. Follow `reorder`'s shape in `packages/web/app/stores/wishlist.ts`.

ticket.title: Web - Save as collection: create new, or overwrite an existing one
ticket.description:
## Task

Replace the staging bar's single **Create collection from these** with a **Save as collection** flow offering two destinations:

- **New collection** — what exists today: post an unpublished manual collection, PUT the ordered membership, land on its edit form.
- **Overwrite an existing collection** — pick from the manual collections, confirm, then `PUT /api/admin/collections/:id/products` with the wishlist's ids.

The choice is made at save time. The wishlist does NOT remember which collection its contents came from — load and save are independent, so loading collection A and saving over collection B is legitimate rather than a mistake to prevent.

The overwrite confirm must name the target and what it currently holds: this replaces a collection's whole membership, it does not merge into it.

Only manual collections are offered. `GET /api/admin/collections` already returns `kind`, so filter client-side — offering a rule collection would be offering an operation the API refuses.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-collection-editing, Phase 2. Depends on the load action existing, so the loop can be exercised.

`packages/web/app/components/wishlist/WishlistStagingBar.tsx`. `PUT /api/admin/collections/:id/products` (#468) already replaces membership transactionally and validates every id, so overwrite needs no new endpoint.

ticket.title: E2E - the full loop: load a collection, reorder it, save it back
ticket.description:
## Task

One spec on `chromium-admin`, covering the round trip this feature exists for:

1. create a manual collection with a known order (staging from the wishlist is fine)
2. open it in the admin, **Load into wishlist**
3. confirm the wishlist holds its members **in the collection's order**
4. reorder them
5. **Save as collection → overwrite** that same collection
6. open `/collections/<slug>` and confirm the NEW order

Step 6 is the assertion that matters. Read the order off the storefront, not the admin form — the form can hold the right order and fail to persist it, which is precisely how #503's membership-wiping bug looked from the inside.

Also cover: loading warns before replacing, and a rule collection offers no load action at all.

## Context

Feature: wishlist-collection-editing, final phase.

Mark the spec **serial**, as `wishlist-staging.admin.spec.ts` is: every test signs in as the same staff account, one account has one wishlist, and in parallel they overwrite each other and trip the reorder guard.

Poll rather than reading order once — a move applies optimistically while the store's `load()` may still be in flight, which is #505.

Stamp slugs per run and clean up; the staff specs create real collections.

ticket.title: Cart page mixes two cart sources, so the saving row can describe lines it is not showing
ticket.description:
## Task
The storefront cart has **two independent sources of truth** and the page now reads both:

- `packages/web/app/stores/cart.ts` — a Zustand store with `localStorage` persistence. `routes/cart/index.tsx` takes `useCartItems`, `useCartSubtotal`, `useCartItemCount` from it (lines 178-180).
- `GET /api/cart` — the server cart (`packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts`), reached through `cartApi` / `useCart.ts`. This is where #429 resolves sale pricing, and where #430 re-resolves at order creation.

#436 wired `useServerCart` into the page to render the saving row, so the page now shows **line items from Zustand and savings from the server**. Nothing synchronises the two. A line added while logged out, or on another device, or before a `localStorage` clear, puts them out of step — and then the saving row quotes a number computed over a basket the customer is not looking at.

This predates the sale work; the sale work is what makes it visible and consequential, because the saving row is the gate's single point of contact with the customer.

## Decide, then implement
- **Server as truth** — the page renders `GET /api/cart`; Zustand becomes an optimistic cache in front of it. Matches where pricing, the member gate and order creation already live. Bigger change to the page.
- **Sync on read** — keep Zustand as the render source but reconcile against the server on cart mount, and render savings only for lines present in both. Smaller, but leaves two sources alive.

Server-as-truth is the recommendation: order creation already re-resolves server-side and ignores the client, so any divergence is a display lie rather than a pricing bug — but a display lie about a discount is exactly the thing this feature must not ship.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 4 — Frontend
Found while verifying #436 (commit aa24b758). Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5, §7

Affects the E2E in #438 and #447: a spec driving the UI cart while asserting server-resolved savings will be testing the seam, not the feature. Settle this before writing those assertions.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
✅ Landed as the smaller fix, not server-as-truth — commit `6eb64913` (originally 4487c24e; another session rebased the branch and folded its own `SalePrice.tsx` edit into it).

**Why the recommended option was not taken.** Server-as-truth is unreachable from this page: *nothing in the web app writes to the server cart*. `cartApi.addItem` / `updateItem` / `removeItem` / `clear` / `merge`, and the `useAddToCart` / `useUpdateCartItem` / `useRemoveFromCart` / `useClearCart` / `useMergeCart` hooks in `packages/web/app/hooks/useCart.ts`, all have **zero call sites**. The only server-cart consumer in the app is the `useServerCart()` read at `routes/cart/index.tsx:188`, added by #436. So `GET /api/cart` is empty for real customers, and rendering the page from it would show everyone an empty cart. Per the escape hatch in the brief, the smaller correct fix was landed instead of a half-migration.

Corollary worth its own ticket: the #436 saving row is effectively dead in production today, since it can only render against a server cart that nothing populates.

**What was implemented.** Every figure the page quotes is confined to lines present in *both* sources. `readCartSaving` now takes the displayed line keys and:
- restricts `byLine` and the locked total to displayed lines;
- passes the server's `savingTotal` through **verbatim** whenever it is wholly attributable to displayed lines — the ordinary case, unchanged;
- falls back to the sum of the server's own per-line `base − sale` figures only when a discounted, *unlocked* line is missing from the page (locked lines already total zero server-side, so they cannot make `savingTotal` overstate).

No discount is recomputed client-side; the numbers stay the server's, narrowed to the basket on screen.

**Files changed**
- `packages/web/app/routes/cart/index.tsx` — `readCartSaving(cart, displayed)`; displayed-line set built from the store in `CartContent`.
- `packages/web/tests/routes/cart-saving.test.tsx` — 6 new tests under "when the two cart sources disagree".

**Verification**
- `cd packages/web && bunx vitest run tests/routes/cart-saving.test.tsx` → PASS (18 tests; 3 of the 6 new ones failed first against the old code, quoting 11,720 for a one-line basket).
- `bunx vitest run tests/stores/cart.test.ts tests/stores/cart-drawer.test.ts tests/components/cart/CartDrawer.test.tsx` → PASS (70 tests, unchanged).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → no errors in either changed file (24 pre-existing package errors, unchanged).

New tests cover: the cart-level total never quoting an undisplayed line; the same for the locked total; rendered lines reconciling to the rendered total; **no behaviour change when no promotion is active even with divergent carts**; a store line the server has never seen; and pass-through of `savingTotal` when both carts agree (the guard against over-correcting into client-side arithmetic).

**A full server-as-truth migration would need**: wiring the cart writes into `components/product/ChooseOptions.tsx` + `ProductDetail.tsx`, `components/cart/CartDrawer.tsx`, `components/layout/Header.tsx` (item count), `routes/checkout/index.tsx` and `components/checkout/PaymentButton.tsx`, plus guest merge-on-login and a one-time localStorage→server migration for existing carts. Feature-sized, and two of those files are held by live agents (#437, #435).

⚠️ **Tracker data issue**: two tickets share the number **510** — this one and `todo/feature-sale-promotions/ticket-0510-decision-needed-orders-subtota.yaml` ("DECISION NEEDED - orders.subtotal semantics"). `showTicketDetails(510)` and `updateTicketStatus(510)` resolve here, but `updateImplementationStep(510, …)` and `addComment(510)` resolve to the *decision* ticket. Both stray writes to it (two steps marked done, one comment) have been reverted; it is back to all-pending, `comments: []`, `current_step: 1`. ticket.title: Schema - gift_card, gift_card_transaction and order_gift_card tables
ticket.description:
## Task
New `packages/api/src/database/schema/gift-cards.ts` holding the three tables, exported from `schema/index.ts`. Migration included.

Mirror `schema/wallet.ts` exactly in shape and units: integer paise, a denormalized balance column, and an append-only ledger carrying a `balanceAfterPaise` snapshot. That file is the precedent; do not invent a second money-modelling style.

## Status is derived, never stored
A card is `disabled` when `disabledAt` is set, `expired` when `expiresAt` has passed, `spent` when `balancePaise` is zero, otherwise `active`. No status column — it would fall out of sync with the balance on every redemption.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 1 — Schema + contracts
