ticket.title: The web app never writes to the server cart, so order creation reads an empty basket
ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify this ticket by title, not number — ticket numbers collided on 2026-08-06 under concurrent sessions.**

The storefront keeps its cart in a Zustand store persisted to `localStorage` (`packages/web/app/stores/cart.ts`). A complete server cart also exists — `packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts`, reached through `cartApi` and the mutation hooks in `packages/web/app/hooks/useCart.ts`.

**Nothing connects them.** Every cart-write hook has zero call sites:

```
grep -rn "useAddToCart|useUpdateCartItem|useRemoveFromCart|useClearCart|useMergeCart" packages/web/app --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts | grep -v hooks/useCart.ts
(no results)
```

`useServerCart` is read in exactly one place — `routes/cart/index.tsx:235`, added during the sale work — and `cartApi.addItem/updateItem/removeItem/clear/merge` are never called from anywhere.

Meanwhile checkout submits through `ordersApi.create()` (`components/checkout/PaymentButton.tsx:162`), and the API builds the order from the **database cart**: `routes/orders.ts:407-421` loads `userCart.items` and filters `isSavedForLater`. Nothing the customer added is in that table.

So an order placed by a real customer is assembled from an empty basket. Either checkout is failing outright in production, or it is succeeding against a cart that no longer reflects what was bought — both are severe, and both are invisible to the current tests because every route suite mocks `db` and every store test exercises Zustand alone.

## Why it surfaced now
The sale work put server-resolved pricing on `GET /api/cart` and re-resolves it at order creation, which is correct — the server must be the pricing authority. That made the missing write path visible: sale prices computed over the server cart cannot reach a customer whose cart only exists in `localStorage`.

## What to decide
The repo has two half-built carts and needs one. The server cart is the one order creation, pricing, the member gate and guest-session merging already assume, so wiring the writes to it is the smaller correction — but it touches add-to-cart call sites, `CartDrawer`, the header count, `checkout/index.tsx`, `PaymentButton`, guest merge-on-login, and a one-time `localStorage` → server migration for existing baskets.

## Context
Found 2026-08-06 while verifying the cart-source bug during the sale-promotions build. Predates that feature entirely.

Related: `ticket-0510-cart-page-mixes-two-cart-sourc.yaml` (narrow fix already landed — savings are confined to lines present in both sources) and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5.

**Verify against a real database.** `packages/api/tests/setup.ts:15` defaults `DATABASE_URL` to port 5433, which is a different application; chobii is on 5440. A suite whose `beforeAll` fails there is reported as *skipped*, not failed, which reads as green.

ticket.title: Lib - gift card code generation, normalization and hashing
ticket.description:
## Task
New `packages/api/src/lib/gift-card-code.ts`: generate a code, normalize typed input, hash for lookup.

## Why the alphabet matters
Sixteen characters of Crockford base32 — the alphabet excludes I, L, O and U, so nothing is misread off a phone screen and no accidental words are generated. Displayed grouped as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. That is roughly 2^80 of entropy.

**Entropy comes from `crypto.randomBytes`, never `Math.random`.** `Math.random` is seeded predictably and is not a security primitive; a predictable gift card code is free money.

Generate by rejection or by masking whole bytes — never `randomBytes(n) % 32` over a 256-value byte, which biases the first 24 letters of the alphabet.

## Normalization
Input is uppercased and stripped of everything outside the alphabet before hashing, so `7qf3-a8k2…` and `7QF3A8K2…` resolve to the same card. Hash is sha256 over the normalized code plus a server-side pepper from the environment — the pepper means a leaked database still cannot be brute-forced offline against a 2^80 space using rainbow tables of common codes.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 2 — Code and service
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §4 "The code"

Add `GIFT_CARD_CODE_PEPPER` to `.env.example`. Startup must fail loudly if it is missing in production rather than silently hashing with an empty pepper.

Its projection was missing both `rooms` *and* `isFeatured`, and its cache key `related:${slug}:${limit}` had no viewer suffix. Same three-line shape as featured, same file, covered by the same test file.

**Found and deliberately NOT fixed — `GET /api/collections/:slug` (`collections.ts:426`).** This is a genuine storefront price surface: `app/routes/collections/$slug.tsx:323` casts its `items` to `ProductCardData`, so every collection grid (Best Sellers, curated lists) shows base prices during a sale. It needs the same treatment plus `rooms` in the projection.

It is not fixed here because it is not a three-line change: `collectionsApp` is `new Hono()` with **no `optionalAuth`** and no `OptionalAuthVariables`, so there is no member state to resolve against. Pricing it as a guest unconditionally would be worse than the current bug — it would stamp `locked: true` on members. Wiring the middleware in pulls `src/auth` into that module's import graph, and neither `collection-detail.test.ts` nor `collections.test.ts` mocks `../../src/auth` (they mock only `db` and redis), so they would need auth mocks added too. That is a separate ticket's worth of change to another feature's route and test files, and it could not be verified inside this ticket's test budget. **Recommend a follow-up ticket.**

`GET /api/products/search` returns unpriced rows, but its only consumer is `SearchDrawer.tsx`, which renders no price at all — there is nothing to disagree with today. Worth pricing if that drawer ever grows a price; not worth widening this diff for.

`GET /api/products/:slug/variants` returns `productVariants.price` with no promotion applied. Noting it rather than fixing it: the PDP reads its variants from the detail route's payload (`response.variants`), not from this endpoint, and whether a promotion discounts a per-size variant price is a design question the resolver (which only knows `basePrice`) does not currently answer.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 2 SPLIT — buy panel is NOT won. Critic 1 picked ours "CLOSE: no"; critic 2 (committability lens) picked the reference, "CLOSE: yes". A split is not a win, so this stays open.

Critic 2's findings against OURS, in priority order:

1. REAL DEFECT — our sticky site header floats over the top ~90px of the artwork: "greying out the piece's top edge and frame — the one thing a large-artwork buyer needs unobstructed". Fix is an opaque header or scroll padding so the image starts below it. This is a genuine bug, not taste.

2. CORROBORATED — frame swatches carry no visible names and no per-frame price delta: "choosing a frame is a guess about both appearance and cost — and nothing on screen confirms the price on the button corresponds to the frame currently ringed." Two independent critics have now said this. Our names and prices are sr-only. Acting on it: visible names and price deltas. This makes us BETTER than the reference on a pattern we copied from it, which is the right call — the reference loses points for it too.

3. At 700px scroll our size control is out of frame and the swatches are half-sliced, while a ~380px trust stack and the share row occupy the space next to the button. Critic wants a one-line configuration summary above the button — "24x36 in · Black float frame · ₹2,499" — so the buyer can confirm what they are committing to without scrolling back.

NOT acting on: critic 2 wants the four trust rows demoted below the fold. Critic 1 explicitly credited having reassurance in the buying frame, and the reference also places its trust list directly under the buttons. Two critics disagree on this one, and the reference agrees with critic 1 — so demoting it would be thrashing on a split opinion. Leaving it.

Also of note: critic 2 broke the brief deliberately and said so. The brief tells critics to ignore promo banners; it argued that for a committability judgement it could not, because the reference's "40% off / Auto-discount applied in cart!" tells the buyer the price on the button is not what they will be charged. It still gave the reference the round. That is the critic arguing against its own preferred winner, which makes the verdict more trustworthy, not less.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 FIX LANDED (FrameSelector.tsx + its test only).

Each swatch is now circle → visible name → visible price uplift, inside one button. The sr-only node is GONE — the visible text now IS the accessible name, so there is one string instead of two that can drift. A test asserts zero .sr-only nodes in the component.

Zero-delta option reads "Included" rather than "+₹0.00" or a blank: blank leaves the price row gap-toothed (the exact raggedness the critics objected to), "+₹0.00" is noise, and "Included" is true in a way "free" is not — the rolled canvas is inside the price already being quoted.

Went beyond the ticket to answer critic 2's "nothing on screen confirms the price on the button corresponds to the frame currently ringed". New caption names the base figure in rupees:
  nothing selected → "Frame prices below are added to the ₹2,499.00 size price."
  frame selected   → "Stretch + Gold Frame adds ₹999.60 to the ₹2,499.00 size price."
  zero-modifier    → "Rolled Canvas is included in the ₹2,499.00 size price."
The capture shows that caption directly above a button reading "Add to cart - ₹3,498.60", so a buyer can check the arithmetic without leaving the frame.

Grid changed from flex-wrap to a fixed grid-cols-4. Seven free-flowing swatches wrapped five-then-two leaving a three-cell hole; four columns give 4+3 and, more importantly, align the names into vertical stacks. Circle is now w-full max-w-[104px] aspect-square rather than a hard 92px — renders 104px in the 485px panel, shrinks to ~83px at 390px, cannot overflow. Verified scrollWidth === 390 at mobile with the last-column swatch selected so its check badge stays in the viewport.

Layout bug found and fixed in passing: min-h-[2.4em] on the name was ~3px short of two real line boxes, so every wrapped cell's price sat lower than its neighbours' — a visibly wobbling price row. Flat min-h-8 puts them on one baseline.

28 tests (was 20). The old test asserting the swatch had NO visible text was the encoded defect and was replaced. ChooseOptions + ProductTabs also run: 109 passed, nothing collateral broken.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the sticky-header bug: this builder could not capture at scroll 700 because "the frame block sits under the sticky header" and had to shoot at 480/580 instead. That is the second independent report of the same defect. Fix is queued behind the mobile builder, which currently owns ProductDetail.tsx.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Built. New DeliveryEstimate.tsx — check glyph, "Arrives soon! Get it by <bold range> if you order today".

No exported lead-time constant existed. The real figure lives as prose, duplicated in app/routes/shipping.tsx and app/routes/faq.tsx: production 2-4 business days, delivery a further 3-7. That gives DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME_DAYS = { min: 5, max: 11 }, exposed as an overridable prop rather than hardcoded dates. Date formatting uses en-US rather than the site's usual en-IN, because the reference format is month-first ("Aug 13") and en-IN renders "13 Aug". Worth a second look at integration — en-IN may be the more correct choice for our actual customers even though it diverges from the reference.

Worth noting as a follow-up: the lead time being prose in two route files rather than one exported constant means it can drift. A shared constant would be the better home.

Still needs a blind critic verdict before this is done.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 BLIND VERDICT: ours won, "CLOSE: no" — and this is a REVERSAL BY THE SAME LENS.

Round 2's committability critic gave this region to the reference ("CLOSE: yes"). Round 3, same lens, fresh context, new coin flip, picked ours and was not close. Both the general brief lens (round 2, critic 1) and the committability lens have now chosen ours, so the buy panel is settled on two independent lenses rather than two runs of one.

What flipped it — the three fixes dispatched off round 2's complaints:
1. Frame swatches now carry visible names and price uplifts. The critic's remaining complaint on that point was aimed squarely at the reference: "B's seven frame/material options are unlabelled circular swatches with no names and no price deltas... picking any other means guessing both what it is and what it adds to the total." That was OUR defect two rounds ago; it is now only theirs.
2. The configuration summary line. The critic: "B never states the configuration back to the buyer; A's '16"H × 12"W · No frame selected · ₹2,499.00' line is the single most committable element in either image."
3. The sticky header no longer covers the artwork.

Note the honesty design paid off directly. The critic attacked the reference for quoting "a firm 'Add To Cart - $218.00'" beside an unchosen "Select a Size": "either $218 belongs to some silent default the panel never names, or it will change the moment the dropdown is opened, and nothing on screen tells the buyer which." We preselect a real variant and restate it, so our number always refers to something nameable. The frame caption does the same job for the frame — "adds ₹999.60 to the ₹2,499.00 size price" above a button reading ₹3,498.60.

Marking #515, #516, #517, #519, #520 done. Eleven of twelve regions judged; below-fold and mobile verdicts still pending.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Built. New ShareRow.tsx — "Share:" label with glyphs on the left, "? Need help?" on the right.

ticket.title: web: description and details move into a tab bar
ticket.description: Reference groups the long-form content into four tabs with an underline marking the active one: About The Artwork, Details And Customization, Shipping And Returns, Review. Ours renders flat stacked sections (Description at ProductDetail.tsx:520-528, Perfect For at :531-545) plus a separate reviews wall. Build the tab bar and route the existing content and the existing ProductReviewSection into it without breaking the #reviews anchor or the review deep links.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Built. New ProductTabs.tsx — four tabs (About The Artwork / Details And Customization / Shipping And Returns / Review) with real tablist semantics, arrow-key + Home/End navigation with wraparound, and aria-controls/labelledby wiring. 22 tests pass.

#reviews anchor: the component self-manages the hash in uncontrolled mode. On mount it checks for #reviews and opens the Review tab; a hashchange listener catches a later click on the existing buybox-reviews-link and then calls scrollIntoView itself, because the native browser jump is a no-op against a tabpanel that was not mounted at click time. The reviewPanel ReactNode is rendered as-is so ProductReviewSection keeps its own id="reviews" and data-testid="product-reviews". Caveat for the integrator: driving it in controlled mode disables the hash-sync effects by design, and the integrator then owns hash syncing.

Shipping And Returns copy sourced from our own routes, NOT from mesonart: app/routes/shipping.tsx (free over ₹999, 2-4 day production + 3-7 day delivery, tracking via /track) and app/routes/returns.tsx (30-day window from delivery, /account/orders or support@chobii.art, 48-hour damaged-item exception, 5-7 business day refunds). Tabs link out to /shipping and /returns for full text.

Details tab is driven by fields we actually have: sku, orientation, styles, subjects, primaryColor, per-variant sizeLabel, and frame name/material. Fields the reference shows that we have no column for and therefore omitted rather than invented: print medium and paper stock, print technology, item weight, care instructions, indoor/outdoor rating. Worth considering as a schema follow-up.

Knock-on for integration: tests/e2e/product-detail.spec.ts:843 and :878 assert `h2:has-text("Description")` and `h2:has-text("Perfect For")` as top-level headings. Those move inside the About tabpanel once wired.

Still needs a blind critic verdict before this is done.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 2 BLIND VERDICT: LOST, "CLOSE: no". The critic picked the reference for the below-fold region.

Its biggest gap, on us: "B's post-purchase region is nearly empty. The tab panel resolves to a single 90-character line of body copy plus two 'Perfect For' chips — roughly 250px of content — and then the page hands off to a beige trust strip and the footer at the halfway line of a 900px viewport."

Findings I judge to be real and actionable:
1. The Review tab carries no count and no star summary, so there is no signal that reviews exist at all before a click. For an expensive considered purchase, social proof should be visible before the click, not behind it.
2. The section has no vertical weight. The reference fills this region with an artist block, a second "More to Love" carousel, an Instagram row and a why-us band; we go straight from one short paragraph into the footer.
3. The tab panel collapses when the description is short. Our seed copy is one sentence, but the layout should not fall in on itself when content is thin.

Findings I am NOT acting on, with reasons:
- The critic argued for replacing tabs with stacked always-visible sections. Rejecting that: the reference uses tabs and won this comparison with tabs, so tabs are not what lost it — the emptiness behind them is. Fixing the content weight is the correct response.
- "The related-artwork row is reduced to floating title stubs with no images" is largely an artefact of the 1750px capture slicing through the carousel mid-card. Worth re-checking on the next capture rather than treating as a defect.

Separately, this capture exposed a real duplication the loop was not looking for: the page now carries TWO trust strips saying nearly the same thing — the new per-product TrustList in the buy panel, and the global footer USP strip (Archival Inks / Free Over ₹999 / 30-Day Returns / Safe Payments) directly above the footer. The critic read the latter as footer boilerplate. That needs a decision, tracked separately.

Staying open. Fixes dispatched.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 FIX LANDED (ProductTabs.tsx only; e2e specs and ProductDetail/$slug untouched).

Review signal, now visible without a click: the Review tab carries the count, and a star/average summary sits beside the tab bar (centred below xl, right-aligned from xl — measured clearance at 1440, no collision). The summary is itself a control that opens the Review tab.

Playwright trap found and avoided: getByRole('tab', { name }) compares the accessible name by EQUALITY, not substring — verified against playwright-core's matchesAttributePart. product-detail.spec.ts locates the Review tab by name in three places, so "Review (104)" as an accessible name would have broken all three silently. The count is rendered aria-hidden and the number reaches screen readers via aria-describedby on the tab instead. Worth remembering for any future tab or button label that gains a badge.

Panel collapse fixed by layout, not filler: min-h-[20rem] / sm:min-h-[24rem], About is flex-1 with the cross-link row at mt-auto, so slack on a one-sentence description lands between the copy and the cross-links rather than trailing off the bottom. Region went from ~250px to ~460px and now clears the footer trust strip. No invented copy.

Zero reviews handled as THREE states, not two: count>0 shows the badge and summary; count===0 shows muted "No reviews yet" as plain text, not a button, and no "(0)" badge — a (0) reads as a broken counter and a control that opens an empty wall is a promise the page cannot keep; rating null/undefined renders nothing at all, because "we did not load an aggregate" is not the claim "there are none". That null-is-not-zero distinction matches what ProductReviewSection already does.

About now carries At A Glance (styles/subjects/colour moved out of the Details spec table, since they describe the artwork rather than the printed object), an artist byline, and a cross-link row answering the critic's three questions with real numbers — "17 sizes · 7 finishes", "Free over ₹999 · 30-day returns", "4.8 from 104 reviews". Policy numbers are named constants shared with the Shipping panel so the two cannot drift.

41 tests (was 25). The "Product Detail - Tabs" e2e block passes 5/5.

STILL NEEDED — two purely additive props at the $slug.tsx call site, blocked while the mobile builder owns that file: rating={product.rating} and artist on the spec projection. Until those land the rating summary, tab count and byline render nothing.

HONEST ASSESSMENT of what remains: About is now thin because of DATA, not layout. What we hold is exhausted. To match the reference's About region the schema would need an artist bio/portrait/statement (we hold a name and a slug), print medium and paper/canvas stock, ink and edition info, care instructions, and editorial description copy of real length — the seed sentence is a fixture, not marketing copy. `tags` exists on the shared Product but is not projected onto ProductDetailData. This is worth its own schema ticket; no amount of layout work will fix it.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 CONFIRMED — two independent blind critics, different lenses, both picked ours, both "CLOSE: no". This region lost round 2 and has now been retaken. Marking #521 and #522 done.

Critic 2 (doubt-retirement lens) on the reference: its tab strip "is jammed against the very bottom edge of the viewport with none of its panel content visible, and the sticky add-to-cart bar is layered on top of it — occluding the 'Reviews' tab label down to a single letter and burying the 'Write a review' control." It also caught that the reference's star row "renders as five empty outline stars with no numeric rating and no review count next to it, which reads as 'nobody has ever reviewed this' — the strongest possible reason not to buy, stated by accident." That is precisely the defect the round-2 fix removed from our page, arrived at independently.

ONE CRITICISM THAT APPLIES TO US TOO, despite the win. The critic faulted the reference for spending "its entire below-fold screen on 'Visually Similar Artworks' — five competing products with prices, shown before a single specification of the item the buyer already chose, which invites them off this page instead of closing them on it." We deliberately copied that order, because #522 specified matching the reference's sequence. We won both verdicts with it, so I am not changing it now — but the argument for hoisting the tabs above the carousel is sound and independent of parity, and it is the kind of change that should be A/B'd against real buyers rather than settled by a critic or by imitation. Recording it rather than acting on it.

Also unresolved from round 2 and still true: About is thin because of DATA, not layout. Matching the reference's About region needs schema we do not have — artist bio and statement, print medium and stock, ink and edition, care instructions, and description copy of real length. Worth its own ticket.

ticket.title: web: related products become a Visually Similar Artworks carousel
ticket.description: Reference shows 'Visually Similar Artworks' as a horizontal carousel with circular prev/next arrows and 5 visible cards, each image + title + 'from Rs. X' + '#SKU'. Ours is a static 'You May Also Like' grid (routes/posters/$slug.tsx:527-540) using ProductGrid. Build the carousel, keep it keyboard and screen-reader navigable.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Built. New ProductCarousel.tsx — heading taken as a prop so it serves both "Visually Similar Artworks" and "More to Love". Reuses the existing ProductCard rather than reimplementing a card; 2 cards visible at mobile, 3 at sm, 5 at lg against a 20px gap track.

Accessibility: arrows are real buttons carrying the heading in their accessible name (so two carousels on one page stay distinguishable), and they use the `disabled` attribute at true start/end rather than dead-clicking. The track itself is a tab stop with its own ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handler, since native horizontal-scroll-on-focus is inconsistent across browsers. prefers-reduced-motion is handled both in the programmatic scrollBy behaviour and via motion-reduce:scroll-auto for wheel scrolling.

No new dependency — built on the repo's existing scroll-snap utilities and buttonVariants, following the DiscoverChips rail pattern.

19 tests pass. tsc clean for this file.

Not yet wired into routes/posters/$slug.tsx — the integrator replaces RelatedProductsSection. Still needs a blind critic verdict before this is done.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 BLIND VERDICT: ours won, "CLOSE: no" — reversing round 2's loss for this region.

Round 2 the critic called our post-purchase region "nearly empty" and gave it to the reference. After the ProductTabs fixes (min-height, review count + star summary visible without a click, At A Glance, cross-link row with real numbers), a fresh critic with a new coin flip picked ours and was not close.

Every gap it named was against the reference:
- "all four [tabs] set in the same pale grey with no active state, no underline, no panel content beneath them, and the fourth label plus the 'Write a review' button are physically covered by the floating add-to-cart bar, while the chat launcher covers the star row" — two floating widgets parked on the exact content the section exists to deliver.
- "The MESONART watermark is stamped across the centre of every recommendation thumbnail, obscuring the one thing a browsing buyer is scanning."
- "Card metadata is ragged: the title wraps to two or three lines down the left while the price stays pinned to the right of line one, so prices float unanchored and no two cards end on the same baseline."

WORTH CHECKING ON OUR SIDE despite the win: our seed images are sourced from the reference site and carry the same MESONART watermark, so that criticism may apply to our thumbnails too — the critic was looking at their capture, but we should confirm our own product imagery is not watermarked with another company's brand before this ships. That is a content/asset issue, not a layout one, and it is out of this ticket's scope, but it should not go unrecorded.

Confirming critic running with a doubt-retirement lens before this is marked done.

ticket.title: web: PDP mobile layout matches the reference at 390px
ticket.description: At 390px the reference gives the main image a rounded card with ~16px side padding, moves the thumbnails to a horizontal scroll strip of ~72px squares directly beneath it, keeps the expand button pinned top-right, then stacks the social-proof line, H1 and sold-count line. comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
BUILT, awaiting blind verdict.

The builder probed the live reference rather than trusting the spec doc, and found two errors in it — both now corrected in docs/design/pdp-parity-reference.md:
- mobile thumbnails are 62px on a 78px pitch (x = 20/98/176/254/332), not the "~72px" the doc claimed

Structural fix worth recording: the CTA had min-w-0, which switches off the min-content floor on a whitespace-nowrap button, letting the flex line squeeze the button narrower than its own label — the text then escapes and the document gains a horizontal scrollbar. Removing min-w-0 means the label's true width drives the wrap decision, so an unusually long price BREAKS THE ROW instead of overflowing. Now left-aligned below md, centred from md. Two-per-row is arithmetically impossible there — the labels measure 143 + 203 = 346 in a 350px column — so it stays three rows, just aligned.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
ROUND 3 CONFIRMED — two independent blind critics at 390x844, different lenses, both picked ours, both "CLOSE: no". Marking done.

Both landed on the same criticism of the reference, independently: it spends the highest-value block on the phone screen — directly under the thumbnail strip — on "… saves · In 17 carts now" and "4 sold in last 81 hours", pushing the price below the fold entirely.

Critic 2: "On a phone, on a bad connection, from an unknown brand, that inverts the deal: the page is asking for panic before it has told me what the thing costs... the counters read as dropshipper furniture and actively reduce belief that anyone will crate and ship a large canvas."

This is now the THIRD independent critic across two viewports to attack those counters. The decision made at the very start of this work — that we would not fabricate social-proof numbers we have no data for — has been vindicated four times over by critics who had no idea which page was which. It was taken as an honesty constraint and it turned out to be the single biggest competitive advantage in the comparison.

Both critics also flagged the reference's two-line breadcrumb repeating the product title verbatim, and a floating widget clipping its social-proof line mid-sentence.

One criticism aimed at the reference that is worth weighing for us: critic 2 argued the hero slot should be the flat framed shot with the room scene demoted to thumbnail 2, because in a staged room scene "the artwork itself occupies under half the frame". Our seed product leads with the flat artwork already, so we are on the right side of this — but it is a rule worth applying deliberately to image sort order across the catalogue rather than by accident of seeding.

ticket.title: Bug - /sale and /posters cards print base prices during a sale
ticket.description:
## Bug

The two main product grids list discounted products but render every card at its **base price**. The `/sale` landing page is the worst case: it exists only to show the sale, and every card on it is wrong.

## Root cause

Both routes rebuild `ProductCardData` field by field and neither mapper copies the `sale` block that the API returns on every product:

- `packages/web/app/routes/sale.tsx` — `fetchSaleProducts()`, the `(response.items || []).map(...)` object literal has no `sale` key.
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` — same shape, same omission.

`ProductCard` itself is fine: it renders `<SalePrice sale={product.sale ?? null} …>` and works wherever it is handed raw API items. The "You May Also Like" row on a PDP proves it — that row goes through `toFeaturedProducts()`, which is a pass-through, and its cards show the struck price, the `price-was` and the `N% off` badge correctly.

## Fix

Add `sale: (item.sale as SalePricing | null) ?? null` to both mappers. `ProductCardData.sale` already exists on the type.

## Verification

`tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts` (#438) already covers the passing surfaces. When this is fixed, the grid assertion in `grid cards print the struck sale price` can be pointed at `/sale` and tightened to "every card on the page carries a sale price", which is the assertion the ticket originally wanted:

```ts
const cards = page.getByTestId('sale-page').getByTestId('product-card')
const cardCount = await cards.count()
await expect(page.getByTestId('sale-page').getByTestId('sale-price')).toHaveCount(cardCount)
```

The spec's header comment and the comment on that test both name this ticket's defect as the reason the coverage sits where it does.

## Context

Found while writing the lifecycle E2E for #438. `/sale` is #437; the card integration is #435.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `3a3ba18d` — fix(web): the grid mappers keep the sale they were handed

**Root Cause**: Both grid loaders rebuild `ProductCardData` as a hand-written object literal, which is a whitelist — any field the API grows must be added by hand or it is dropped before a card ever sees it. `sale` was never in either literal.
**Location**: `packages/web/app/routes/sale.tsx:132-148` (`fetchSaleProducts`) and `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx:156-171` (`fetchPostersData`).
**Fix**: Both mappers now copy `sale: (item.sale as ProductCardData['sale']) ?? null` straight through. Nothing is recomputed client-side — `resolveSalePrice` produced the figures server-side and the cart re-resolves them at checkout.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/routes/sale.tsx` — `sale` added to the loader's card mapper
- `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` — same
- `packages/web/tests/routes/card-sale-mapping.test.tsx` — new, 14 tests

**Full sweep of every API-row → card-props mapping**

Audited all seven mapping sites. Exactly two dropped the field, and they are the only two written as field-by-field literals:

| Site | Style | `sale` |
|---|---|---|
| `routes/sale.tsx:132` | field-by-field literal | **dropped → fixed** |
| `routes/posters/index.tsx:156` | field-by-field literal | **dropped → fixed** |
| `routes/posters/$slug.tsx:207` (You May Also Like) | `toFeaturedProducts` pass-through | ok |
| `routes/index.tsx:72` (home featured rail) | `toFeaturedProducts` pass-through | ok |
| `routes/collections/$slug.tsx:323` | cast pass-through | ok |
| `components/wishlist/WishlistContents.tsx:76` | pass-through by id | ok |
| `lib/api.ts:89` `toFeaturedProducts` | pure pass-through | ok |

Also checked and deliberately left alone:
- `routes/posters/$slug.tsx:108-162` — the PDP detail mapper is a field-by-field literal too, but it already carries `sale` (line 161). That is why the PDP was right while the grids were wrong.
- `components/layout/SearchDrawer.tsx:26` — narrows results to a 4-field `SearchResult` and renders its own rows, not `ProductCard`. No card involved.
- `hooks/useProducts.ts:55-77` — `ProductListItem` has no `sale` field, so `useFeaturedProducts` / `useProductsByIds` / `useProductSearch` would hide it. All three have **zero consumers** in `app/`; noted rather than changed.

**Tests pin the mapping, not the rendering**

The suite mocks `productsApi.list` and drives the two *real* route loaders through one `describe.each`, asserting on the objects the loader hands the grid. A hand-built `ProductCardData` fixture carrying `sale` passes whether or not the mapper preserves it — it never went through the mapper — which is precisely how this survived #435's green card suite. Two of the fourteen also render the loader's output through `ProductGrid` and assert the struck price reaches the DOM, so the whole API-row → pixels path is covered.

Includes a whole-row anti-drop guard (`preserves every card field the API sends`). This is the fourth field the feature has lost to a projection or a mapper; asserting only on `sale` would have fixed today's field and left the mechanism intact.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/card-sale-mapping.test.tsx tests/routes/sale.test.tsx tests/routes/posters-*.test.ts* tests/components/product/{SalePrice,ProductCard,ProductCard.tokens,ProductGrid}.test.*`
- Result: PASS — 12 files, 168/168 tests
- Red-first evidence: the new suite was 10 failed / 4 passed before the fix, every failure reading `expected undefined to deeply equal {…}` on `sale`. The 4 passing were the no-sale negative controls.
- Typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/web` → 22 errors, all pre-existing (baseline ~26), **zero** in the three touched files.

**Concurrency note**: `packages/web/app/routes/posters/index.tsx` also carried an uncommitted `sku:` line from another in-flight session (the card-parity change that holds `ProductCard.tsx`). Only my `sale` hunk was staged, via a hunk-scoped `git apply --cached` — no stash, no amend. That session's `sku` line and its whole `ProductCard.tsx` integration are still uncommitted and untouched in the working tree.

**Follow-up available**: `tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts`'s `grid cards print the struck sale price` can now be repointed from the PDP's related row to `/sale` and tightened to "every card on the page carries a sale price", as this ticket's description sketches. Not done here — another agent owns `tests/e2e/` this session.

ticket.title: Bug - promotion writes leave stale prices in the product response cache
ticket.description:
## Bug

Enabling, editing or expiring a promotion does not take effect on the storefront for up to 5–10 minutes. An admin who starts a sale sees the strip and the countdown appear immediately, but product grids and PDPs keep quoting pre-sale prices; when a sale ends, they keep quoting the discount.

## Root cause

The admin promotion routes (`packages/api/src/routes/admin/promotions.ts`) call `invalidateActivePromotions()` and nothing else. That clears the 60s in-memory active-promotion list, which is why `GET /api/promotions/active` and all the promotion-driven chrome update at once.

The **product responses** are a separate Redis cache and carry the resolved `sale` block:

- `product-list:<query><viewer>` — `CACHE_TTL_PRODUCTS = 300s`
- `product:<slug><viewer>` — `CACHE_TTL_PRODUCT_DETAIL = 600s`
- `product:featured:<limit><viewer>` — `CACHE_TTL_FEATURED = 900s`
- `product:related:<slug>:<limit><viewer>`

Nothing purges these on a promotion write, so they serve the prices from before the change until their own TTL runs out. Admin *product* writes already do the right thing (`deleteCached(CacheKeys.PRODUCT_LIST)` in `routes/admin/products.ts`); the promotion routes just never got the equivalent.

The `viewerCacheSuffix` member/guest split means each variant has to be purged, so a prefix/pattern delete is the right tool — `deleteCachedPattern` already exists in `packages/api/src/lib/redis.ts`.

## Fix

In the create / update / enable / disable / delete handlers, alongside `invalidateActivePromotions()`:

```ts
await deleteCachedPattern(`${CacheKeys.PRODUCT_LIST}*`)
await deleteCachedPattern(`${CacheKeys.PRODUCT}*`)
```

## Evidence

Reproduced by hand against the dev stack: two identical `GET /api/products?page=1&pageSize=7&onSale=false` calls return `fromCache: undefined` then `fromCache: true`, and a promotion created between them changes nothing until the key expires.

`tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts` (#438) has to work around this — `purgeProductCache()` in `tests/e2e/helpers/promotions.ts` drops the `product-list:*` and `product:*` keys between legs, because the spec reads the same PDP in the "no sale" and "on sale" legs well inside the 600s TTL. Once this is fixed, that helper stays useful as fixture hygiene but stops being load-bearing.

The expiry leg of that spec is written to keep the two apart: it asserts the chrome vanishes with nothing purged and nothing touched, and only purges before asserting on prices.

## Context

Found while writing the lifecycle E2E for #438.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `17b5f421` — fix(api): promotion writes purge the product response cache

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/lib/redis.ts` — `deleteCachedPattern` now iterates with SCAN instead of KEYS; new `purgeProductResponseCache()` globbing the `product-list:` and `product:` prefixes
- `packages/api/src/lib/promotion-pricing.ts` — new `saleCacheTtl(activePromotions, ttl, now)`, the expiry half
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/promotions.ts` — all five mutating handlers now `await invalidatePricingCaches()` (resolver list + Redis purge)
- `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts` — the four cache writes that carry a `sale` block pass their TTL through `saleCacheTtl`
- `packages/api/tests/lib/promotion-pricing.test.ts` — 8 new tests for the TTL clamp
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/promotion-cache-purge.test.ts` — new, 11 tests

**Root Cause**: `packages/api/src/routes/admin/promotions.ts` called only `invalidateActivePromotions()`, which clears the resolver's 60s in-process active list. The Redis product-response cache (`product-list:` 300s, `product:<slug>` 600s, `product:featured:<n>` 900s, `product:related:<slug>:<n>` 900s) carries the resolved `sale` block and was never purged, so a sale switched on in admin kept serving base prices until the TTL lapsed — and kept serving discounts after the sale ended.

**Purge strategy — prefix purge over SCAN, not a generation counter.** A cache-generation counter folded into the key prefix is race-free and O(1) per bump, but it costs a Redis read on *every* storefront product request to resolve the current generation. Promotion writes are a handful of admin actions a day; product reads are constant. Paying an O(keyspace) scan a few times a day is far cheaper in aggregate than an extra round trip on every read, and the key shape stays unchanged so the E2E `purgeProductCache()` helper and the admin product-write invalidation keep working. `deleteCachedPattern` was switched from `KEYS` to `SCAN` in the same change — `KEYS` walks the whole keyspace inside one command and blocks every other client, and the three review route files already calling this helper were paying that.

**Expiry — TTL clamp.** Nothing runs when a promotion simply ends; active state is derived from the clock, so there is no write to hang a purge off. `saleCacheTtl` shortens each entry to the soonest active `endsAt`, floored at 1s (`setex` rejects a non-positive TTL, and `getActivePromotions`'s own 60s memo can hand a route a row whose window already closed). Rounded down, so an entry never outlives the sale by a part second. Open-ended promotions clamp nothing.

**Known gap, deliberately not closed here**: a promotion that has not *started* yet. The resolver only ever returns active rows, so a body cached now can still outlive a sale scheduled to begin in a minute. Enabling that sale is an admin write and does get purged; a start time reached on the clock does not. Covering it needs the route to know the next `startsAt`, which changes the resolver's query shape — worth its own ticket.

**Also noticed, not fixed (out of scope)**: `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts` calls `deleteCached(CacheKeys.PRODUCT_LIST)` in five places. `deleteCached` takes an *exact* key, so that deletes a literal `"product-list:"` key that is never written — admin product writes are not actually busting the list cache. Contrary to this ticket's description, that path has the same bug. Worth a follow-up ticket.

**E2E**: `tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts` was read and not modified. Its expiry leg asserts the chrome vanishes *before* any purge — that half is driven by `GET /api/promotions/active`, which is not Redis-cached, so the premise is untouched. The price assertions later in that leg still purge first and still pass; the purge is now redundant rather than load-bearing, which is what this ticket was for.

**Verification**:
- Command: `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 bunx vitest run tests/lib/promotion-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/admin/promotion-cache-purge.test.ts tests/routes/admin/promotions.test.ts` (with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at :5440)
- Result: PASS — 3 files, 75 tests, 75 passing
- Command: `bunx tsc --noEmit` in packages/api
- Result: PASS — 0 errors
- Red-first evidence: the 8 TTL tests failed with `saleCacheTtl is not a function`, and the purge suite failed 7/11 with seeded `:member`/`:guest` keys surviving and `scan` call count 0.

**Pre-existing failures confirmed unrelated**:
- `tests/lib/redis.test.ts` fails a varying set (2, then 4, then 10 across three identical runs) in `setCached`/rate-limit tests — a lazy-connect race against the live Redis on :6380, in code this ticket did not touch. Its `deleteCachedPattern` runtime test passes.
- `tests/routes/products.test.ts > should filter by styles` returns 400 from the query validator, before any handler code runs.

ticket.title: Bug - joining is invisible to server pricing for 5 minutes, so a fresh member is charged base price
ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify by title, not number — ticket numbers collided on 2026-08-06.**

better-auth's `session.cookieCache` serves the session from a signed cookie for 5 minutes. `galleryMember` rides that session (declared in `packages/api/src/auth/index.ts` under `user.additionalFields`, #439). `POST /api/gallery/join` (#440) writes the database row but never refreshes the cookie.

So for up to five minutes after joining, every server-side read of `isMember` is **false**:

- `GET /api/products` and `/:slug` resolve `locked: true` and serve a members-only price the customer supposedly cannot have
- `GET /api/cart` reports the saving as locked and contributes 0 to `savingTotal`
- **`POST /api/orders` charges the base price** — the design's own rule is "if the viewer is not a member at the moment the order is created, they pay base" (design §5), and the server correctly believes they are not one

The UI hides the problem: the shared optimistic membership signal (#446) flips immediately, so the customer sees prices unlock, joins, checks out — and is charged full price. **A customer who is shown a discount and then billed without it is the worst failure mode this feature has**, and it is invisible from the browser.

Verified directly by the #447 E2E agent, whose fixtures drop that one cookie rather than encode the stale behaviour as expected.

## Fix direction
Make the join refresh the session rather than only the row. Options, in rough order of preference:
1. Have `POST /api/gallery/join` re-issue the session cookie so the new `galleryMember` value is in it before the response returns — the join already knows the user and is the one place the flag changes.
2. Read membership with `disableCookieCache: true` on the paths where money is decided (cart pricing, order creation) — correct but pays a database read on every priced request.
3. Read `galleryMember` from the database rather than the session in `resolveSalePrice`'s callers — most robust, least dependent on better-auth behaviour, but touches every call site.

Option 1 plus option 2 narrowed to order creation is probably the right combination: the cookie refresh fixes the common path, and order creation — the only place money is actually taken — never trusts a cached flag.

## Context
Feature: gallery-membership. Found 2026-08-06 by the #447 E2E work (commit f5432bc3).
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5, §8.

Second, smaller finding from the same run: there is no "leave the gallery" endpoint, so E2E non-member legs each register a throwaway account — a shared fixture would become a member on run one and pass vacuously thereafter. Worth a test-only helper or an admin-side reset.

**Verify against the real database:** `export $(grep -m1 '^DATABASE_URL=' /Users/dhruv/work/masonart.com/.env)` — the default port 5433 is a different application, and a failed `beforeAll` there reports as *skipped*, which reads as green.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `1d46167a` — fix(api): a fresh gallery member is charged the member price, not base

**Root Cause**: `session.cookieCache` (5 min, `packages/api/src/auth/index.ts:325`) serves the whole session — `galleryMember` included, it is a `user.additionalFields` entry — from a signed cookie. `POST /api/gallery/join` wrote the users row and nothing else, so every server-side read for the rest of that window still resolved the joiner as a guest. `POST /api/orders` read `isMember` off that session and charged base, while the optimistic client signal (#446) showed the discount unlocked.

**Fix**: options 1 + 2 from the ticket, as suggested.

1. **The join re-issues the session** — `packages/api/src/lib/session-refresh.ts` (new). Uses better-auth's own primitive rather than hand-writing a cookie: `auth.api.getSession({ query: { disableCookieCache: true }, returnHeaders: true })`. That endpoint skips the cached payload, reads session+user from the database, and *ends by calling `setCookieCache` with what it found* — so asking better-auth for the session IS the refresh; `returnHeaders` hands back the `Set-Cookie` it produced. Deliberately NOT `setCookieCache` directly: it needs a `GenericEndpointContext`, which a Hono handler does not have, and `lib/session-cookie.ts` is already one hand-rolled encoding too many.
   - Cookies are **appended**, not set. A real refresh comes back as two `chobii.session_data` headers (the cached payload is chunked); `headers.get('set-cookie')` would comma-join them into something a browser cannot parse.
   - Best-effort: a refresh that throws does not fail the join, and cannot cost a wrong price because of (2).

2. **Order creation resolves membership from the row** — `isGalleryMember(userId)` in `services/gallery-membership.ts`, called from `orders.ts`. Closes the mirror case too: a stale *"member"* cookie can no longer buy a discount nobody earned. The read is **lazy** — `resolveSalePrice` consults `isMember` only for `membersOnly` promotions, so with none active the query is not issued and an ordinary order costs no extra round trip.

Left `cart.ts` / `products.ts` on the session, per the ticket: they render prices, and (1) makes them correct on the very next request after a join.

**Verified against the real library (better-auth 1.4.17)**, not just mocks — a memory-adapter harness reproduced the bug and the fix end to end:
```
row now says galleryMember: true
cached getSession galleryMember: false      <- the bug
fresh getSession galleryMember: true        <- disableCookieCache
re-issued set-cookie: [chobii.session_data, chobii.session_data]
cached-again getSession galleryMember: true <- next request is correct
```

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/lib/session-refresh.ts` (new) — the better-auth-native session re-issue
- `packages/api/src/routes/gallery.ts` — join refreshes the session after writing
- `packages/api/src/routes/orders.ts` — `resolveMembership` reads the row, lazily; `readIsMember` removed
- `packages/api/src/services/gallery-membership.ts` — `isGalleryMember`; note on the #441 limitation
- `packages/api/tests/routes/gallery-join-order-pricing.test.ts` (new) — 15 tests
- `packages/api/tests/routes/order-promotion-pricing.test.ts` — membership fixtures now drive the row, not the session, + one new regression test

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/gallery-join-order-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/order-promotion-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/gallery.test.ts tests/routes/gallery-join-intent.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (4 files, **79 passing**)
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/orders.test.ts` against the real DB (`:5440`, not the 5433 decoy)
- Result: PASS (**115 passing**, 0 skipped — beforeAll genuinely connected)
- Command: `bunx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0

The acceptance-bar test was written first and watched fail for the right reason: `expected '0.00' to be '800.00'` on join-then-order, and `expected '800.00' to be '0.00'` on the mirror case. 7 failed / 7 passed at RED.

---

⚠️ **Follow-up worth its own ticket — the #441 registration-intent path has the same staleness and cannot fix itself.** Verified against 1.4.17: better-auth writes the sign-in's cookie cache *after* `session.create.after` returns, from the user object it fetched *before* the hook ran, so anything `consumeJoinIntent` sets is overwritten a moment later. A visitor who joins by registering therefore carries a `galleryMember: false` cookie for up to five minutes.

Impact is bounded and **not financial** — order creation reads the row, so no price can be wrong; it is a stale render that #446 already papers over, and it self-heals in five minutes. Closing it properly means intercepting better-auth's own sign-in response. Documented in the `consumeJoinIntent` docblock so it is not rediscovered the hard way.

ticket.title: Bug - admin product writes never bust the product list cache (deleteCached against a key that is never written)
ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify by title, not number — numbers collided on 2026-08-06.**

`packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts` calls `deleteCached(CacheKeys.PRODUCT_LIST)` in five places. That is an **exact-key** delete against the literal string `"product-list:"`, which is only ever used as a PREFIX — real keys are `product-list:{queryHash}{:member|:guest}`. The literal key is never written, so the delete removes nothing and admin product edits do not bust the list cache at all.

This predates the sale work and is not limited to it: editing a product's title, price or status in admin leaves stale rows in the storefront list cache until the TTL lapses.

#525 (commit `17b5f421`) added `purgeProductResponseCache()`, which globs `product-list:*` and `product:*` via a SCAN cursor loop and correctly covers both `:member` and `:guest` variants. The fix here is to call that instead of the five no-op deletes.

While there: audit other `deleteCached(CacheKeys.X)` call sites for the same prefix-vs-key confusion. The bug is invisible in tests because a delete that matches nothing still resolves successfully.

## Context
Found by the #525 agent while implementing the promotion cache purge. Related: `packages/api/src/lib/redis.ts` (`deleteCachedPattern` is now SCAN-based, not `KEYS`).

**Verify against the real database:** `export $(grep -m1 '^DATABASE_URL=' /Users/dhruv/work/masonart.com/.env)` — port 5433 is a different application and a failed `beforeAll` there reports as *skipped*, which reads green.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:

**Commit**: `b6c6c493` — fix(api): admin product writes actually bust the storefront cache

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts` — all six mutating handlers now call `purgeProductResponseCache()`
- `packages/api/src/lib/redis.ts` — docstring only; records why naming keys cannot work, so a second purge does not grow beside it
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/product-cache-purge.test.ts` — new, 13 tests

**Root Cause**: `deleteCached(CacheKeys.PRODUCT_LIST)` is an exact-key `DEL` against the literal `"product-list:"`, which is only ever a *prefix*. Real keys are `product-list:<query-json><:member|:guest>`. `DEL` on a missing key resolves successfully, so five no-op deletes looked healthy.

**Location**: `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts:501, 625, 626, 628, 682, 683, 753, 845, 907`

**Fix**: `purgeProductResponseCache()` (already shared in `lib/redis.ts` from #525 — no lifting needed) on every mutating path.

**Two findings beyond the ticket's five call sites:**

1. **The detail-key deletes were broken too, not just the list ones.** `deleteCached(`${CacheKeys.PRODUCT}${slug}`)` targets `product:<slug>`, but the real key carries a viewer suffix (`viewerCacheSuffix`, `routes/products.ts:111`) — `product:<slug>:member` / `:guest`. |---|---|

ticket.title: A promotion that starts later still serves pre-sale prices from cache until the TTL lapses
ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify by title, not number.**

#525 (commit `17b5f421`) solved cache staleness at both ends of a *running* sale: writes purge the product response cache, and `saleCacheTtl` clamps every sale-carrying cache entry to the soonest active `endsAt` so it lapses with the sale.

The uncovered case is a sale **scheduled to start later**. The resolver only ever sees promotions that are already active, so a response cached at 09:00 for a sale starting at 10:00 carries no clamp and keeps serving base prices past the start time until its ordinary TTL expires. Nothing runs at 10:00 — active state is derived from the clock, which is exactly what makes the design self-managing everywhere else.

Same shape as the expiry problem, opposite end. Options:
- Clamp the TTL to the soonest *upcoming* `startsAt` as well as the soonest active `endsAt` — symmetric with what already exists, and cheap: the promotion list is already loaded and cached in process.
- Fold a coarse time bucket into the cache key.
- Accept it and require sales to be enabled at start time rather than scheduled — in which case say so in the admin UI beside `startsAt`, because a scheduling field that does not reliably schedule is worse than no field.

The first is recommended: `getActivePromotions()` would need a sibling that also returns the next start boundary, and `saleCacheTtl` takes `min(endsAt, nextStartsAt)`.

## Context
Found by the #525 agent. Files: `packages/api/src/lib/promotion-pricing.ts`, `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts`, `packages/api/src/routes/admin/promotions.ts`.

Related: the admin editor exposes `startsAt` as a first-class field (#433), so a merchandiser can reasonably expect scheduling to work.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `a24b0cce` — fix(api): a sale scheduled to start later starts on time

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/lib/promotion-pricing.ts` — new `getNextPromotionStart()`; `saleCacheTtl` takes `min(soonest active endsAt, next startsAt)`; the in-process memo now holds enabled+not-yet-ended rows and `getActivePromotions` filters them against the caller's `now`
- `packages/api/src/routes/products.ts` — `loadSaleContext` also returns `nextPromotionStart`; all four priced cache writes pass it
- `packages/api/tests/routes/product-scheduled-sale-cache.test.ts` — new end-to-end suite (TTL-honouring fake Redis, faked clock, real resolver)
- `packages/api/tests/lib/promotion-pricing.test.ts` — new signature + start-boundary and `getNextPromotionStart` cases
- `packages/api/tests/routes/product-sale-pricing.test.ts` — stubs the new loader alongside its siblings

**Summary**:
Took the recommended symmetric fix. One thing the ticket did not anticipate: clamping the response TTL alone does **not** fix it. The resolver's 60s memo stored "the rows that were active when I ran", so an entry expiring exactly on the start boundary was rebuilt from a memo that still reported nothing on sale — same wrong body, up to a minute more. The memo now holds every enabled, not-yet-ended row (active or scheduled) and active state is derived at read time. Still one query per minute; `getNextPromotionStart` shares the memo, so it costs nothing per request.

Side benefit: expiry tightened too — a promotion whose window closes mid-memo now stops pricing at once instead of when the memo lapses. `tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts` was read and not touched; its expiry leg polls `waitForNoActivePromotion()` with a timeout, so it only returns sooner.

A scheduled-but-disabled promotion clamps nothing — excluded in SQL and re-checked in JS, since nothing happens when the clock passes the `startsAt` of a switched-off sale.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/lib/promotion-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/product-sale-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/product-scheduled-sale-cache.test.ts tests/routes/product-facet-filters.test.ts tests/routes/product-facets.test.ts tests/routes/product-sort.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (6 files, 128 tests)
- Also PASS: `tests/routes/admin/promotion-cache-purge.test.ts` (11, the #525 suite, real DB) and the seven cart/order/promotion suites (88)
- New suite verified RED before the fix (4/6 failing), GREEN after
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the touched files

**Pre-existing, not mine**: `tests/routes/products.test.ts > should filter by styles` 400s because the test sends `styles=minimalist,abstract` and neither is a valid style id in `STYLE_OPTIONS` (`minimalist-art` is; `abstract` is a *subject*). Untouched by this change.

ticket.title: Home hero — full-bleed image carousel with peek slides replaces the text hero
ticket.description:
BAR: mesonart.com hero. Full-bleed lifestyle photograph carousel, rounded corners, adjacent slides peeking at both edges, campaign artwork burned into the image, single large outline pill CTA (SHOP All ART) bottom-right, dot indicators. Sits directly under the category rail with no white gap.

OURS TODAY: HeroSection in routes/index.tsx renders a centred text block on white — badge pill, two-line h1, 3-line paragraph, two buttons, trust row. Reads as a SaaS landing page, not an art storefront. This is the single biggest gap on the page.

Build a HomeHero component under app/components/home/. Desktop 1440 and mobile 390 both judged. Mobile: single slide, full-bleed, no peek, CTA stays reachable.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Blocker found while scoping, applies beyond this ticket: the repo has no interior/lifestyle photography. Everything available is product artwork in MinIO (products/*.webp), 7 frame swatches in public/frames/, 4 category jpgs in public/images/categories/, and two OG images. mesonart's hero, room band and promo tiles are all built on room photography of art hanging in styled interiors.

The previous hero pass hit the same wall — see the comment above HeroSection in routes/index.tsx: "The photography itself is Phase D — a contained slideshow needs room mockups we do not have yet."

So the carousel structure, peek slides, rounded frame, overlay and pill CTA can all reach parity now; the imagery inside them cannot until we have room mockups. Build the structure against real product artwork and flag the imagery gap rather than faking an interior.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Built `packages/web/app/components/home/HomeHero.tsx` (+ `packages/web/tests/components/home/HomeHero.test.tsx`, 17 tests). `app/routes/index.tsx` untouched — the integration step wires it in.

SUPERSEDES `HeroSection` in `app/routes/index.tsx` (the centred badge pill / h1 / paragraph / two-buttons / trust-row block). Left in place for the integration step to delete.

## Geometry — measured off the captured bar at device-pixel accuracy, then verified in a headless browser

| | bar | ours |
|---|---|---|
| desktop slide | 1344 x 553 at x=48 | 1344 x 553 at x=48 |
| desktop gap / peek | 30 / 18px each edge | 30 / 18px each edge |
| desktop pill | 229.5 x 45, inset 60/60 from the slide's right and bottom | 218 x 45, inset 60/60 |
| mobile slide | 349.5 x 513.5 at x=20, no peek | 350 x 514 at x=20, no peek |
| mobile pill | 309.5 x 40, inset 20/20, 10px off the bottom | 310 x 40, inset 20/20, 10px off the bottom |
| band padding | none — slide starts 10px under the category rail | none |

The peek is not positioned anywhere: with a track inset `I` and gap `G` a neighbour shows exactly `I - G`. 48/30 gives the desktop's 18px, 20/20 gives the phone's zero. Slide width is `100%` of the track's content box (already narrowed by the inset), so no `100vw` and no scrollbar overhang. The track is capped at `--page-width` and centred, so past 1600px the hero stays 56px narrower than `.container-wide`, as it is at 1440.

## Decisions

- **Both edges peek** — the bar shows a slide at the LEFT edge while its first slide is showing, which `scrollLeft: 0` cannot do. The track renders `[last, ...slides, first]` and starts one step in; when a clone settles under the snap point the position jumps to its real twin with `behavior: 'instant'`, invisible because they are the same photograph. Scroll position is the only state, so a swipe and an arrow press cannot disagree.
- **Two source crops per slide** via `<picture>`: a wide asset above `md`, a tall one below. Desktop `aspect-[1344/553]`, mobile `aspect-[349/513]` (the mobile box matches the source ratio, so nothing is cropped there).
- **Pill border is 1px, not the system's 2px `--border-button`.** Measured: their standard buttons sit on white and carry 2px; the hero pill sits on a photograph and carries 1, and the difference is visible side by side. Everything else is `buttonVariants({ variant: 'outline' })` retinted white, so the hover wipe and pill radius stay the system's.
- **No scrim.** I built one, screenshotted it next to the bar, and removed it: the bar has none and a scrim greys the bottom of the photograph the band exists to show. Legibility comes from the pill's white outline, as it does on the bar.
- **No arrows or dots at rest**, matching the bar. The track is a real tab stop with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (same shape as `product/ProductCarousel`); circular arrows fade in on hover or keyboard focus only, so they are absent from a screenshot. Autoplay 6s, pauses on hover/focus, does not run at all under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **An `sr-only` h1.** The bar's hero has no heading element — its words are pixels — but dropping ours would leave the home page with no h1. It carries the route's own `<title>` claim.
- **CTA "Shop All Art" -> `/posters`**, one for the whole band (the overlay sits above the track, not inside every slide) so N slides do not put N identically-named links on the page.

## Real data

Nothing in this component reads or prints a promotion. The "Late Summer / Home Refresh Event / 40% off" wording in the band is pixels inside the placeholder JPEG, not copy this file writes — and that is also how the real band will work, since the slide is a merchandising slot with the campaign composited into the asset, exactly as the bar does it. A test asserts the rendered band contains no `%`, no "off", no "sale", and that the file never touches `/api/promotions/active`. The sale surfaces (`SaleStrip`, `SaleBanner`, sale pricing) keep owning that, against a real row.

I did build and then remove a promotion-driven HTML lockup (headline + `percentOff`, de-duplicated when the headline already quoted a percentage). It double-printed against the burned-in artwork and, more importantly, it was my invention — the bar's hero does not read its promotion table. Worth revisiting only if we ever want a campaign line over photography that has none.

## Photography

Per the coordinator's brief the slides are the bar's own, from the git-ignored `packages/web/public/dev-reference/hero/`. Routed through ONE exported constant, `HERO_SLIDES` (with `HERO_IMAGE_BASE` beside it); a test asserts the directory is named on exactly one non-comment line of the file, so replacing them is an edit to that table and nothing else. Nothing outside this band references the directory. #544 blocks go-live.

The directory is git-ignored, so a clone that has not run `scripts/dev/fetch-reference-imagery.sh` has no images. An `onError` on any slide hides the WHOLE band rather than painting broken-image glyphs above the fold — pinned by a test.

## Correction to the scoping comment above

"the repo has no interior/lifestyle photography" is no longer true of the seeded catalogue. Every one of the 41 dev products carries three `room-mockup` images, and a good share of them are exactly what this band wants: the artwork photographed hanging in a styled interior (`digital-cosmos-1` is a lounge with a sofa and a cane chair, `neon-dreams-1` a living room, `wabi-sabi-study-1` an entryway). They come from `.cache/seed-media` via `packages/api/src/database/seed-images.ts`. Two caveats, which is why they are not the source here: they are square 1500x1500, so both a wide and a tall crop would have to be cut before they can fill these boxes, and the set is mixed — some mockups are tight detail shots of a frame edge rather than a room. Noted in the file header as the second source for when #544 comes round. (Watermarks on some of them are #546 and were not a factor in any choice here.)

Status stays in-progress until a critic picks ours blind.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Blind A/B result: OURS WINS on both desktop and mobile. The critic did not know which page was which.

Faults it named on the reference: three unrelated type treatments inside one three-line lockup (light wide teal geometric, heavy tight white grotesque, ultra-bold gold carrying both a white keyline and a drop shadow) reading as three one-offs from a discount banner; their CTA pill centred 145px right of the copy it belongs to; their nominally-centred stack drifting 21px left line by line so no two lines share an axis; their mobile inverting the hierarchy relative to their own desktop. comments.text:
Fix round after the blind A/B loss (desktop + mobile). All five defects addressed; measurements before/after below. Still in-progress — needs a re-run of the blind A/B.

== 1. Artwork scale not normalised across a row (the decisive desktop failure)

ROOT CAUSE, and it is NOT a card defect. `matToSquare` bakes the mat into the pixels: art is contained at MAT_ART_INSET (88%) of its LONGEST side on a 1500x1500 canvas. That normalises one axis and nothing else, and the stored asset then says `1500x1500` for a 3:1 panorama and a perfect square alike — the storefront has no way to tell them apart. Measured art aspects in the dev catalogue run 0.53:1 to 1.96:1, and `product.orientation` does not track them (desert-bloom is labelled `square`, its photograph is 1.96:1), so no existing field could stand in.

Measured on the rail at 1440 (plate 321px), ink as a share of the plate:
  BEFORE  79% / 41% / 77% / 42%   -> 1.93:1 spread
  AFTER   55% / 46% / 55% / 50%   -> 1.20:1 spread
  BAR     65% / 65% / 73% / 70%   -> 1.12:1 spread
The bar gets its evenness for free: all four of its photographs are between 0.77:1 and 1.02:1.

FIX — supply the missing measurement, then use it:
- `ProductImage.artBox` (optional, `@chobii/shared`): where the art sits inside its square master, normalised. Additive to the existing `images` JSONB, so no migration.
- `measureArtBox()` (`packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts`): recovers the box from the composited output by scanning for non-MAT_COLOR pixels at MAT_CANVAS/4 with a nearest kernel. Reads the stored asset rather than the geometry that produced it, which is what lets one function serve both new uploads and the backfill.
- `buildProductMedia` populates it for every new artwork upload.
- `bun run backfill:art-box` (`packages/api/src/database/backfill-art-box.ts`): one-off, additive, idempotent, `--dry-run`/`--force`. Fetches each asset over HTTP (public bucket, no credentials), measures, writes one key into the JSONB. No re-processing, no re-upload, no URL changes. RUN AGAINST DEV: 41/41 products, 163 images scanned, 41 measured, 122 skipped (only `main` is matted; cropped photographs are full-bleed and correctly get no box), 0 failed.
- `app/components/product/artFraming.ts`: given a box, returns `clip-path` (crops the baked mat off) + `transform` (scales and centres the piece to ART_AREA = 0.52 of the plate, clamped so no side passes ART_MAX_SIDE = 0.95). Both are paint-time only, so the row-alignment contract — one in-flow image carrying MEDIA_RATIO, hover slides `absolute inset-0` — is untouched, and `ProductCardMedia`'s existing structure tests still pass unchanged.

Air is now symmetric per card (gapT == gapB: 46/46, 83/83, 47/47, 8/8), which is the bar's own rule — its four cards measure 32/32, 32/32, 8/8, 7/7.

DEGRADES CLEANLY: no `artBox` -> no style -> exactly today's rendering. Nothing in the pipeline changed for existing pixels.

== 2. Plate at #FAFAFA on white (2% contrast)

The plate could not simply be recoloured: the visible grey WAS the baked mat, so the image covered the plate edge to edge and `--mat` was inert. Cropping the mat away in (1) is what makes a plate colour visible at all.

- New `--plate` token, separate from `--mat`. They are different things: `--mat` is what sharp bakes into pixels (still pinned to MAT_COLOR by tests/styles/mat-token.test.ts, unchanged); `--plate` is the surface the card draws under them and no pixels depend on it.
- Value rgb(239 239 239), measured directly off the reference capture as the mode of the plate ring across all four Best Seller cards (12,228 samples). The other review's #ECEDEA is 3 levels off this; both are ~4% against white where ours was 2%.
- Held as `PLATE_BG = 'bg-[hsl(var(--plate))]'` in productCardTokens rather than a `colors` entry, because a tailwind.config colour needs a dev-server restart to exist and a token that only a restart can make real silently does nothing.
Verified rendered: plate computes to rgb(239, 239, 239).

== 3. Mobile: no shared picture baseline

Equal-area framing plus symmetric air narrows the bottom-gap delta between neighbours from 60px (19 vs 79) to 38px (44 vs 82), and the band under a picture is now a visible plate rather than an invisible one. Deliberately NOT hard baseline-anchored: the bar centres its pieces (gapT == gapB on all four), and a baseline anchor pushed a 1.96:1 piece into a large empty top band and clipped the tallest piece.

== 4. Mobile "Choose Options"

Was a 163x37 white pill printed permanently across the artwork's lower third — white on pale cream, no edge of its own, centred horizontally and bottom-anchored 25px, i.e. centred on one axis and arbitrary on the other. Flagged independently by three reviews.

Below `md` it is now a 40px round corner button at the same 16px inset the quick-view eye uses on the opposite corner, with a shadow so it has an edge against a light picture. From `md` up it is unchanged: the measured 172x40 white pill at radius 60, revealed on hover, which costs the picture nothing because at rest it is not drawn. Accessible name stays "Choose Options" (`sr-only md:not-sr-only`), so it is not an unlabelled glyph.

== 5. Band rhythm

The bar's Best Seller band runs 617px from heading top to pill foot; ours runs 616 — the content stacks are the same object. The difference was air. Overrode SectionBand's `py-16 sm:py-24` with `py-12 sm:py-14` on the rail only (both breakpoints named — twMerge only resolves a conflict within one variant, so `py-12` alone would leave `sm:py-24` standing), and tightened the heading margin.

  desktop  heading->artwork 46 -> 34 (bar: 32) | track->pill 48 (bar: 46.5, kept)
           pill->band edge 96 -> 56 | band height 814 -> 722
           pill pocket 48/96 -> 48/56 (bar's own ratio: 46.5/63.5)
  mobile   pill pocket 41/64 -> 40/48

Remaining page-level item, NOT this ticket: two adjacent bands still put 56 + 96 = 152px between this pill and the next heading against the bar's 63.5, because every other band still carries SectionBand's default. That is a SectionBand change affecting every band on the page.

== LCP

`ProductCardMedia` hardcoded `loading="lazy"`. Added `priority` on ProductCardMedia -> ProductCard -> ProductRail; BestSellersRail sets it, NewInRail does not. Only the FIRST card of the first band under the hero goes `loading="eager" fetchpriority="high"`; hover slides stay lazy. Verified rendered: Best Seller card 1 `eager`, New In card 1 `lazy`.

== Not regressed — kept as measured

The meta row is untouched: heart in slate #647B8B sharing an exact right edge with the price, price 15px under the title. Both reviews called it the better-finished one against the bar's near-invisible #D6D6D6 heart.

== /posters and /collections/$slug (both signed off at parity)

Screenshotted at 1440 and 390 before and after. Nothing became opt-in — every change improves those surfaces too, so gating them per surface would have shipped the worse version to the pages that are already signed off:
- /posters desktop: same grid, same chrome, same heights (no CLS). Plates visible, row ink evened out the same way.
- /posters mobile: the biggest single win — four permanent white "Choose Options" slabs across four artworks replaced by four 40px corner buttons.
- PDP: pixel-diffed before/after. The ONLY differing region is y 1439-1691, the "Visually Similar Artworks" row, which is ProductCard. Gallery, buy box, frame swatches and tabs are byte-identical.

== Tests

  web  tests/components/product + tests/components/home + tests/styles: 820 passed, 1 failed
       The failure is tests/styles.test.ts "no dark: utility variants in app source", offender
       app/routes/admin/promotions/index.tsx — committed code I did not touch. PRE-EXISTING.
  web  tsc --noEmit: 22 errors, all in admin/track/ai-generator. Exactly the known baseline, none
       in any file touched here.
  api  tsc --noEmit: 0.  shared tsc --noEmit: 0.
  api  image-processing mat/crop/seed-media suites: 38 passed (unchanged).

New tests: tests/components/product/artFraming.test.ts (14), packages/api/tests/lib/image-processing-art-box.test.ts (10), plus framing/LCP cases on ProductCardMedia, the two trigger shapes on ChooseOptions, and LCP + band-padding cases on ProductRail. ProductCard.tokens.test.ts's "keeps the baked mat colour" assertion now asserts PLATE_BG and the absence of bg-mat, with the reason inline — the mat/plate split is the point, and --mat is still pinned to MAT_COLOR where that pairing belongs.
