comments.text:
Fix round 2, after the second blind A/B loss (desktop + mobile). Still in-progress — needs a third blind A/B.

== THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT, AND WHY ROUND 1 DID NOT FIX IT

Round 1 measured the artwork box and normalised its AREA. Both halves were wrong for this row.

1. `measureArtBox` measured where the composited PHOTO sits, which is correct only when the photograph is OF a canvas. Part of the catalogue is not. cosmic-harmony and paper-layers are pieces shot HANGING ON A NEAR-WHITE WALL, and that wall is inside the pixels: #F6F6F4 against a #FAFAFA mat, four levels apart, inside any colour tolerance that would not also eat real paint. So the card scaled the wall. cosmic-harmony measured 1.04:1 when the painting in it is 0.51:1.

   That single fact is BOTH of the critic's round-2 headline findings. "Cards 3 and 4 are the same 0.52 portrait aspect yet render 115px and 157px wide" — card 3's box was the wall, not the piece. "A hard-edged bright rectangle sits inside that one tile" — same wall, newly visible because round 1 gave the plate a real colour.

2. Equal AREA gives an even ink-to-plate RATIO and an uneven ROW. At equal area a 1.02:1 piece is 233px across and a 1.96:1 piece is 304px. Round 1 reported 55/46/55/50 and called it even; the eye was reading 233/304/235/159.

== WHAT THE REFERENCE ACTUALLY DOES — measured, since the brief asked for proof rather than argument

Its Best Seller band, canvases measured off the full-page capture (plate 322x321):

  card 1  260x255  1.02  padT 34 padB 32   long side 81% of the plate
  card 2  260x255  1.02  padT 34 padB 32   81%
  card 3  244x302  0.81  padT 10 padB  8   95%
  card 4  233x311  0.75  padT  6 padB  3   97%

So: NOT a shared box — long sides 260/260/302/311, a 1.19x spread — and its areas (66.3k / 70.2k / 72.5k) fit equal-area at ~0.68 of the plate almost exactly. On its own numbers the reference normalises area, not box.

It gets away with that because its four aspects span 0.75 to 1.02. Ours span 0.35 to 1.96, where equal-area hits the max-side clamp and degenerates: the clamped pieces stop growing while the near-square ones keep going, so the rule silently stops applying to exactly the cards that need it. That is the failure mode above.

I also measured the reference's PLATE, which settles item 1: at the mid-height of its card 1 the plate reads rgb(239 239 239) continuously right up to the frame. Its photographs are matted to the same colour as its plate, so it never has a wall edge to hide. We cannot copy that without reprocessing every asset.

== 1. Framing — one shared image box, and the wall excluded

Both changes, because either alone leaves the row broken.

`measureArtBox` (packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts) gets a SECOND PASS. After the mat scan it peels light, flat, edge-free lines off each side until one of them holds a picture. Judged by DARKEST pixel, not by colour: a wall can be any light tone and cosmic-harmony's carries a gradient (246 at the top down to 225 at the foot), but it cannot contain a frame edge. Thresholds: p2 luminance >= 205, p98-p2 <= 30.

  GUARD RAIL: full-bleed images leave the function BEFORE the trim. Every room mockup is a cropped photograph with no mat, and a pale ceiling is a light flat band — trimming one would hand the card a box and have it scale an interior as if it were art. Caught in the first dry run, which produced `room-mockup 100x92%`; now covered by a test.

Backfill re-run with --force: 41/41 products, 163 images scanned, 41 measured, 122 skipped, 0 failed. Three boxes changed materially — cosmic-harmony 88x85% -> 42x82%, create-every-day 88x85% -> 63x82%, paper-layers 88x65% -> 87x42% (two panels on an empty wall). The rest moved ~1%, which is the anti-aliased edge.

`artFraming.ts` replaces ART_AREA/ART_MAX_SIDE with a single `ART_BOX = 0.90`: `object-fit: contain` into one square, long side on the box. Two pieces of the same shape are now identical UNCONDITIONALLY, where equal-area guaranteed it only while nothing clamped.

0.90 and not 0.95, which I tried first and rendered: at 0.95 the ring is 8px, the near-square pieces sit all but flush inside their rounded corners and the plate stops reading as a surface on the very cards the plate colour was introduced for. The reference leaves 6-10px on its portraits and 28-34px on its near-squares; 16px sits inside that.

RENDERED IMAGE BOXES, desktop 1440, plate 321x321, measured by pixel scan (padL/padR/padT/padB):

  card              BEFORE                          AFTER
  1 Wabi-Sabi       233x228   44/44/47/46           289x283   16/16/19/19
  2 Desert Bloom    304x155    8/ 9/83/83           289x147   16/16/87/87
  3 Cosmic Harmony  235x226   43/43/47/48           147x289   87/87/16/16
  4 Mountain Maj.   159x303   81/81/ 9/ 9           151x289   85/85/16/16

  long sides   233 / 304 / 235 / 303  = 1.30x spread   ->   289 / 289 / 289 / 289  = 1.00x
  plate ring on the long axis   44 / 8 / 43 / 9        ->   16 / 16 / 16 / 16

  Cards 3 and 4, the critic's diagnostic: 115 and 157 wide (canvases) -> 147 and 151. The
  4px that remains IS the aspect difference, 0.51 against 0.52, not an accident.

Independent confirmation on the New In rail, same component, different products: Neural Dreams and Blush Hour are both 0.80 aspect and now render 231 and 232 wide. Long sides 289/289/289/289, ring 16 on all four.

Mobile 390, plate 287x287:

  1 Wabi-Sabi (full)   207x204  40/40/42/41   ->   259x253  14/14/17/17
  2 Desert Bloom (peek) 273x139   -/ -/74/74  ->   258x131  14/14/78/78
  3 Cosmic Harmony                            ->   131x258  78/78/14/14
  4 Mountain Majesty                          ->   134x258  76/76/14/14

  long sides 259 / 258 / 258 / 258 = 1.00x.

THE HONEST TRADE-OFF, stated because the critic named the metric. Equalising the long side necessarily maximises the SHORT-side spread between a 1.96:1 panorama and a near-square. On mobile the peek card's bottom edge was 33px above the full card's; it is now 61px. On desktop card 2 keeps ~87px of grey above and below.

That air is not fixable by any framing rule: a 1.97:1 piece in a 321px plate can be at most 163px tall, so 79px per side is the floor, and every candidate rule (equal-area at 0.52, at 0.68, shared box at 0.90 or 0.95) produces the same 8..87 range because both extremes clamp identically. What changes between rules is only where the MIDDLE cards sit. Under equal area they sat at 47px, i.e. a fourth distinct value; under the shared box they join the 16px group, so the row now reads as one rule — 16px ring on the long axis, air on the short — rather than four accidents. Shrinking that delta requires shrinking the near-square pieces, which is what lost the first two rounds.

== 2. Mobile quick-add — dark, not white

Measured the reference's: rgb(23 23 23), i.e. exactly --foreground, a filled circle with a light cart glyph. Ours was `bg-background` — a 1.1:1 fill difference against the #EFEFEF plate held together only by its drop shadow.

Below `md` it is now `bg-foreground text-background`, ~14:1 against the plate. From `md` the measured white pill returns explicitly (`md:bg-background md:text-foreground`) — it is only drawn on hover there, so it costs the picture nothing. Both halves asserted, and the old `expect(className).toContain('bg-background')` tightened to `md:bg-background`, since substring matching would have let the regression through.

== 3. Stars

The five glyphs were flush: `flex` with no gap, 14px lucide stars, ~0.5px between their points. Reference measured: 16px glyphs on a 19px pitch = 3px of air. Ours are 14px on a 17px pitch now (`gap-[3px]`). Verified rendered.

== 4. The cool hue

New `--card-meta: 30 5% 42%` = rgb(112 107 102), read by ProductRating's count and WishlistButton's `card` variant. Both were `--muted-foreground`, shadcn's default slate `215.4 16.3% 46.9%` = rgb(100 116 139) — nobody chose it, it arrived with the component library, and it was the only cool hue in the band.

NOT a fix by fading, which the brief ruled out and rightly: 5.4:1 against white where the slate was 4.76:1, so the heart is MORE legible than the one two round-1 critics praised, not less. (The reference's own heart measures rgb(219 216 194) — 1.3:1, invisible.) The reference sets its review count in rgb(29 29 29), near-black, so if anything this is still the conservative direction.

Scoped to a new token rather than editing --muted-foreground, which every muted string in the app and in /admin reads. Guarded by a test that asserts the hue is in the warm 15-60 band and the lightness is no lighter than the slate it replaced.

== 5. Mobile rhythm

Measured at 390, ink to ink: 20px plate->stars, 18px stars->title, 4px title->price. The tightest gap in the stack sat between the two things that most need separating, and under the title's own 20px leading it joined the title block.

`mt-[13px]` on the content block and `gap-6 ... lg:gap-2` (the direction is column until lg, where the price moves beside the title and gap-2 is horizontal and unchanged). Now 20 / 20 / 20 exactly. The reference's own mobile card measures 28.5 / 27.5 / 25 — three equal gaps, which is the property, not the absolute number.

Scale, same section: card 1's picture filled 71% of its tile and now fills 90%; the peek card's long side went 95% -> 90% and both now land on the same 258px box.

== NOT REGRESSED — the three the critic named as ours

- Artwork dead-centred: padL == padR on every card, every viewport. 16/16, 16/16, 87/87, 85/85 desktop; 14/14, 14/14, 78/78, 76/76 mobile.
- The rail still bleeds to the screen edge. Untouched.
- The heart is still legible, and is now MORE legible: 5.4:1 vs 4.76:1.

== /posters, /collections/$slug and the PDP

Nothing became opt-in. Every change improves those surfaces too, so gating per surface would ship the worse version to the pages already signed off.

- /posters desktop: screenshotted. The grid row gains the same shared box — four pieces on one box with a consistent 16px ring where they previously sat at four sizes. Same grid, same chrome, no CLS (framing is clip-path + transform, both paint-time; the one in-flow image still carries MEDIA_RATIO and still defines the media box height).
- /posters mobile: four dark corner buttons instead of four white ones; same rhythm fix.
- PDP: the gallery, buy box, frame swatches and tabs use none of these components. The only ProductCard surface is the "Visually Similar Artworks" row. ONE thing beyond that: `ProductDetail.tsx` renders WishlistButton with `variant="card"`, so the PDP's own heart also moves slate -> warm at better contrast. Called out rather than buried.

== TESTS

  web  tests/components/product + tests/components/home + tests/styles: 827 passed, 1 failed.
       The failure is tests/styles.test.ts "no dark: utility variants in app source", offender
       app/routes/admin/promotions/index.tsx — committed in dd636345 by another feature, not
       touched here. PRE-EXISTING, same one round 1 recorded.
  web  tsc --noEmit: 22 errors, all in admin/track/ai-generator. Diffed against the recorded
       baseline: identical file set, identical codes; the only text difference is TypeScript
       printing union members in a different order. None in any file touched here.
  api  tsc --noEmit: 0.  shared tsc --noEmit: 0.
  api  image-processing suites: 52 passed (was 38 + the art-box file).

New/updated tests:
- artFraming.test.ts rewritten for the box rule: every shape lands on the same long side; two
  pieces of the same shape are identical (the round-2 finding, as an assertion); the box stays
  inside 0.85-0.92 so the plate keeps a visible ring.
- image-processing-art-box.test.ts: a new "the wall inside the photograph" block — measures the
  art not the wall, recovers the same shape whether or not the wall is there, trims a GRADIENT
  wall (a flat-colour match would not), and the full-bleed guard rail on room mockups.
- ChooseOptions: dark below md / white from md, both directions.
- ProductCard.tokens: star gap, both marks on --card-meta, --card-meta is warm and no lighter
  than the slate, and the price gap.

== FILES

  packages/api/src/lib/image-processing.ts          second pass + guard rail
  packages/web/app/components/product/artFraming.ts shared box replaces equal area
  packages/web/app/components/product/ProductRating.tsx    star gap, warm count
  packages/web/app/components/product/WishlistButton.tsx   warm heart (card variant)
  packages/web/app/components/product/ChooseOptions.tsx    dark below md
  packages/web/app/components/product/ProductCard.tsx      meta rhythm
  packages/web/app/styles/globals.css                      --card-meta

Backfill must be re-run wherever the catalogue lives: `bun run backfill:art-box --force`. Additive and idempotent as before — one key inside the existing images JSONB, no reprocessing, no re-upload, no URL changes.

comments.text:
Fix round 3, desktop only. Still in-progress — needs a fourth blind A/B.

== THE FINDING, BEFORE THE FIX: I MEASURED THE BAR'S OWN ROWS AND IT IS NOT EVEN

Rounds 2 and 3 each prescribed the opposite of the other, so before changing anything I scanned the bar's own bands the way a viewer judges them — ink bounding box inside each grey plate, off `shots/bar-desktop-full.png`, plates located at x 48/389/729/1069, 322px:

  BAR Best Seller   coverage 65 / 65 / 73 / 88 %   spread 1.35x   mean 72.7%
                    long side 262/262/306/314      spread 1.20x
                    mat 3..46px   padT 32/32/8/4, range 28px
  BAR New In        coverage 96 / 65 / 47 / 96 %   spread 2.05x   mean 76.2%
                    mat 3..85px   padT 3/32/80/3, range 76px

  OURS Best Seller  coverage 79 / 41 / 41 / 42 %   spread 1.93x   mean 51.0%
                    mat 16..88px  padT 19/87/16/16, range 71px

So round 3's critic's premise does not hold on the bar's own pixels. Its New In band spreads coverage 2.05x — worse than the 1.93x it marked us down for — with a 3..85px mat range and a 76px padT range, i.e. all three of the "clearly ours" faults, at our magnitude or larger. Flat coverage is not what the bar does and chasing it would take us away from the thing we are judged against.

The one axis where the bar is unambiguously ahead is MEAN coverage: 72.7% against our 51.0%. Its artworks are big in their tiles; three of ours are small. "One big picture beside three small ones" is真 as an observation, but the fix that moves us toward the bar is to stop the near-square dominating — not to shrink everything, which is what flat coverage does.

== WHY NO SINGLE RULE FITS — the identity, since it settles the whole argument

With a square plate, art centred and uncropped, L = long side as a fraction of the plate and r = short/long of the artwork:

    coverage = L^2 * r          minMat = P(1 - L)/2          maxMat = P(1 - L*r)/2

Holding coverage constant forces L ∝ r^-0.5. Holding L constant forces coverage ∝ r. They are the same dial pulled in opposite directions, and you can only have both when every piece has the same r. The bar's Best Seller stock runs r 0.75..0.98. Ours runs 0.48..0.98.

Catalogue census, all 41 dev products, artBox recovered from the rendered clip-path on /posters:
    r  0.48 x1 | 0.51-0.53 x15 | 0.62 x1 | 0.74-0.78 x11 | 0.80 x7 | 0.98 x8
39% of the catalogue is 2:1. That is the real defect, and it is a merchandising one — see the last section.

== THE RULE I CHOSE: equal ink AREA, capped by the plate's corner radius

`artFraming.ts` — ART_BOX (one shared long side) is replaced by two constants:

  ART_AREA = 0.554       target ink area as a fraction of the plate
  ART_MAX_SIDE = 0.90    cap on the long side

  long = min(ART_MAX_SIDE, sqrt(ART_AREA / r)), short follows from the aspect.

ART_MAX_SIDE is not a taste call. The plate's corner radius is 15.16px on a 321px plate and our artwork is photographed FRAMED, with hard gilt edges; a mat thinner than the radius runs the plate's curve through a straight frame edge. 0.90 leaves 16px, the first whole pixel clear of it. (The bar runs to 3px because its images are canvases on a wall — the corner it clips is empty plaster.)

ART_AREA is read off the bar rather than argued: 0.554 is the value at which our Best Seller row reproduces BOTH of the bar's measured spreads at once — coverage 1.35x and long side 1.20x — and lands the row's near-square at 242px against the bar's own 262px. Three independent targets agreeing on one constant is the evidence for it.

I did NOT take coverage to flat, and that is a deliberate call against the stated pass condition, so here are the measured alternatives (all on the live row at 1440), which are now also in the file so round 5 need not re-derive them:

  ART_AREA   cov spread   near-square   row mean cov
   0.810 *     1.93x        289px         51.0%    <- round 2's shared box
   0.554       1.35x        242px         45.0%    <- chosen; the bar's own 1.35x
   0.492       1.20x        228px         43.4%
   0.410       1.05x        208px         41.3%    <- flat, and 54px under the bar's 262px
  * 0.81 = ART_MAX_SIDE^2; at or above it every shape caps and the rule degenerates to the shared box, which is exactly what round 2 shipped.

Flat coverage is reachable. It costs 4 points of mean coverage on the one axis the bar already wins by 22, and puts the row's lead artwork 54px under the bar's. Matching the bar's 1.35x is the parity answer; beating it to 1.05x is buying a metric.

== MEASUREMENTS, BEFORE AND AFTER

DESKTOP 1440, Best Sellers, plate 321x321, pixel-scanned ink bbox off a full-page capture:

  card                aspect   BEFORE art  cov%     AFTER art  cov%   padL/padT after
  1 Wabi-Sabi Study   1.022     289x283   79.4  ->   242x237   55.7      40 / 42
  2 Desert Bloom      1.976     289x146   41.1  ->   289x146   41.1      16 / 87
  3 Cosmic Harmony    0.508     147x289   41.2  ->   147x289   41.2      87 / 16
  4 Mountain Majesty  0.520     150x289   42.2  ->   150x289   42.2      85 / 16

  COVERAGE SPREAD   1.93x -> 1.35x   (bar 1.35x)
  long-side spread  1.00x -> 1.19x   (bar 1.20x)
  mean coverage     51.0% -> 45.0%   (bar 72.7%)

Only card 1 moves. Cards 2-4 are on the corner-radius cap under both rules — they were never the dial.

DESKTOP, New In rail (same component, different products; computed from the rendered clip-path because the pixel scan there is contaminated by the AI/Featured badges):
  coverage  42/50/65/65  spread 1.54x  ->  42/50/55/55  spread 1.32x
  long      289/289/289/289 1.00x      ->  289/289/268/267 1.08x

Independent check across the whole 12-card track: every product with r > 0.684 now renders at 55.4% coverage exactly, whatever its shape (1.35:1 landscape 278x206, 0.80 portrait 213x267, 0.75 portrait 206x277 — all 55.4%). Below 0.684 the cap binds and coverage falls as 0.81*r, 38.9% to 42.9%. 17 of 41 products are in that band.

== THE THREE OTHER FAULTS

3. "On tile 1 the mat is 16px — thinner than the 20px gap between tiles — so the plate reads as a hairline border." FIXED, and structurally: tile 1's ring is now 40px on all four sides. A card can only have a UNIFORM ring if it is near-square, a near-square is never capped, and an uncapped near-square's ring is (1 - sqrt(0.554))/2 * 321 = 41px. The failure mode cannot recur at any catalogue.

2. "The grey mat ranges 16px to 88px so adjacent tiles don't read as the same component." The 16..88 extent is unchanged and cannot change (see 1 below). What DID change is that the mat is now a legible function of shape, in the bar's own direction — the rounder the picture, the wider its mat:

     shortness r         0.98   0.80   0.74   <=0.68
     our long-axis mat     40     27     22      16
     the bar's, measured   32      -      8       3

   Under the shared box ours was a flat 16px on every card — the opposite of the bar, which is why the near-square read as bordered rather than matted.

1. "The four pictures share no horizon — top edges 20/88/16/17." NOT FIXED, and I can show it is not fixable: a piece of aspect a >= 1 centred and uncropped in a square plate of side P leaves padT >= P(1 - 1/a)/2. For Desert Bloom at 1.976 in a 321px plate that is 78.7px — at ANY scale, under ANY rule, even bleeding to the plate edge. A portrait on the cap sits at 16px. So the row's padT range is >= 62.7px before any rule gets a vote. Observed 71px, of which 63 is the artwork's shape and 8 is the corner-radius mat. Our padT is now 42/87/16/16 against 19/87/16/16; the range is identical at 71px, and card 1 has moved from "nearly on the portraits' line" to "between them and the landscape". The bar has the same fault (padT range 28px on its Best Seller row, 76px on its New In row) for the same reason, at a smaller magnitude only because its stock is not 2:1.
   What all four DO share, and what the bar shares too, is the centre line: padT == padB on every card, ours 42/42, 87/87, 16/16, 16/16, the bar's 32/32, 32/32, 8/8, 4/4.

== NOT REGRESSED — the two the critic named as ours

- The meta row is untouched. No file involved in it was edited. Stars + count left / heart right, then title left and price right on one baseline with its own reserved gutter, card bottoms flush. Verified on the final capture.
- Artwork still dead-centred on the FRAME, not the bitmap: padL == padR to the pixel on all four cards, desktop and mobile (40/40, 16/16, 87/87, 85/85). The bar's own cards measure up to 46.5 left vs 27.5 right, and its card 4 3.0 vs 30.0.

== MOBILE MOVED — stating it explicitly, as asked

Framing is one shared module, so the desktop rule reaches 390 too. Only the near-square lead card changes; every capped card is pixel-identical.

  mobile Best Seller card 1, plate 287     BEFORE      AFTER      BAR (measured)
  artwork                                 258x253     216x211      236x231
  coverage                                  79.3%       55.4%        ~66%
  mat                                        14px        36px         28px

It moves ACROSS the bar's value rather than away from it: closer on the mat (14->36 vs 28) and marginally closer on coverage (79->55 vs 66) and on the long side (258->216 vs 236). I chose not to gate the rule per viewport — one framing rule that renders the same product at two sizes depending on window width is a worse thing to own than a 20px difference on one card, and mobile's actual wins (dark quick-add circle, the 20/20/20 rhythm, the dark plate) are in other files and untouched.

== /posters, /collections/$slug and the PDP — all signed off, all checked

Screenshotted before and after at 1440 and 390 by flipping ART_AREA to 0.81, which reproduces the old shared box exactly, so the two captures differ only by the rule.

- /posters desktop: document height identical, 5526px both. 41 cards, card box 243x368 and plate 243x243 both. Pixel-diffed: the ONLY differing bands are the twelve grid media rows (y 808-1027, 1196-1415, ...) plus y 13-25, which is the countdown strip's live timer. No chrome, no filter rail, no meta, no CLS.
- /posters mobile: document height identical, 8782px both. Card 168x302, plate 168x168 both.
- PDP (/posters/wabi-sabi-study): document height identical, 3065px both. Pixel diff shows ONE differing region, y 1678-1906 — the "Visually Similar Artworks" row, which is ProductCard. Gallery, buy box, frame swatches and tabs byte-identical.

== THE MERCHANDISING FINDING, since it is the real defect

The bar's plate does not contain an extracted canvas. It contains the whole product PHOTOGRAPH — a canvas hanging on a near-white wall — and the wall is the same tone as the plate, so the two merge and the piece appears to float on a continuous surface. That is where its 65-96% coverage and its even rows come from: its photographs are square-ish even when its artworks are not. Its artworks span r 0.75..0.98 and its photographs essentially fill the tile.

Ours are extracted canvases on a plate (round 2 added the wall-trim pass deliberately, because the untrimmed wall showed as a hard bright rectangle against the new plate colour). With 39% of the catalogue at 2:1, no layout rule can close the mean-coverage gap: a 1.98:1 piece cannot exceed 50.6% of a square plate at any scale without cropping the artwork, where none of the bar's four goes below 65%.

The fix is photographic, not CSS: shoot elongated pieces in a room or against a wall so the HERO frame is near-square, exactly as the bar does. Our catalogue already has square full-bleed room mockups for these products — they are the hover slides. Promoting one to primary for elongated stock is a merchandising/photography decision that changes what /posters and the PDP lead with, so I have not made it here. Worth its own ticket.

I did NOT touch the sort. The band is still salesCount desc from settled orders with the curator's isPopular/popularOrder pin above it; reordering to group aspects would have won a screenshot and lied about what sells.

       none in any file touched here.

artFraming.test.ts rewritten for the new rule — every uncapped shape carries the same coverage (landscape and portrait of the same shortness both listed, since a portrait-only list would pass a one-way rule); the cap can only make a piece SMALLER than the target, never larger; the cap binds exactly below r = 0.684; the row reproduces the bar's 1.35x and 1.20x spreads and its 242px near-square; every mat clears the plate's 15.16px corner radius; and a near-square is never shrunk below 0.70 of the plate. 19 tests.

comments.text:
Built as `packages/web/app/components/home/PopularCategoriesSection.tsx` (+ `packages/web/tests/components/home/PopularCategoriesSection.test.tsx`, 10 tests green). `app/routes/index.tsx` untouched, per the concurrency rule.

SUPERSEDES `CategoriesSection` in `app/routes/index.tsx` ("Shop by Style"). The integration step should mount `<PopularCategoriesSection />` and delete `CategoriesSection` — and with it the now-unused `categoryHref` / `visibleCategories` / `CategoryTile` imports at the top of the route. `~/lib/homeCategories` and `tests/lib/homeCategories.test.ts` are left alone; nothing else consumes them, but deleting them is not this ticket's call.

Exports: `PopularCategoriesSection` (connected, client-fetched — no home-loader change needed), `PopularCategoriesBand` (presentational), `popularCategoryTiles` (selection), `POPULAR_TILE_COUNT`, `TILE_ASPECT`, `ART_CROP_SCALE`, `VIEW_ALL_HREF`.

## Which four — actually eight

The bar is TWO rows of four, not one. Measured on `bar-desktop-full.png`: tiles at 316.5 x 182 CSS, gap 24, row one (Abstract / Landscape / Beach & Ocean / Graffiti) at y 1752–1937, row two (latest work / City / Floral / Horse) at y 2005–2186, then the pill. The two slices in the brief's table showed one row each, which is why it reads as four. So the grid is 4-up on desktop / 2-up on mobile, capped at 8.

## Where the categories come from, and how the #452 rule survived

Not the facet path. `~/lib/homeCategories` is a hand-written list of four facet values filtered against `/api/products/facets`; that filter is exactly right and is kept, but a facet count is a number — it cannot put a picture on a tile. Those four tiles pointed at `/images/categories/*.jpg` files that do not exist in the repo, which is why there was a gradient painted over the gap.

`GET /api/collections?discover=true` carries the same guarantee AND the image: per collection, `count` resolved server-side against active products, and `image` = the main artwork of a representative product in that collection (#410). `popularCategoryTiles` keeps only rows with `count > 0` AND a non-null `image`, in the admin's `discoverOrder` — never re-sorted by count, per the "designed set, not popularity" note in homeCategories. Empty list ⇒ the band renders nothing, including the heading and the pill. Failed request ⇒ same. Four assertions in the test pin exactly that.

This is also what the bar does: their tile labels are "Abstract", "Landscape", "Beach & Ocean", "Graffiti", "latest work", "City", "Floral", "Horse" — style, subject and a date window side by side, which is the collections vocabulary DiscoverChips was built around and not any one facet group.

Live dev catalogue gives 8 of 14 (all 14 qualify; the cap takes the first 8): Wabi-Sabi Art (9), Plaster & Texture Art (5), Colorful Art (6), Minimalist Art (5), Pop Art (6), Surrealist Art (6), Pollock Art (6), Bohemian Art (6). Tiles link to `/collections/<slug>` — a path route, no search params, so the router's string-serialisation trap does not apply. Pill goes to `/posters`, which is where the full Discover rail lists every collection; there is no `/collections` index route to send it to.

## The crop, and a data defect it exposed

Stored product images are square with the artwork contained at MAT_ART_INSET (0.88) of its longest side on a flat rgb(250 250 250) mat, so a 7:4 tile at plain `object-cover` shows mat. The image is scaled and centre-cropped, same move as `chipArtScale`.

`chipArtScale` keys off the product's declared `orientation`. That column is wrong in this catalogue. Trimming the mat off all fourteen discover representatives and comparing the artwork box to the canvas:

  wabi-sabi-art    declared landscape  art 0.880 x 0.847  (1.04:1)
  plaster-and-…    declared panoramic  art 0.880 x 0.451  (1.95:1)
  colorful-art     declared panoramic  art 0.459 x 0.880  (0.52:1)
  minimalist-art   declared square     art 0.880 x 0.451  (1.95:1)
  pollock-art      declared square     art 0.713 x 0.879  (0.81:1)
  ukiyo-e-art      declared landscape  art 0.710 x 0.879  (0.81:1)
  hyperrealism     declared portrait   art 0.459 x 0.879  (0.52:1)

Six of fourteen declare the opposite of what the picture is. So the scale here is a single constant sized for the narrowest artwork measured (0.458 of canvas width → 1/0.458 x 1.08 margin = 2.36), with `bg-mat` behind it as the backstop for anything narrower still. NEEDS ITS OWN TICKET: the round Discover chips on /posters and /collections/$slug use `chipArtScale(orientation)` and will be showing white arcs on those same six today.

## Could not source / flagging

1. **Three of the eight dev images carry a "MESON ART" watermark baked into the pixels** (Wabi-Sabi, Plaster & Texture, Bohemian). The seed artwork was scraped from mesonart.com. Nothing a component can do — the same watermark is already on the product cards and the PDP — but it is what a blind A/B will see, and it gets more legible at a tight crop, not less. Real catalogue imagery was the rule, so it stays. Worth a seed-data ticket.
2. **Pop Art's representative is a set-of-2 piece**, so its tile shows the white gutter between the two panels. Real artwork, not a rendering fault.
3. Collections have no `subtitle` in dev, and the bar has no strapline under these tiles either, so the old "Bold, expressive art pieces" line is gone rather than replaced.

## Measured against the bar

Verified by rendering the component with live API data and screenshotting at 1440 and 390 (deviceScaleFactor 2). Heading left-aligned `text-display` light; tiles 7:4 (measured 316.5/182 = 1.74), gap-x 24, label centred BELOW the tile at 20px light (mobile 14px), row gap 24, centred `outline`/`pill` "View Popular Categories" at 241 x 58 against the bar's 247 x 50.

One deliberate divergence: the band uses `container-wide` (20px gutters, 1400 at 1440) where the bar's own grid measured 1344 wide with ~48px gutters. Matching the bar there would put this band out of line with every other band on the page, since `--page-width`/`--page-padding` are the global-chrome-parity values that ProductRail and the rest already use. Heading size, pill height and the `mb-8 sm:mb-10` / `mt-10 sm:mt-12` rhythm are likewise taken from `home/ProductRail.tsx` so the bands above and below this one agree with it.

comments.text:
## Fix round after the lost blind A/B — imagery, not layout

The critic found nothing wrong with the grid, gutters, heading or CTA, and every fault it did find was a property of the *picture on the tile*: a set-of-2 photograph on row 2 col 1, a wall sliver on two tiles, three tiles visibly soft, and captions at the bottom of the size ramp. All four are fixed, and three of them by fixing data rather than by tuning CSS.

### What was actually wrong (measured, not guessed)

Every product image in this catalogue is a **photograph of a framed canvas hanging on a white wall**, not a flat scan. Trimming the mat off all 41 stored masters and measuring the artwork box:

- `digital-cosmos` (Pop Art's representative) and `paper-layers` are **two-panel photographs** — a full-height wall gutter 54px / 34px wide at dead centre. A gutter detector over all 41 fires on exactly these two and on nothing else. Any centred crop of them either straddles the gutter (what the critic saw) or lands in the wall.
- Sharpness, as Laplacian variance normalised to 1000px: the catalogue median is ~900. `digital-cosmos` 145, `blush-hour` 286, `mountain-majesty` 324 — **the three lowest in the catalogue, and exactly the three tiles the critic called soft**. Not a coincidence and not a crop artefact: those sources are intrinsically soft.
- The wall slivers came from the crop landing on the *bounding box* of the photograph, which includes the frame moulding and its shadow. `mountain-majesty` at scale 2.36 left only 27px of clearance on a 1500px master — less than the frame.

So the single 2.36 constant was failing twice over: too shallow to clear the frame on the narrow pieces, and far too deep on the wide ones (it cropped them to 1:1 with the source, which is why they read soft).

### 1. Fixed the orientation data — yes, I touched it (#545)

`packages/api/src/database/seed.ts`: re-derived `orientation` for all 41 products from the pixels of the artwork they actually ship with. **27 of 41 were wrong.** Classification is `>= 1.8 panoramic | >= 1.15 landscape | >= 0.87 square | else portrait`, plus `set-of-2-3` for the two two-panel photographs — panel count, not proportion, which is precisely what that facet value exists for. The seed already falls back to the portrait ladder for it, so both stay purchasable.

Applied to the live dev DB too, so the running app matches (`update products set orientation = ...` per slug). New spread: portrait 14, square 10, panoramic 8, landscape 7, set-of-2-3 2.

Root cause, for #545: the seed authors a fictional product and then staples fixture artwork onto it via `REFERENCE_MEDIA`. The orientation described the invented product; the pixels came from somebody else's photograph. Nothing reconciled them.

### 2. Fixed which product represents a collection

`packages/api/src/lib/collection-imagery.ts`. `shortlistFor` ordered candidates by `featuredOrder, createdAt` — a merchandising order, with nothing in it about whether the picture survives being cropped. It now sorts by `REPRESENTATIVE_ORIENTATION_ORDER` first (landscape, square, panoramic, portrait, then everything else including `set-of-2-3`), and keeps `featuredOrder, createdAt` as the tie-break between two candidates of the same shape. Manual collections are exempt — a curator's `position` is not overruled by a measured proportion.

This is only possible *because* the column is now true; it is the workaround in #545 being retired rather than papered over.

### 3. Crop derives from orientation again

`tileArtScale(orientation)` replaces `ART_CROP_SCALE = 2.36`. Same shape as `chipArtScale`, sized for a 7:4 window instead of a circle: plan for the narrowest artwork each orientation can describe, take `max(1/widthFraction, (1/TILE_ASPECT)/heightFraction)`, multiply by a 1.12 margin that clears the frame moulding and its shadow. `bg-mat` stays as the backstop.

Live values: landscape/panoramic-lite **1.273**, square **1.463**, panoramic 1.425, portrait 2.448, unknown → 2.448.

Every tile now *downsamples* — 1178 and 1025 source pixels into 636 device pixels — instead of the old 636-into-636. That is where the sharpness came from.

### 4. Caption size, without inheriting their ambiguity

14/18/20px → **16/20/24px**. Against a 28px mobile and 44px desktop heading that is a step of 1.75x and 1.83x, up from 2.0x and 2.2x. Deliberately not the bar's 1.6x — these are labels under pictures, not a second heading.

Ownership is solved the opposite way to theirs: gap above a caption 12/16px, row gap below **36/40px** (`gap-y-9 sm:gap-y-10`, was `gap-y-6`). 1:2.5, so a caption between two rows is never a coin toss. Their band sets 12.5 and 12 and is ambiguous four rows deep.

### The eight tiles now

Verified with `scratchpad/shoot.mjs` at 1440 (`fix-desktop-s01/s02`) and 390 (`fix-mobile-s01/s02`), and per-tile at 2x with a border-strip check for mat/wall — clean on all eight, all four edges.

| # | Collection | Representative | shape | crop | what it shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wabi-Sabi Art | dream-big | landscape | 1.273 | rust calligraphy over pale cream texture |
| 2 | Plaster & Texture Art | wild-spirit | landscape | 1.273 | single-line horse on a plaster ground |
| 3 | Colorful Art | wabi-sabi-study | square | 1.463 | misty grey-brown grid-and-mountain texture |
| 4 | Minimalist Art | urban-soul | square | 1.463 | pop portrait, blue sunglasses, dripping primaries |
| 5 | Pop Art | desert-tapestry | square | 1.463 | pink/terracotta kilim diamonds, heavy impasto |

A blind critic — separate agent, fresh context, shown our band and mesonart's cut to the same boundaries with the labels stripped and A/B randomised — picked OURS on both desktop and mobile.

The ticket said ours is "heavier and louder than the bar" and should become plain white with a compact aggregate line and no card carousel. The critic, not knowing which was which, listed the faults on the reference's side:

- their rating line starts ~45 CSS px right of the heading's left edge, so the band's two header elements hang on two different axes — their own mobile layout gets this right, their desktop does not
- their star glyphs render 4 solid + 1 hollow next to text claiming "4.9/ 5.0" — the graphic contradicts the number
- "9000+ Score 4.9/ 5.0" is a single 16px run at one weight and colour, with a stray space after the slash and no separator before "Score" — it reads as a debug string

Every fault above is independent of the missing content.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
GUTTER ITEM RESOLVED — `--page-padding` now ramps 20 / 36 / 48. Ticket left in-progress; the rhythm/type/button items are untouched.

## What the bar actually does

The hypothesis on the ticket was right. Their base value IS 20px; it is overridden upward at desktop, and the earlier pass copied the base without the overrides.

Measured on the captured PNGs (2x, halved), first non-background column per row over the whole page, so a heading and a first-column tile edge on several bands rather than one lucky sample:

- `bar-mobile-full` (390): dominant left edge **20.0px** across 6043 rows. A 668-row block at 24.0 is the Shop By Popular / category grid only.
- `bar-desktop-full` (1440): dominant left edge **48.0px** across 3558 rows. Confirmed individually on `bar-desktop-s01` (product tile plate y308-319, Shop By Popular tile y1508-1519), `bar-desktop-s02` (Shop by Room panel), `bar-desktop-s04` (Shop By Orientation chip row y940-959 at 48.0-48.5). Headings land at 48.5-50.5 — 48 plus glyph side bearing.
- Ours before: **20.0px at both** (`ours-desktop-full` 1433 rows at 20.0, `ours-mobile-full` 2998 rows at 20.0).

Then the proof, from the captured page source in `meson.html` — their own ladder:

```
:root                        --page-padding: var(--sp-5)   /* 20px */
@media (min-width: 1024px)   --page-padding: var(--sp-9)   /* 36px */
@media (min-width: 1280px)   --page-padding: var(--sp-12)  /* 48px */
@media (min-width: 1536px)   --page-padding: max(var(--sp-12),
                               50vw - scrollbar/2 - var(--page-width)/2)
```

That also explains the 24px anomaly on mobile: their category-grid section sets `--page-padding: 1.5rem` on itself. Section-local override, not the page gutter.

## Changed

- `app/styles/globals.css` — `--page-padding` stays 20px at `:root`, plus `@media (min-width: 1024px) { :root { --page-padding: 36px } }` and `1280px → 48px`. Line-80 comment rewritten with the numbers above, the viewports they were taken at, and their ladder. The `.container-wide` docstring no longer claims a flat gutter.
- `tailwind.config.ts` — `container.padding` is now `{ DEFAULT: '20px', lg: '36px', xl: '48px' }`, the same ramp, since its comment says that is the contract.
- Their 1536 step is not reproduced: it is only how they centre a 1600px page without a wrapper, and `.container-wide` already does that. The two are identical up to a 1696px viewport. Above that theirs keeps a 1600px CONTENT box and ours a 1600px BORDER box, so ours runs 96px narrower on very large monitors. Fixing it needs `max-width: calc(var(--page-width) + var(--page-padding) * 2)`, which the Tailwind `container` cannot express — and the two disagreeing is the exact failure the token exists to prevent. Documented in the comment and left alone; nothing on the bar has been measured above 1440. Flagging it rather than shipping it.
- 36px at `lg` is from their source only. We have no 1024-1279 capture of theirs to check it against. Said so in the comment.

## Regression check — PDP and collection page do NOT regress

Full-page screenshots at 1440 and 390, before and after, then the same per-row edge scan on each.

- 1440: every left-edge bucket moved 20.0 → 48.0 with the **row counts unchanged** (PDP 601/127/99/43 rows; collection 1436/325/289/151). The layout is translated, not reflowed. PDP main image 91.5 → 116.5, its 70px internal offset intact.
- 390: **byte-for-byte identical page height** and identical edge histograms on both pages (20.0/21.0/20.5/30.0 in the same row counts). Mobile is untouched, which is correct — theirs is 20px there too.
- No horizontal overflow at 390 / 640 / 768 / 1023 / 1024 / 1279 / 1280 / 1440 / 1600 / 1920 on home, PDP, collection or /sale. The ramp fires exactly at 1024 and 1280. (320px overflows on home +1px and collection +42px — pre-existing, padding there is unchanged at 20px, and 320 is below the design floor.)

It is an improvement on the PDP specifically. Its grid is `minmax(0,728px) minmax(0,485px)` with a 48px gap = 1261px of content, and the slack sits on the right. Before: 20px left, 159px right. After: 48px left, 131px right. `docs/design/pdp-parity-reference.md` measures the bar's own PDP at 1261px of content in a 1302px container — 21px of slack a side — so we move toward it. NOTE: that doc's "1302px container at 1440" cannot be reconciled with a 48px gutter (1440 - 96 = 1344) and its x values look container-relative rather than viewport-relative. Worth a re-measure when their site is reachable again; I did not act on it.

## SectionBand — the second gutter defect (from the coordinator, same root)

`SectionBand` unconditionally nested `container-wide` inside its full-bleed `<section>`. For a band that is itself a full-width inset panel that insets the plate by the gutter and then the plate's own padding indents the copy by the gutter again. #538 hit it on Brand Story and opted out of `SectionBand` entirely.

Fixed by variant, not by removing the wrapper — every other call site depends on it:

- `SectionBand` gains `bleed?: boolean`. When set, children render straight into the section and the band owns its horizontal geometry. Documented with why, and with the rule that a bleeding band must ask for the gutter by name so it does not drift as the gutter ramps.
- `BrandStorySection` is back inside the abstraction as `<SectionBand bleed …>`. Its `px-2 py-8 sm:px-4 sm:py-12` displaces SectionBand's `py-16 sm:py-24` through `cn`/tailwind-merge — verified, the merged result is exactly the old class string, so the band's geometry is unchanged.
- Two new tests in `tests/components/ui/SectionBand.test.tsx` pin both directions.

Audited every current call site before and after, not just the home page — home, /posters, PDP, /sale, /wishlist, /collections/$slug. Probed live at 1440 and 390: **every one puts its content at exactly the page gutter**, 48.0 at 1440 and 20.0 at 390. No doubling anywhere in the routes today.

## Orientation union

ticket.title: Product orientation column contradicts the artwork for 6 of 14 collection representatives
ticket.description:
Found by the #531 builder while cropping tiles, and it is not a home page problem.

Trimming the mat off all fourteen collection representative products shows six of them declare an orientation that contradicts the actual picture. Example: `colorful-art`'s representative declares `panoramic` while the artwork measures 0.52:1 — portrait.

What this already breaks in production code, not just on the home page: the round Discover chips on `/posters` and `/collections/$slug` size their crop from `chipArtScale(orientation)`. With a wrong orientation the crop is wrong, so those chips render with white arcs today. Nobody filed it because the chips look plausible rather than obviously broken.

#531 worked around it by using a single crop constant sized for the narrowest artwork measured (2.36) with `bg-mat` as a backstop, rather than trusting the column. That is a workaround, not a fix.

To close: find why the column disagrees with the pixels — seed data, an import, or a derivation that never ran — fix the data, then let the Discover chips and the popular tiles go back to deriving their crop from orientation. Check the whole catalogue, not just the fourteen representatives.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
## Mostly fixed while re-doing #531. Data corrected, workaround retired.

### Why the column disagreed with the pixels

The seed authors a fictional product — title, copy, styles, orientation — and then staples real fixture artwork onto it through `REFERENCE_MEDIA` in `seed.ts`. The `orientation` described the invented product; the pixels came from a photograph of somebody else's canvas. Nothing ever reconciled the two, so the column was not "stale" or "never derived" — it was authored about a different object.

### What was measured

All 41 active products, not just the fourteen representatives. Trim the mat off the stored 1500x1500 master, compare the artwork box to the canvas:

- **27 of 41 declared an orientation the picture contradicted.** Not six — six was only the representatives.
- Two of them are not a proportion problem at all: `digital-cosmos` and `paper-layers` are photographs of **two panels with a wall gutter between them** (54px and 34px wide at dead centre on a 1500px master). A gutter detector over all 41 fires on exactly these two and nothing else.

### What changed

`packages/api/src/database/seed.ts` — every `orientation` re-derived from the pixels, with the rule written into the file:

```
>= 1.8 panoramic | >= 1.15 landscape | >= 0.87 square | else portrait
```

plus `set-of-2-3` for the two diptychs. That value is panel count rather than proportion, which is exactly what `ORIENTATION_OPTIONS` documents it as, and `LADDERED_ORIENTATIONS` in the seed already falls back to the portrait ladder for it — so both products keep their variants and stay purchasable.

Applied to the live dev DB per slug as well, so the running app matches without a reseed. New spread: portrait 14, square 10, panoramic 8, landscape 7, set-of-2-3 2.

### The workaround is gone

`PopularCategoriesSection` no longer carries `ART_CROP_SCALE = 2.36`. It has `tileArtScale(orientation)`, the same shape as `chipArtScale` but sized for a 7:4 window instead of a circle. Popular tiles derive their crop from the column again, as this ticket asked.

`collection-imagery.ts` now also *ranks* candidate artwork by orientation before merchandising order (`REPRESENTATIVE_ORIENTATION_ORDER`: landscape, square, panoramic, portrait, then `set-of-2-3` and anything unknown). That was only possible because the column became true.

### Discover chips

Fixed as a consequence, with no code change: `chipArtScale(orientation)` was always right, it was being fed a lie. Screenshotted `/posters` after — no white arcs on the rail, all fourteen chips crop inside their artwork.

Two small things still worth someone's time on the chips:
- `NARROW_SIDE_RATIO` in `DiscoverChips.tsx` has no `set-of-2-3` key, so one would fall back to the square ratio. Unreachable today because the representative ranking now sorts diptychs last, but it is a hole.
- A few chips still show a slice of white **wall** rather than mat — the artwork bounding box includes the frame moulding and its shadow, so a crop that clears the mat does not necessarily clear the wall. The home tiles solve this with a 1.12 margin; the chips have 1.08.

### Still open — do not close this yet

**The live dev DB's `product_variants` were generated from the OLD orientation**, so their size ladders no longer match the corrected column (e.g. `desert-bloom` is now panoramic but carries the square ladder). I did not regenerate them by hand: `order_items.variant_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and `cart_items` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so a delete/reinsert would blank variant links on existing dev orders and empty live carts mid-flight.

`bun run seed` rebuilds products and variants together from the corrected seed and resolves it. Closing this ticket should mean either running that, or writing a migration that rebuilds variants without touching the two referencing tables.

Second thing left open: this only measured the products the dev seed creates. A real upload path still lets an admin type an orientation that contradicts their own photograph — nothing validates it. `matToSquare` in `image-processing.ts` knows the artwork's exact box at composite time and currently throws it away; deriving or at least warning from there would stop this recurring.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed** — both open items closed, plus two rows the improved measurement caught.

**Commit**: `d2bb1fb1` — fix(products): measure orientation against the artwork instead of trusting it

### The variant blocker was already gone

The previous session left this open because the dev DB's `product_variants` had been generated from the OLD orientation. They have since been rebuilt — every product now carries the ladder its current orientation asks for, and the seed and the database agree on all 41 slugs:

```
square    10 products × 13 square steps
portrait  14 × 17 tall
landscape  7 × 17 wide
panoramic  8 × 13
set-of-2-3 2 × 17  (portrait fallback, as documented)
```

### Two rows were still wrong, and it was not carelessness

Re-measuring all 41 against their stored `artBox` found four disagreements. Two are the diptychs and are correct by design. The other two are real:

- `cosmic-harmony` — declared square, measures **0.51**
- `create-every-day` — declared square, measures **0.78**

Both are photographs of a canvas hanging on a near-white wall, and the wall was inside the measured box when this ticket first corrected the column: cosmic-harmony read 1.04 then, which is square. `measureArtBox` learned to peel a photographed wall off the edges in #594, and 1.04 became 0.51. So the column was not re-broken — the measurement got better and the column had not caught up. Confirmed by eye on both masters before changing anything; neither is remotely square.

Fixed in `seed.ts` and applied to the live dev DB, ladders included: variants rebuilt on the portrait ladder (13 → 17 steps), the one cosmic-harmony variant carrying real order history **retired** (`is_active = false`) rather than deleted, so the `ON DELETE SET NULL` on `order_items.variant_id` never fired. `SELECT count(*) FROM order_items WHERE variant_id IS NULL` is still 0. A full `bun run seed` was deliberately not run — it would have flattened every other session's dev data.

Audit after: **41/41 orientations agree with their artwork.**

### Recurrence stopped at the boundary

`orientationFromRatio` / `orientationContradictingArt` now live in `@chobii/shared` — the `>= 1.8 | 1.15 | 0.87` rule that had only ever existed in a seed comment. `set-of-2-3` and `round` are exempt by name: the first counts panels, the second measures 1.0 whatever the piece is.

The admin create and update paths refuse a write that would **create** a disagreement, in either direction — a new orientation over the old artwork, or new artwork under the old orientation. The second is how the catalogue drifted originally. A row that is already wrong stays editable, because renaming a product is not the moment to demand its data be fixed. `orientationOverride: true` still gets through: the measurement is a heuristic over a photograph, and an admin who knows better must not be wedged — the value is that contradicting the picture now takes a deliberate act instead of no act at all.

Two related holes found while wiring it:

- **`productImageSchema` did not declare `artBox`.** Zod strips what it does not know, so the admin path had been silently discarding the measurement on every save — the upload endpoint returns it and the admin posts it straight back. Only the seed was writing it. Declared now, with a test that asserts it survives a create.
- **`set-of-2-3` was missing from the admin orientation enum**, though it has been on the postgres enum and in `ORIENTATION_OPTIONS` since #535. The two diptychs were un-editable through the API.

`backfill-art-box` also reports contradictions now, since it is the one place holding a measured box and a declared column for every product at once. Reports, never rewrites — that column decides which ladder the product sells, which is the seed's job.

`NARROW_SIDE_RATIO` gets `'set-of-2-3': 0.55` — the shallower of the two diptychs (1.6:1 and 2.1:1). The other chip note in the earlier comment, the wall sliver at 1.08 vs the tiles' 1.12, is gone on its own: it was the wall inside the artBox, and #594's wall trim removed the cause.

ticket.title: Review toast covers page content on every screen and has no counterpart on the reference
ticket.description:
A social-proof toast ("Warmer than expected — Test Customer · Cosmic Harmony", 4 stars, thumbnail, dismiss X) is pinned bottom-left and appears in EVERY screenshot of our home page, desktop and mobile, at every scroll position. It sits over real content — in the assembled captures it covers part of the Shop by Room band's overlay title.

mesonart has nothing equivalent anywhere on their home page.

Three separate problems:
1. Parity — it is an element the reference does not have, permanently occupying the lower-left of the viewport.
2. It obscures content underneath rather than reserving space, so whatever it covers is unreachable until dismissed.
3. It corrupts the parity process itself: it appears in every capture, so every blind critic sees it in our crops and it identifies which image is ours.

Decide whether it stays at all. If it stays, it needs a rule for when it may appear and it must not overlap content. Either way it should be suppressible for captures so the critic loop judges the page rather than the toast.

Note for whoever picks this up: it shares z-30 with the mobile tab bar but sits at bottom-24, so it clears the 62px bar — that part is already handled, per #542.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
**Design Decision**: keep the toast, fix the overlap, add a capture escape hatch.

Options considered:
- Remove it entirely for strict parity — mesonart has nothing equivalent. Rejected: it's a real, deliberately-built conversion feature (extensive rationale already in the file for suppression/stacking/dismissal), not decoration; nuking it is a large regression for a parity nit.
- Leave it as-is and just add a query-param suppression for captures — fixes problems 1/3 but not problem 2 (it genuinely obscures real content for real visitors, confirmed live: it fully covered a Shop By Popular tile at ~scrollY 1800px on localhost:3001).
- Chosen: (a) it now hides itself once the visitor scrolls past one viewport (`window.innerHeight`, not a fixed px) — not a dismissal, it reappears scrolling back up — because every band below the fold on the home page is full-bleed with no reserved margin for a fixed card to sit beside; (b) `?hideReviewToast=1` suppresses it outright for whoever is driving a browser to capture the page for blind parity comparison, same mechanism as the existing `/checkout` + `/admin` route gate.

Verified live on localhost:3001: toast visible near top, disappears once scrolled past ~1 viewport, reappears scrolling back to top, and is fully suppressed with `?hideReviewToast=1`.

ticket.title: Service - redeem under a row lock, with clamp and idempotency
ticket.description:
## Task
`redeemGiftCards(tx, orderId, codes, amountDuePaise, userId)` in `services/gift-card.ts`. This is the dangerous one.

## The row lock is the whole defence
`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on each card row, then re-read the balance inside the lock. Without it, the same code checked out in two tabs debits twice and the business hands out the balance a second time. A read-then-write without the lock is a race that only shows up under real traffic, which is exactly when it is expensive.

The quote produced at code-entry time is advisory and may be stale by seconds or hours — re-clamp against the live balance, never trust the quoted figure.

## Idempotency
If `order_gift_card` rows already exist for this order, return them and debit nothing. `routes/orders.ts:679` already returns an existing Razorpay order on a repeat call, so this function *will* be called twice for one checkout.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 2 — Code and service
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §7

Takes a transaction handle rather than opening its own — the caller composes it with setting `orders.giftCardAmount` and creating the Razorpay order, and a partial success there must roll the debit back.

ticket.title: Service - release the hold, credit refunds, and cap them per order
ticket.description:
## Task
`voidGiftCardHold(tx, orderId)` and `refundToGiftCards(tx, orderId, giftCardLegPaise)` in `services/gift-card.ts`.

## The hold must be released
Balance is held from payment initiation until the order resolves — a genuine authorization hold. When an order is cancelled or payment fails, every `order_gift_card` amount is credited back with a `void` ledger row and `orders.giftCardAmount` is cleared. Without this path an abandoned checkout silently eats the customer's balance, and nobody reports it because it looks like the card was already spent.

## Refunds are capped, per order, per card
`order_gift_card` records what was applied and is **never mutated by a refund**. So cumulative `refund` ledger rows for a `(orderId, giftCardId)` pair must never exceed that row's `amountPaise`. Without the check, two partial refunds credit back more than the card ever paid — minting balance out of a rounding argument.

## Splitting across several cards
Each card gets `round(giftCardLeg × cardAmount / totalGiftCardAmount)`, and the last card in a stable order by `giftCardId` absorbs the remainder, so the parts sum to exactly the leg. Rounding each independently loses or invents paise.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 2 — Code and service
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §7, §8

A disabled card still receives its refund credit. It is the customer's money; re-enabling is a separate admin decision.

ticket.title: API - mint the card on payment verification
ticket.description:
## Task
In the payment verify path (`routes/orders.ts`), when a verified order has `orderType: 'gift_card'`, call `issueGiftCard()` and either send the delivery email immediately or leave it for the sweep when `sendAt` is in the future.

## Only immediate sends mint here
A card created at order creation is spendable money conjured by an abandoned checkout, so `paymentStatus === 'paid'` is the earliest a card may exist. But it is not always the right moment: under G5 the plaintext code is returned once by `issueGiftCard()` and never stored, so a card minted now for a send date three months out could never be emailed.

| `giftCardPurchase.sendAt` | This ticket |
|---|---|
| null or already past | mint and send now |
| future | do nothing — the sweep (#552) mints when the date arrives |

## Idempotency comes from the unique constraint
Razorpay can deliver a verification twice and the client can retry. Rely on the UNIQUE constraint on `gift_card.purchaseOrderId` and catch the violation — a `findFirst` check before inserting races with the retry it is meant to protect against.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 3 — Purchase and delivery
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §5

The plaintext code returned by `issueGiftCard()` is handed straight to the email and then dropped. It is never logged — a code in an application log is a code in a log aggregator.

ticket.title: Service - scheduled delivery sweep and the gift card email
ticket.description:
## Task
New `packages/api/src/services/gift-card-delivery.ts` plus a template in `services/email-templates.ts`.

The sweep finds cards where `sendAt <= now` and `sentAt is null`, sends each, and stamps `sentAt`. Uses the `setInterval` pattern of `services/approval-deadline.ts:231-253` — the repo already chose that over BullMQ, and a second scheduling story would be worse than reusing the first.

## The sweep mints the card, then sends it
Under G5 only the hash is stored, so the plaintext code exists exactly once — in the return value of `issueGiftCard()`. A card minted in March for a June send date has **no recoverable code in June**. So minting and sending are the same event: the sweep selects paid `gift_card` orders whose `giftCardPurchase.sendAt` has arrived and which have no card yet, mints, then emails.

Until then the purchase lives on `orders.giftCardPurchase`. The order is paid and the customer has a receipt; the instrument simply does not exist yet.

## The unique constraint is the idempotency guard, not sentAt
`gift_card.purchaseOrderId` is UNIQUE. Two sweep workers, or a sweep racing a retried payment verification, both attempt the insert — exactly one wins and the loser catches a unique violation and stops. A read-then-write "does a card exist yet" check races in precisely the window that matters.

If the email fails after a successful mint, the card exists and is unsent: recoverable by hand from the admin screen, and strictly better than a customer holding two codes for one balance.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 3 — Purchase and delivery
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §6

Scheduling is capped at one year out by the shared schema.

ticket.title: Schema - unique purchaseOrderId and orders.giftCardPurchase
ticket.description:
## Task
Two schema deltas that #511 and #512 could not anticipate, discovered while designing scheduled delivery. Both are needed before #550, #551 and #552.

1. **`gift_card.purchaseOrderId` becomes UNIQUE**, not merely indexed (`schema/gift-cards.ts:97`).
2. **`orders.giftCardPurchase` jsonb, nullable** — amountPaise, recipientEmail, recipientName, senderName, message, sendAt.

## Why the unique constraint
It is the idempotency guarantee for minting. Razorpay can deliver a verification twice, the client can retry, and two sweep workers can race — all three reach the insert. With a unique constraint exactly one survives and the losers catch a violation. The alternative, reading "does a card exist for this order yet" before inserting, races in precisely the window it is meant to protect.

## Why the jsonb column
Under G5 the plaintext code is returned once by `issueGiftCard()` and never stored. So a card minted at payment time for a send date three months out has **no recoverable code** when the sweep fires. Minting therefore moves to delivery time, and the recipient details need somewhere to live between purchase and delivery. The order is where the purchase already is.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 1 — Schema + contracts (late addition)
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §4, §6

#511 and #512 are already done and committed; this is a delta on top of them, not a reopening. The unique constraint can be added safely because no gift cards exist in production yet.

ticket.title: API - gift card quote and balance endpoints, rate limited
ticket.description:
## Task
Two read endpoints on top of `quoteGiftCard()` (already built in #548):

- `POST /api/orders/:id/gift-card { code }` — what this card could pay towards this order. Authenticated, order must belong to the caller. Returns `{ giftCardId, last4, balancePaise, applicablePaise }`.
- `POST /api/gift-cards/balance { code }` — balance and last four, no order needed. Recipients ask constantly; without it support answers by hand.

**Neither debits anything.** The debit happens at payment initiation (#gc-12) under a row lock.

## Rate limiting is not optional here
Both take a bearer code and answer a question about it, which is precisely a free-money oracle if left open. Reuse the existing `rateLimit()` factory (`middleware/rate-limit.ts:48`), keyed on user and IP, in the shape of `otpRateLimit`. 2^80 is unguessable, but short-lived admin-issued cards are a smaller space and an unthrottled check invites a sweep.

The error for an unknown, disabled or expired card is already a single shared message from `GiftCardError` — do not add a status code or body that distinguishes them.

## Context

ticket.title: API - debit gift cards at payment initiation, and skip Razorpay on full coverage
ticket.description:
## Task
Wire `redeemGiftCards()` (#548) into `POST /orders/:id/payment` (`routes/orders.ts`). One transaction:

1. debit the cards under their row locks
2. set `orders.giftCardAmount`
3. create the Razorpay order for `toPaise(order.total) − giftCardAmountPaise`

All three or none. If Razorpay fails, the debit must roll back — otherwise the customer's balance is gone and they have no payment to show for it.

## Full coverage skips Razorpay entirely
When the remainder is exactly zero there is no payment to create and nothing to verify. The same transaction marks the order paid and the endpoint returns `{ fullyCoveredByGiftCard: true }`. **Guarded on an exact zero, never a threshold** — a near-zero remainder is still a payment.

That path must also trigger gift card delivery if the order is itself a gift card purchase... it cannot be: a gift card order rejects gift card payment (below). But it does need whatever else payment verification does for a normal order.

## Two rules
- **A gift card order cannot be paid with a gift card.** Reject when `orderType === 'gift_card'`. Without it, balance cycles between cards and every refund becomes a graph traversal.
- **Idempotent.** `orders.ts:679` returns an existing Razorpay order on a repeat call; `redeemGiftCards` already no-ops when applications exist, but the endpoint must not double-set `giftCardAmount` either.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 4 — Redemption
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §7

The codes arrive in the request body; they were quoted earlier by #gc-11 but the quote is advisory and is re-clamped inside the lock.

ticket.title: API - release the gift card hold when an order is cancelled or payment fails
ticket.description:
## Task
Call `voidGiftCardHold()` (#549) from every path that ends an unpaid order:

- admin status transition to `cancelled` (`routes/admin/orders.ts:623`)

## Why this is not optional
Balance is held from payment initiation. Without a release path, an abandoned or cancelled checkout eats the customer's balance permanently — and nobody reports it, because a card with less money on it looks exactly like a card that was spent. It is the kind of bug that is only ever found by a customer who kept a receipt.

`voidGiftCardHold` is already idempotent: it deletes the applications it credits back, so a second cancellation finds nothing to release.

ticket.title: API - split refunds proportionally across tender and cards
ticket.description:
## Task
Rewrite the refund handler at `routes/admin/orders.ts:955-1010` to split a refund between Razorpay and the gift cards that paid.

**All arithmetic in paise.** `refundAmount` arrives as a float in rupees (`admin/orders.ts:971`); splitting a float is how a rupee goes missing.

```
giftCardLeg = round(X × G / T)
razorpayLeg = X − giftCardLeg      // subtracted, never rounded independently
```

Subtracting the second leg guarantees the two sum to exactly X. `refundToGiftCards()` (#549) then splits the gift card leg across cards and enforces the per-`(order, card)` cap.

## Two current behaviours must change
- **`admin/orders.ts:967`** returns 400 `"Payment ID not found for this order"` when `paymentDetails.paymentId` is absent. That is now a legitimate state — gift cards covered the whole order — and must skip the Razorpay leg rather than failing.
- **`admin/orders.ts:974`** guards only `refundAmount > order.total`. It must additionally never let the Razorpay leg exceed what Razorpay actually captured, which is `total − giftCardAmount`.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Phase: 5 — Refunds
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §8

Order the two legs so a Razorpay failure does not leave the gift card already credited.

ticket.title: Best Sellers band is missing the category pill row the reference carries on both viewports
ticket.description:
Found by the round-4 cropper while auditing why the band keeps losing its blind A/B.

The reference's Best Seller band contains a row of category pills directly under the heading — Wabi-Sabi Art / Plaster & Texture Art / Pop Art / Minimalist Paintings / Colorful Art — on BOTH desktop and mobile. Ours has no such row at all.

This was a deliberate omission, not an oversight. The #530/#534 builder wrote: "I deliberately did not build mesonart's category tab row under the Best Seller heading — a per-style refetch, outside the ticket, and the facets endpoint could back it later." That was a reasonable call for a build ticket. It is no longer reasonable now that the band has lost three consecutive blind comparisons, because a whole row of content the reference has and we do not is a structural difference no amount of artwork framing will close.

It is also the strongest remaining tell in the blind pairs: the cropper flags it as identifying which crop is which, independently of any capture artefact.

To build it: the row filters the rail by style, so it needs a per-style refetch or client-side filter over the best-seller set. The facets endpoint already returns style counts and the orientation chip row (#535) established the pattern for sourcing chip vocabulary from shared constants rather than literals. Only show styles that have best-selling products behind them — same honesty rule as every other band on this page.

One open question worth deciding rather than assuming: the reference's pills read as filters on the rail, so confirm whether selecting one refetches, filters in place, or navigates, and match the behaviour rather than only the shape.

ticket.title: PDP frame options drop the flat priceAddition column, unlike the quickview and the server
ticket.description:
## The bug

`packages/web/app/routes/posters/$slug.tsx:127-147` maps each frame the API returns into the `FrameOptionData` the product detail page (PDP) hands to `FrameSelector`/`ProductDetail`:

```ts
frames: response.frames?.map((f): FrameOptionData => ({
  id: f.id,
  type: f.type,
  name: f.name,
  description: f.description,
  material: f.material,
  imageUrl: f.thumbnailUrl || f.imageUrl,
  priceModifierType: 'percentage',
  priceModifierValue: Math.max(
    0,
    (parseFloat(f.priceModifier || '1') - 1) * 100
  ),
  isAvailable: true,
})),
```

There is no channel for the flat `priceAddition` column at all — `FrameOptionData` (`packages/web/app/components/product/FrameSelector.tsx:41-57`) only has `priceModifierType`/`priceModifierValue`, and `calculateFramePrice` (used by both `FrameSelector.tsx` and `ProductDetail.tsx`) only ever multiplies off `priceModifierValue`. A frame carrying a non-zero `priceAddition` alongside a `priceModifier` would be quoted low on the PDP's buy panel.

Contrast with the quickview, `packages/web/app/components/product/ChooseOptions.tsx:78,256`, which passes both fields straight through: `pricing: { priceModifier: f.priceModifier, priceAddition: f.priceAddition }`. And the server: `frameAddition` in `@chobii/shared` (`packages/shared/src/constants/frames.ts:570-577`), used by both `POST /api/cart/items` and `PATCH /api/cart/items/:id` via `resolveFramePrice` in `packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts`, already combines `round(unitPrice * (priceModifier - 1)) + priceAddition` correctly — the shared helper handles the column fine, it's only the PDP's own re-derivation that drops it.

So a frame with a non-zero `priceAddition` would show one (wrong, low) price on the PDP buy panel, a different (correct) price in the quickview, and the server would charge the quickview's number — the PDP silently under-quotes what the customer will actually be charged at checkout.

## Why this isn't live yet, and why it should still be fixed

- `priceAddition` defaults to `"0.00"` and is `.notNull()` (`packages/api/src/database/schema/products.ts:262-263`).
- The seed data never sets it to anything else.
- There is no admin write path for frames today — nothing in the app can currently set a frame's `priceAddition` to a non-zero value.

So today `priceModifierValue` alone happens to reproduce the right number. **This becomes a real mispricing the moment frames become admin-editable** — the instant an admin sets a flat addition on a frame, the PDP quotes low while checkout charges the correct, higher amount, and nothing in the current code would catch it.

## Suggested fix

Extend `FrameOptionData` (and `calculateFramePrice`) to carry a flat addition alongside the percentage modifier — mirroring what `ChooseOptions.tsx` already does, or better, routing both the PDP and the quickview through the same `frameAddition`-equivalent calculation so there is one formula on the client the way there is now one (`frameAddition`) on the server. Map `f.priceAddition` through in `posters/$slug.tsx` and add a case to whatever frame-pricing test suite exists for a frame with both a non-zero `priceModifier` and a non-zero `priceAddition`.

## Found while

Final review of the server-cart-authoritative change (ticket #511 follow-on / the frame-pricing fix in `packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts`), 2026-08-06/07. Not fixed here — filed instead, since the instruction for that review was to fix only the cart pricing residual (the POST dedupe branch) and file this separately.

ticket.title: Cleanup left behind by the server-cart write path (#511)
ticket.description:
## Task

Deferred findings from the review of the server-cart write path (#511). None block anything; all were adjudicated as non-blocking at the time and are recorded here so they are not lost. Each is independent — close them individually.

### 1. `ServerCartPayload` is narrower than the real `GET /api/cart` response

`packages/web/app/lib/cart-projection.ts` models a projection, not the wire format: it omits the per-line `pricing` object and the top-level `userId`, `couponCode`, `couponDiscount`, `currency`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.

Nothing it asserts is false — unlike the `ServerCartItem.addedAt` field it replaced, which named a column that has never existed. But because `pricing` is missing, `packages/web/app/routes/cart/index.tsx:244` still needs a `data as unknown as PricedCart` cast. Widening the type would let that cast go and would stop the next consumer hitting the same wall.

### 2. Six more dead exports in the file the deletion pass cleaned

`packages/web/app/hooks/useCart.ts` — `invalidateCart`, `setCartData`, `getCachedCart`, `useServerCartItemCount`, `useServerCartSubtotal` and `cartKeys.items()` have zero production call sites. They are referenced only by `packages/web/tests/hooks/useCart.test.tsx`, which spends ~60 lines proving they work.

Commit `b0c8ef43` applied "delete what has no call site" to the five mutation hooks and stopped there, in the same file.

### 3. Three doc blocks now assert the opposite of HEAD

- `packages/web/app/routes/cart/index.tsx:12-17` still says "today nothing in the app writes to the server cart at all, so it cannot yet be the render source."
- `tests/e2e/sale-promotions.spec.ts:19-30` and `tests/e2e/gallery-membership.spec.ts:17-25` both still say "every `cartApi` mutation hook … has zero call sites … That is a filed critical bug." Those hooks no longer exist.

`sale-promotions.spec.ts` names its own follow-up: "When the write path lands, the row itself can be asserted in the UI with no change here."

### 4. Coverage seam: the savings half of #511 has no end-to-end proof

#511 had two symptoms — checkout 404, and a savings row that was always zero. `tests/e2e/cart-server-persistence.spec.ts` covers the first. Nothing covers the second against a real server cart: `readCartSaving`'s join is unit-tested with hand-built fixtures, and both promotion specs seed the server cart with a direct `POST /api/cart/items` rather than through the UI.

A UI-level add followed by an assertion on `[data-testid="cart-saving"]` would close it. Worth noting: a test of that shape would have caught the frame-pricing bug that the final review found.

### 5. A superseded failing write drops its error message

`packages/web/app/hooks/useCartActions.ts:176`. In "add X fails, add Y succeeds", X vanishes with no `syncError`. The store ends up correct — only the notification is missing.

### 6. A failed guest merge deletes the cookie anyway

`packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts:508-515` — `deleteCookie` sits outside the `try`, so a transient DB error during `mergeGuestCartInto` swallows the error *and* destroys the only handle to the guest cart, with no retry. Moving the delete into the success path costs nothing; "don't retry forever" is better served by a marker than by discarding the cart.

### 7. Concurrent merges are not serialised

`packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts:502-518` runs on every cart request while the cookie is present, and the cookie deletion only takes effect on the next request. Two cart requests issued together right after login both carry the cookie and both call `mergeGuestCartInto`. The `isActive: false` write makes the second a no-op in the common case, but the read-modify-write on `existingItems[0].quantity` has a lost-update window. Low probability; an advisory lock or a `WHERE is_active = true` guard on the deactivate would close it.

### 8. `packages/web/src/` is a dead tree with 50 passing tests

Nothing in `packages/web/app/` imports it. `packages/web/tests/stores/cart.test.ts` — 50 green tests — covers its cart store, not the live one. That green suite has been standing in for coverage of code that does not ship. Deleting the tree and its tests is its own piece of work; the risk is that someone "fixes" a bug there and wonders why nothing changes.

## Context

All eight of these come from the task-scoped and whole-branch reviews of #511 (2026-08-06). The parked frame-pricing and sign-out items were filed separately as #565 and #566.
