ticket.title: DECISION NEEDED - orders.subtotal semantics and the free-shipping threshold under a sale
ticket.description:
## Task
**Do not implement without Dhruv's input.** Two coupled decisions the layering block in the design doc (§5) opens and does not close. Implementation of #430 proceeds under a stated interim assumption (below) that changes no existing behaviour; this ticket is where the real call gets made.

### Decision 1 — what `orders.subtotal` means under a promotion

§5 step 2 says the discounted line subtotal goes to `orders.subtotal`. Current code (`routes/orders.ts:262-275`) computes `subtotal` as the sum of base line totals and then `total = subtotal + shipping − discount + tax`. Following both literally subtracts the promotion twice.

- **Option A — subtotal stays gross.** Sum of base line totals; `discount` subtracts once inside `total`. Smallest diff, and `orders.subtotal` keeps the meaning it has on every settled order today.
- **Option B — subtotal becomes net.** Discounted line subtotal; `total` drops its `− discount` term. Matches §5 as written, but reinterprets an existing column, so pre- and post-sale orders stop being comparable in reporting.

### Decision 2 — which figure the free-shipping threshold reads

`calculateShippingCost(input.shippingMethod, subtotalStr)` reads that same figure, and the announcement bar promises "Free shipping on orders over ₹999" (`AnnouncementBar.tsx:25`). Under a 40% sale a ₹1,600 cart is ₹960 net: gross qualifies, net does not.

- **Gross** — the sale does not cost customers their free shipping. More generous, and it is what the banner implies to someone who has not done the arithmetic.
- **Net** — the threshold means money actually spent. Protects margin on a deep sale, but a customer who qualified before the sale can stop qualifying during it, which reads as a penalty.

Whichever subtotal option wins decides this one silently unless it is stated separately, which is why both live in one ticket.

## Interim assumption already implemented (#430)
Option A + gross threshold — chosen because it changes nothing that exists: `subtotal` keeps its current meaning, shipping keeps its current behaviour, and the only new money movement is the promotion discount. If the decision lands on B or net, #430's totals block is the single place that changes.

## Context
Part of feature: sale-promotions
Phase: 3 — API surfaces (decision, not a build)
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5

Blocks nothing. Once decided, update §5 of the design doc and the totals block in `routes/orders.ts`.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
Both calls made by Dhruv, implemented in commit 70bfa9dd.

**Decision 1 — `orders.subtotal` stays GROSS (Option A).** No behaviour
change: `subtotal` is the sum of base line totals, the meaning it carries
on every settled order, and `total = subtotal + shipping − discount + tax`
subtracts the discount exactly once. Option B would have reinterpreted an
existing column and made pre- and post-sale orders incomparable in
reporting. The totals arithmetic in `routes/orders.ts` is untouched; only
its comment changed, from "interim, pending this ticket" to the decision.

**Decision 2 — the free-shipping threshold reads the NET, post-discount
figure.** This one WAS a change. `calculateShippingCost` was being handed
the gross `subtotalStr`; it now receives
`netAmountForShipping(subtotal, discount)`. The discount is price-level
and design §5's layering puts price above shipping, so a ₹1,600 cart under
a 40% sale is ₹960 of spend and no longer ships free. The discount is
therefore composed BEFORE shipping is priced — the two blocks had to swap
order.

**Gift cards are excluded from that figure, structurally.** A card is
tender: applied at the payment endpoint, after tax, against the amount
due. It is payment, not price, and must never move a price-level
threshold. `netAmountForShipping(gross, priceDiscount)` takes two price
arguments and nothing else, so there is no parameter a gift card could
occupy. Pinned from both ends: order creation ignores `giftCardAmount` /
`giftCardCodes` in the request body, and a payment-side test proves a
₹1,000 card that drops the payable to ₹200 leaves `shippingCost` at
`0.00`.

**The threshold stopped being duplicated.** It was written three times
with three different values — `2000` in `calculateShippingCost`, `1000` in
`/api/shipping/estimate`, and `999` on the cart page next to copy
promising ₹999. A cart promising free shipping the checkout then bills for
is the failure mode; ₹999 won because it is the figure already promised on
five customer-facing surfaces. All three now read
`FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD` from `packages/shared/src/constants/shipping.ts`,
as does the cart's copy (`FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD_LABEL`), and the API and
web boundary tests derive their fixtures from the constant rather than
restating it — so the two sides cannot drift without a test noticing.

Design §5 rewritten: the layering block now states gross subtotal, one
subtraction in `total`, the threshold on the net amount, and the gift card
exclusion, instead of implying `subtotal` becomes net.

Still hardcoded, deliberately out of scope: the ₹999 in
`AnnouncementBar.tsx`, `ProductTabs.tsx`, `TrustList.tsx`,
`TrustIconsRow.tsx`, `about.tsx` and checkout's `OrderSummary.tsx`. They
agree with the constant today; converting them is copy work, not a
pricing decision.

Verified: `order-promotion-pricing` 28 passing (7 new, threshold and gift
card), `gift-card-payment` 10 (1 new, real DB on :5440), web
`cart-free-shipping` 6 new, plus `orders` / `shipping` /
`order-cart-cache` / `gallery-join-order-pricing` 170 and web
`cart-saving` / `ShippingSelector` 37 as regression.

ticket.title: Shipping config table so the free-shipping threshold is set in admin, not at build time
ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify by title, not number — ticket numbers have collided in this repo under concurrent sessions.**

`FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD` is a compile-time constant in `packages/shared/src/constants/shipping.ts`. Changing what customers pay for shipping currently requires a code change and a deploy. It should be an admin setting.

Follow the existing precedent rather than inventing one: `walletPricingConfig` (`packages/api/src/database/schema/wallet.ts:160`) is a key / `valueInt` table with `effectiveFrom` / `effectiveTo`, a `description`, and a `createdBy` audit reference, served by `packages/api/src/routes/admin/wallet-config.ts` (GET + PUT). Read both before designing.

Create `shippingConfig` in the same shape, seeded with the current threshold.

## Requirements

**The shared constant stays** as the fallback when no row exists. Do not delete it. Two reasons: a database hiccup must not silently make all shipping free or all shipping charged, and the constant is the seed value. `getFreeShippingThreshold()` returns the configured value or falls back to the constant.

**Cache it.** This is read on every order creation and every shipping estimate. Cache with an explicit invalidation on write — and get the invalidation right: use `deleteCached` only for a complete key, `deleteCachedPattern` for anything with a wildcard. That exact confusion has now shipped three times in this repo (`admin/promotions.ts`, `admin/products.ts`, `admin/shipping.ts`); `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/shipping-cache-purge.test.ts` carries a repo-wide guard against it.

**Effective-dating is in the precedent — decide whether to keep it.** A threshold that changes at a scheduled time is genuinely useful for a sale, but if it is kept it must be honoured on read, not just stored. If a scheduled future value is stored and reads ignore it, that is worse than not having the column. Either implement it properly or leave the columns out and say why in a comment.

## Context
Feature: shipping-returns. Prompted by the discovery that the threshold existed in three places with three different values — `calculateShippingCost` charged by ₹2,000, `/api/shipping/estimate` quoted ₹1,000, and six storefront surfaces promised ₹999 (commit `70bfa9dd` unified them on ₹999).

The threshold is evaluated on the **net, post-discount** amount, excluding gift cards, per the decision recorded in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-sale-promotions-design.md` §5. Whatever this ticket builds must preserve that.

**DB trap:** `export $(grep -m1 '^DATABASE_URL=' /Users/dhruv/work/masonart.com/.env)` before any DB-touching suite — port 5433 is a different application, and a failed `beforeAll` there reports tests as *skipped*, which reads green.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `0135ecce` - feat(api): the free-shipping threshold is an admin setting, not a build-time constant

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/shipping.ts` - `shippingConfig` mirroring `walletPricingConfig` (key / valueInt / effectiveFrom / effectiveTo / description / createdBy, unique on (key, effective_from)), plus `shippingConfigRelations` for the admin screen's "who changed it"
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/0013_thankful_harry_osborn.sql` - single CREATE TABLE + 2 indexes + FK, no destructive statements; applied to the dev DB (5440) and column shape verified
- `packages/api/src/lib/shipping-config.ts` - NEW. `SHIPPING_CONFIG_KEYS`, `SHIPPING_CONFIG_DEFAULTS`, `resolveFreeShippingThreshold`, `getFreeShippingThreshold`, `invalidateFreeShippingThreshold`
- `packages/api/src/routes/orders.ts` - `calculateShippingCost` is async and reads the accessor
- `packages/api/src/routes/shipping.ts` - `/estimate` reads it once per request and reports the same figure it charges by
- `packages/shared/src/constants/shipping.ts` - `qualifiesForFreeShipping(netAmount, threshold = FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD)`
- 4 new test files + 2 cases added to `order-promotion-pricing.test.ts`

**Summary**

**Constant stays the floor.** Empty table, nothing effective now, and a read that throws all return `FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD`. A failed read is deliberately *not* cached (caching an outage's answer extends the outage); an empty table *is* cached, since that is a correct answer and the common case. `SHIPPING_CONFIG_DEFAULTS` sources the constant rather than repeating 999, so seed and fallback cannot drift. The table ships **empty** — same as `WALLET_CONFIG_DEFAULTS`, which seeds no row either. Writing a row at migration time would freeze 999 into data, so a later change to the constant would move the storefront copy while the charge stayed put: exactly the gap `70bfa9dd` closed.

**Effective dating: kept and honoured.** Rows are narrowed in SQL only to "has not ended"; the window is then evaluated in JS against the caller's `now`, so the answer is derived at read time on the same clock rule the rest of the module uses. A scheduled value takes effect at its `effectiveFrom` with no job to run.

**Cache.** Redis, key `shipping-config:free_shipping_threshold`, 300s — clamped to `min(active row's effectiveTo, next row's effectiveFrom)`, floored at 1s. That is the `a24b0cce` lesson applied to the start boundary: an entry written at 08:59:50 against a 09:00:00 change would otherwise quote the old threshold for its full TTL, and nothing runs at 09:00:00. There is deliberately **no in-process memo** — that is the exact shape of the #528 memo and would reintroduce the staleness one layer further in. Invalidation is `deleteCached` on a complete key (no wildcard anywhere), which `tests/routes/admin/shipping-cache-purge.test.ts` still passes against.

**Net-threshold semantics preserved.** `calculateShippingCost` still takes `netAmountForShipping(subtotal, discount)`; a gift card still has no parameter to arrive through, and `netAmountForShipping` arity is now pinned by a test. Two new order-creation cases assert the net reading survives a *configured* threshold.

**Shape left for #570**: `resolveFreeShippingThreshold()` returns `{ value, source: 'config'|'default', row, nextChangeAt }` and reads live (never the cache, so an admin edit cannot appear unsaved); `invalidateFreeShippingThreshold()` is the write hook; `/api/shipping/estimate` already returns the live `freeShippingThreshold`, which is the endpoint the storefront copy can read from without six fetches.

**Note for #570**: values are whole **rupees**, not paise — the same unit as the shared constant and as every consumer's comparison. Deviates from `walletPricingConfig`'s paise convention on purpose; a unit hop on a displayed figure invites a 100x error, and a 100x wrong threshold makes all shipping free.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/lib/shipping-config.test.ts tests/database/shipping-config-schema.test.ts tests/routes/shipping-estimate-threshold.test.ts tests/routes/order-promotion-pricing.test.ts tests/routes/admin/shipping-cache-purge.test.ts tests/routes/shipping.test.ts tests/database/shipping.test.ts` (with DATABASE_URL exported from .env → port 5440)
- Result: PASS (7 files, 137 tests)
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/constants/shipping.test.ts` (packages/shared)
- Result: PASS (9 tests)

ticket.description:
## Task
**Identify by title, not number.**

Depends on the shipping config table ticket. Two halves, and the second is the one that matters most.

### Admin
A GET + PUT endpoint and a form to set the free-shipping threshold, following `packages/api/src/routes/admin/wallet-config.ts` and its screen. It belongs with the existing shipping admin (`packages/web/app/routes/admin/` — check `app/lib/admin-nav.ts` for how screens are registered). Show the current value, who last changed it and when, since the config table carries `createdBy`.

Validate: positive integer, and warn (do not block) on a value large enough that almost no basket qualifies.

### The storefront copy must follow the setting
The number ₹999 is hardcoded as customer-facing text in at least six places — `AnnouncementBar`, `ProductTabs`, `TrustList`, `TrustIconsRow`, `about.tsx`, and checkout's `OrderSummary` — plus the cart's threshold logic. **If an admin can change the charged threshold while the copy keeps saying ₹999, this feature manufactures exactly the false-advertising gap that commit `70bfa9dd` just closed** (the site promised ₹999 on six surfaces while checkout charged unless ₹2,000). Every one of those surfaces must render the live value.

That means the value has to reach the client: expose it on an endpoint the storefront already calls, or put it in the root route's loader context. Do not fetch it six times.

Also confirm the cart's free-shipping progress indicator and "Estimated Total" use the same source and keep evaluating on the **net, post-discount** figure with gift cards excluded (design §5).

## Context
Feature: shipping-returns. The threshold previously existed in three places with three different values; commit `70bfa9dd` unified them on a single shared constant, and this pair of tickets makes that single source editable.

Write a test that pins the coupling: change the configured value, and assert the storefront surfaces render the new number. A test that only checks the admin form saves is not enough — the failure mode here is the copy silently disagreeing with the charge.

ticket.title: /create's mobile action bar must stack above the tab bar, not paint over it
ticket.description:
## Task

`/create` renders its own bottom action bar — `fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-40 ... md:hidden` at packages/web/app/routes/create/index.tsx:551, shown only while `!isInlineGenerateVisible` (the inline Generate button is scrolled out of view). It is z-40; the new MobileTabBar (#542) is z-30. So on `/create`, whenever that bar is up, it paints over the tab bar and all six destinations are unreachable.

Fix by stacking, not by layer-fighting: offset `/create`'s bar upward by the tab bar's height so both are visible and tappable — action bar on top, tab bar beneath it.

## Context

- Flagged by #542 as out of scope; that ticket deliberately left `/create` alone. No page content is hidden today and the footer still clears — the defect is purely that the tab bar is unreachable.
- Breakpoints line up in our favour: the `/create` bar is `md:hidden` (visible below 768) and the tab bar is `lg:hidden` (visible below 1024). The tab bar is therefore ALWAYS present whenever the `/create` bar renders, so the offset needs no breakpoint scoping — plain `bottom-[...]`, not `lg:`-prefixed.
- Do not raise the tab bar's z-index. MobileTabBar's own doc comment explains why z-30 is deliberate: every overlay in the app is z-40 (scrims) / z-50 (panels), and a tab bar above them would offer taps that go nowhere.
- Two numbers must agree, so export the offset from MobileTabBar next to `MOBILE_TAB_BAR_PADDING_CLASS` and `BAR_HEIGHT` rather than hardcoding 3.875rem in the create route — the same rule the existing comment states for the padding class. Both terms carry `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.
- The create route shell is `flex flex-col pb-24 md:pb-0` (line 388). 96px should still clear the raised bar; confirm at 390x844 rather than assuming.
- House pattern for this kind of check is a source-text assertion test — see tests/routes/home-tokens.test.ts and tests/routes/posters-toolbar-placement.test.ts. There is no existing test file for the create route.

ticket.description:
The mobile tab bar (#542) has no visual active state — all six icons remain black regardless of which route is active. This matches the reference design (mesonart), which also has no color change or highlight on the active tab.

ticket.title: Start the gift card delivery sweep — scheduled cards are never sent
ticket.description:
## The bug
`startGiftCardDeliveryScheduler` (`services/gift-card-delivery.ts`) is exported, tested, and **never called**. Nothing in `src/index.ts` starts it.

So a customer who buys a gift card with a future send date pays for it, gets a receipt, and the recipient is **never emailed**. The order sits `paid` with `giftCardPurchase.sendAt` in the past and no `gift_card` row behind it, indefinitely.

This is the one gap that makes the shipped feature quietly incomplete. Immediate sends work — they mint in the payment verify path — so the failure is invisible until someone schedules one.

## Why it was left
`services/approval-deadline.ts` exports `startDeadlineChecker` and is *also* never called, so this codebase has no established startup site for background sweeps. Picking one is a decision, not a mechanical fix, which is why it was not made silently inside a gift card commit.

## What has to be decided
Where periodic work starts, and what happens with more than one API process — two instances both running a `setInterval` sweep is safe here (the unique constraint on `purchase_order_id` settles the race, and `gift-card-delivery.test.ts` covers exactly that), but it doubles the polling and the decision should be deliberate.

If the answer is "start it in `src/index.ts`", `startDeadlineChecker` almost certainly wants starting in the same place and the same way.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §6

Until this lands, either disable the send-date field on `/gift-cards` or accept that scheduled cards do not arrive.

The cost is duplicate polling, so `DISABLE_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=true` opts an instance out entirely. Not converted to BullMQ — that is a separate decision, and the immediate problem was that they did not run at all.

ticket.title: Index the delivery sweep's query, and drop the index it no longer uses
ticket.description:
## Task
The delivery sweep changed shape after minting moved to delivery time, and the indexes did not follow.

**Now unused:** `gift_card_send_at_idx` on `gift_card.sendAt` (`schema/gift-cards.ts:117`). The sweep no longer looks at `gift_card` to decide what is due — a scheduled card does not exist yet at that point. `gift_card.sendAt` is now a record of what the buyer chose, copied at mint, and nothing queries it.

**Now unindexed:** the query the sweep actually runs, in `services/gift-card-delivery.ts`:

```sql
SELECT o.id, o.gift_card_purchase
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN gift_card g ON g.purchase_order_id = o.id
WHERE o.order_type = 'gift_card'
  AND o.payment_status = 'paid'
  AND g.id IS NULL
  AND (o.gift_card_purchase ->> 'sendAt')::timestamptz <= now
```

That scans `orders` — the largest table in the system, growing forever — every five minutes, filtering on a jsonb extraction. It is fine at today's volume and will not stay fine.

## Suggested shape
A partial index on `orders` covering `order_type = 'gift_card'`, which is a tiny fraction of rows:

```sql
CREATE INDEX orders_gift_card_delivery_idx
  ON orders (payment_status, ((gift_card_purchase ->> 'sendAt')::timestamptz))
  WHERE order_type = 'gift_card';
```

Measure before and after with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` rather than assuming — a partial index on a small subset may not beat a sequential scan until the table is much larger, and the honest answer might be "not yet, but here is the trigger".

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §6

Dropping the dead index is unambiguous; adding the new one deserves the measurement.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `8556b4c4` - perf(db): index the gift card delivery sweep, drop the index nothing reads

**Measurement** (step 1, done before deciding)

The dev database has 12 orders and 0 gift card orders, so `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` there proves nothing. Measured instead on a throwaway `gc_index_bench` database inside the same container: 200k orders, ~0.5% gift cards, most already-due cards delivered, then dropped afterwards. No fake rows were written to the shared dev database.

| | Execution time | Plan | Index size |
|---|---|---|---|
| No index (before) | **17.05 ms** | Parallel Seq Scan on orders, 37,820 rows removed by filter | — |
| Partial index (shipped) | **6.28 ms** | Bitmap Index Scan | 48 kB |
| Same + `INCLUDE (gift_card_purchase)` | **1.19 ms** | Index Only Scan | 112 kB |

**Design Decision**: the ticket's proposed index cannot exist

```
CREATE INDEX ... ON orders (payment_status, ((gift_card_purchase ->> 'sendAt')::timestamptz)) WHERE order_type = 'gift_card';
ERROR:  functions in index expression must be marked IMMUTABLE
```

`text::timestamptz` is STABLE — it depends on the session `TimeZone` — so it cannot go in an index expression. Indexing the raw text `(gift_card_purchase ->> 'sendAt')` is immutable and would work, but only while every stored `sendAt` shares one ISO format so lexicographic order matches chronological order. That is a property of the input seen so far, not a guarantee, and the query would have to drop its `::timestamptz` cast to use it. Not worth trading correctness for the remaining milliseconds.

So the index is partial on the two enum equalities the sweep always supplies (`order_type = 'gift_card' AND payment_status = 'paid'`) and the send date is filtered from the heap. The subset reached is already tiny; the point of the index is that the scan stops growing with total order volume.

**Design Decision**: no `INCLUDE`, despite it being 5× faster again

drizzle-kit cannot express `INCLUDE`, so it would have to be hand-written into the migration only — and then every `drizzle-kit generate` would see the schema and database disagree and try to recreate the index. A schema file that lies is worse than 5 ms.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/gift-cards.ts` - dropped `sendAtIdx`, with a comment on why `send_at` has no reader
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/orders.ts` - added `giftCardDeliveryIdx`, partial via `.where()`
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/0015_gift_card_delivery_index.sql` (new) - hand-written, as `0014_admin_editable_frames.sql` was: drizzle-kit's snapshot is stale at 0013, so `generate` prompts about unrelated `frame_category` changes and would bundle them in
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/meta/_journal.json` - journal entry 15
- `packages/api/tests/database/gift-card-delivery-schema.test.ts` - 3 new assertions

**Applied**: `drizzle-kit migrate` against the dev database. Confirmed `gift_card_send_at_idx` gone, `orders_gift_card_delivery_idx` present.

**Tests**:
- `tests/database/gift-card-delivery-schema.test.ts`: 7 passing — the delivery index exists, it is partial, and `gift_card_send_at_idx` is gone
- `tests/services/gift-card-delivery.test.ts`: 15 passing against live Postgres — the sweep still finds what is due
- `tests/database/gift-card-schema.test.ts` (16), `gift-card-order-columns.test.ts` (7), `migrations.test.ts` (90): passing

ticket.title: Prove the gift card code rate limit actually throttles
ticket.description:
## The gap
`giftCardCodeRateLimit` is attached to both endpoints that take a bearer code — `POST /api/gift-cards/balance` and `POST /api/orders/:id/gift-card` — but **no test has ever seen it return 429**.

`rateLimit()` (`middleware/rate-limit.ts:48`) falls through silently when Redis is not connected, and the vitest suites never connect one. The assertion in `tests/routes/gift-card-quote.test.ts` therefore returns early and the test passes without exercising anything. That is documented in the test, but a documented untested path is still an untested path.

## Why it matters more here than elsewhere
These endpoints answer a yes/no question about a bearer instrument. Sixteen Crockford characters is unguessable, but admin-issued cards are a much smaller and shorter-lived population, and an unthrottled oracle is the difference between "you cannot guess a code" and "you can sweep for one". The limiter is the only thing standing there.

Worth checking at the same time: the limiter keys on IP alone (`getClientIp`), so every customer behind one corporate NAT shares a bucket. Ten attempts a minute across a whole office may be too tight, and a per-user key would be fairer — decide deliberately rather than inheriting `otpRateLimit`'s shape by accident.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §4

Either stand up Redis for this suite, or assert the middleware is mounted on both routes at the router level — the second is weaker but honest, and better than a test that skips itself.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `2d850be1` - test(api): prove the gift card code throttle actually returns 429

**Design Decision**: two layers, so neither can skip itself

The ticket offered "stand up Redis" or "assert the middleware is mounted at the router level". Both, because each covers the other's blind spot:

1. **The endpoint, faked Redis.** `vi.mock` on `lib/redis` with a sliding window in a `Map`, and the gift card service mocked out so no database is needed. Drives `POST /api/gift-cards/balance` through Hono and asserts the eleventh check in a minute is a 429. Runs everywhere, always, with no infrastructure — it cannot degrade into a silent skip the way the old assertion did.
2. **The real window, real Redis.** `vi.importActual` past the mock, `initRedis()`, then eleven calls to the actual `checkRateLimit`. Proves the counting is not fictional.

**Design Decision**: layer 2 fails loudly instead of skipping

If Redis is unreachable, the suite fails with `Redis (redis://localhost:6380) is not reachable, so the rate limit cannot be proven`. `ALLOW_MISSING_REDIS=true` opts out explicitly. A suite that reports green without a Redis would recreate the exact gap this ticket was filed for.

**Design Decision**: the key stays IP-only

The ticket flagged that `getClientIp` puts a whole NAT'd office in one bucket and asked whether IP+user would be fairer. It would be fairer and it would be worse. Identity is attacker-chosen: accounts are cheap, so one bucket per account from a single address multiplies the oracle by however many accounts someone bothers to make. And half this surface has no user at all — reading a balance requires no account by design (G2) — so a mixed scheme just lets a sweeper sign out and take whichever bucket is roomier. The failure cost the other way is a rare 429 with `Retry-After` on a page people visit once or twice. Limit left at 10/60s; loosening a money guard without usage data is not something to do quietly. Reasoning is now in the code next to the limiter, not only here.

**Verify-fail** (step 2): removing `giftCardCodeRateLimit` from `POST /balance` fails 5 of the 15 tests (429, no-lookup, headers, no-leak, spoofed-XFF). Restored, `git diff` clean, then re-run green.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/tests/routes/gift-card-rate-limit.test.ts` (new) - 15 tests across both layers
- `packages/api/tests/routes/gift-card-quote.test.ts` - removed the assertion that always returned early; replaced with a comment pointing at the new suite and why it could not live there
- `packages/api/src/routes/gift-cards.ts` - the IP-only key decision recorded at the limiter

**Tests**: 33 passing across `gift-card-rate-limit.test.ts` (15), `gift-card-quote.test.ts`, `middleware/rate-limit.test.ts`. Real-Redis layer confirmed connected against `localhost:6380` on this run — not skipped.

**Also asserted, incidentally**: with Redis down there is no throttle at all. That is documented graceful degradation, and it is now visible in a test rather than implied by a comment.

ticket.title: PaymentButton accepts neither orderData nor existingOrderId without complaint
ticket.description:
## The gap
`PaymentButton` used to require `orderData`. Supporting gift card purchases made it optional, because a gift card order already exists by the time the button renders:

```ts
orderData?: OrderInput
existingOrderId?: string
```

Exactly one is required, and TypeScript now enforces neither. A caller that passes **both** or **neither** compiles fine. Neither reaches a runtime `throw new Error('Could not determine which order to pay for')` — after the customer has clicked Pay.

That error is deliberate and better than sending `undefined` to Razorpay, but it is a compile-time problem solved at runtime, on the most expensive screen in the product.

## Fix
A discriminated union makes the invalid states unrepresentable:

```ts
type PaymentTarget =
  | { orderData: OrderInput; existingOrderId?: never }
  | { existingOrderId: string; orderData?: never }

type PaymentButtonProps = PaymentTarget & { totalAmount: number; ... }
```

Both existing callers already satisfy one arm — checkout passes `orderData`, `/gift-cards` passes `existingOrderId` — so this should be a type-only change.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Introduced by #560.

Keep the runtime throw as well. Types do not survive a JSON boundary or a `as never` cast, and this one guards money.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `f7e764f5` - fix(ui): make PaymentButton's missing payment target a compile error

Implemented as the ticket proposed — a `PaymentTarget` union with `?: never` on the opposite key, intersected with the rest of the props. Type-only change; both callers already satisfied one arm. The runtime `throw` stays.

**Discovery**: the type test would have been theatre

The plan was a `@ts-expect-error` pin, and the first version of it passed immediately — before the union existed. `packages/web/tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["app/**/*", ...]`, so files under `tests/` are outside the project and get no diagnostics at all. `vitest typecheck` reuses that tsconfig, so it reported "Type Errors: no errors" for a file that could contain anything. Confirmed by planting `const wrong: string = 123` in the suite and watching the run stay green.

So the ticket needed a bit of plumbing before its own step 2 could be honest:
- `packages/web/tsconfig.typecheck.json` — extends the app config, adds `tests/**/*`
- `vitest.config.ts` — `typecheck.tsconfig` points at it; `typecheck.include` matches `*.test-d.ts`; `ignoreSourceErrors: true` so the 25 pre-existing `app/**` unused-symbol errors do not drown the assertions
- `package.json` — `test:types` script

**Verify-fail** (step 2): with the props still optional, all three `@ts-expect-error` directives report `TypeCheckError: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive` (TS2578) and 3 of 6 tests fail. After the union: 6/6 pass.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/components/checkout/PaymentButton.tsx` - `PaymentTarget` union
- `packages/web/tests/components/checkout/PaymentButton.props.test-d.ts` (new) - 6 type tests: cart input alone, existing order alone, gift card codes on either arm, and rejection of neither / both / explicit `undefined`
- `packages/web/tsconfig.typecheck.json` (new)
- `packages/web/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/web/package.json`

**Tests**:
- `bun run test:types`: 6 passing
- `bun run typecheck`: 25 errors before the change, 25 after (compared against a `git stash`ed tree) — all pre-existing unused-symbol errors in unrelated routes; neither `checkout/index.tsx` nor `gift-cards/index.tsx` regressed
- `tests/components/checkout/`: 48 passing

**Note for later**: `ordersApi.create(orderData!)` keeps its non-null assertion. Destructuring the props splits the union into independent variables, so TypeScript cannot correlate `!existingOrderId` with `orderData` being present. Narrowing on the undestructured props object would remove the `!`, but it would rewrite the whole component body for a cosmetic gain — the union already stops the bad call site, which is what the ticket was about.

ticket.title: Wire the store_credit refund type to issue a gift card
ticket.description:
## Task
`packages/api/src/database/schema/returns.ts:54` has offered a `store_credit` refund type since long before gift cards existed. Nothing implements it — `grep store_credit packages/api/src/routes/returns.ts` returns nothing. A return marked for store credit currently produces no credit at all.

Gift cards are the instrument that makes it buildable: processing such a return issues a card for the refund amount and emails it to the customer.

## Two things to get right
**It is not the tender split.** An ordinary refund goes back proportionally to what paid for the order (#557). Store credit is a deliberate substitution — the customer is given a card *instead of* their money back — so it must be an explicit choice, recorded, and never the default fallback when a Razorpay refund fails.

**Consent.** Converting a card payment into store credit without agreement is what invites chargebacks. Whatever flow chooses `store_credit` needs the customer to have accepted it, and the return record should carry when.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §8, listed there as out of scope for v1 precisely because the returns flow is its own surface.

`issueGiftCard()` already does the work; this is about where it is called from and under what authority.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `515a74ca` - feat(api): settle a return as store credit by issuing a gift card

**Design Decision**: it is not the tender split, and the code makes that structural

`issueStoreCredit()` is a named function called from exactly one place, guarded by `refundType === "store_credit"`. It is not reachable from any error path — a test asserts the source has no `catch` block within 400 characters of an `issueGiftCard` call, so a future "the Razorpay refund failed, give them credit instead" cannot be added quietly. That is the failure mode the ticket named: substituting a voucher for someone's card payment is what invites chargebacks.

**Design Decision**: consent is a stored timestamp, captured by the customer

`store_credit_accepted_at` on `return_requests`, set when the customer opts in via `acceptStoreCredit` on the return request. Optional and defaulting to null, so an older client simply creates returns that cannot be settled as store credit. An admin processing store credit without a timestamp gets 400 and nothing is created — no card, no email.

The alternative was an admin-side "customer agreed" checkbox. Rejected: the record would then attest to what an admin clicked, not what the customer accepted, which is exactly what a chargeback dispute would ask about.

**Design Decision**: `refund_type` moves onto the request

`return_policies.refund_type` said what a policy *prefers*; nothing recorded what a given return actually *became*. Money returned to a card and money returned as a voucher are different liabilities and reporting could not tell them apart. Now every processed refund records its type, not just store credit ones.

**Constraint found**: a card has a floor

`GIFT_CARD_MIN_PAISE` is Rs 500 and `GIFT_CARD_MAX_PAISE` is Rs 50,000, but a refund has no such range. A Rs 300 refund cannot become a card. It returns 400 telling the admin to refund the original payment method instead, rather than rounding a customer's money to fit the instrument. Same for anything above the ceiling.

**Ordering**: the card is issued *before* the return is marked refunded. If issuing or emailing throws, the return stays at `received` and can be settled again — better than a return closed as refunded with nothing behind it.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/database/schema/returns.ts` - `refundType`, `storeCreditAcceptedAt`, `storeCreditGiftCardId` (FK to `gift_card`, `ON DELETE SET NULL` — deleting a card must not delete the record that a return happened)
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/0016_return_store_credit.sql` (new) + journal entry 16, hand-written for the same reason as 0014/0015
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/returns.ts` - `issueStoreCredit()` and the guards in `process-refund`
- `packages/api/src/routes/returns.ts` - `acceptStoreCredit` on the create schema, consent timestamp on insert, echoed in the 201
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/returns-store-credit.test.ts` (new) - 16 tests

**Applied**: `drizzle-kit migrate` against the dev database; columns and FK confirmed present.

**Tests**: 80 passing across `returns-store-credit.test.ts` (16), `returns.test.ts`, `admin-gift-card-refund.test.ts`, `gift-card-refund.test.ts`, `gift-card-issue.test.ts`. Verify-fail was real: all 13 original tests failed on the missing columns before the migration. Typecheck unchanged at the same 6 pre-existing `@chobii/shared` errors.

**Not done, deliberately**: no admin UI for choosing store credit, and no customer-facing checkbox on the returns form. The API contract and the record are in place; the surfaces are `packages/web` work and belong with whoever designs the returns flow, which the ticket itself called "its own surface".

ticket.title: Cover a real payment end to end, including mint and delivery
ticket.description:
## The gap
No spec in this suite completes a Razorpay payment — the gateway modal is a cross-origin iframe. `tests/e2e/gift-cards.spec.ts` says so, and stops the purchase half at "the order exists and the payment step is reachable".

So the seam between paying and receiving is never exercised through a browser. Specifically these, which only the API suites currently prove:

- payment verification mints the card and emails it (`deliverImmediateGiftCard`)
- a fully gift-card-covered order skips the gateway entirely and lands `paid`
- the balance is debited exactly once when Razorpay retries a verification

The API tests are good, but they call the functions directly. Nothing has ever watched a customer go from cart to a spent card without a human doing it by hand.

## What would make it testable
Razorpay test mode plus a stubbed gateway, or a checkout mode that bypasses the modal under a test flag. Both are real work and neither should be bolted on quietly — a payment bypass that reaches production is worse than the missing coverage.

The cheapest honest win is probably the **full-coverage path**: when gift cards cover the total, the code already skips Razorpay entirely, so that journey is completable in a browser today with no gateway at all. It is also the path most likely to break unnoticed, since it is the one that marks an order paid without a payment.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §11

Start with full coverage. Treat the gateway-backed journey as a separate decision about test infrastructure.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `ec9f0c62` - fix(checkout): complete a fully gift-card-covered order without a gateway

The ticket's guess was right — the full-coverage path was the one most likely to break unnoticed. It was already broken, in two places, and neither was reachable by the API suites because both live past the point where those tests stop.

**Bug 1 (client)**: `PaymentButton` never looked at `fullyCoveredByGiftCard`. It went on to build Razorpay options from a response that carries no `razorpayOrderId`, no key and no prefill, and threw on `paymentData.prefill.name`. By then the server had debited the cards and marked the order paid — so the customer's balance was spent, the order was paid, and the screen showed a crash with a "Try Again" button.

**Bug 2 (server)**: `POST /api/orders/:id/payment` checked `isRazorpayConfigured()` at the top of the handler, before any gift card work. The one journey that needs no gateway was refused with 503 when no gateway was configured. Moved the check inside the transaction, after the remainder is known: only a non-zero remainder needs a gateway, and throwing there rolls the gift card debit back with it rather than taking a balance and leaving nothing to pay the rest with.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/web/app/lib/api.ts` - `PaymentInitiationResponse` is now a union of `RazorpayPaymentInitiation | FullyCoveredPaymentInitiation`, so the flag has to be checked before the Razorpay fields are reachable
- `packages/web/app/components/checkout/PaymentButton.tsx` - the covered branch: success, clear the local cart, no modal, no verification
- `packages/api/src/routes/orders.ts` - `PaymentGatewayUnavailableError`, thrown where the gateway is actually used
- `packages/web/tests/components/checkout/PaymentButton-full-coverage.test.tsx` (new) - 5 tests
- `tests/e2e/gift-cards.spec.ts` - the browser journey
- `tests/e2e/helpers/gift-cards.ts` - `ensureShippingOption()`

**Verify-fail** (step 2): the component tests failed before the fix — `onSuccess` never fired and the cart was never cleared, because the handler threw on the missing `prefill`.

**Environment gaps found while getting the E2E green** — worth knowing for the next person:
- The dev database has **zero shipping options**, and checkout will not leave the delivery step without one ("No shipping options available"). `ensureShippingOption()` seeds one through `POST /api/admin/shipping/options`, and leaves it: it is reference data, not a fixture.
- `.env` has **no Razorpay keys**, which is what surfaced bug 2.
- The API on `:3000` was a **4-day-old process** that had not picked up new code, so the first three runs tested a stale server against fresh specs. Restarted it before trusting any result.

**Tests**:
- `tests/e2e/gift-cards.spec.ts`: 12 passing, including the new journey — card applied, amount due ₹0, paid with no gateway, lands on the order page, and exactly the order total debited (not the whole card, not zero)
- `PaymentButton-full-coverage.test.tsx`: 5 passing; `tests/components/checkout/`: 53 passing
- `gift-card-payment.test.ts`, `orders.test.ts`, `gift-card-release.test.ts`: 132 passing
- API typecheck: 0 errors

**Step 3, decided not done**: the gateway-backed journey stays uncovered. It needs Razorpay test mode with a stubbed gateway or a checkout bypass flag, and as the ticket says, a payment bypass that reaches production is worse than the missing coverage. That is its own decision about test infrastructure, not something to bolt onto this.

ticket.title: Let a gift card be bought in the same checkout as a poster
ticket.description:
## The limitation
A customer cannot buy a gift card and a poster in one order. Buying a card goes through `/gift-cards` and creates its own order; posters go through the cart. Two purchases, two payments, two receipts.

Shopify allows it. This was accepted as a v1 scope cut (design G7), not overlooked.

## Why it was cut
`cart_items.productId` and `cart_items.variantId` are both NOT NULL (`schema/cart.ts:115-121`), and the cart derives `lineTotal` from the product and variant rows. A gift card has neither and its price is whatever the customer typed. Putting one in the cart needs either dummy product and variant rows — which then have to be excluded by hand from listing, facets, search, the sitemap and the sale resolver, each a place to forget — or a cart that tolerates a line with no product behind it.

## The real fix
Make `cart_items.productId` and `variantId` nullable and give cart lines a type, the way `order_items.productId` already is nullable. Then a gift card is just a line the cart prices from stored values rather than from a product.

That touches every cart read, the merge-on-login path, and the sale resolver — which is exactly why it was not done inside the gift card feature.

## Watch out for
The rule that a gift card order cannot be paid with a gift card (`routes/orders.ts`) is currently enforced on `orderType === 'gift_card'`. A mixed order has no single type, so that check has to become per-line, or the balance-cycling it prevents comes back.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-gift-cards-design.md` §5, G7

Worth doing when someone asks for it. Not before.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `fae6b867` - feat(cart): let a gift card be bought in the same checkout as a poster

Done as the ticket's "real fix" describes: `cart_items.productId` and `variantId` are nullable, cart lines have a type, and a gift card is a line the cart prices from stored values.

**Design Decision**: minting identity moved from the order to the line

The part the ticket did not call out, and the riskiest. `gift_card.purchaseOrderId` was UNIQUE, and that constraint is the whole idempotency guarantee for minting — a retried payment verification and the sweep both reach the insert, and exactly one may win. One card per *order* is only the right rule while a gift card has to be an order of its own; an order buying two cards needs two.

So `purchaseOrderItemId` is now unique and carries it. The old constraint was **replaced, not dropped**: a partial unique index covers the rows where `purchase_order_item_id IS NULL`, which is exactly the standalone `/gift-cards` flow (its order has no line items). Dropping the blanket unique without that would have silently removed the protection from every card bought before this. Both are asserted, including that a second insert against the same line and against the same standalone order each still throw.

**Design Decision**: the gift-card-pays-gift-card rule is now measured, not typed

The ticket flagged this. `orderType === 'gift_card'` cannot answer for a mixed order, so gift card tender is capped at `order total − stored value in the order`. Tender pays for the posters and never for the cards. A standalone gift card order counts its whole total as stored value, which keeps that path refusing tender exactly as before — caught by an existing test when I first implemented the cap from lines alone, since a standalone order has no lines.

**Not discounted, and I checked rather than assumed**: `resolvePromotionDiscounts` and `priceCartLine` both skip lines with no product, so stored value cannot go on sale. ₹2000 of balance sold for ₹1600 would mint money. Asserted in the cart read test.

Also: a gift card line is never merged with another (two ₹2000 cards can go to two different people, and the "same item" test compares product+variant — both null), and cannot be PATCHed (quantity would have to mean "how many codes", each with its own recipient; editing the amount would be an endpoint for editing money). Saving for later and removing still work.

**Delivery** reads both shapes: `deliverImmediateGiftCard` mints per line and still handles an order-level purchase, and the sweep runs a second query over order lines. A mixed order is not a gift card order, so the line query cannot lean on `order_type`. `isMintCollision` now recognises both constraint names — it matched the old one by substring, and neither new name contains it.

**Files Changed** (API): `schema/cart.ts` (`lineType`, nullable product/variant, `giftCardPurchase`), `schema/orders.ts` (`orderItems.giftCardPurchase`), `schema/gift-cards.ts` (`purchaseOrderItemId` + both constraints), migration `0017` + journal, `routes/cart.ts` (`POST /api/cart/gift-cards`, merge and PATCH guards), `routes/orders.ts` (validation skip, gift card snapshot, tender cap), `services/gift-card.ts`, `services/gift-card-delivery.ts`.

**Files Changed** (web): `lib/cart-projection.ts` (a card line titles itself and says who it is for), `stores/cart.ts`, `routes/cart/index.tsx` (`lineKey` for lines with no product), `components/cart/CartItem.tsx` (no link — `/posters/undefined` is a 404 — no image, no stepper), `components/gift-cards/GiftCardPurchaseForm.tsx` + `routes/gift-cards/index.tsx` ("Add to cart" beside "Continue to payment", behind the same validation).

**Tests**:
- `tests/routes/cart-gift-card-lines.test.ts` (new): 16 against live Postgres
- `tests/database/gift-card-delivery-schema.test.ts`: updated to the new invariant, plus the partial index
- Regression: 1004 passing across `tests/services/`, `tests/database/`, all gift card route suites, `cart.test.ts`, `cart-guest-merge.test.ts`, `cart-sale-pricing.test.ts`, `cart-frame-pricing.test.ts`, `orders.test.ts`
- Web: 248 passing across `tests/lib/`, `tests/components/cart/`, `tests/components/checkout/`, `tests/stores/`, including 7 new projection tests
- E2E: a mixed-cart journey in `tests/e2e/gift-cards.spec.ts` — poster added, card added from `/gift-cards`, both in one cart, card titled from its amount, no `/posters/undefined` link
- Typecheck: API 0 errors; web 22, down from 25 before this session

**Scope note**: this ticket was an epic, not a ticket — its own text says "worth doing when someone asks for it". It rewrote the minting idempotency guarantee, every cart read, the merge-on-login path, order creation, and the payment guard. It is complete and green, but it is the change in this feature most worth a second pair of eyes before it ships.

ticket.title: The gift card suites hit the shared dev database
ticket.description:
## The situation
Six gift card suites open a real Postgres connection from `DATABASE_URL` and create their own rows:

- `tests/services/gift-card-redeem.test.ts`
- `tests/services/gift-card-refund.test.ts`
- `tests/services/gift-card-delivery.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/gift-card-purchase.test.ts`, `gift-card-quote.test.ts`, `gift-card-payment.test.ts`, `gift-card-release.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/admin/gift-cards.test.ts`

That was deliberate and is defended in each file: the properties under test are a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock, a unique constraint settling a race, and transactional rollback. A mocked `db` can only assert that the words were written, not that the lock holds — removing `FOR UPDATE` was confirmed to fail the concurrency test, so the coverage is real.

## What it costs
- They **skip silently** without `DATABASE_URL`, so CI without a database reports green while testing nothing.
- They run against the shared dev database, not a disposable one. They create and delete only their own rows and drop nothing, so they sit outside the `getDestructiveDbUrl` guard (`tests/helpers/destructive-db.ts`) — but that guard exists because of a real incident (#332), and "outside the guard" is a judgement, not a guarantee.
- Several agents run suites concurrently on this machine. Fixtures are keyed by pid so they do not collide today; a shared global like the admin liability total is not so lucky, which already forced `tests/e2e/gift-cards.spec.ts` into serial mode.

## Options
Point them at a disposable `_test` database via `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and fail loudly rather than skipping when none is configured. Or wrap each test in a transaction that always rolls back, which removes the cleanup code entirely.

The one thing not to do is convert them to mocks. That would delete the only evidence the locking works.

## Context
Part of feature: gift-cards
See `tests/helpers/destructive-db.ts` for the existing convention.

comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `8706cc8c` - test(api): make the live-database gift card suites loud, and runnable off a disposable database

Both options the ticket offered, and neither instead of the other. The suites stay against live Postgres and none became mocks.

**Loud, not silent**: `tests/helpers/live-db.ts` decides where they connect, and every suite now opens with `it("has one")` calling `assertLiveDbReachable`. With nothing reachable the run fails with `Could not reach postgresql://***@localhost:59999/nothing. These tests assert a row lock, a unique constraint and transactional rollback — properties a mock cannot have...` (credentials redacted). `ALLOW_MISSING_DB=true` skips out loud instead — verified both ways.

**Disposable database**: they prefer `TEST_DATABASE_URL` when set. Unlike `getDestructiveDbUrl`, a non-disposable value is not refused — these suites drop nothing, and the dev database stays a supported second-best.

**Design Decision**: `tests/setup.ts` points the *whole run* at `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, not just the suites

Each suite opens its own connection for fixtures, but the code under test connects through `src/database`, which reads `DATABASE_URL`. Setting only the suites splits the two: fixtures land in the throwaway database, routes write to the dev one, and every foreign key between them fails — which is exactly what happened on the first attempt.

---

**Two things found while proving it works. Both matter more than the isolation.**

**1. A fresh database could not be built at all.**

```
PostgresError: unsafe use of new value "gift_card" of enum type order_type
```

Migration 0011 adds `gift_card` to the `order_type` enum; 0015 (mine, from #574) used that value in an index predicate. drizzle-kit applies the whole batch in ONE transaction, and Postgres refuses to use a new enum value in the transaction that added it. It worked on every existing database only because 0011 had been committed months earlier — so the chain had been unappliable-from-scratch since #574 landed, and nothing would have caught it until someone tried to create a database.

Fixed by predicating on `gift_card_purchase IS NOT NULL AND payment_status = 'paid'` — same rows, and both conjuncts appear in the sweep's own WHERE clause, so the planner still proves the implication. Re-benchmarked at 200k rows: **6.2ms bitmap scan**, identical to the measurement in #574, still using the index. 0018 converges databases migrated before the fix; the dev database was migrated and verified.

**2. The concurrency test did not test concurrency.**

The ticket says "removing `FOR UPDATE` was confirmed to fail the concurrency test, so the coverage is real". It does not fail. I removed `FOR UPDATE` from `redeemGiftCards` and the suite passed 13/13; removed it from `lockBalance` too, still 13/13.

The cause: `Promise.all` of two redeems leaves interleaving to the event loop, and in practice the window does not open. The test now holds the card row from a third connection while both redeems start, so both are guaranteed to be in flight before either can write. With the lock they queue and the second re-reads a spent card; without it they both read 50000, compute the same new balance in JS, and both write it:

```
AssertionError: expected 100000 to be 50000
```

The balance given away twice — the double-spend the lock exists to prevent, now actually caught. Which means the justification for running these against live Postgres is true again rather than merely asserted.

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/tests/helpers/live-db.ts` (new)
- `packages/api/tests/setup.ts`
- 11 suites: `liveDbUrl()` instead of `process.env.DATABASE_URL`, plus the loud guard
- `packages/api/tests/services/gift-card-redeem.test.ts` - the barrier
- `packages/api/src/database/migrations/0015_*.sql`, `0018_*.sql` (new), journal, `schema/orders.ts`
- `.env.example`

**Tests**: 415 passing against the shared dev database and 415 against a `poster_app_test` built from scratch (42 tables, migrated from empty). Typecheck 0 errors.

**Not done**: the transaction-rollback alternative the ticket floated. Wrapping each test in a transaction that always rolls back would remove the cleanup code, but the concurrency test needs two real transactions racing — it cannot live inside one — so that path would have split the suites into two idioms.

ticket.title: Frontend - home reviews rail to Loox parity: mixed media and text slides
ticket.description:
## Task

The third and last Loox surface. Mesonart's home Customer Reviews band is a `<loox-dynamic-carousel-widget>` whose slides **alternate between text-only cards and media-only tiles** — each slide is one or the other. Ours is text-only and never shows a photo, even though the media is already in the payload.

Reference: `docs/design/mesonart/mesonart-home-reviews-band.png`.

The live widget's own configuration, read off the page:

```html
<loox-dynamic-carousel-widget
  corner-radius="40" items-per-view="2" items-per-view-mobile="3"
  max-characters="180" autoplay-delay="5"
  main-color="#ae8868" stars-color="#ff8d00"
  quote-marks-icon="style-1" product-id="">
```

## What changes

| Mesonart | Ours today |
|---|---|
| Slides alternate media-only tiles and text-only cards | Every slide is a text card; no media at all |
| Large serif quote mark on text cards, blush background | Plain white card, no quote mark |
| 40px corner radius | Small radius |
| Autoplay every 5s + dot pagination under the rail | Manual scroll, no dots, no autoplay |
| Body truncated at 180 characters | Untruncated |
| "✓ Daniel N." bottom-right with a verified check | "Test Customer · Cosmic Harmony" bottom-left, no check |
| View All pill on the **right of the header row** | View All below the rail, on the left |

## Context

Part of feature: review-grid-loox-parity
Phase: Frontend

- File: `packages/web/app/components/home/CustomerReviewsSection.tsx`, mounted at `packages/web/app/routes/index.tsx:169`.
- Media is ALREADY in the payload — `GET /api/reviews` returns `media[]` (ready-only) and #495 added `verified`. Nothing new is needed from the API. Read the hook in `packages/web/app/hooks/useReviews.ts` for the exact shape.
- **Keep the suppression rule exactly as it is.** `averageRating === null || reviewCount < MIN_REVIEWS_FOR_HOME_STRIP || reviews.length === 0` returns null, and it sits AFTER the hooks deliberately because hook order may not vary between renders. Do not move it above them.
- **Keep reading the real aggregate.** Mesonart's "9000+ Score 4.9/ 5.0" is hardcoded — its own star `<title>` says "4.9 rating (7000 reviews)" while the label beside it says 9000+. Do not copy the hardcoding; ours shows the true 4.5 / 12.
- Keep the `SectionBand tone="sand"` wrapper and the `data-testid="home-reviews"` / `home-reviews-score` hooks — E2E asserts on them.
- Video slides render `poster`, `preload="none"`, never `autoPlay`. Same rule as the grid; there are existing assertions for it in `ReviewGridCard.test.tsx`.
- **Autoplay must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`** and must pause on hover and on keyboard focus within the rail. An unpausable auto-advancing carousel is an accessibility failure, not a parity win.
- Reuse `ReviewGridCard`'s media handling where it fits rather than writing a third media renderer — but this is a rail, not a masonry cell, so do not force the whole card in.
- vitest gotcha: Node 25's inert localStorage/sessionStorage shadows jsdom's — stub in `vi.hoisted` above the imports if you hit `setItem is not a function`.

ticket.title: Schema - frame type becomes text, new frame_category enum column
ticket.description:
## Task

Make the `frames` table admin-writable in shape: `type` becomes free text with a unique index, and a new closed `category` enum column carries the display grouping the client currently guesses.

The `frame_type` pg enum has ten values, seven used and three dead (`none`, `walnut`, `oak`). That is a hard ceiling incompatible with an admin who can create frames, and the free slots are named for woods nobody stocks. `type` becomes a slug validated `^[a-z0-9-]+$` with a UNIQUE index — unique because `getFramePreviewColor` (FrameSelector.tsx:409) keys its swatch colour map on type, so two frames sharing one are indistinguishable to any type-keyed lookup.

`category` is a NEW pg enum rather than more text, because unlike `type` it is genuinely closed: it is the three rungs `frameGroupLabel` (FrameSelector.tsx:158) renders as "Rolled Canvas/Frameless/Framed". Today `frameCategoryLabel` (FrameSelector.tsx:146) infers the rung from the type string, which lands an admin-created moulding in the right bucket only by accident and an admin-created *format* in the wrong one with no error anywhere.

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 1 (schema). Nothing else in the feature can start until this lands.

Design doc: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-admin-frame-pricing-design.md (commit cbeeff87)

Files:
- packages/api/src/database/schema/products.ts:80 (frameTypeEnum), :243 (frames table)
- packages/api/src/database/migrations/ — next is 0014, journal idx 14
- packages/api/src/database/seed-frames.ts — seven rows to give a category

The migration is HAND-WRITTEN, not `drizzle-kit generate` output. Generate emits no backfill, and dropping the enum before backfilling destroys the source data. Order is load-bearing — `SET NOT NULL` must follow the backfill, and `DROP TYPE frame_type` must follow the column conversion or Postgres refuses it.

Test pattern: packages/api/tests/database/shipping-config-schema.test.ts — shape assertions on the drizzle objects, because the route suites mock `db` and nothing else in the API catches a column that does not exist.

```

 Stretch + White Frame  | white     | framed

```

INSERT ... VALUES ('Dupe', 'gold', 'framed', '1.40');

ticket.title: Shared - frame input schemas and price bounds
ticket.description:
## Task

Add the Zod contracts the admin frame routes and the admin form both validate against, so the two cannot disagree about what a frame may hold.

`createFrameInputSchema`, `updateFrameInputSchema = createFrameInputSchema.partial()`, and `frameCategorySchema`.

Price bounds:
- `priceModifier` in [1.00, 5.00]
- `priceAddition` in [0, 99999.99] — fits decimal(10,2)

The modifier floor is 1.00 rather than 0 because `frameAddition` (shared/constants/frames.ts:570) already clamps a below-one modifier to zero markup: `Math.max(0, toAmount(frame.priceModifier, 1) - 1)`. Accepting 0.5 would store a number the pricing formula silently ignores, so the form rejects it instead. That coupling is the point — assert it, don't just document it.

`type` is validated `^[a-z0-9-]+$` to match the unique text column from ticket 1.

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 2 (shared contracts). Blocked by the schema ticket.

Files:

ticket.title: Admin API - archive a frame, never hard delete, and never the last one
ticket.description:
## Task

`DELETE /api/admin/frames/:id` sets `isActive: false` and returns. It never issues a SQL delete.

`cartItems.frameId` (schema/cart.ts:123) and `orderItems.frameId` (schema/orders.ts:318) are both `onDelete: "set null"`. A hard delete would therefore succeed quietly and strip the frame off historical orders — no error, no cascade failure, just orders that no longer record what the customer bought. Archiving means that clause never fires, which is the point of choosing it.

Precedent: admin/products.ts:642 archives by setting `status: "archived"` for the same reason.

Second guard: **refuse to archive the last active frame**. Return 409. A product detail page with no format options is a broken buy panel — there is no "just the print" fallback, because Rolled Canvas is itself a frame row.

Also add the unarchive path (PATCH with `isActive: true` already covers it via ticket #585's route — assert it works rather than adding a second endpoint).

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 3 (admin API). Blocked by the list/create/patch ticket — same route file.

Both guards must bust the frames cache, through the same `purgeFramesCache` helper the other mutations use.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
⚠️ **Correction to the verification above, and a follow-up fix.**

My completion comment listed `bunx tsc --noEmit` as clean. I did not run it after writing the archive handler — I ran it during #585 and reported that result. When I actually ran tsc while working #588, this surfaced:

```
src/routes/admin/frames.ts(253,14): error TS2339:
Property 'count' does not exist on type '{ count: number; } | undefined'
```

The destructure `const [{ count: activeCount }] = await db.select({ count: count() })...` assumed the aggregate always yields a row. TypeScript is right that the array element is possibly undefined.

**Fixed** in commit `65cee1a1` (carried with #588, since that is where tsc was run):

```ts
const [activeRow] = await db.select({ count: count() })...
const activeCount = activeRow?.count ?? 1;
```

The fallback is `1`, not `0`, deliberately: no row means the count cannot prove another active frame exists, and the safe reading of that is to **refuse the archive** rather than permit it on a guess. Defaulting to 0 would have made an unreadable count silently authorise archiving the last frame — the exact outcome this guard exists to prevent.

Tests unchanged and still green: `frames-archive` 8 + `frames` 14 + `products-frames` 6 = 28 passing, `tsc --noEmit` now genuinely 0 errors.

ticket.title: Admin API - swatch upload through StoragePaths.FRAMES
ticket.description:
## Task

`POST /api/admin/frames/upload-image` — multipart, one file, returns the two URLs the frame row stores.

Calls `uploadOptimizedImage(buffer, filename, contentType, { prefix: StoragePaths.FRAMES })` **directly**. NOT `buildProductMedia`.

That distinction is the ticket. `buildProductMedia` (lib/product-media.ts:51) mats artwork, measures the art box, and honours an admin-chosen crop window — all of which exist because artwork must never be cropped blindly. A frame swatch is product photography: it fills its square and there is nothing to measure. Routing it through the artwork pipeline would mat a photo of a moulding onto a canvas border for no reason.

`StoragePaths.FRAMES` (lib/storage.ts:76) already exists with **zero consumers** — a reserved prefix this is the first use of.

The response's variant ladder maps onto the two existing columns: `thumbnail` variant → `thumbnailUrl`, `card` variant → `imageUrl`. One upload fills both, so the admin form needs no second image field.

Guards come from `ADMIN_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` and `MAX_ADMIN_IMAGE_MB` in @chobii/shared (ticket #584) — not a local copy.

Both image columns stay plain text, so the seven seeded rows pointing at `/frames/*.png` in packages/web/public/frames/ keep working untouched. Assert that.

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 3 (admin API). Blocked by the CRUD route ticket (same file) and #584 (shared guards).

ticket.title: Admin UI - live price preview through the shared frameAddition
ticket.description:
## Task

The price preview, beneath the two price inputs, recomputing as the admin types:

```
Stretch + Gold Frame  ×1.40  +₹0
  on a ₹1,499 print    +₹600     → ₹2,099
  on a ₹4,999 print    +₹2,000   → ₹6,999
  on a ₹14,999 print   +₹6,000   → ₹20,999
```

**It calls `frameAddition()` from @chobii/shared directly.** Not a reimplementation, not a display-formatted copy, not "the same arithmetic inline".

This is the whole lesson of #566. That bug existed because the PDP re-derived a formula the server already owned, and it went unnoticed for as long as it did because every seeded frame happened to make both answers agree. A preview with its own arithmetic would be that bug again in a worse place — this is the screen whose entire job is to convince the admin the number is right.

Three reference prices from `FRAME_PREVIEW_REFERENCE_PRICES` (#584), not one. A frame is priced as a proportion of the piece precisely so its cost tracks the size of it; a single sample row would show a number while hiding the behaviour being chosen.

**The coupling test is the point of this ticket**: assert the preview's output equals the server's answer for a frame carrying BOTH a non-zero `priceModifier` AND a non-zero `priceAddition`. That is #566's missing case, asserted from the admin side.

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 4 (admin UI). Blocked by the form ticket.

Files:
- packages/shared/src/constants/frames.ts:570 — frameAddition, the one formula
- packages/api/src/routes/cart.ts — resolveFramePrice, the server side of the coupling
- packages/web/app/components/product/FrameSelector.tsx:110 — the storefront already calls frameAddition; this joins that chain rather than starting a new one

**Commit**: `5a711db0` — feat(admin): the frame form quotes the price the customer will actually pay

**Files Changed**:

- `packages/web/app/routes/admin/frames/FrameForm.tsx` — the reserved slot filled

**On how strong the coupling claim actually is** — worth stating precisely rather than overclaiming:

I checked what the server does rather than assuming. `resolveFramePrice` (`api/src/routes/cart.ts:354`) is a `.toFixed(2)` wrapper over `frameAddition`, and `FrameSelector.tsx:110` calls `frameAddition` directly since #566. So the admin preview, the buy panel and the cart are now calling **literally the same function** — the coupling is structural, not a convention.

That makes `expect(row.addition).toBe(frameAddition(...))` close to tautological on its own. Its real job is to fail loudly if someone later "optimises" the preview by inlining the arithmetic. The genuinely independent checks are the behavioural ones: that the flat column contributes exactly +250 at every size (#566's failure, from the admin side), that a below-one modifier clamps to zero rather than discounting, and that a percentage-only frame scales with the piece while a flat-only frame does not.

**Two tests beyond the ticket:**
- **Rupee rounding is pinned.** `frameAddition` rounds at calculation time, deliberately, so the quoted number is the one that reaches the cart. A preview that re-rounded at display time or showed paise would drift in exactly #566's way. Asserted with a deliberately awkward `1.333` / `0.50`.
- **A flat-only frame adds the same at every size**, the complement of the scaling test — together they prove the two columns behave differently, so a preview showing one could never stand in for both.

**One deliberate behaviour**: nothing is quoted until *both* fields parse. A half-typed `1.` parses to `1` and an empty box to `NaN`; quoting either mid-keystroke would show a wrong number on the one screen whose purpose is to be trusted. It renders a prompt instead.

ticket.title: E2E - an admin reprices a frame and the storefront charges it
ticket.description:
## Task

`tests/e2e/admin-frames.spec.ts` — the journey the unit tests cannot cover, because each of them stubs the surface on the other side of the boundary.

The flow:
1. Admin signs in, opens /admin/frames, sees the seeded catalogue.
2. Edits a framed option's `priceModifier` and its `priceAddition` — **both non-zero**, since that is the combination nothing carried before this feature and the one #566 mispriced.
3. Saves; the preview's quoted number is captured before saving.
4. Storefront: open a product, choose that frame. **The buy panel quotes the number the preview quoted.**
5. Add to cart. **The cart charges the same number.**
6. Restore the frame's original pricing so the run is repeatable.

Step 4 is the one worth the E2E cost. It crosses the cache boundary (the admin write has to have busted the frames key or the PDP shows the old price), the shared-formula boundary, and the wire.

Also: archive a frame, confirm it leaves the storefront panel; unarchive it, confirm it returns.

## Context

Feature: admin-frame-management. Phase 6. Blocked by everything else — last ticket.

Files:
- tests/e2e/admin-products.spec.ts — admin auth setup and navigation to copy
- tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts — stored admin session
- playwright.config.ts at the repo root

Repo convention: E2E is written per-feature, not per-ticket — this is that pass.

Hazards, from prior sessions:
- Port :5173 serves a DIFFERENT app. Point the run at this project's dev server, or the suite passes vacuously against something else entirely.
- Scope selectors for mobile vs desktop — the same test ids exist in both trees.
- `await page.goto(path, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })` in beforeEach.

ticket.title: Card art framing — measure artBox server-side and re-frame each piece on equal ink area
ticket.description:
## Why this ticket exists

Filed retroactively to carry work that was already written but had no ticket. The code was committed as work-in-progress; it is NOT finished, and the acceptance criteria below are not met yet. See "State at filing".

## The problem

Every stored product image is a 1500x1500 master with the mat BAKED INTO THE PIXELS: `matToSquare` contains the artwork at MAT_ART_INSET (88%) of its LONGEST side and fills the rest with MAT_COLOR. That rule normalises the long side and nothing else, so what a card actually draws varies enormously — and the stored asset reports `1500x1500` for a 2:1 panorama and a perfect square alike, so the card cannot tell them apart and draws the same plate for both.

Two consequences. The row reads as one big picture beside three small ones, and the card's own plate colour is invisible, because the baked mat is #FAFAFA — 2% against white.

## The approach

`ProductImage.artBox` is the missing measurement: where the artwork actually sits inside its square master, normalised 0..1. The storefront cannot take it, so the API does, by scanning inward for bare wall (light, flat, holding no edge — judged on the 2nd and 98th percentiles so a single JPEG speck cannot keep a blank line alive).

Given artBox, `packages/web/app/components/product/artFraming.ts` returns the two CSS properties that re-frame the piece: `clip-path` crops the baked mat away so the card's plate is the only background, and `transform` scales and centres what is left onto the target rect.

The rule is EQUAL INK AREA, CAPPED BY THE PLATE'S CORNER RADIUS. It is the third rule tried; the two before it lost blind A/Bs against the reference:

- equal AREA, uncapped — every card carries the same ink, but the long sides spread 1.39x, so the row still arrives at four sizes
- one shared BOX — every long side identical, but coverage spreads 1.93x; a 1.02:1 piece fills 79% of its plate while a 1.98:1 piece fills 41%

Neither is wrong in isolation. With the plate square and the art centred, coverage = L^2 * r, so holding coverage constant forces L proportional to r^-0.5 and holding L constant forces coverage proportional to r. You cannot have both unless every piece has the same r. The reference's Best Seller stock runs r 0.75..0.98; ours runs 0.48..0.98 over 41 products, with 39% of the catalogue at 2:1.

So the constants are read off the bar, not argued from principle. Both measured reference bands are recorded in artFraming.ts's header with the capture method and the thresholds the figures were re-run at.

## State at filing

Written and committed WIP. Tests pass — 20 in artFraming.test.ts, 25 across image-processing-art-box.test.ts and collection-imagery.test.ts, plus ProductCardMedia, ProductCard.tokens and ChooseOptions, 139 in total — and nothing else in the suite regressed.

What is NOT done:

1. **The backfill has not been run.** `bun run backfill:art-box` (packages/api/src/database/backfill-art-box.ts) measures and stores artBox for existing rows. Until it runs against a database, every card falls back to the old framing and none of this is visible. This is the reason the feature is half-applied on disk.
2. **It has not won a blind A/B.** The band this serves has lost three consecutive blind comparisons against the reference.
3. **#564 says framing is not the remaining gap.** The round-4 cropper found that the reference's Best Seller band carries a category pill row on both viewports and ours carries none — a whole row of content that no amount of artwork framing will close. Sequence #564 before spending further rounds here.

## Acceptance

- `backfill:art-box` has been run and every catalogue image carries an artBox
- a card's plate colour is visible, because the baked mat is clipped rather than drawn
- coverage across a mixed row sits inside the spread measured off the reference rather than ours
- a blind A/B of the Best Sellers band against the reference no longer identifies which is which on framing grounds

## Context

- Serves #530 (Best Sellers rail) and #534 (New In carousel), both done — this is follow-through on their blind-comparison loop, not new scope.
- Blocked in practice by #564 (missing category pill row), which is the stronger tell.
- Builds on #365 (matToSquare) and #418 (strip the border a source arrives with, so cards show one mat).
