ticket.title: Mobile chrome scroll rule is inverted — top bar and tab bar both behave opposite to mesonart
ticket.description:
## Task
`useMobileNavScroll` drives both mobile bars off scroll DIRECTION, and in the direction opposite to the reference.

Current (`packages/web/app/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.ts:47-52`):
```ts
isTopMenuVisible: isScrollingDown,     // top bar appears when scrolling DOWN
isBottomMenuVisible: !isScrollingDown, // tab bar disappears when scrolling DOWN
```

Measured on mesonart.com at mobile width:
- top bar: visible at/near the top; once past the threshold it takes `translateY(-72px)` and STAYS hidden — scrolling back up ~300px does not bring it back, only returning near the top does. No direction term at all.
- bottom dock: `translateY(62.6px)` (hidden) at scroll 0; slides to `translateY(0)` once scrolled and stays up while scrolling in BOTH directions. Also no direction term.

So the fix deletes the direction logic rather than flipping it.

## Context
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.ts` — `THRESHOLD_PX = 60`, `JITTER_PX = 6`; with direction gone, `JITTER_PX` and the `lastY` ref are dead and should go with it
- Consumers: `Header.tsx:99` and `:197` (top bar transform), `MobileTabBar.tsx:117-119` (`isVisible`)
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.test.ts` currently asserts the direction cases — rewrite, do not extend
- The hook has an uncommitted working-tree change that introduced the current inversion; this ticket supersedes it

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `784f2564` - fix(web): mobile chrome follows scroll position, not scroll direction

**Root Cause**

Two commits on Aug 9 built the rule off scroll direction, and neither referenced a ticket:
- `cb54d267` added `useMobileNavScroll` with a direction term
- `40b77ef1` "reveal when page moves up" coupled both bars to `delta > 0`

An uncommitted working-tree change then flipped the bottom bar to `!isScrollingDown`. All three variants were wrong in the same way — the reference has no direction term at all, so the fix deleted the logic rather than flipping it. That working-tree change is now superseded, as the ticket anticipated.

**Files Changed**
- `packages/web/app/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.ts` — reduced to a position test; `lastY` and `JITTER_PX` deleted
- `packages/web/tests/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.test.ts` — rewritten around the threshold rule
- `packages/web/app/components/layout/Header.tsx` — comment only; the existing `#421` note sat above both hook calls and read as if it covered both

**Design Decisions**

1. **State is one boolean, not the pair.** Every scroll event re-sets it, and React bails out of the re-render when the value is unchanged. Returning a fresh `{isTopMenuVisible, isBottomMenuVisible}` object each time would have re-rendered the header on every scroll event instead. The object is assembled on return.

2. **The effect calls `sync()` on mount.** A route change can land mid-page; without it the bars mount in the top-of-page state and flash before the first scroll event corrects them. Same reasoning `useNavReveal` uses for seeding `lastY`.

3. **Initial state is `isAtTop: true`** — top bar visible, tab bar hidden. Matches the reference at scroll 0 (`translateY(62.6px)` on the dock) and keeps SSR deterministic.

**Verified: no conflict with #421.** The desktop nav rows are `md:block` and the header transform this drives is `md:translate-y-0`, so `useNavReveal` and this hook never both apply. Left `useNavReveal` untouched.

**Tests**
- `tests/hooks/useMobileNavScroll.test.ts` — 7 tests: threshold boundary (60 vs 61), direction-independence when scrolling back up mid-page, return-near-top, mount-mid-page, and a 59→61 crawl that the old `JITTER_PX` guard used to swallow
- Green: hook 7/7, `MobileTabBar` 16/16, `Header.structure` 27/27
- Full web suite: **2926 passed / 1 failed**

**Two notes for the tracker**

- The ticket's step commands say `pnpm --filter @chobii/web test` — the project is configured for bun and pnpm refuses to run it. Actual command: `cd packages/web && bun run vitest run <path>`. Worth fixing in the ticket template.
- The one suite failure is `tests/routes/wishlist-page.test.ts` (asserts the wishlist route source contains no `beforeLoad`). Pre-existing on this branch and unrelated — that file is untouched and unmodified in the working tree. Not fixed here; may deserve its own ticket.

ticket.title: Panoramic products sell a portrait size ladder — every step is stored tall
ticket.description:
Found while auditing the catalogue for #545.

All 8 panoramic products in the dev catalogue carry the panoramic ladder — correct — but every step of it is stored SHORT SIDE FIRST, so the PDP offers a panorama in `12" × 36"`, `18" × 36"`, `16" × 48"` … which is a tall poster, not a wide one.

```
SELECT p.orientation,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.width_inches > v.height_inches) AS wide,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.width_inches < v.height_inches) AS tall
FROM products p JOIN product_variants v ON v.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY 1;

 panoramic  |  0  | 104
```

Where it comes from: `PANORAMIC_SIZES` in `packages/shared/src/constants/sizes.ts` is written `[12, 36], [18, 36], [16, 48] …` — width first, so every literal is a 1:3 tall rectangle. `orientFor` in `packages/api/src/database/seed-variants.ts` transposes only `landscape`, on the strength of a comment that says "panoramic is already stored wide". It is not. That comment is the bug; the data disagrees with it and nothing tests the claim.

Compare `square` (13 square steps), `portrait` (17 tall) and `landscape` (17 wide) — all three are right. Panoramic is the only family whose stored dimensions contradict its own name.

To close: decide which layer owns the transposition — either write `PANORAMIC_SIZES` long-side-first, or extend `orientFor` to flip panoramic the way it flips landscape — then add the assertion that keeps it fixed, beside `swaps width and height for landscape against portrait` in `packages/api/tests/database/seed-variants.test.ts`. `sizeLabel`, `widthCm`/`heightCm` and `ProductSize.displayLabelDual` all follow from the same numbers, so check every one of them ends up oriented. Existing panoramic variants in the dev DB need rebuilding afterwards; `order_items.variant_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and `cart_items` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so retire referenced rows rather than deleting them (see the approach recorded on #545).

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `e47aa077` — fix(sizes): a panoramic product sells wide sizes, not tall ones

### Root cause

Two statements in the codebase contradicted the data, and neither was tested.

`PANORAMIC_SIZES` in `packages/shared/src/constants/sizes.ts` is written short-side-first — `[12, 36]`, `[18, 36]`, `[16, 48]` — exactly like `PORTRAIT_LANDSCAPE_SIZES`, because every ladder here is a list of manufacturing rectangles rather than a shape. Its own docstring said "wide format for landscape scenes" over literals that are 1:3 **tall**.

`orientFor` in `packages/api/src/database/seed-variants.ts:38` turned only `landscape`, on the strength of a comment reading "Square is unaffected; panoramic is already stored wide". It is not.

So the emitted rows were the ladder untouched: `12" × 36"` for a panorama.

**This was customer-facing.** `ChooseOptions.tsx` documents why — the size list has to be the product's real variants, because the cart carries `variantId` through to checkout, so it cannot be synthesised from `getSizesForOrientation()` on the client. The PDP and the Choose Options panel were reading these rows directly. Every one of the eight panoramic products offered a tall poster.

### Which layer owns the transposition

Kept in the seed, in `orientFor`, now a `TURNED_ORIENTATIONS` set of `landscape` and `panoramic`.

Rewriting the ladder literals long-side-first was the alternative and is worse. `buildLadder` derives each step's id from its dimensions, so every `panoramic-12x36` becomes `panoramic-36x12` — churning ids across the shared tests for a **labelling** decision that is not the ladder's to make. And the ladder's model is already the right one: one set of manufacturing sizes, labelled per orientation, exactly as mesonart shares rect-14 between Vertical and Horizontal (§5.2). Panoramic simply belonged in the turned group all along.

Checked before deciding: `getSizesForOrientation` has exactly one real caller in the monorepo — `seed-variants.ts`. The three other hits (`ChooseOptions.tsx`, `schema/products.ts`, `facets.ts`) are all prose in comments. There is no `size_id` column on `product_variants`, so no persisted id depends on the literals either way.

The misleading docstring on `PANORAMIC_SIZES` is corrected to say short-side-first and to name who turns it.

### Dev database

Rebuilt all 8 panoramic products' variants. Two variants carried real order history (`desert-bloom`, `ocean-horizon`) and were **retired** (`is_active = false`) rather than deleted, per the `ON DELETE SET NULL` / `ON DELETE CASCADE` hazard recorded on #545. `SELECT count(*) FROM order_items WHERE variant_id IS NULL` is still 0.

Every orientation's active variants now agree with its own name:

```
 orientation | wide | tall | sq  | retired
-------------+------+------+-----+---------
 square      |    0 |    0 | 104 |       0
 portrait    |    0 |  272 |   0 |       1
 landscape   |  119 |    0 |   0 |       0
 panoramic   |  104 |    0 |   0 |       2
 set-of-2-3  |    0 |   34 |   0 |       0
```

Live API after a cache purge — `GET /api/products/ocean-horizon`:

```
orientation: panoramic
36" × 12" / 91 × 30 cm | 36" × 18" / 91 × 46 cm | 48" × 16" / 122 × 41 cm
variants: 13
```

**Files changed**
- `packages/api/src/database/seed-variants.ts` — `TURNED_ORIENTATIONS`, and the comment that caused this rewritten to state which orientations turn and why
- `packages/shared/src/constants/sizes.ts` — `PANORAMIC_SIZES` docstring corrected

**Tests added** (`packages/api/tests/database/seed-variants.test.ts`, 4 new, all red first)
- every panoramic step is wider than it is tall
- every panoramic step lands in the panoramic band under `orientationFromRatio` — the same rule the orientation column is measured against (#545), applied to the poster instead of the picture, so "is it oriented" has one definition
- cm and `sizeLabel` turn with the inches rather than separately; `displayLabelDual` is written for the stored order and would have printed the sides backwards
- turning changes neither the price taper nor the ascending-area order

**Verification**: seed-variants 14 passed; shared 956 passed; api database + products + admin routes 1239 passed. Three pre-existing failures, none touched by this work — `products-role-access.test.ts` ×2 (the `unitsSoldSql` timeout recorded 2026-08-04) and `products.test.ts > should filter by styles`, which requests `styles=minimalist,abstract` and gets a 400 because neither is in the STYLE_OPTIONS vocabulary (`minimalist-art` is; `abstract` is a subject). API typecheck clean.

ticket.title: Admin dashboard shows 0 products / 0 low stock — /api/admin/products/stats does not exist
ticket.description:
## Problem

The admin dashboard renders fabricated zeros for every product tile. Operators will read "0 products, 0 low stock, 0 out of stock" and trust it.

## Root cause

`packages/web/app/routes/admin/index.tsx` `fetchProductStats()` calls:

```
GET ${getApiUrl()}/api/admin/products/stats
```

No `/stats` route is registered in `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts`. Grepped the whole of `packages/api/src` — there is no products stats handler anywhere. The request therefore falls through to the `GET /:id` handler (products.ts:468) with `id="stats"`, which cannot resolve.

The client then swallows the failure:

```ts
if (!response.ok) {
  // Return default stats if endpoint doesn't exist yet
  return {
    totalProducts: 0,
    activeProducts: 0,
    lowStockProducts: 0,
    outOfStockProducts: 0,
  }
}
```

So there is no error state, no console warning, no empty state — just plausible-looking wrong numbers on the first screen an admin sees. Low-stock is exactly the tile you would launch on.

Compare `fetchOrderStats()` in the same file, which hits the real `GET /api/admin/orders/stats` (orders.ts:356) and throws on failure. The two sit side by side with opposite error contracts.

## Fix

1. Implement `GET /api/admin/products/stats` in `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts`, returning `{ totalProducts, activeProducts, lowStockProducts, outOfStockProducts }`. Register it **above** `GET /:id` so the literal path wins. Mirror the shape of the orders stats handler.
2. Remove the silent zero fallback in `fetchProductStats()` — throw like `fetchOrderStats()` does, and let the dashboard show its error state.
3. Decide and document the low-stock threshold (there is no constant for it today).

## Verification

- API test asserting `GET /api/admin/products/stats` returns the four counts against seeded fixtures, and that a product with stock below threshold lands in `lowStockProducts`.
- API test asserting `GET /api/admin/products/stats` is not shadowed by `GET /:id`.
- Web test asserting the dashboard surfaces an error (not zeros) when the stats call fails.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `138209f9` — fix(admin): implement products stats endpoint and stop faking zeros

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/products.ts` — `GET /stats` registered ABOVE `GET /:id` (Hono matches in registration order; below it, "stats" hits the UUID validator and 400s — the original bug). Returns the four counts; a failed query answers 500, never zeros.
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/product-stats.test.ts` — mocked driver: route not shadowed by `/:id`, four numeric keys, 500 on query failure.
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/product-stats-counts.test.ts` — real Postgres, 9 seeded `T602-` fixtures, delta assertions (additive + self-reaping, so it is correct against a populated dev DB).
- `packages/web/app/routes/admin/index.tsx` — `fetchProductStats()` throws like `fetchOrderStats()`; error banner gets `role="alert"`; Active Products tile renders `—`, not `0`, when stats are unavailable.
- `packages/web/tests/routes/admin/dashboard-product-stats.test.tsx` — error surfaced, no fabricated zero, order tiles unaffected.

**Threshold decision (item 3 of the fix)**: no new constant. `product_variants.low_stock_threshold` already exists per variant (default 5) — a 12x16 print and a gallery canvas do not run out at the same number, and a hard-coded value here would silently override what a merchandiser set on the row.

**Counter scopes** (deliberately not the same population, documented in the handler):
- `totalProducts` — every product row, drafts and archived included.
- `activeProducts` — `status = 'active'`.
- `lowStockProducts` / `outOfStockProducts` — ACTIVE products only; these are restocking alarms, and a draft or retired product is not work waiting for an operator. Low = any active variant with `0 < stock <= its own threshold` (at-threshold counts: "5 left, threshold 5" is the moment to reorder). Out = no active variant with stock left, which includes a product carrying no sellable variant. Mutually exclusive by construction.

**Verification**:
- Command: `DATABASE_URL=…:5440 npx vitest run tests/routes/admin/product-stats.test.ts tests/routes/admin/product-stats-counts.test.ts`
- Result: PASS (2 files, 10 tests)
- Command: `npx vitest run tests/routes/admin/dashboard-product-stats.test.tsx` (web)
- Result: PASS (1 file, 4 tests)
- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` — api 0 errors; web 22 errors, all pre-existing, none in touched files.

**Two things worth recording:**
1. The counts suite passed VACUOUSLY on its first run — the baseline `/stats` request sat inside the same try/catch as the connectivity check, so a missing route read as "database unreachable" and the suite skipped itself green against the exact bug it was written for. Fixed by probing the driver (`select … limit 1`) and letting the endpoint request fail loudly. Mutation-checked afterwards (expected low delta 3 → 99) to confirm the assertions bind.
2. `tests/routes/admin/products-role-access.test.ts` has 2 failures ("allows content-manager/admin to list admin products", 500 vs 200). Confirmed pre-existing by running it against the HEAD copy of `products.ts` — unrelated to this change, not fixed here.

**Out of scope, but adjacent**: `fetchOrderStats()` failing still renders ₹0 revenue and 0 orders through the same `?? 0` pattern — same class of bug on the order tiles. Not touched; worth its own ticket.

ticket.title: Admin sidebar links to four routes that do not exist (ai-generations, analytics, categories, settings)
ticket.description:
## Problem

Four of the sixteen admin nav items 404. They are among the first things a new operator clicks.

| Link | Declared at | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| `/admin/ai-generations` | `AdminSidebar.tsx:113`, `admin/index.tsx:324` | No route. The screen was renamed to `/admin/ai-moderation`; the nav was never updated. |

Product taxonomy is collections. The nav item points at a concept the data model does not have. |
| `/admin/settings` | `AdminSidebar.tsx:156` | No route, no API. |

Verified against `packages/web/app/routeTree.gen.ts` — the only `/admin/*` paths that exist are: ai-moderation, approvals, collections, customers, frames, gift-cards, orders, products, promotions, returns, reviews, shipping.

Note both the sidebar **and** the dashboard quick-action cards carry the stale links, so removing them from `AdminSidebar.tsx` alone is not enough.

## Fix

- Point `AI Generations` at `/admin/ai-moderation` and relabel it to match the screen (or drop it, since `AI Moderation` is already listed at `AdminSidebar.tsx:103` — right now they are two nav entries for one screen).
- Remove `Analytics`, `Categories`, `Settings` from `NAV_ITEMS` / `SECONDARY_NAV_ITEMS` until the screens exist. `Categories` should not come back at all unless a categories model is introduced.

Add a test in `packages/web/tests/components/admin/AdminSidebar.test.tsx` that asserts every `href` in `NAV_ITEMS` and `SECONDARY_NAV_ITEMS` resolves to a path present in the generated route tree. That turns this class of drift into a failing test rather than a 404 in production.

ticket.title: Orders list ships an Export button that fires a blocking native alert('Export functionality coming soon')
ticket.description:
## Problem

`packages/web/app/routes/admin/orders/index.tsx:407`:

```tsx
{/* Export Button (placeholder) */}
<button onClick={() => alert('Export functionality coming soon')}>
```

Two problems, not one:

1. A shipped, enabled-looking button that does nothing. On a launched store an operator will try to export orders for accounting on day one.
2. `alert()` is a **blocking native dialog**. It freezes the browser automation harness outright, so any E2E run that clicks near it stalls — the same hazard `reviews.tsx:269` documents in its own comment about `window.confirm`.

## Fix

Pick one:

- **Remove the button** until CSV export is built (cheapest, unblocks launch), or
- **Implement it**: `GET /api/admin/orders/export?...` streaming CSV with the same filters the list is currently showing, so what you download matches what you see.

Either way the `alert()` must go. If some interim messaging is wanted, use the inline pattern, never a native dialog.

## Verification

- If removed: assert no Export control renders on `/admin/orders`.
- If implemented: API test for the CSV payload and header row; E2E asserting the download applies the active status/date filters.
- Grep guard: no `alert(` under `packages/web/app/routes/admin`.

ticket.title: Admin dashboard renders ₹0 revenue / 0 orders when the order stats call fails
ticket.description:
## Problem

Same class as #602, other half of the same screen. `fetchOrderStats()` throws correctly, but `packages/web/app/routes/admin/index.tsx` swallows it:

```ts
const [orders, products, recent] = await Promise.all([
  fetchOrderStats().catch(() => null),
  ...
])
```

`orderStats` becomes `null` and every tile fed by it renders a fabricated figure through `?? 0` / `|| 0`:

- Total Revenue — `formatPrice(parseFloat(orderStats?.totalRevenue || '0'))` → **₹0**
- This Month — same → **₹0**
- Today's Orders — `orderStats?.todayOrders || 0` → **0**
- Pending Orders — derived from `orderStats.byStatus`, defaults to **0**
- Total Orders / Paid Orders — reduced over an empty object → **0**

An operator reads "₹0 revenue, 0 orders today, 0 pending" and cannot tell a dead endpoint from a dead trading day. Revenue is the worst possible tile to be confidently wrong about.

Unlike #602 the endpoint exists (`GET /api/admin/orders/stats`, `packages/api/src/routes/admin/orders.ts:356`), so this only bites on a 5xx, an auth expiry, or a network failure — rarer than #602, and correspondingly more likely to be believed when it happens.

## Fix

Mirror what #602 did for products (commit `138209f9`):

1. When `orderStats` is null, set the dashboard error state naming the orders half, same as the products branch already does.
2. Render `—` rather than a number in each order-fed tile. Money tiles need it most: `formatPrice(0)` produces a real-looking ₹0.00.
3. Keep the failure scoped — a dead orders call must not blank the product tiles, and vice versa.

## Verification

- Web test: orders stats call fails → an alert is surfaced and no order tile renders `0` or `₹0.00`.
- Web test: orders fails while products succeeds → product tiles still show their real counts.
- Existing `packages/web/tests/routes/admin/dashboard-product-stats.test.tsx` covers the mirror case and should keep passing.

ticket.title: Database Schema - Vendor core tables (vendors, contacts, capabilities, rates)
ticket.description:
## Task
Add the vendor directory tables: `vendors`, `vendor_contacts`, `vendor_capabilities`, `vendor_rates`. Table definitions, relations and type exports only — no routes, no validation logic (that lands in the access-control and API phases).

## Context
Feature: vendor-management (sub-project 1 of 5). Phase 1 of 7.

Follow `packages/api/src/database/schema/ai-generation-reviews.ts` for file shape: pgTable + pgEnum + explicit `index()` entries in the table's second argument, `relations()` block, `$inferSelect`/`$inferInsert` type exports at the bottom.

Key design constraints from the approved design:
- Money is `decimal(10,2)` INR, matching orders/products. NOT walletPricingConfig's paise, NOT shipping_config's whole rupees. The repo documents this 100x hazard.
- `vendor_capabilities` is one row per capability, so "prints up to 24x36, frames up to 40x60" is two rows and neither constrains the other.
- `vendor_rates` bands match on the item's LONGEST EDGE in inches, inclusive-min / exclusive-max, effective-dated via `effectiveFrom` / nullable `effectiveTo`. Overlap enforcement is a write-time concern and belongs to the Phase 2 ticket, not to the schema.
- `vendor_contacts` is a child table rather than loose columns on vendors: a shop has an owner and a production contact, and it is the seam the portal needs.

Export the new module from `packages/api/src/database/schema/index.ts`. Do NOT generate the migration in this ticket — the migration is generated once, after all Phase 1 tables exist.

implementation_steps.description: Create the vendor core schema module
implementation_steps.code:
/**
 * Vendor Directory Schema
 *
 * Third-party print shops and framers, their contacts, what they can make,
 * and what they charge. Sub-project 1 of the fulfilment decomposition.
 *
 * Money is decimal(10,2) INR, matching orders and products — NOT
 * walletPricingConfig's paise and NOT shipping_config's whole rupees. Vendor
 * money is transactional, so it follows orders.
 */

import {
  pgTable,
  text,
  timestamp,
  uuid,
  pgEnum,
  index,
  boolean,
  integer,
  decimal,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'
import { relations } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { users } from './users'

export const vendorStatusEnum = pgEnum('vendor_status', ['active', 'inactive', 'suspended'])

/** A capability, and a rate, is either for printing or for framing. */
export const vendorCapabilityKindEnum = pgEnum('vendor_capability_kind', ['print', 'frame'])

export const vendors = pgTable(
  'vendors',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    name: text('name').notNull(),
    status: vendorStatusEnum('status').default('active').notNull(),
    addressLine1: text('address_line1'),
    addressLine2: text('address_line2'),
    city: text('city'),
    state: text('state'),
    postalCode: text('postal_code'),
    country: text('country').default('IN'),
    notes: text('notes'),
    createdBy: text('created_by').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at')
      .defaultNow()
      .notNull()
      .$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
  },
  (table) => ({
    statusIdx: index('vendors_status_idx').on(table.status),
    nameIdx: index('vendors_name_idx').on(table.name),
  })
)

/**
 * A child table rather than loose columns on `vendors`: a shop has an owner
 * and a production contact, and this is the seam the portal invite needs.
 */
export const vendorContacts = pgTable(
  'vendor_contacts',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    vendorId: uuid('vendor_id')
      .references(() => vendors.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    name: text('name').notNull(),
    phone: text('phone'),
    email: text('email'),
    contactRole: text('contact_role'),
    isPrimary: boolean('is_primary').default(false).notNull(),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at')
      .defaultNow()
      .notNull()
      .$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
  },
  (table) => ({
    vendorIdIdx: index('vendor_contacts_vendor_id_idx').on(table.vendorId),
  })
)

/**
 * One row per capability, so "prints up to 24x36, frames up to 40x60" is two
 * rows and neither constrains the other. Drives the assignment filter.
 */
export const vendorCapabilities = pgTable(
  'vendor_capabilities',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    vendorId: uuid('vendor_id')
      .references(() => vendors.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    kind: vendorCapabilityKindEnum('kind').notNull(),
    maxWidthInches: integer('max_width_inches'),
    maxHeightInches: integer('max_height_inches'),
    finishes: text('finishes').array(),
    statedTurnaroundDays: integer('stated_turnaround_days'),
    notes: text('notes'),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at')
      .defaultNow()
      .notNull()
      .$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
  },
  (table) => ({
    vendorIdIdx: index('vendor_capabilities_vendor_id_idx').on(table.vendorId),
    kindIdx: index('vendor_capabilities_kind_idx').on(table.kind),
  })
)

/**
 * Rate bands match on the item's LONGEST EDGE in inches. Ranges are
 * inclusive-min, exclusive-max, and must not overlap for a given
 * (vendorId, kind, finish) at any instant — enforced on write, in the
 * validation helper, not by a constraint here.
 *
 * Effective-dated following the shipping_config precedent: a vendor
 * announcing a price rise from the 1st is the ordinary case.
 */
export const vendorRates = pgTable(
  'vendor_rates',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    vendorId: uuid('vendor_id')
      .references(() => vendors.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    kind: vendorCapabilityKindEnum('kind').notNull(),
    longestEdgeMinInches: integer('longest_edge_min_inches').notNull(),
    longestEdgeMaxInches: integer('longest_edge_max_inches').notNull(),
    finish: text('finish'),
    amount: decimal('amount', { precision: 10, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
    effectiveFrom: timestamp('effective_from').defaultNow().notNull(),
    effectiveTo: timestamp('effective_to'),
    createdBy: text('created_by').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at')
      .defaultNow()
      .notNull()
      .$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
  },
  (table) => ({
    vendorIdIdx: index('vendor_rates_vendor_id_idx').on(table.vendorId),

ticket.title: Database Schema - Production job, items, QC reviews and settlements
ticket.description:
## Task
Add `production_jobs`, `production_job_items`, `production_job_reviews` and `vendor_settlements`. The job RECORD only — the workflow over it belongs to production-pipeline.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 1 of 7. Depends on the vendor core schema ticket.

Design constraints:
- The `production_job_status` enum defines the VOCABULARY only. Legal transitions are out of scope here and land in production-pipeline. Do not add transition guards.
- `production_job_items` joins jobs to `order_items` (not to orders), so a mixed basket — rolled poster plus framed piece — splits across vendors cleanly instead of forcing one vendor per order. `orderItems` lives in `schema/orders.ts`.
- `production_job_reviews` is APPEND-ONLY and multiple rows per job are expected: that is how reject -> rework -> re-review keeps its history. Deliberately mirrors `schema/ai-generation-reviews.ts`. The defect vocabulary is open at this stage (`text[]`); a controlled vocabulary lands with production-qc-inspection.
- `amountExpected` is computed from the rate card live at assignment; `amountActual` is the nullable override, because print shops negotiate.
- Payables are DERIVED, never stored: `SUM(COALESCE(amountActual, amountExpected))` over jobs where `settlementId IS NULL`. Do not add a balance column anywhere.
- Money is `decimal(10,2)` INR.

implementation_steps.description: Create the production job schema module
implementation_steps.code:
/**
 * Production Job Schema
 *
 * The minimal record a QC rating and a payable attach to. This module defines
 * the job RECORD; production-pipeline defines the WORKFLOW over it — the
 * status enum here is a vocabulary, not a state machine, and deliberately
 * carries no transition guards.
 *
 * Payables are DERIVED from these rows, never stored:
 *   SUM(COALESCE(amount_actual, amount_expected)) WHERE settlement_id IS NULL
 * There is no balance column anywhere, so there is no parallel ledger to drift.
 */

import {
  pgTable,
  text,
  timestamp,
  uuid,
  pgEnum,
  index,
  decimal,
  unique,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'
import { relations } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { users } from './users'
import { orders, orderItems } from './orders'
import { vendors } from './vendors'

export const productionJobStageEnum = pgEnum('production_job_stage', ['print', 'frame'])

/** Vocabulary only. Legal transitions belong to production-pipeline. */
export const productionJobStatusEnum = pgEnum('production_job_status', [
  'draft',
  'assigned',
  'sent',
  'received',
  'qc_passed',
  'qc_failed',
  'cancelled',
])

export const productionJobVerdictEnum = pgEnum('production_job_verdict', ['pass', 'fail'])

/** Out-of-band payment record. The system records what was paid; money moves elsewhere. */
export const vendorSettlements = pgTable(
  'vendor_settlements',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    vendorId: uuid('vendor_id')
      .references(() => vendors.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' })
      .notNull(),
    amount: decimal('amount', { precision: 10, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
    reference: text('reference'),
    paidAt: timestamp('paid_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    note: text('note'),
    createdBy: text('created_by').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (table) => ({
    vendorIdIdx: index('vendor_settlements_vendor_id_idx').on(table.vendorId),
    paidAtIdx: index('vendor_settlements_paid_at_idx').on(table.paidAt),
  })
)

export const productionJobs = pgTable(
  'production_jobs',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    orderId: uuid('order_id')
      .references(() => orders.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    stage: productionJobStageEnum('stage').notNull(),
    vendorId: uuid('vendor_id').references(() => vendors.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' }),
    status: productionJobStatusEnum('status').default('draft').notNull(),

    assignedAt: timestamp('assigned_at'),
    sentAt: timestamp('sent_at'),
    dueAt: timestamp('due_at'),
    receivedAt: timestamp('received_at'),

    /** Computed from the rate card live at assignment. */
    amountExpected: decimal('amount_expected', { precision: 10, scale: 2 }),
    /** The override. Print shops negotiate; making that invisible is worse. */
    amountActual: decimal('amount_actual', { precision: 10, scale: 2 }),

    /** NULL is the definition of unsettled — the payables query keys on it. */
    settlementId: uuid('settlement_id').references(() => vendorSettlements.id, {
      onDelete: 'set null',
    }),

    createdBy: text('created_by').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at')
      .defaultNow()
      .notNull()
      .$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
  },
  (table) => ({
    orderIdIdx: index('production_jobs_order_id_idx').on(table.orderId),
    vendorIdIdx: index('production_jobs_vendor_id_idx').on(table.vendorId),
    statusIdx: index('production_jobs_status_idx').on(table.status),
    stageIdx: index('production_jobs_stage_idx').on(table.stage),
    /** Drives the payables query: unsettled jobs for one vendor. */
    settlementIdx: index('production_jobs_settlement_idx').on(table.vendorId, table.settlementId),
  })
)

/**
 * Jobs join to order_items rather than to orders, so a mixed basket splits
 * across vendors instead of forcing one vendor per order.
 */
export const productionJobItems = pgTable(
  'production_job_items',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    jobId: uuid('job_id')
      .references(() => productionJobs.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    orderItemId: uuid('order_item_id')
      .references(() => orderItems.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (table) => ({
    jobIdIdx: index('production_job_items_job_id_idx').on(table.jobId),
    orderItemIdIdx: index('production_job_items_order_item_id_idx').on(table.orderItemId),
    jobItemUnique: unique('production_job_items_job_item_unique').on(table.jobId, table.orderItemId),
  })
)

/**
 * Append-only. MULTIPLE rows per job are expected and are how rework history
 * is preserved — hence no updated_at. Mirrors ai_generation_reviews.
 *
 * `defects` is an open vocabulary at this stage; production-qc-inspection
 * replaces it with a controlled one.
 */
export const productionJobReviews = pgTable(
  'production_job_reviews',
  {
    id: uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    jobId: uuid('job_id')
      .references(() => productionJobs.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    reviewerId: text('reviewer_id').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
    verdict: productionJobVerdictEnum('verdict').notNull(),
    defects: text('defects').array(),
    notes: text('notes'),
    createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (table) => ({
    jobIdIdx: index('production_job_reviews_job_id_idx').on(table.jobId),
    createdAtIdx: index('production_job_reviews_created_at_idx').on(table.createdAt),
  })
)

export const productionJobsRelations = relations(productionJobs, ({ one, many }) => ({
  order: one(orders, { fields: [productionJobs.orderId], references: [orders.id] }),
  vendor: one(vendors, { fields: [productionJobs.vendorId], references: [vendors.id] }),
  settlement: one(vendorSettlements, {
    fields: [productionJobs.settlementId],
    references: [vendorSettlements.id],
  }),
  items: many(productionJobItems),
  reviews: many(productionJobReviews),
}))

export const productionJobItemsRelations = relations(productionJobItems, ({ one }) => ({
  job: one(productionJobs, { fields: [productionJobItems.jobId], references: [productionJobs.id] }),
  orderItem: one(orderItems, {
    fields: [productionJobItems.orderItemId],
    references: [orderItems.id],
  }),
}))

export const productionJobReviewsRelations = relations(productionJobReviews, ({ one }) => ({
  job: one(productionJobs, { fields: [productionJobReviews.jobId], references: [productionJobs.id] }),
  reviewer: one(users, { fields: [productionJobReviews.reviewerId], references: [users.id] }),
}))

export const vendorSettlementsRelations = relations(vendorSettlements, ({ one, many }) => ({
  vendor: one(vendors, { fields: [vendorSettlements.vendorId], references: [vendors.id] }),
  jobs: many(productionJobs),
}))

export type ProductionJob = typeof productionJobs.$inferSelect
export type NewProductionJob = typeof productionJobs.$inferInsert
export type ProductionJobItem = typeof productionJobItems.$inferSelect
export type NewProductionJobItem = typeof productionJobItems.$inferInsert
export type ProductionJobReview = typeof productionJobReviews.$inferSelect
export type NewProductionJobReview = typeof productionJobReviews.$inferInsert
export type VendorSettlement = typeof vendorSettlements.$inferSelect
export type NewVendorSettlement = typeof vendorSettlements.$inferInsert
export type ProductionJobStage = (typeof productionJobStageEnum.enumValues)[number]
export type ProductionJobStatus = (typeof productionJobStatusEnum.enumValues)[number]
export type ProductionJobVerdict = (typeof productionJobVerdictEnum.enumValues)[number]

ticket.title: Database Schema - vendor role, vendor_users link and the migration
ticket.description:
## Task
Add `vendor` to the `user_role` pgEnum, add the `vendor_users` link table, then generate and apply the single migration covering all of Phase 1.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 1 of 7. Last Phase 1 ticket — depends on both schema tickets.

Design constraints:
- `userRoleEnum` is at `packages/api/src/database/schema/users.ts:56`. Append `vendor` at the END of the enum. Postgres enum values are ordered and drizzle-kit emits `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`; inserting in the middle produces a far messier migration for no gain.
- `vendor_users` has a UNIQUE constraint on `userId`: one user belongs to exactly one vendor. That uniqueness is what makes `requireVendor` a lookup rather than a choice.
- Adding the role value does NOT grant anything. Two existing guards must keep turning a vendor away, and the design says to confirm them by test rather than assume: `app/routes/admin.tsx` beforeLoad admits only admin/super-admin/content-manager, and `staffAreaLabel`/`staffAreaHref` in `app/lib/admin-nav.ts` return null for unrecognised roles. Add those two tests here — they are cheap now and are the regression net for the whole feature.
- Migration generation is `bun run db:generate` in `packages/api` (drizzle-kit). Migrations land in `src/database/migrations/` as `00NN_*.sql`; the last one is `0018_gift_card_delivery_index_predicate.sql`, so expect `0019_*`.
- DB HAZARD: the real dev database is on port 5440, not the 5433 baked into `vitest.config.ts`. Pass `DATABASE_URL` explicitly when applying the migration; do not assume the default is pointing where you think.

ticket.title: Access Control - requireVendor middleware and the scoped query module
ticket.description:
## Task
Add `requireVendor` middleware that resolves the caller's `vendorId` into request context, and a scoped query module through which ALL vendor-facing data access must pass.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 2 of 7. Depends on Phase 1 schema.

**This is the security core of the feature.** The reason it exists as a module rather than as care taken per route:

Every existing role in this system is a blanket grant — a content-manager sees ALL products, so `requireRole` is a complete check for them. A vendor sees only their own rows, which `requireRole` cannot express. `requireVendor` alone is therefore NOT sufficient, and that distinction is the whole point of this ticket.

So: every vendor-facing read takes `vendorId` as a REQUIRED FIRST ARGUMENT, and routes never touch the tables directly. This makes unfiltered access inexpressible rather than merely discouraged, and puts the isolation guarantee in one testable place instead of an audit across every route forever.

Two tests carry the weight:
1. Vendor A cannot read vendor B's rows through any exported function.
2. The module REFUSES TO RUN without a vendorId — throws, does not fall back to an unscoped query. If a later route bypasses the module, that second test is what catches it.

Other constraints:
- A caller with role `vendor` but no `vendor_users` row is 403, never an unscoped query.
- A suspended vendor's logins are refused — suspending the vendor suspends the portal.
- Follow `packages/api/src/middleware/auth.ts` for shape: `createMiddleware<{ Variables: ... }>`, `createForbiddenError` / `createUnauthorizedError` from the same error helpers `requireRole` uses (`src/middleware/auth.ts:227`).
- **Vendors need ZERO customer data.** No function in this module may return a customer name, address, phone, or person-linked order reference. That is a consequence of the fulfilment model (dispatch is in-house, the piece returns to you before it ships), which is why it can be tested as a blanket rule.

implementation_steps.code:
/**
 * Vendor-Scoped Data Access
 *
 * ALL vendor-facing reads go through this module. Routes do not reach the
 * tables directly.
 *
 * Why a module and not care-taken-per-route: every other role in this system
 * is a blanket grant, so `requireRole` is a complete check for it. A vendor
 * sees only their own rows, which `requireRole` cannot express. Putting the
 * filter in one place with `vendorId` as a required first argument makes an
 * unfiltered query inexpressible rather than merely discouraged, and gives the
 * isolation guarantee ONE testable home instead of an audit across every route
 * that will ever be added.
 *
 * Second rule, equally absolute: **no return value here contains customer
 * data.** Not a name, not an address, not a phone, not a person-linked order
 * reference. Dispatch is in-house — the piece comes back to us before it ships
 * — so a vendor never needs any of it. Stated as an absolute so it can be
 * tested as one.
 */

import { and, desc, eq, isNull, sql } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { db } from '../database'
import {
  productionJobs,
  productionJobItems,
  productionJobReviews,
  vendorSettlements,
} from '../database/schema/production-jobs'
import { vendorRates } from '../database/schema/vendors'

/**
 * The guard every export starts with. Throws rather than returning empty:
 * an empty result reads as "this vendor has nothing", which is a lie that
 * looks like data. A throw is a bug report.
 */
function assertVendorId(vendorId: string | null | undefined): asserts vendorId is string {
  if (!vendorId || typeof vendorId !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('vendor-scope: vendorId is required and was not supplied')
  }
}

export async function listVendorJobs(
  vendorId: string | null | undefined,
  opts: { status?: string; limit?: number; offset?: number } = {}
) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  const limit = Math.min(opts.limit ?? 20, 100)
  const offset = opts.offset ?? 0

  return db
    .select({
      id: productionJobs.id,
      stage: productionJobs.stage,
      status: productionJobs.status,
      dueAt: productionJobs.dueAt,
      sentAt: productionJobs.sentAt,
      receivedAt: productionJobs.receivedAt,
      amountExpected: productionJobs.amountExpected,
      amountActual: productionJobs.amountActual,
      createdAt: productionJobs.createdAt,
      // Deliberately absent: orderId, any customer field, any retail price.
    })
    .from(productionJobs)
    .where(
      opts.status
        ? and(eq(productionJobs.vendorId, vendorId), eq(productionJobs.status, opts.status as any))
        : eq(productionJobs.vendorId, vendorId)
    )
    .orderBy(desc(productionJobs.createdAt))
    .limit(limit)
    .offset(offset)
}

export async function getVendorJob(vendorId: string | null | undefined, jobId?: string) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  if (!jobId) return null

  const [job] = await db
    .select({
      id: productionJobs.id,
      stage: productionJobs.stage,
      status: productionJobs.status,
      dueAt: productionJobs.dueAt,
      sentAt: productionJobs.sentAt,
      receivedAt: productionJobs.receivedAt,
      amountExpected: productionJobs.amountExpected,
      amountActual: productionJobs.amountActual,
    })
    .from(productionJobs)
    // vendorId in the WHERE, not checked afterwards: a wrong-vendor job is
    // NOT FOUND, which is also the right thing to leak (nothing).
    .where(and(eq(productionJobs.id, jobId), eq(productionJobs.vendorId, vendorId)))
    .limit(1)

  return job ?? null
}

export async function listVendorRates(vendorId: string | null | undefined) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  return db
    .select()
    .from(vendorRates)
    .where(eq(vendorRates.vendorId, vendorId))
    .orderBy(desc(vendorRates.effectiveFrom))
}

export async function listVendorSettlements(vendorId: string | null | undefined) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  return db
    .select()
    .from(vendorSettlements)
    .where(eq(vendorSettlements.vendorId, vendorId))
    .orderBy(desc(vendorSettlements.paidAt))
}

/**
 * Payables are DERIVED, never stored: no parallel ledger to drift.
 * owed = SUM(COALESCE(amountActual, amountExpected)) over unsettled jobs.
 */
export async function getVendorPayableTotal(vendorId: string | null | undefined) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  const [row] = await db
    .select({
      total: sql<string>`COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(${productionJobs.amountActual}, ${productionJobs.amountExpected})), 0)`,
    })
    .from(productionJobs)
    .where(and(eq(productionJobs.vendorId, vendorId), isNull(productionJobs.settlementId)))

  return row?.total ?? '0'
}

/** Item rows for a job the caller owns. Artwork/size/finish only — no customer. */
export async function getVendorJobItems(vendorId: string | null | undefined, jobId: string) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  const job = await getVendorJob(vendorId, jobId)
  if (!job) return []
  return db
    .select({ id: productionJobItems.id, orderItemId: productionJobItems.orderItemId })
    .from(productionJobItems)
    .where(eq(productionJobItems.jobId, jobId))
}

/** QC history for a job the caller owns. */
export async function getVendorJobReviews(vendorId: string | null | undefined, jobId: string) {
  assertVendorId(vendorId)
  const job = await getVendorJob(vendorId, jobId)
  if (!job) return []
  return db
    .select({
      id: productionJobReviews.id,
      verdict: productionJobReviews.verdict,
      defects: productionJobReviews.defects,
      notes: productionJobReviews.notes,
      createdAt: productionJobReviews.createdAt,
      // reviewerId omitted: that is our staff, not their business.
    })
    .from(productionJobReviews)
    .where(eq(productionJobReviews.jobId, jobId))
    .orderBy(desc(productionJobReviews.createdAt))
}

ticket.title: Access Control - rate resolution, band overlap rejection and payables derivation
ticket.description:
## Task
Three pure-ish helpers the API phase depends on: resolve the rate in force, reject overlapping rate bands on write, and derive payables.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 2 of 7. Can run alongside the requireVendor ticket — different files.

**Rate resolution.** Bands match on the item's LONGEST EDGE in inches: `max(widthInches, heightInches)` from `productVariants` (`schema/products.ts:206-207`). Ranges are inclusive-min, exclusive-max. Effective dating follows the `shipping_config` precedent — `lib/shipping-config.ts` resolves against the caller's clock, do the same. The test that matters: a rate scheduled to start next month must NOT be returned today. A vendor announcing a price rise from the 1st is the ordinary case, and quietly charging it early is the bug.

**Overlap rejection.** Two bands must not overlap for a given `(vendorId, kind, finish)` AT ANY INSTANT. Two rows covering 0-24 and 12-36 overlap only if their effective windows also intersect — the same size band at two different times is the normal way a price changes, and rejecting that would make effective dating useless. This is enforced on write in this helper, not by a database constraint.

**Payables derivation.** `SUM(COALESCE(amountActual, amountExpected))` over jobs where `settlementId IS NULL`. Derived, never stored. `getVendorPayableTotal` in `lib/vendor-scope.ts` is the vendor-facing read; this ticket adds the admin-facing per-vendor and per-job breakdown that the payables tab needs. Both must agree — add a test asserting they produce the same total for the same vendor, because two implementations of one sum is exactly how a ledger drifts.

Money is `decimal(10,2)` INR throughout. Drizzle returns decimals as STRINGS — do not let a float into the sum.

ticket.title: Admin API - rate card routes with effective dating and overlap rejection
ticket.description:
## Task
`/api/admin/vendors/:id/rates` — list, create, update, close. Every write runs the overlap check; every read can be asked for the card as of a given instant.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 3 of 7. Depends on `lib/vendor-rates.ts` (Phase 2) and the admin vendors router.

This is a separate ticket from vendors CRUD because the write path has real rules and deserves its own test file.

- Every POST/PATCH loads the vendor's existing rates and calls `findOverlappingBand`. A collision is **422 with the conflicting row in the response** — the admin needs to know WHICH band they collided with, not just that they did. A bare 400 sends them hunting.
- `GET ?at=<iso>` resolves the card in force at that instant via `selectRateInForce`, defaulting to now. This is what the assignment screen calls.
- Closing a rate sets `effectiveTo`; it does not delete the row. Historical jobs reference the price that was live when they were assigned, and a deleted rate makes an old job's amount unexplainable.
- **Do not clobber a scheduled future rate.** `wallet-config.ts` ends every open row for its key on write; `shipping-config.ts` deliberately departed from that because it silently deleted scheduled values. Follow shipping-config: close only the row actually in force at the new value's start, let later rows survive, and return them in `warnings` so the admin is told their new rate has an expiry they did not set.
- Money is `decimal(10,2)` INR. The payload carries a string or a number of rupees; it must never be paise.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
Done in ea326fc3.

New files:
- packages/api/src/routes/admin/vendor-rates.ts — separate Hono app mounted at /api/admin/vendors alongside adminVendorsApp (Hono merges additively), so vendors.ts was not touched and #614/#615 files were not touched.
- packages/api/tests/routes/admin/vendor-rates.test.ts — 37 tests, same recording-db + real-middleware harness as tests/routes/admin/vendors.test.ts.

Routes: GET /:id/rates (?at, ?includeExpired, ?kind + ?longestEdge | ?widthInches&?heightInches), POST /:id/rates, PATCH /:id/rates/:rateId, POST /:id/rates/:rateId/close. No DELETE, deliberately.

Decisions worth recording:
- Overlap => 422 with `conflict` carrying id, kind, finish, size range, amount and window; the prose error names the range too. Nothing is written on a conflict.
- Supersede is keyed on an EXACT (kind, finish, min, max) match. A same-band write with a later effectiveFrom is a re-price and closes the incumbent; a merely intersecting band (e.g. 12-36 over 0-24) is a conflict, because half-repricing a band silently is worse than refusing.
- Scheduled rows survive: only the row in force at the new start is closed, later same-band rows cap the new row's effectiveTo and come back in `warnings`. Follows shipping-config, not wallet-config.
- The overlap check runs against a PROJECTED card (incumbent modelled as closed at startsAt) rather than by excluding the incumbent, so findOverlappingBand still decides whether the closure removed the collision.
- No band or effective-dating arithmetic in the route: findOverlappingBand, selectRateInForce (also used to find the incumbent for a band at an instant) and longestEdgeInches do it. lib/vendor-rates.ts was not modified.
- amount accepts a rupee string or number, normalised to a 2dp string; 3+ decimals rejected rather than rounded.

ticket.title: Admin API - production jobs, assignment pricing and QC reviews
ticket.description:
## Task
`/api/admin/production` — job queue, job creation from order items, vendor assignment (which computes `amountExpected`), the `amountActual` override, and QC review recording.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 3 of 7. Depends on Phase 1 + 2 and the admin vendors router.

**This spec defines the job RECORD; production-pipeline defines the WORKFLOW.** Status is settable, but do NOT add a transition state machine, routing rules, reprint loops or lead-time calculation — all four are explicitly the next sub-project. If a transition guard feels missing, that is correct.

- `POST /api/admin/production` takes an `orderId`, a `stage` and a list of `orderItemIds`, and creates the job plus its `production_job_items` rows in ONE transaction. Items join to `order_items`, not to the order, so a mixed basket splits across vendors.
- `POST /:jobId/assign` takes a `vendorId`. It resolves each item's longest edge from the variant (`productVariants.widthInches` / `heightInches`, `max()` of the two), calls `selectRateInForce` against the vendor's card **at the assignment instant**, sums the results into `amountExpected`, and sets `assignedAt` + `status = 'assigned'`. If any item has no covering band, respond 422 naming the item and the size — do NOT default the missing band to zero. A silent zero is how a job ends up unbillable with nothing to show why.
- `PATCH /:jobId` allows an `amountActual` override and the date fields. Print shops negotiate; making that invisible pushes staff into workarounds.
- `POST /:jobId/reviews` appends a QC review. **Append-only — never update an existing review row.** Reject -> rework -> re-review must leave multiple rows; a test asserting three reviews after two rejections is what protects that.
- `GET /api/admin/production` — paginated queue filterable by stage, status and vendor.
- Gated `requireAuth, requireAdmin`. content-manager 403.

ticket.title: Admin API - payables, settlements and the vendor account invite
ticket.description:
## Task
Payables read, settlement recording, and the invite that mints a vendor login.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 3 of 7. Depends on Phase 1 + 2 and the admin vendors router.

**Payables** — `GET /api/admin/vendors/:id/payables` returns the unsettled jobs and a running total, derived via `lib/vendor-payables.ts`. No stored balance anywhere. Add a test that this total equals `getVendorPayableTotal` from `lib/vendor-scope.ts` for the same vendor: two implementations of one sum is exactly how a ledger drifts, and the vendor portal reads the other one.

**Settlements** — `POST /api/admin/vendors/:id/settlements` takes an amount, a reference, a paid-at and a list of job ids. In ONE transaction it inserts the `vendor_settlements` row and stamps `settlementId` onto those jobs. Guards: every job must belong to this vendor (else 422), and no job may already be settled (else 422 — double-settling is a silent overpay). The system records what is owed and what was paid; **executing the payment stays outside the system permanently.**

**Invite** — `POST /api/admin/vendors/:id/invite` takes a contact email. In ONE transaction it mints the user account with `role = 'vendor'` and creates the `vendor_users` link. Vendors cannot self-register, so this is the only path to a vendor login. Two failure modes worth their own tests: an email that already has a non-vendor account must not be silently converted, and a user already linked to another vendor must be refused (the UNIQUE on `user_id` will also stop it, but a 422 beats a constraint violation surfacing as a 500).

Suspending a vendor suspends its logins — that is already handled by `requireVendor` checking vendor status, so add a test asserting it rather than a second mechanism.

ticket.title: Vendor Portal API - jobs, rates and payments through the scoped module
ticket.description:
## Task
`/api/vendor/*` — the four reads the portal needs, every one of them through `lib/vendor-scope.ts`.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 4 of 7. Depends on Phase 2 and Phase 3.

Endpoints, all gated `requireAuth, requireVendor`:
- `GET /api/vendor/jobs` — my jobs; assigned, in progress, due. Answers "what do I work on next" and nothing else.
- `GET /api/vendor/jobs/:id` — items, size, finish, due date, QC history
- `PATCH /api/vendor/jobs/:id` — mark received / in progress / ready. The ONLY write a vendor gets, and it may only touch status and the date fields, never amounts.
- `GET /api/vendor/rates` — my rate card, read-only
- `GET /api/vendor/payments` — my amounts and settlement history

**Routes do not touch the tables.** Every read goes through the scoped module with `vendorId` from context. If a handler here needs data the module does not expose, add a scoped function to the module — do not reach around it. The Phase 2 test that asserts no unscoped exported query exists is what keeps that honest.

The write path needs its own scoping care: `PATCH /jobs/:id` must load the job through `getVendorJob(vendorId, id)` first and 404 on a miss, rather than updating by id and checking ownership afterwards. Same result on the happy path, very different result when someone gets the ownership check wrong.

**Zero customer data** in any response. Not a name, not an address, not a phone, not an order number that identifies a person. The isolation test ticket asserts this over every response shape here.

ticket.title: Vendor Portal API - signed artwork URLs and the isolation property tests
ticket.description:
## Task
Job-scoped signed artwork URLs, plus the isolation test suite that asserts the feature's three security properties as properties rather than per-route afterthoughts.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 4 of 7. Depends on the vendor portal API ticket.

**Artwork delivery.** `GET /api/vendor/jobs/:id/artwork/:itemId` returns a signed, expiring, job-scoped URL. `getPresignedDownloadUrl` already exists in `src/lib/storage.ts:463`. Never a public CDN path: a leaked permanent URL to a customer's commissioned artwork is a worse incident than a leaked job list. Short expiry — minutes, not days.

**The three properties, tested as properties:**
1. Vendor A cannot read or write vendor B's data — one case per vendor-facing endpoint, driven from a list of the routes so a newly added route without a case is visible. Plus the Phase 2 test that the scoped module refuses to run without a vendorId; if a later route bypasses the module, that is what catches it.
2. No vendor-facing payload contains a customer field — asserted over EVERY vendor response shape by walking the JSON for forbidden keys, not by eyeballing each handler.
3. Artwork URLs are signed, expiring and job-scoped; vendor B's session cannot obtain a URL for vendor A's artwork.

Property 2 is worth the awkward implementation. Dispatch is in-house — the piece returns to us before it ships — so a vendor needs zero customer data, which is what makes a blanket assertion possible at all. A per-endpoint eyeball check would pass today and rot the first time someone adds a convenience field.

Mark this ticket security-relevant: it is the one that proves the portal safe to expose.

Key resolved by a new scoped read getVendorJobArtwork(vendorId, jobId, itemId) — enrolled in the vendor-scope contract test. Job loaded scoped FIRST, so the presigner is never reached on a cross-vendor miss (asserted as call count 0, not as a 404).

Isolation suite (tests/routes/vendor/isolation.test.ts) is driven from ROUTE_TABLE, diffed both ways against vendorApp.routes so an uncovered new route fails the first test. Property 2 asserts on the SELECT projection (no wholesale db.select(), no forbidden column) as well as a recursive case-insensitive body walk, and the walker has its own not-vacuous test.

TWO REAL LEAKS FOUND AND FIXED, both narrowed at source:
1. getVendorJobItems selected production_job_items.orderItemId — a direct handle into the customer's order, contradicting the module's own "no person-linked order reference" absolute. Nothing consumed it (artwork keys on production_job_items.id). Dropped from the select.

Several prefixes are user-partitioned (ai-generations/<userId>/, avatars/<userId>/) and the key rides inside the signed URL where a JSON-key assertion cannot see it. ticket.title: Admin UI - payables tab and settlement recording
ticket.description:
## Task
The payables tab on `/admin/vendors/$id`: unsettled jobs, a running total, and recording a settlement against selected jobs.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 5 of 7. Depends on the payables API and the vendor detail screen.

This is the screen where a mistake costs money, so two things matter more than usual:

**The total must never be fabricated.** If the payables request fails, show an error state — not a zero, not a dash pretending to be a total. #602 and #606 are both open tickets about admin surfaces rendering a fabricated 0 when the underlying request failed, and a fabricated 0 on a payables screen reads as "we owe this vendor nothing".

**Settlement is not undoable from this screen.** Selecting jobs, entering the amount paid, and submitting stamps `settlementId` on those rows. Use the inline two-step confirm (never native `confirm()`) and show the exact set of jobs and the exact total in the second step, so the confirming click is against the real number rather than against a remembered one.

The amount field defaults to the selected jobs' derived total but is editable — a vendor may be paid a rounded figure. Show the difference when the entered amount and the derived total disagree, rather than silently accepting it.

Money is INR rupees with two decimals throughout. Do not introduce a paise conversion on this screen: the API speaks decimal rupees and the repo already documents a 100x hazard from mixed units.

ticket.title: Vendor Portal UI - /vendor route tree, guard and the four screens
ticket.description:
## Task
A new top-level `/vendor` route tree with its own layout guard, and exactly four screens.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 6 of 7. Depends on Phase 4.

**Four screens deliberately.** A print shop will not learn more than that, and every added screen is another thing that must be right about isolation.
- `/vendor` — my jobs: assigned, in progress, due. Answers "what do I work on next" and nothing else.
- `/vendor/jobs/$id` — items, artwork download (signed URL), mark received / in progress / ready
- `/vendor/rates` — my rate card, read-only
- `/vendor/payments` — my amounts and settlement history

**The layout guard** mirrors `/admin`'s `beforeLoad` (`app/routes/admin.tsx:38`): no session redirects to login with a `redirect` param; a session whose role is not `vendor` gets Access Denied rather than a redirect loop. Do not reuse the admin guard — mirror its structure with its own role check, because sharing it would make a change for one tree silently apply to the other.

**Confirm the reverse direction too**, and by test rather than assumption: an admin visiting `/vendor` is not a vendor and gets Access Denied, and the vendor-role user gets no staff entry point rendered anywhere (`staffAreaLabel` returns null for `vendor` — already covered by the Phase 1 test, so just don't regress it).

Artwork download hits the signed-URL endpoint at click time and uses the returned short-lived URL. Do not fetch and hold URLs at page load — an expiring URL rendered into a page that sits open for an hour is a broken download, and a long-lived one to sidestep that is the incident the signing exists to prevent.

Same UI rules as the admin screens: no native `confirm()`, skeleton/empty/error on every list, URL state via a coercing `validateSearch`, pagination from day one.

ticket.title: E2E - vendor lifecycle happy path and the access-denied cases
ticket.description:
## Task
Playwright coverage of the full loop: admin creates vendor -> invites contact -> assigns job -> vendor logs in and sees only their own -> marks ready -> admin rates QC -> admin records settlement.

## Context
Feature: vendor-management. Phase 7 of 7. Last ticket — depends on everything.

Specs live in `tests/e2e/` at the repo root, `*.spec.ts`. Follow the existing `admin-*.spec.ts` files.

**Repo hazards to honour rather than rediscover:**
- **Port.** `:5173` is a DIFFERENT app on this machine. Pointed there, the whole suite passes vacuously — it is not a flake, it is a false green. Confirm the base URL resolves to this app before trusting a pass.
- **Do not run admin suites in parallel with other admin suites.** They interfere.
- **Scope selectors for mobile/desktop** — the same test ids exist in both trees. `const desktopFilters = page.locator('div.hidden.lg\\:block')` is the established pattern.
- Use `await page.goto('/path', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })` in `beforeEach`.
- Diff any failure against the main baseline before treating it as new.

Also cover the two access-denied paths, because they are the ones a regression would make silently permissive:
- a vendor session at `/admin` gets Access Denied
- a content-manager session at `/admin/vendors` gets Access Denied

The destructive step — recording a settlement — is reachable by E2E precisely because these screens use the inline two-step confirm rather than a native dialog. Native dialogs block the automation harness outright, which is why nine existing admin files have no coverage on their destructive paths. If this spec cannot drive the settlement, that is a signal a native dialog crept in, not a reason to skip the step.

ticket.title: Tech debt - drizzle-kit db:generate is unusable, meta snapshots drift from migrations
ticket.description:
## Problem
`bun run db:generate` in `packages/api` cannot be used. The drizzle meta snapshots in `src/database/migrations/meta/` stop at 0013 while the migrations themselves run to 0018. Drizzle-kit therefore diffs the current schema against a five-migration-stale snapshot, tries to replay unrelated drift, and interactively prompts to rename `frame_type` -> `frame_category`.

Accepting that prompt would emit a migration containing changes nobody asked for, against tables this work does not touch.

## How it surfaced
Found while implementing #609 (vendor-management Phase 1). That ticket's migration — `0019_vendor_management_phase_1.sql` — was hand-assembled from drizzle's own DDL and audited additive-only before being applied: 9 CREATE TABLE, 5 CREATE TYPE, 19 CREATE INDEX, 17 ADD CONSTRAINT (all on the new tables), 1 ALTER TYPE. No DROP, no TRUNCATE, no ALTER COLUMN, nothing touching a pre-existing table. `meta/_journal.json` was updated to idx 19 by hand to match.

## Why it matters beyond this feature
Every future schema change in this repo hits the same wall, and the workaround — hand-writing migrations and hand-editing the journal — is exactly the practice that produced the drift. It also means the snapshot is now further out of date than before, because 0019 exists as a journal entry without a corresponding regenerated snapshot.

No remaining vendor-management phase adds a migration, so this does not block that feature.

## Fix direction
Rebuild the meta snapshots to match the applied migration history — most likely by regenerating snapshots 0014-0019 from the schema state each migration produces, rather than by resolving the spurious `frame_type` rename. Confirm afterwards that a no-op `db:generate` against an unchanged schema produces no migration at all; that is the check that proves the drift is gone.

ticket.title: Bug - broken = ANY() bind still 500s in returns, shipments and reviews admin routes
ticket.description:
## Problem
An `= ANY()` parameter bind is constructed incorrectly and throws at query time, 500ing the endpoint. It was found and fixed in `/api/admin/orders` while building the vendor-management E2E spec (#622, commit 9fe39902), but **the same broken bind is still present in the returns, shipments and reviews admin routers**.

## How it surfaced
The vendor-management E2E spec drives `/admin/orders/$id` as part of the production panel flow. That page 500ed. The cause was the bind, not anything vendor-related — it is a pre-existing defect that no existing test covered, because these particular admin list paths have no E2E coverage.

Why they have no E2E coverage is itself worth recording: nine admin files use native `confirm()` for their destructive actions, and a native dialog blocks the Playwright harness outright. The untested paths and the native dialogs are the same problem wearing two hats.

## Scope
Three routers still carry it:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/returns.ts`
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/shipments.ts`
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts`

Compare against the corrected form in `packages/api/src/routes/admin/orders.ts` as of commit 9fe39902.

## Why this is high priority
Each one is a live 500 on an admin surface, reachable by ordinary use, with no test catching it. The fix is already written and proven in the orders router — this is applying a known-good correction in three more places, not diagnosing something new.

## Related
A second route-shadowing bug was fixed in the same commit: `GET /api/admin/:id` in the shipments router was matching and 400ing `/api/admin/vendors`, `/api/admin/production`, `/api/admin/returns` and `/api/admin/approvals`. That one is fixed; check whether any other router declares a similarly greedy top-level `:id` route.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `e3c2620d` - fix(api): bind id arrays as arrays in admin returns, shipments and reviews

**Root Cause**: `sql\`${users.id} = ANY(${userIds})\`` does not bind the array as an array — drizzle interpolates one parameter per element, rendering `"user"."id" = ANY(($1, $2))`, i.e. ANY over a row expression. Postgres refuses it with `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`, so the endpoint 500s the moment its list contains one row with a userId.
**Location**: `packages/api/src/routes/admin/returns.ts:263`, `shipments.ts:210`, `reviews.ts:283` (line numbers before the fix)
**Fix**: `inArray(...)`, which renders `in ($1, $2)` — the correction already proven in `orders.ts` (9fe39902).

**Files Changed**:
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/returns.ts` - customer lookup via `inArray`; `inArray` added to the drizzle import
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/shipments.ts` - same
- `packages/api/src/routes/admin/reviews.ts` - product lookup via `inArray` (`inArray` was already imported)
- `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/list-array-membership-bind.test.ts` - new, 4 tests
- `packages/api/tests/routes/route-shadowing.test.ts` - new, 4 tests (step 5)

**Summary**:
The mock `src/database` these admin suites use executes no SQL, so it cannot reproduce Postgres's complaint. The test instead renders the condition the handler actually built through `PgDialect` and asserts the shape Postgres accepts. Reintroduce the `ANY()` form in any of the four routers and it goes red. Orders is included as the control: already fixed, green before and after, which is what makes the three failures meaningful rather than an assertion that rejects everything.

Step 5 (other greedy top-level `:id` routes) is a second test rather than a note. It asserts against the **composed** app's route table — 469 routes — that no literal path sits behind an earlier `/:param` sibling. The rule is order-aware on purpose: `/api/reviews/stats` in front of `/api/reviews/:reviewId` is the correct pattern and must not be flagged. Today there are zero collisions, so that assertion is green from the start; the detector's teeth are proved separately against a synthetic app carrying the exact #622 shape. Per-router suites structurally cannot see this class of bug — the collision only exists once every router is mounted together.

**Verification**:
- Command: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/admin/list-array-membership-bind.test.ts` (from `packages/api`)
- RED first: `Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4)`, all three failing on the identical rendered SQL — `"user"."id" = ANY(($1, $2))` for returns and shipments, `"products"."id" = ANY(($1))` for reviews. One cause, not three.
- Result after fix: PASS (4 tests, 0 failing)
- `bunx vitest run tests/routes/route-shadowing.test.ts` → PASS (4 tests)
- Regression: `bunx vitest run tests/routes/admin/{returns,shipments,reviews,orders}.test.ts` → `Test Files 4 passed (4)  Tests 299 passed (299)`. Those suites print "Database not available, skipping runtime tests", which is exactly why this defect survived them.
- Type-check: `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/api` → 0 errors.

**Not done**: no live-Postgres test was added. The rendered-SQL assertion pins the defect at its true location and needs no database; a live test would need an admin session plus seeded rows in four tables, on a database shared with other agents.
