ticket.title: Admin screens open 16 blocking native prompt()/confirm() dialogs — replace with one shared dialog primitive
ticket.description:
## Problem

#604 removed one `alert()` from the orders list and left a source guard behind. The guard is scoped to `alert(` only, so it does not catch the rest of the family. A grep across the admin tree finds **16 blocking native dialogs in 9 files**:

| File | Calls |
|---|---|
| `app/routes/admin/orders/index.tsx` | `prompt(` :296 (status update), `confirm(` :330 (cancel order), `prompt(` :344 (refund reason) |
| `app/routes/admin/reviews.tsx` | `confirm(` :557 (delete), :595 (bulk approve), :616 (bulk reject) |
| `app/routes/admin/products/index.tsx` | `confirm(` :204, :219, :237 |
| `app/routes/admin/products/$id.tsx` | `confirm(` :352 |
| `app/routes/admin/promotions/index.tsx` | `window.confirm(` :326 |
| `app/routes/admin/collections/index.tsx` | `window.confirm(` :164 |
| `app/routes/admin/ai-moderation.tsx` | `confirm(` :408 |
| `app/routes/admin/approvals/$id.tsx` | `confirm(` :254 (delete all photos) |
| `app/components/admin/OrderDetail.tsx` | `confirm(` :743 (initiate refund) |

Three things are wrong with these, and the E2E one is the reason this is not cosmetic:

1. **They freeze the browser automation harness.** A native dialog blocks the page's event loop, so any E2E run that clicks a Delete, Cancel or Refund control stalls until a human dismisses it. `reviews.tsx:269` already documents this hazard in a comment — and then calls `confirm()` three times anyway. Every destructive admin flow is therefore untestable end-to-end today.
2. **`prompt()` for a status is a correctness bug, not just a style one.** `orders/index.tsx:296` asks the operator to *type* an order status into a free-text native prompt, then string-matches it against an 11-value enum. A typo is a silent no-op with an error banner. This is a `<select>` of the eleven valid statuses, and nothing else.
3. **They are unstyleable and unbrandable**, sit outside the app's focus management, and on iOS Safari can be suppressed entirely by the browser — so a destructive action can fire with no confirmation shown at all.

## Fix — one shared primitive, not nine inline dialogs

Nine bespoke in-page dialogs would be nine chances to get focus trap, Escape handling, backdrop click, `aria-modal` and scroll lock wrong. Build it once:

- `app/components/admin/ConfirmDialog.tsx` — the presentational modal. `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, labelled by its title, Escape and backdrop cancel, focus moved in on open and restored to the trigger on close, destructive variant styling. Follows the existing in-repo modal pattern (`SearchDrawer.tsx:172`, `ChooseOptions.tsx:505`) rather than inventing a new one — there is no dialog primitive under `components/ui/` yet, so this becomes it for admin.
- `app/components/admin/useConfirm.tsx` — provider + hook returning a promise, so the call sites stay one line and read almost exactly like the native call they replace:

  ```tsx
  const confirmAction = useConfirm()
  if (!(await confirmAction({ title: 'Cancel order?', body: `Order ${order.orderNumber} will be cancelled.`, confirmLabel: 'Cancel order', destructive: true }))) return
  ```

- The two `prompt()` sites need a value back, not a boolean. Same primitive, `fields` option: a `select` of the 11 order statuses for the status update, a required `textarea` for the refund reason. Resolves to the values or `null` on cancel.
- Mount the provider once in the admin layout route so every admin screen has it.
- Migrate all 16 call sites.

## Then widen the guard

`tests/routes/admin/orders-export-button.test.tsx` already walks every `.ts`/`.tsx` under `app/routes/admin` asserting no `alert(`. Widen that regex to `alert|prompt|confirm` (bare or `window.`-qualified), extend the walk to `app/components/admin`, and move it into its own `tests/routes/admin/admin-native-dialogs.test.tsx` since it is no longer about the export button. The lookbehind that already excludes `setAlert(` also has to leave `onConfirm(`, `confirmed`, `confirmLabel` and friends alone — case-sensitive matching handles most of it; assert that explicitly with a fixture string so the guard cannot rot into a false-positive nuisance.

## Verification

- Unit: the dialog resolves `true` on confirm, `false` on cancel, `false` on Escape; focus returns to the trigger; the prompt variant resolves the field values and `null` on cancel.
- Screen-level: on `/admin/orders`, stub `window.confirm`/`window.prompt` to throw — cancelling an order must open the in-page dialog and never touch the native ones.
- Source guard: no `alert(`, `prompt(` or `confirm(` under `app/routes/admin` or `app/components/admin`.
- E2E: one destructive admin flow (cancel order) driven to completion without the run stalling — the thing that was impossible before.

## Context

- Related: #604 (the `alert()` half, done, commit `f72c9b81`) — this ticket is its explicit follow-up.
- The vendor and production screens (#620, #621) were built with no native dialogs on purpose; `production/$id.tsx:45` states the rule. This ticket brings the older admin screens up to it.
- `components/ui/` currently holds only `Button`, `DisplayHeading`, `OptimizedImage`, `SectionBand` — there is no dialog to reuse and no shadcn dialog installed, so this is a new primitive, deliberately placed under `components/admin/` until a second consumer outside admin appears.

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `2411e0df` — fix(admin): replace 15 blocking native dialogs with one shared ConfirmDialog

**Count correction**: the ticket said 16 call sites. **15 were real** — the sixteenth grep hit was the comment in `production/$id.tsx:45` that documents the no-native-dialogs rule.

**New files**
- `app/components/admin/ConfirmDialog.tsx` — the modal. `role=dialog`, `aria-modal`, labelled by title, Escape + backdrop cancel, focus trap, focus moved in on open and restored to the trigger on close, scroll lock, destructive variant. Takes a `fields` option (select / textarea / text) for the call sites that need a value back, resolving the values object or `null` on any dismissal.
- `app/components/admin/useConfirm.tsx` — `useConfirmDialog()` returning `confirmAction` (boolean), `promptForValues` (values or null) and the `dialog` node.

**Design change vs the plan**: the ticket specified `ConfirmProvider` in the admin layout plus a context-reading hook. Rejected during implementation — every admin route test in this repo renders its screen component directly, never the layout, so a context-required hook becomes a render-time throw in each of them and every future screen test carries a wrapper it has no other reason to know about. The hook owns its own state and hands back a node instead. **Step 9's "mount the provider in the admin layout" was therefore not done, and nothing needs it.**

**Migrated (15 sites, 9 files)**: `orders/index.tsx` (prompt ×2, confirm ×1), `reviews.tsx` ×3, `products/index.tsx` ×3, `products/$id.tsx`, `promotions/index.tsx`, `collections/index.tsx`, `ai-moderation.tsx`, `approvals/$id.tsx`, `components/admin/OrderDetail.tsx`.

**Two bugs fixed on the way**
1. `orders/index.tsx` asked the operator to **type** a status into a free-text prompt, then string-matched it against an eleven-value enum — "shiped" was a silent no-op with an unhelpful banner. Now a select of the eleven; the typo-catching validation branch is gone with the typos.
2. `OrderDetail.tsx` sent the literal string `"Admin initiated refund"` as the reason for **every** refund on the platform. Now a required textarea, matching what the orders list already collected.

Also: the OrdersTable row-actions trigger gained an `aria-label` — an icon-only button with no accessible name is unreachable to a screen reader and to anything driving the table (it is what the new test could not click).

**Guard**: moved from `orders-export-button.test.tsx` to `tests/routes/admin/admin-native-dialogs.test.tsx`, widened `alert` → `alert|prompt|confirm` (bare or `window.`-qualified), extended over `app/components/admin`. It strips comments and string literals before matching — every file explaining the ban mentions the banned names, and #604 had to reword a comment to get past the narrower version. Fixtures pin both directions: catches `confirm(`, `window.confirm(`, `prompt(`, `alert(`, `window.alert (`; ignores `setAlert(`, `onConfirm(`, `confirmLabel`, `confirmAction`, `promptForValues`, and prose in `//`, `/* */` and string literals.

**Existing test updated**: `promotions.test.tsx` "confirms before deleting" asserted the native `confirm` via a spy. Rewritten to drive the in-page dialog, with the natives stubbed to **throw** rather than answer — a spy that returns `true` would let the screen regress to a native dialog with the suite still green. ticket.title: packages/web does not typecheck: 22 errors across router navigation, unused imports and unguarded nullables
ticket.description:
## Problem

`npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/web` reports **22 errors**. None are new — they accumulated because the typecheck is not a gate — but their existence is what makes every ticket's verification step ambiguous: an agent that introduces a real type error has to diff against a 22-error baseline to notice, and #604 and #625 both had to do exactly that.

Six clusters:

| Cluster | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `TS2345` — `navigate({ to })` without required `search` | 6 | `orders/$id.tsx:228`, `products/$id.tsx:346,364,384`, `products/new.tsx:138,148` |
| `TS6133` — unused imports/locals | 6 | `track/index.tsx:27,28,29`, `track/$token.tsx:24,25,142`, `ai-generator/PromptSuggestions.tsx:15` |
| `TS2741` — `<Icon />` element passed where `LucideIcon` component expected | 4 | `ai-moderation.tsx:538,545,552,559` |
| `TS2322` — `updateSearch` reducer not assignable | 2 | `orders/index.tsx:308`, `products/index.tsx:177` |
| `TS18048` / `TS18047` — unguarded nullable | 2 | `ai-moderation.tsx:770,772` |
| `TS2339` — `user.role` missing on the session user type | 1 | `admin.tsx:51` |

## Notes per cluster

- **The navigate ones are a real latent bug, not noise.** Those routes declare required search params, so a `navigate({ to: '/admin/products' })` with no `search` pushes a URL that fails the route's own `validateSearch` — and a throw inside `validateSearch` error-boundaries the route to a blank page rather than showing a message. `app/lib/admin-nav.ts` already exports `ADMIN_PRODUCTS_SEARCH` and friends for exactly this; the fix is to pass them.
- **`admin.tsx:51` is the admin guard.** `context.session.user.role` is read to decide who may enter the admin panel, and the session user type has no `role`. It works at runtime; it is unchecked at compile time, which is the wrong way round for an authorization decision. `routes/vendor.tsx` already solved this with an explicit `VendorPortalUser` interface — mirror it.
- **The `ai-moderation` icons** pass `icon={<Clock />}` where `StatsCard` declares `icon?: LucideIcon` and renders `<Icon />` itself. Every other caller passes the component.
- **The risk score** is rendered from `generation.moderationResult.riskScore` behind a `?.` guard that does not cover the arithmetic.

## Fix

Drive the count to zero, cluster by cluster, changing behaviour nowhere except where the types are pointing at a real defect (the navigate calls). Then the typecheck is usable as a gate and later tickets can assert "no type errors" instead of "no NEW type errors".

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/web` exits 0.
- `npx vitest run tests/routes tests/components` shows no regression against the pre-change run.
- The admin guard keeps refusing non-admin roles — its existing tests must still pass, since that is the one cluster touching an authorization path.

ticket.title: Three unit tests are red on main: vendor portal trips the storefront token guard, wishlist guard test trips on a comment
ticket.description:
## Problem

`npx vitest run tests` in `packages/web` is 3264 passing / **3 failing** on main. Both failures are guards firing at the wrong target, which is worse than useless: a red suite trains everyone to ignore it, and these two guards exist precisely to be believed.

### 1 & 2. The vendor portal trips the storefront token guard

`tests/styles/storefront-token-compliance.test.ts` forbids `font-bold` and `(bg|from|to|ring|border)-brand-*` outside a short exempt list (`components/admin/`, `routes/admin`, `components/ai-generator/`). The vendor portal (#621) is neither exempt nor storefront, so it fails on four lines:

- `routes/vendor.tsx:165` — `data-[active=true]:bg-brand-50 data-[active=true]:text-brand-700`
- `routes/vendor.tsx:206` — `font-bold` on the Access Denied heading
- `routes/vendor.tsx:214` — `bg-brand-500 ... hover:bg-brand-600`
- `routes/vendor/jobs/$id.tsx:234` — `bg-brand-600 ... hover:bg-brand-700`

The vendor portal is an internal supplier tool built to follow the admin screens, not a customer-facing surface — the same category as `routes/admin`, which is exempt for exactly that reason. The exemption list is the fix, not a restyle. The test file states that widening it requires making the case in writing, so the case goes in the comment.

**One caveat to record while doing it**: the `font-bold` rule is not a palette preference. Weight 700 is never loaded (see the font link in `__root.tsx`), so `font-bold` renders as synthesised faux-bold *anywhere*, admin and vendor included. Exempting the tree hides that, and the exempt trees already carry the same defect. Worth its own ticket rather than silently accepting it.

### 3. The wishlist guard test trips on a comment

`tests/routes/wishlist-page.test.ts` asserts the route source does not contain `beforeLoad` — the point being that `/wishlist` must not gain an auth guard, since saving needs no account (#477). The word now appears at `routes/wishlist.tsx:38` inside a comment explaining where the session comes from. The rule is right; the matcher reads prose as code.

Same defect the #625 guard had to solve: strip comments and string literals before matching. `tests/routes/admin/admin-native-dialogs.test.ts` already exports a `stripCommentsAndStrings` helper for this.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run tests/styles/storefront-token-compliance.test.ts tests/routes/wishlist-page.test.ts` — PASS.
- The guards still bite: adding `bg-brand-500` to a storefront file, or a real `beforeLoad` to `wishlist.tsx`, must still fail. Assert that with fixtures rather than by trusting the regex.
- Full web unit suite back to zero failures.

ticket.title: Make the typecheck a gate locally, now that it is at zero
ticket.description:
## Context

#626 took `packages/web` from 22 type errors to 0, and `bun run typecheck` (turbo, all three packages) now passes repo-wide in ~7s. CI already runs it — `.github/workflows/test.yml` has a `lint` job doing `bun run typecheck`, and the summary job fails the build if it fails. That job has presumably been red for a long time, and is only meaningful as of #626.

What is missing is the local half. Nothing stops a commit that reintroduces an error; the author finds out from CI minutes later, or — with several agents committing on this machine — someone else finds out instead.

## Fix

A committed pre-commit hook, no new dependency:

- `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `bun run typecheck`. Turbo caches it, so an unchanged tree costs a cache hit rather than a compile.
- Root `package.json` gains `"prepare": "git config core.hooksPath .githooks"`, so `bun install` wires it up for everyone without anyone having to read a README.
- The hook must be skippable (`git commit --no-verify` already is, and that is enough — do not invent a second escape hatch).

## Watch out for

- **The stale `.tsbuildinfo` problem #626 hit.** `packages/web` is `composite: true`, and a stale build info file hid ~130 errors until an edit invalidated it. A hook that trusts an incremental cache can report clean on a tree that is not. Confirm the hook's result matches a cold run before trusting it.
- Several agents share this machine and commit concurrently. The hook must not hold a lock or leave processes behind.

## Verification

- With a deliberate type error staged, `git commit` is refused and names the error.
- With the tree clean, `git commit` succeeds and the hook adds no noticeable delay on a warm cache.
- A fresh clone plus `bun install` gets the hook without extra steps (`git config core.hooksPath` reads `.githooks`).

comments.author: mcp-client
comments.text:
✅ **Completed**

**Commit**: `f51dd5b1` — chore: refuse commits that do not typecheck

**Correction to the ticket's premise**: CI was already running the typecheck — `.github/workflows/test.yml` has a `lint` job doing `bun run typecheck`, and `test-summary` fails the build on it. Nothing needed adding there. What that job has been doing all along is failing, silently as far as local work was concerned; it became a real gate the moment #626 took the count to zero. Verified: `bun run typecheck` across all three packages (`@chobii/shared`, `@chobii/api`, `@chobii/web`) now passes in ~7s cold.

**What was actually missing was the local half**
- `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `bun run typecheck`, and exits immediately when no `.ts`/`.tsx` is staged so doc and tracker commits stay instant.
- Root `package.json` gains `"prepare": "git config core.hooksPath .githooks"`, so `bun install` wires it up — no README step to miss.
- Skippable only via `git commit --no-verify`. Deliberately no env-var escape hatch: one nobody remembers setting is how a gate turns into decoration.

**Verification, both directions**
- Staged `export const probe: number = 'not a number'` → commit **refused**, output naming `app/lib/__gate-probe.ts(1,14): error TS2322`, in **2.5s** (turbo served 3 of 4 tasks from cache). Probe removed afterwards.
- Clean tree → this ticket's own commit went through the hook normally.

**Limit recorded in the hook itself**: `packages/web` is `composite: true`, and a stale `.tsbuildinfo` can under-report — that is how #626 hid ~130 errors until an edit invalidated the cache. A hook that trusts the incremental cache can therefore pass on a tree that would fail cold. CI runs cold on a fresh checkout, which is the backstop; the comment says so, so the next person does not assume the hook is exhaustive.

**Worth knowing for future tickets**: "no new type errors" is no longer the standard to verify against. It is "zero", and both a hook and CI now enforce it.

Extract into a shared hook, e.g. `packages/web/app/hooks/useScrollTrack.ts`, returning the ref plus the derived `canScrollLeft` / `canScrollRight` (or equivalent) state and the scroll handlers. Both components then consume the hook.

This is the highest-value clone in the scan: pure app code, self-contained, low risk.

ticket.title: Deduplicate test scaffolding and shared UI blocks across api and web packages
ticket.description:
Remove the remaining duplications found by the DRYwall/jscpd scan on 2026-08-17. The two pure app-code clones are handled in the sibling ticket; this ticket covers the copied test harnesses plus two shared-UI clones.

Scan baseline: 389 clones, 9,171 duplicated lines, 3.47% of 264,475 lines across `packages/**` (TS/TSX; generated drizzle migration snapshots and the mirrored `.claude`/`.agents`/`.gemini` skill docs were excluded as noise).

   `packages/web/tests/routes/admin/dashboard-product-stats.test.tsx:15-73`
   Same `vi.mock('@tanstack/react-router', ...)` block.

7. **Review fixtures — 55 lines**

   `packages/web/tests/routes/posters-review-section.test.tsx:52-108`
   Duplicated `ReviewCardData` fixture block.
   Extract to `packages/web/tests/fixtures/reviews.ts`.

8. **Admin route test harness — 52 lines**
   `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/collection-membership.test.ts:12-63`
   `packages/api/tests/routes/admin/frames.test.ts:17-67`
   Same `selectMock`/`insertMock`/`updateMock` scaffolding. Fold into the shared helper from item 2 if the shapes line up.

## Shared UI clones

9. **Paginated list block — 98 lines**
   `packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/ai-creations.tsx:554-651`
   `packages/web/app/routes/_authed/account/orders.index.tsx:328-424`
   Same loading/error/empty handling plus the `<Pagination>` wiring.
   Extract a `<PaginatedList>` component (or a `usePaginatedList` hook if the rendering diverges too much).

10. **Admin table pagination controls — 54 lines**
    `packages/web/app/components/admin/OrdersTable.tsx:675-728`

- Each listed clone pair is replaced by a single shared helper, fixture, or component.
- Extracted test helpers live under a `tests/helpers/` or `tests/fixtures/` directory in their own package — do not cross the api/web package boundary.
- No test behaviour changes: the same assertions run, and every touched suite still passes.
- Shared UI extractions are behaviour-preserving; the account pages and admin tables look and act the same.

- Prefer doing this in small commits, one clone group at a time — a single sweeping commit is hard to review and risks silently changing a mock's behaviour.

ticket.title: font-bold renders as synthesised faux-bold in the admin and vendor trees — weight 700 is never loaded
ticket.description:
## Problem

`__root.tsx` loads Poppins 300/400/500 and Urbanist 300/500. **Nothing above 500 exists in the document.** Every `font-bold` (700), `font-extrabold` (800) and `font-black` (900) is therefore drawn by the browser's synthetic-bold algorithm — the real glyphs smeared wider and heavier than either face draws, which is exactly the artefact the storefront sweep removed from 47 files.

The storefront is guarded against it by `tests/styles/storefront-token-compliance.test.ts`. The guard carries three exemptions — `components/admin/`, `routes/admin`, `components/ai-generator/`, plus `routes/vendor` added in #627 — and those trees are where the defect still lives: **21 sites across 17 files**.

The exemptions are right about the palette (the `--brand-*` scale is deliberately admin-only) and wrong about the weight. A missing font weight is not a styling preference: the internal tools render the same muddy synthetic glyphs, and nobody has looked because the guard says they are exempt.

## Fix

1. Sweep the 21 sites. `globals.css` already sets `--font-heading` on `h1–h6` at the base layer, precisely so the storefront sweep could **delete** `font-bold` from headings rather than replace it — same here. The handful of non-heading sites (sidebar wordmark, stat values) take `font-medium`, which is the heaviest weight actually loaded.
2. Split the guard's exemption model. The weight rule applies to every file under `app/`; the palette and idiom rules keep the exempt list. Today one flat `EXEMPT` array governs all five patterns, which is what let this hide.

## Out of scope, but found while measuring

`font-semibold` is 600, also not loaded, also synthesised — **176 uses, 45 of them in storefront files the guard already covers**. The guard never banned it. Fixing that means changing the visual weight of most of the customer-facing site, so it is a separate decision, not a sweep to bundle in here.

## Verification

- No `font-(bold|extrabold|black)` anywhere under `app/`.
- The widened rule fails if one is reintroduced in an admin file (fixture, not trust).
- The palette rules still exempt admin: adding `bg-brand-500` to an admin file must still pass, or the split broke them.
- Full web unit suite stays at zero failures.

**Commit**: `1515c4d9` — fix(web): stop rendering faux-bold in the admin and vendor trees

**Swept**: 21 sites across 17 files, all `font-bold` → `font-medium`. Files: `components/admin/{AdminSidebar,OrderDetail,StatsCard}.tsx`, `routes/admin.tsx`, `routes/vendor.tsx`, and `routes/admin/{index,orders/index,orders/$id,products/index,products/$id,products/new,reviews,returns,customers,ai-moderation,approvals/index,approvals/$id}.tsx`.

**Why `font-medium` and not simply deleting the class**: `globals.css` styles `h1–h6` at the base layer precisely so the storefront sweep could delete rather than replace, and most of these sites are headings. But admin and vendor are dense operational screens, and a page title at Urbanist 300 reads as a caption there. 500 is the closest true weight to the intent, and unlike 700 it is a weight the document actually has. Deliberate, and stated in the commit.

**The guard change is the durable half.** It was one flat `EXEMPT` array governing all five patterns, so exempting a tree from the palette rules silently exempted it from everything — which is exactly how this defect survived in the internal tools while the storefront was clean. Rules now carry a scope:
- `storefront` — taste, and the exempt trees are allowed their own (the `--brand-*` scale really is admin-only).
- `everywhere` — the document is wrong and no surface opts out. A missing font weight is not a preference.

Both halves are pinned by assertions: the storefront must stay in scope for the palette rules, **and** the admin tree must stay out of them while staying in scope for the weight rule. ticket.title: Decide what to do about font-semibold — weight 600 is not loaded either, and the storefront uses it 176 times
ticket.description:
## The finding

#631 swept `font-bold` out of the last trees that still rendered it, on the grounds that weight 700 is never loaded and the browser synthesises it. Measuring for that sweep turned up the same problem one notch down:

`__root.tsx` loads **Poppins 300/400/500** and **Urbanist 300/500**. `font-semibold` is **600**. It is not loaded, so it is synthesised too — the identical artefact, one step milder.

**176 uses**, 45 of them in storefront files the token guard already covers. The guard has never banned it, so this is not drift; it is a rule that was drawn at 700 when the evidence points at 600.

## Recommendation: sweep to the real weights (option 1), split by element type

Three options were weighed. The recommendation is the sweep, and the reasoning is evidence rather than taste:

1. **The reference design never uses 600.** `docs/design/mesonart/mesonart-parity-analysis.md` measures mesonart at Poppins 300 body, Urbanist 300 headings, Poppins 500 product titles and nav (§2 rows 147–150). There is no 600 anywhere in the spec. Loading it would mean paying a font request to keep a weight nobody chose.
2. **Most storefront `font-semibold` sits on headings, which already contradicts Phase A.** The uses are `h2`/`h3` in `ProductTabs`, `AddressForm`, `OrderSummary`, `FilterSortDrawer`. `globals.css` styles `h1–h6` as Urbanist 300 at the base layer precisely so headings stop carrying weight classes, and the Phase A finding was recorded as *"every heading `font-bold` at a weight that was never loaded"*. A `font-semibold` on an `h3` is the same override, one notch down and still synthetic.
3. **Accepting it fails the rule's own logic.** The ban exists because the weight is not loaded and the browser fakes it. That is equally true at 600. Leaving the line at 700 means the guard enforces a boundary drawn by accident.

### The plan

- **Headings (`h1`–`h6`): delete the class.** The base layer already supplies Urbanist 300, which is the measured spec. This is the bulk of the 176.
- **Non-heading emphasis (`<strong>`, spans, labels, captions): `font-medium`.** 500 is real, and is what mesonart uses for product titles and nav.
- **Widen the guard** to `font-(semibold|bold|extrabold|black)` on the `everywhere` scope added in #631, so 600 cannot return.

### Check before committing, not after

Small uppercase tracking labels (`text-xs font-semibold uppercase`, e.g. `track/$token.tsx`) lose the most apparent weight. If any read too faint, the fix is size, tracking or colour — not a fake weight. Screenshot home / PDP / checkout / account against the current build before and after; hold the commit if anything reads wrong.

Risk is bounded: one mechanical sweep, revertible in a single commit, with 3269 unit tests and the token guard around it.

## Whichever way it goes

The answer goes into `tests/styles/storefront-token-compliance.test.ts` — either as a widened `everywhere` pattern, or as a comment on the existing weight rule stating why 600 is deliberately allowed. The point of that file is that the next person does not have to re-derive this.

ticket.title: Deduplicate the gift-card live-database test harness across 11 suites
ticket.description:
## Task

Eleven gift-card suites each stand up the same live-database harness by hand. #630 shared one slice of it (`tests/helpers/gift-card-fixtures.ts` — the Razorpay reset and the row purge for two suites); this ticket finishes the job across the whole family.

Every suite that imports `tests/helpers/live-db.ts`:

- `tests/routes/admin-gift-card-refund.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/admin/gift-cards.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/admin/returns-store-credit.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/cart-gift-card-lines.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/gift-card-payment.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/gift-card-purchase.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/gift-card-quote.test.ts`
- `tests/routes/gift-card-release.test.ts`
- `tests/services/gift-card-delivery.test.ts`
- `tests/services/gift-card-redeem.test.ts`
- `tests/services/gift-card-refund.test.ts`

## The duplicated pieces

**1. Connect-or-mark-unreachable (~20 lines x 11)**
`admin-gift-card-refund.test.ts:65-84`, `gift-card-payment.test.ts:65-84`, `gift-card-release.test.ts:69-88`, `services/gift-card-delivery.test.ts:45-64`, `services/gift-card-refund.test.ts:49-64`.

Every one is the same block:

```ts
const DATABASE_URL = liveDbUrl()
let client: ReturnType<typeof postgres>
let db: ReturnType<typeof drizzle<typeof schema>>
let reachable = false

beforeAll(async () => {
  if (!DATABASE_URL) return
  try {
    client = postgres(DATABASE_URL, { max: 5, onnotice: () => {} })
    await client`SELECT 1`
    db = drizzle(client, { schema })
    reachable = true
  } catch {
    reachable = false
  }
  // ...suite-specific seeding
})

afterAll(async () => {
  if (client) await client.end()
})
```

Extract a `connectLiveDb()` helper returning `{ client, db, reachable }` plus a matching teardown, into `tests/helpers/live-db.ts` (it already owns `liveDbUrl` / `assertLiveDbReachable`).

**2. `freshCode()` — 7 copies**

```ts
let counter = 0
function freshCode(): string {
  counter += 1
  return `PAY${String(process.pid).padStart(6, '0')}${String(counter).padStart(7, '0')}`.slice(0, 16)
}
```

`services/gift-card-redeem.test.ts:67-88` deletes **transactions → orderGiftCards → giftCards → orders**.
`tests/helpers/gift-card-fixtures.ts` (from #630) deletes **orderGiftCards → transactions → giftCards → orders**.

ticket.title: Bug - the actor FK and the immutability trigger contradict each other
ticket.description:
## Bug
`admin_audit_log.actor_user_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, which Postgres implements as an `UPDATE` on the audit row. The immutability trigger from #636 refuses every `UPDATE`. Net effect: **deleting any user who has ever appeared in the audit log fails**, with a confusing error that names the user delete but reports the audit trigger.

Found by `tests/routes/admin/gift-cards.test.ts` teardown (`afterAll` deletes its test admin):

```
Error: Failed query: delete from "user" where "user"."id" = $1
Caused by: PostgresError: admin_audit_log is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted
where: SQL statement "UPDATE ONLY "public"."admin_audit_log" SET "actor_user_id" = NULL ..."
```

Same failure in `tests/routes/admin/customers.test.ts`.

## Fix
Drop the FK; keep `actor_user_id` as plain text. An append-only ledger must not carry a constraint whose whole job is to rewrite it. The actor is already snapshotted (`actor_email`, `actor_role`), so a dangling id is the intended state after a user is deleted — history should record who acted even when the account is gone. Reads use a LEFT JOIN, which they would have needed anyway for the SET NULL case.

The rejected alternative was teaching the trigger to permit an UPDATE that only nulls `actor_user_id`: it re-opens the UPDATE path on an append-only table to save a constraint we do not want.

## Steps
- Migration 0022 drops `admin_audit_log_actor_user_id_user_id_fk`
- `schema/audit-log.ts`: drop `.references()`, keep the relation for query convenience
- Update the schema-shape test (no FK) and add a live-DB test: insert a row, delete the user, row survives with its actor id and email intact
